One of its flagship products is the data processing platform for AI analysis, ‘Yennefer.’ In this regard, a Mondrian AI representative explained, “There were inconveniences in the AI research process, such as repetitive confirmation of output and installation environment, as well as difficulties in collaboration due to capacity shortage and version differences caused by local storage. To address these issues, we developed Yennefer, which allows everyone to perform tasks conveniently.”

The platform integrates the essential infrastructure, tools, and services for introducing data-centric AI into enterprises or organizations. Yennefer enables organizations to quickly establish an AI research and development environment, providing various features and requirements necessary for data analysts. It is a platform that allows comprehensive management of data analysis and AI service operations throughout the organization.

One of the advantages of Yennefer is its provision of an On-Premise model, allowing enterprises to use it freely without cost concerns, regardless of usage volume, after the initial setup. It is also integrated with appliances to deploy AI applications to private and hybrid clouds rapidly. This is a turnkey solution with computing and storage resources for quick deployment and scalability, suitable for new data centers, AI centers, and AI graduate schools.

The representative stated, “Yennefer has successfully undertaken platform construction projects with large enterprises, providing private cloud construction and appliances for AI. In addition, the representative mentioned, “In the future, we plan to establish a usage-based billing system through service-type software (SaaS) products and provide an AI model market service, allowing anyone to create and sell algorithms easily. 50578.cap: Liquid Handling Robot ‘NOTABLE’ Pipette │Photo provided by ABLE Labs

50578.x: ABLE Labs(CEO Shin Sang) participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time).

Dedicated to innovating the field of life sciences through cutting-edge automation solutions that enhance efficiency, precision, and reproducibility in laboratory workflows, ABLE Labs showcased its flagship product, ‘NOTABLE.’

NOTABLE is an automated liquid-handling robot designed and developed by ABLE Labs to meet the evolving demands of the life science and bio-research industries. This automation solution addresses manual pipetting and liquid handling challenges in laboratory experiments. According to the company, NOTABLE excels in aspirating and distributing small volumes with high precision, enhancing reproducibility and efficiency in various biological experiments.
The development of NOTABLE involved a comprehensive and iterative process that combined expertise in robotics, bioinformatics, and laboratory workflow.

50578.cap: Liquid Handling Robot ‘NOTABLE’ │Photo provided by ABLE Labs

50578.x: The critical stages of the development process included:
* Evaluation of research and requirements: Understanding challenges researchers face in liquid handling and identifying needs for a comprehensive automation solution.
* Design, features, and functionality brainstorming and conceptualization to meet identified requirements for NOTABLE.
* Prototyping of hardware and software components of the liquid handling robot, testing, and improvement.
* Collaborative user testing with researchers, collecting feedback, and iteratively improving the system for optimal usability and performance.

Subsequent stages involved implementing strict quality assurance measures to ensure NOTABLE’s reliability, accuracy, and safety in diverse laboratory environments. The robot was then released to the market, and continuous monitoring of user feedback led to updates, improvements, and new features.

NOTABLE’s key features include precision and accuracy, high-throughput automation, end-to-end workflow automation, flexibility and adaptability, user-centric UI/UX design, data connectivity and integration, cross-platform compatibility, compact and efficient design, predictive maintenance, and support for enhanced reproducibility, and cost-effectiveness.

ABLE Labs stated, “Based on a passion for automation and a vision for the future of bio experiments, ABLE Labs is at the forefront of leading a new era that accelerates the pace of scientific innovation through technology.”

50580.cap: Rendering of V-Space’s in-house developed AAM ‘V-Speeder’ | Provided by V-Space

50580.x: V-Space (CEO Baek Seung Won) participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas, USA from January 9th to 12th.

V-Space has accumulated independent research and development capabilities in urban air mobility (UAM) and related aircraft. They have collaborated with major aerospace companies, defense industry firms, AAM, and UAM companies and institutions, achieving diverse successes in delivering aircraft and fostering collaborations within the industry.

In particular, V-Space unveiled its self-developed Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) aircraft, ‘V-Speeder,’ last year. The model boasts outstanding performance, with a maximum takeoff weight of 300kg and a top speed of around 90km/h. It gained attention by conducting test flights in the airspace above urban areas in Korea for the first time. This achievement is unprecedented globally, excluding companies like China’s ‘Ehang’ and Germany’s ‘Volocopter.’

At CES this year, V-Space plans to exhibit and present the V-Speeder to explore opportunities in the global market. The V-Speeder complies with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) standards for personal aircraft, incorporating the company’s years of experience and technology in producing UAM aircraft and developing transportation mobility.

The currently mass-produced V-Speeder is an improved model with a payload of 120kg and a maximum speed of 80km/h, offering a full flight time of 20 minutes. Compared to competitors, the superior specifications and performance are realized by applying a high-density, high-output battery propulsion system—V-Space plans to expand sales by leveraging these advantages and a relatively lower price.

A representative from V-Space explained, “The V-Speeder, with outstanding performance relative to its price, is a product with broad applicability. It is equipped with options suitable for various applications, such as logistics delivery systems and emergency disaster rescue aircraft, enhancing its attractiveness.” Additionally, the representative expressed ambitions to diversify the product portfolio through technological diversification and expand purchases globally, aiming to become a world-class air mobility specialist.

50581.cap: On January 9th, Mayor Yoo Jeong-bok introduced the future vision of Incheon’s first-class smart hub city at the Incheon IFEZ Pavilion set up in the North Hall of the Las Vegas Convention Center | Photo by AVING News

50581.x: Incheon Metropolitan City participated in CES 2024, the world’s largest consumer electronics and information technology (ICT) show, from January 9th to January 12th.

During the convention, Incheon operated the Incheon IFEZ (Incheon Free Economic Zone) pavilion at the North Hall of the Las Vegas Convention Center (LVCC), being the only one in the LVCC Hall apart from the other local Korean government booths stationed elsewhere.

Incheon, participating in the CES for the first time, showcased innovative technologies developed by promising companies and startups in their city. The theme was ‘Light up the Future with Smart AI·Robot Solutions,’ focusing on utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) and robot technologies to enhance citizens’ lives. The exhibition featured services leveraging AI and robot technologies, including establishing an AI-based citizen perception social safety net, the designation of autonomous driving pilot zones, and operating a platform based on digital twin technology. Their booth aimed to demonstrate to visitors the transformative changes in future living through AI and robot solutions.

The booth started with a short speech and a presentation by Mayor Yoo Jeong-bok, introducing Incheon as South Korea’s “primary economic city” and a “global city,” home to 3 million citizens. Mayor Yoo highlighted the city as the home to one of the world’s best airports- Incheon International Airport, along with Incheon Port for sea traffic, the country’s first and largest economic free zone. He also mentioned the world-leading pharmaceutical companies like Samsung Biologics and Celltrion calling Incheon their home base, along with 15 UN international organizations. Incheon also focuses on air mobility and eco-friendly energy conversion, hosting the 2nd and 3rd largest companies in semiconductor post-processing, along with over 1,200 related companies. Mayor Yoo expressed pride, stating, “Incheon has become a city of 10 million people, serving as a business hub for 7 million overseas Koreans worldwide, particularly with the opening of the Overseas Koreans’ Chamber of Commerce.”

Mayor Yoo emphasized that Incheon can connect people logistics and cutting-edge technology to anyone or any organization that needs it. He expressed his vision to foster a culture where cities focus on citizen safety, convenience, and a commitment to a green environment and raise awareness with CES. He also wanted to solidify partnerships with other global cities and companies, ensuring a better future for Incheon.

Incheon has been actively developing an intelligent city for over 20 years, focusing on the Incheon Free Economic Zone. They have implemented IoT and Big Data in many facets of their city infrastructure: fire prevention systems, road traffic information analysis using sensor technology, and an AI-based disaster evacuation guidance system in subway stations. Recently, they’ve also constructed smart intersections and innovative parking platforms to enhance citizen safety and convenience and launched ‘smart towns’ to redevelop areas with vulnerable living conditions.

50581.cap: Mayor Yoo shared his future vision for Incheon’s first-class smart hub city with attendees at the IFEZ Pavilion

50581.x: After presenting the ‘First-Class Smart Hub City Future Vision,’ Incheon also stated that they’d like to set an example for other cities, encouraging them to implement new technologies into their infrastructure proactively.

Mayor Yoo outlined ambitious plans for Incheon City, emphasizing establishing a spatial innovation system. This system includes building an AI-based citizen perception social safety net, designating autonomous driving pilot zones, and operating a digital twin-based platform. The primary goal is to propel Incheon into a first-class smart city. The city aims to introduce citizen-focused intelligent solutions in the downtown area via smart transportation, smart life safety, and smart welfare.

He also expressed the city’s readiness for global collaboration, highlighting the establishment of the ‘Incheon-City Cooperation Network.’ The city plans to work with international organizations and global universities to discover and attract strong, diverse talents.

Mayor Yoo Jeong-bok also visited the SK, Samsung Electronics, LG Electronics, and Hyundai Motor booths on the second day of CES 2024, January 10th. During his visit, he met with Lotte Information & Communications’ CEO, Go Du-young, who is involved in constructing Incheon’s Intelligent Transportation System (C-ITS), to discuss collaboration strategies for startup support programs.

50589.x: On January 9th at CES 2024 in Las Vegas, Intflow, a company specializing in bringing AI into the livestock industry, showed off its latest technology,’ EdgeSafe.’ This system automatically measures and records pigs’ number, weight, and health status based on their movement, which landed them the Innovation Award at CES 2024.

The ‘EdgeSafe’ system utilizes camera-based livestock disease prevention management by automatically measuring and recording pigs’ quantity, weight, and health status through their movements. Intflow, an agtech specialist, employs non-contact biometric analysis technology for innovative livestock industry solutions.

Among these solutions, ‘EdgeSafe’ focuses on farm inventory management, optimizing feed efficiency, and disease prevention. It analyzes the activities of pigs through CCTV installed in pigsties using high-intelligence AI, specializing in inventory and specification management monitoring.

50589.cap: Intflow demonstrating their latest technology, ‘EdgeFarm’ at CES 2024

50589.x: Previously, farmers had to manually measure the weight of pigs by mobilizing themselves or a significant number of employees. However, with the introduction of ‘EdgeSafe,’ the number and weight of pigs moving through the corridor are now automatically measured and recorded, making the process even more convenient.

Moreover, by observing pigs through CCTV in the hovel, daily stock quantity, average activity level, average weight, etc., are recorded in a database. Farmers can easily monitor pig farming sites remotely with a PC or smartphone.

Edgesafe also allows the veterinarians to monitor the pigsty remotely without visiting the farm. It will enable them to confirm the effectiveness of disease prevention and treatment, especially during outbreaks. As a result, expectations are high that this will contribute to accelerating the digital transformation of the livestock industry.

50593.x: Raonark (CEO Koo Min-gi) participated in CES 2024, the world’s largest IT and electronics exhibition, held in Las Vegas from January 9th to 12th (local time).

Raonark is a domestic company that has introduced next-generation smart lock integrated solutions with a differentiated technology to the global market. They focus on a consumer-centric premium smart lock product line and possess various smart lock products, technological capabilities, and service expertise. These include automated door-opening systems and blockchain IoT (Internet of Things) security solutions.

With its technological diversity, Raonark positions itself as a ‘multi-platform’ company in the security field. They strive to develop products optimized for national standards, including fire resistance certification and integration with home networks. Through these efforts, Raonark has gained rich expertise in product planning and technological development, expanding its market presence in various domestic and international markets.

At CES 2024, Raonark showcased its smart lock solution ‘KeyinSV.’ This product goes beyond the typical functionality of digital door locks, actively utilizing audio and video-based sources in the personal authentication process.

At the same time, it maintains the traditional appearance of entry doors, including handles and all hardware components, preserving the original look of the front door. It functions as a wall-mounted module with wireless communication capabilities, offering a variety of features.

The integrated module, a core component of KeyinSV, performs various functions simultaneously, acting as a doorbell, providing facial recognition, transmitting video, and functioning as a black box camera. Equipped with precision sensors, it recognizes the faces of registered household members in advance to unlock the door. It captures images of unknown visitors, sending mobile alerts to users for verification. Additionally, it can display real-time video images captured in the entry door area.

50594.x: On January 9th (local time), GhostPass, a specialized company in private biometric information security (CEO Seon Gwan Lee), unveiled a 'Decentralized, remote self-verification solution (tentatively named: Gpass)' at 'CES 2024' held in Las Vegas, USA. This solution allows easy authentication and payment using biometric information stored on smartphones.

GhostPass is a solution that enables more secure and convenient self-verification and payment using biometric information stored on one's smart device (smartphone). The company also conducts technology verification (PoC) with specialized smart home companies, security companies, etc.

In particular, GhostPass has adopted a decentralized system where users manage their biometric information directly on their smartphones, avoiding the heavy operational system of centralized servers. Triple encryption allows data storage processing, enabling remote authentication without taking the smartphone from the bag.

GhostPass has confirmed a Proof of Concept (PoC) with a domestic company, CoMax, for use in smart door locks. It will apply in various fields such as security and construction industries, companies in the lobby form, wall pads, mixed-use buildings, hotels, resorts, etc. Furthermore, it can benefit financial and payment solutions by enhancing user convenience and providing secure solutions across diverse industries.

Seon Gwan Lee, the CEO of GhostPass, stated, "We hold a total of 33 patents, including global patents, and have the right to exercise a monopoly within the scope of those patents." He further mentioned, "Even if 6 billion people simultaneously request authentication, the method we use, with 6 billion smart devices serving as servers, ensures scalability is very easy."

Gary Shapiro, the President of CTA, is a prominent figure representing 1,500 consumer electronics companies as CTA’s CEO and a bestselling author known for works like “Ninja Innovation: The Ten Killer Strategies of the World’s Most Successful Businesses,” published in 2013. Additionally, key personnel from eight major universities in Seoul (Korea University, Konkuk University, Kyung Hee University, Kookmin University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Yonsei University, Hanyang University), one municipal district (Gwanak-gu), and three municipal startup facilities (Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul AI Hub, Seoul Campus Town) participated in the event, showcasing the collaborative efforts involved in the creation of the Seoul Integrated Pavilion.

Mayor Oh Se-hoon, who attended the opening ceremony, congratulated the Seoul Integrated Pavilion’s opening and the global expansion of Seoul’s innovative startups. He expressed his ambition for the advanced development of ‘Future Seoul Lifestyles’ based on the innovative technologies possessed by Seoul startups.

Mayor Oh stated, “This year, 81 companies participated in Seoul Pavilion, the largest ever, thanks to the collaboration of 13 institutions.” He also highlighted that out of these companies, 18 received CES Innovation Awards, recognizing their technological capabilities and serving as a significant stepping stone for their growth.

Moreover, Mayor Oh emphasized the impact of participating in CES, saying, “After investigating 17 companies that received innovation awards in CES Seoul Pavilion last year, they attracted investments of KRW 36.5 billion within a year.” He pledged continued support for research and development, testbeds, business development, and startup spaces to help more innovative companies grow.

In conclusion, Mayor Oh expressed his thoughts on the opening of the Seoul Pavilion, stating, “Seeing the Seoul Pavilion adorned in Sky Coral, the symbol of Seoul, I feel assured that a pink-tinted future is guaranteed. I hope this CES participation will ensure a bright future for Korean companies.”

50599.cap: An overview scene from the Seoul Pavilion | Photo by AVING News
After the opening ceremony, Mayor Oh Se-hoon took a commemorative photo with Seoul Pavilion Supporters | Photo by AVING News

50599.x: 18 of 81 companies participating in the Seoul Integrated Pavilion received ‘CES 2024 Innovation Awards,’ and two even won the ‘CES 2024 Best Innovation Award.’ Seoul Business Agency provided CES Innovation Award specialized consulting to participating companies, contributing to their success. Notably, this year marked the first time in the history of Seoul-operated CES exhibition halls to produce a ‘Best Innovation Award,’ with LordSystem in the data and AI field and TopTable in the healthcare sector receiving the prestigious recognition.

Kim Hyun-woo, CEO of SBA, expressed his reflections, saying, “By operating CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion, we will actively promote Seoul’s changing lifestyle based on advanced technology to the global market and actively support Seoul’s promising startups with innovative technologies for global expansion.”

50600.cap: Mayor Oh Se-hoon delivered a congratulatory speech at the Seoul Innovation Forum hosted by the Seoul Business Agency (SBA) on the evening of the 9th (local time).

50600.x: Seoul Business Agency (SBA), Seoul's innovation support organization working towards creating a smart city in Seoul, held the Seoul Innovation Forum at CES 2024 in Las Vegas on January 9th (local time). CES 2024 is the world's largest IT exhibition in Las Vegas, showcasing innovative technologies from global companies like Samsung, LG, and Google and startups from various countries.

To leverage this global exhibition for the worldwide expansion of Seoul and Seoul-based companies, the city of Seoul and SBA established the CES Seoul Pavilion within CES Eureka Park, consolidating Seoul's leading startup ecosystem. They also organized additional events for technological exchange, including the Seoul Innovation Forum.

The Seoul Innovation Forum saw the participation of around 200 individuals from domestic major corporations, mid-sized enterprises, startup support organizations, and unicorn companies. Representatives from leading Korean companies like Samsung, LG, and SK, exhibiting at CES 2024, shared insights into current technological trends. Representatives from Seoul-based major universities (8 institutions) and startup support organizations (4 organizations) who collaborated at CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion also brightened the forum.

The forum included discussions on CES 2024 technology trends centered around artificial intelligence (AI) and panel discussions on successful strategies for Korean companies to enter the U.S. market. It provided a networking opportunity for participants to share technological insights freely.

50600.cap: Representatives from unicorn companies Noom and FiscalNote are conducting a panel discussion on the global expansion of Seoul companies at the Seoul Innovation Forum.

50600.x: The opening keynote speech was delivered by NCsoft's CEO, Yoon Song-yi, emphasizing the advancement of AI technologies beyond Generative AI starting in 2023 and highlighting the role of AI-native companies in Korea's future.

The second session featured a panel talk with the CEOs of Noom (CEO Jung Se-joo) and FiscalNote (CEO Tim Hwang), both Korean unicorn companies with headquarters in the U.S. They shared their respective strategies for success as Korean companies in the U.S. market.

CEO Jung Se-joo of Noom highlighted the significant progress in the healthcare and AI industries at this year's CES. CEO Tim Hwang of FiscalNote also focused on developing generative AI industries and introduced industry trends involving active collaborations between open AI and startups. Various topics were covered during the forum, including a lecture by neuroscientist Professor Jang Dong-sun on human security, an issue prompted by the development of generative AI.

During the forum, Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon announced the plan to host 'Seoul Smart Life Week' (tentative name) in October 2024, aiming for a global exhibition format where technology companies related to smart life, including those from CES 2024 and international cities, including Seoul, gather to discuss technological advancements and showcase innovative products.

Mayor Oh expressed pride in Seoul's innovative ecosystem, stating, "The innovation ecosystem of Seoul, the capital of South Korea, is sufficient to feel proud." He emphasized the vision of making Seoul Smart Life Week a global event like CES and invited the participation of forum attendees to realize this dream.

50601.cap: On January 10th, at 10:00 AM local time at LVCC Central Hall, Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon visited LG Electronics’ booth. The mayor experienced LG’s latest future mobility concept, Alpha-able, while hearing explanations from the LG’s representative.

50601.x: On Tuesday, January 9th at 5:30 PM PST, Mayor Oh Se-hoon announced ‘Seoul Smart Life Week’ at the ‘Seoul Innovation Forum 2024’ held in Las Vegas, USA. The three-year roadmap outlines Seoul’s plan to use its smart city network as a foundation to promote innovative tech companies globally and lead future technology trends.
Seoul Metropolitan City revealed that ‘Seoul Smart Life Week (Exhibition + Awards + Forum)’ will be held from October 7th to 9th, Monday to Wednesday, at COEX this year.

Leveraging Seoul’s Global Recognition as a Leading Smart City as the winner of the ‘Barcelona Smart City Award’ in 2022 and Host of the ‘Seoul Smart City Prize’ in 2023, the city aims to establish its unique competitiveness. This foundation will seek to secure pathways for innovative companies, attract investments, and develop a global business platform for sharing advanced technologies of the future.

Seoul City, embodying the governance philosophy of ‘Accompanying the Vulnerable,’ organized the inaugural ‘Seoul Smart City Prize’ in September last year. Based on the city’s vision for a future smart city that addresses urban polarization issues and promotes inclusive growth, this event saw the participation of 47 countries and 93 cities worldwide. The aim is to spread the global vision to resolve urban disparities and foster inclusive development.
Establishing the Roadmap for ‘Seoul Smart Life Week’: Utilizing the Brand’ Smart Leading City Seoul’ to create a platform for sales and exchanging innovative technologies.
The roadmap focuses on showcasing Seoul’s excellence in smart city solutions, fostering sales for innovative tech companies, and facilitating the exchange of technological trends.

The city envisions ‘Seoul Smart Life Week’ evolving beyond a simple electronics industry product showcase at CES. It aims to transform itself into a global hub for innovative technologies, with diverse participants from businesses, governments, and organizations. The roadmap plans to present specialized thematic exhibitions annually, aligning with the latest technologies and lifestyle trends, catering to world city officials and global companies attending the event.

During ‘Seoul Smart Life Week,’ Seoul will curate its exhibition space to showcase Seoul’s excellence in smart city solutions and the advanced innovative technologies of domestic companies. It aims to provide opportunities for experiencing daily life in the smart city of Seoul, securing overseas expansion channels for businesses, and attracting investors.

The current roadmap emphasizes activating the city government network, expanding the exchange of innovative products among businesses, and presenting the vision for the future smart city. The goal is to establish ‘Smart Leading City Seoul’ as a prominent global convention for the mutual exchange and collaboration of cutting-edge innovative smart city technologies among cities and companies worldwide.

This year, the focus is on showcasing Seoul’s expertise in smart city technology to the world through the existing ‘Seoul Smart City Prize.’ It serves as a platform for the city and businesses to demonstrate their proficiency in smart city solutions, laying the groundwork for companies to expand internationally.

Seoul City plans to establish a Smart City Seoul Zone by showcasing examples of the city’s leading adoption and utilization of AI technology in areas such as welfare, tourism, safety, and civic issue analysis. Through these cases, the aim is to demonstrate how the quality of services and the lives of Seoul citizens are evolving.

On the other hand, a Smart Life Zone will showcase a comprehensive array of smart technologies from Korean companies. This zone will cover recent trends, including AI technology, and encompass various areas such as mobility, Big Data, smart homes, digital twins, digital healthcare, IoT, and robotics.

Next year, the event will expand to more than twice its size this year through the coordination of international events held in Seoul. This expansion aims to provide a platform for sharing and collaborating on the status of smart cities and technologies worldwide.

In 2026, the plan is to expand advanced technological developments into everyday life across various fields, allowing for the experience of smart living in the present and the future. Technologies that everyone can feel intimately in their homes and daily lives will take center stage, with the participation of numerous global companies, establishing themselves as icons and leading the trends in future smart life technologies.

Furthermore, leveraging the ‘Seoul Smart City Prize,’ a specialized organizing committee called the Seoul Smart Life Week Organizing Committee, consisting of government, industry, and academia experts, will be formed. The committee will put effort into attracting domestic and international companies and buyers and inviting renowned figures to participate in the event.

Additionally, the city plans to gradually expand and connect various events to provide a comprehensive experience of smart city life in Seoul. Simultaneously hosting multiple programs, the goal is to establish ‘Seoul Smart Life Week’ as a leading international event in Asia, aiming to ultimately surpass CES in terms of significance.

In addition, by 2031, the city plans to utilize the 100,000㎡ Jamsil Sports·MICE Complex, part of the Seoul International District, incorporating distinctive design and advanced technology, as a premier platform to share future smart life technologies with the world.

Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon expressed his ambition, stating, “As evidenced by the 143 innovative awards received by Korean companies out of over 700 participants in this year’s CES, the innovation ecosystem of South Korea and Seoul has reached a level of pride that everywhere in the world can feel.” He added, “Now, I will launch ‘Seoul Smart Life Week’ to showcase the products and services of companies leading the innovation ecosystem in Seoul. I aim to challenge and develop it within three years, akin to the growth of CES.”

50601.cap: On January 9th, at 1:40 PM local time, Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon visited the La French Tech booth at CES 2024 to exchange opinions with the representative and discuss cooperation.

50601.x: Promotion of ‘Seoul Smart Life Week,’ visiting the CES exhibition hall for global technology benchmarking: Utilizing technology for vulnerable groups and lifestyle improvements in line with the city’s policy of ‘Accompanying the Vulnerable’

Mayor Oh Se-hoon visited the CES exhibition hall from the 9th to the 10th, Monday to Tuesday. During this time, he promoted Seoul Smart Life Week to the government and businesses, seeking ways to utilize global innovative technology in line with the city’s policies.

On January 9th at 1:30 PM PST, Mayor Oh visited the CES National Startup Exhibition Eureka Park, showing his encouragement and support at the KOTRA booth (Ministry of Industry), the Startup Promotion Foundation booth (Jung-gu Office), as well as other domestic and international booths. Additionally, he explored various startups from countries like Japan, the Netherlands, and France, displaying technologies akin to Seoul’s policies, such as assistive technologies and lifestyle-related innovations.

Eureka Park featured 113 companies from the KOTRA’s Korea Pavilion (representing Gyeonggi, Ulsan, Gangwon, Chungnam, etc.), 100 from the KISED K-Startup Pavilion, 93 from the France’s La French Tech Pavilion, 61 from the Netherlands’ NL Pavilion, and 30 companies from the Japan’s J-Startup Pavilion.

The ‘FINTIN V1,’ developed by the Korean startup ‘ONECOM’ and showcased at the KOTRA Pavilion, has achieved the world’s first implementation of blind typing based on tactile recognition for smooth smartphone use by visually impaired individuals. This innovative technology, allowing users to input keys without confirming the key positions, earned the device the top innovation award in the mobile device category.

ZKRYPTO, a Korean blockchain technology startup affiliated with the Startup Promotion Agency, was awarded the top innovation award at CES 2024 for its ‘zkVoting Booth.’ zkVoting ensures the secure transmission of voting information without disclosing the voter’s identity and ballot content.

A standout product among the 30 startups participating in the J-Startup Pavilion is WILLTEX’s product called “WILLCOOK.” It is a bag-shaped microwave that offers easy food cooking and storage functions simultaneously, catering to the busy lifestyle of modern individuals. This product received the top innovation award in the home appliance category.

The NL Pavilion, participating for the 8th consecutive year, stood out for its healthcare systems, considered among the best in Europe. Most medical device markets comprise small and medium-sized enterprises, resulting from collaborations with medical research and healthcare institutions. WHISPP’s product, Whispp, utilizes AI-based real-time voice assistance technology and a communication app. It helps patients with vocal cord damage and speech disorders by converting whispered or poorly pronounced words into clear, natural-sounding speech.

On January 10th, at 10:00 AM local time at LVCC Central Hall, Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon visited LG Electronics’ booth. The mayor experienced LG’s latest future mobility concept, Alpha-able, while hearing explanations from the LG’s representative.

On the following day, January 10th, Mayor Oh’s group toured the Las Vegas Convention Center (LVCC) Central Hall and West Hall intensively in the morning and afternoon. After exploring the LVCC Central Hall - showcasing key technologies related to smart cities, healthcare, environmental-friendly solutions, lifestyle, and creative industries - they moved to the LVCC West Hall. In this section, the mayor directly experienced innovative technologies from domestic and international companies in the mobility sector. The focus was on exploring collaboration opportunities, including open innovation, to support the growth of Seoul-based companies into global enterprises.

The LVCC Central Hall featured innovative technologies and products in consumer electronics, games, metaverse, and XR. At the same time, LVCC West Hall provided insights into vehicle-related technologies such as autonomous vehicles, electric cars, and robotics.

The Seoul mayor’s group saw Bosch’s gun-detection system that utilizes motion sensors for detecting actions. They considered that this system could integrate into crime prevention efforts to create a safer and smarter Seoul in the current social context, where issues like street crimes and dating violence are prevalent.

They also particularly paid attention to Sony’s carbon-neutral electric scooter, SK Group’s AI-based environmentally friendly waste management system, Samsung Electronics’ mobile health management app, and LG Electronics’ wireless portable display without spatial constraints.

At last, the mayor’s group toured the booth of Supernal, an independent eVTOL subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Group specializing in urban air mobility in the United States. They explored S-A2, Supernal’s eVTOL vehicle product concept, and experienced firsthand arriving at and boarding the Vertiport (UAM landing site). The UAM market involves various fields, such as battery technology, electronic control systems, communication, and AI, being a high-value-added business.

Amazon, Mercedes-Benz, Qualcomm, Hyundai Motor, and other leading companies are examining the latest technological trends poised to dominate the global market. Additionally, they are exploring ways the city of Seoul can support sustainable technological development for these companies. The mayor expected Seoul to become a crucial hub for emerging industries.
Meeting and Booth Tour with the Vice Chairman of HD Hyundai: HD Hyundai’s Interest and Participation Request for ‘Seoul Smart Life Week’

On January 10th, at 3:30 PM PST, Mayor Oh met with the Vice Chairman of HD Hyundai for a regular meeting and toured the HD Hyundai booth, where he observed future construction equipment. During the meeting, Mayor Oh expressed his agreement with HD Hyundai’s innovative direction of applying advanced technology to the construction industry to enhance safety and productivity, utilizing renewable energy for eco-friendly sustainability. He emphasized the importance of coexisting with environmental sustainability for the company’s activities and future. Mayor Oh also sought HD Hyundai’s interest and participation in ‘Seoul Smart Life Week,’ which explores new economic avenues under the theme of ‘Smart Life’ through future advanced technologies.

50602.cap: Lee Tae-Yong, CEO of Human Performance Lab, struck a pose at CES 2024, the world’s largest consumer electronics and IT exhibition held in Las Vegas on January 9th (local time). | Photo by AVING News

50602.x: Human Performance Lab (CEO Lee Tae-yong) participated in CES 2024, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition in Las Vegas from January 9th to 12th.

Human Performance Lab, founded by Professor Lee Tae-yong, a leading figure in the field of biomechanics of the foot, through the Ewha Womans University faculty startup program, attracted industry attention by unveiling an AI-based, non-face-to-face custom-order platform for insoles that optimizes individual foot health.

Their platform, ‘FitSole,’ captures video and images of the foot’s appearance, creates a 3D model based on it, and analyzes it using AI with numerical analysis technology. Human Performance Lab showcased this innovation at CES 2024 to attract global customers.

FitSole provides consumers with insoles that improve and enhance their foot health most effectively based on various criteria, such as materials and shapes. The company explained that the time taken for measurements is reduced by more than 70% compared to face-to-face methods, and the time required for insole production can be shortened to 1/30 of the conventional level.

Moreover, the AI model embedded in the app utilizes data from the soles of feet before and after a load of 30,000 times, ensuring reliability in the therapeutic effects provided by the results. At the same time, Human Performance Lab obtained four patents related to the FitSole solution and demonstrated the effectiveness and functionality of its technology through over 30 SCI papers.

Lee Tae-yong, CEO of Human Performance Lab, expressed his pleasure at participating in CES, the world’s largest event, saying, “I am glad to be able to showcase our technological capabilities to audiences of various nationalities worldwide.” He added, “It was also an opportunity to understand the overall atmosphere and insights of the industry by identifying the presence of other companies that are unveiling similar items, both domestically and internationally.”

He continued, “The value that our company aims for through FitSole is to provide personalized insoles anywhere in the world based on consumer foot data uploaded to the server,” and concluded, “Accordingly, it is crucial to make our existence and name known to people worldwide, and I expect that this CES will significantly contribute to enhancing global recognition.”

50603.cap: Kim Jin-wook, CEO of MindLogic, at the booth with the technology demo in CES 2024 | Photo by AVING News

50603.x: MindLogic (CEO Kim Jin-wook and Kim Yong-woo) participated in CES 2024, the world’s largest electronics and IT expo held in Las Vegas from the 9th to the 12th (local time).

Under the slogan ‘Creating AI that people want to talk more with,’ MindLogic has developed and provided commercial chatbot services based on generative AI. Their social AI metaverse chat platform, ‘OpenTown,’ has proven highly popular in the market, ranking 6th in the social category of ‘2022 Koreans’ favorite Mobile Apps’.

Additionally, among the services currently offered by MindLogic are the following: △ Corporate solution ‘MindLogic Chat API,’ which combines ChatGPT and MindLogic’s conversation engine △ All-in-One Virtubing Solution ‘OpenTown Studio’ △ 1:1 English talk service ‘Deep Learning English’ through AI tutors.
In addition to various AI services aimed at global market entry, MindLogic showcased its chat API service at CES 2024, leading a promotional strategy for user expansion.

MindLogic Chat API is characterized by its unique ‘Persona Chatbot,’ offering differentiated functionality and personality compared to existing services like ChatGPT. The company’s proprietary technology minimizes the risk of hallucination, a persistent issue in generative AI, enhancing the reliability of the information provided by chatbots.

Simultaneously, the ability to remember the user’s name and conversation content for an extended period, along with supporting voice conversations beyond text-based communication, enables the formation of a sense of connection between the chatbot and the user, according to the company’s explanation.

Moreover, the Persona Chatbot can be easily installed on specific web pages using a plugin method without a separate development process. It also provides a console system for administrators to check and manage user communication content easily.

50603.cap: Kim Jin-wook, CEO of MindLogic, interviewing with Jay Kennedy Marcus, a reporter from AVING News, at CES 2024 in Las Vegas on the 9th (local time) | Photo by AVING News

50603.x: Kim Jin-wook, CEO of MindLogic, expressed satisfaction, stating, “From the name ‘Persona Chatbot,’ we were able to meet many global attendees who showed interest in our product.” He added, “Especially the positive responses from potential partners willing to collaborate on providing and expanding services in North America, beyond end-users, are one of the achievements of participating in CES, making us pleased to establish a foundation for substantial revenue generation.”

50604.cap: Leo Thevenet, editor of the French IT·AI media’ Le Café du Geek’ (center), and Toonsquare representatives, including CEO Lee Ho-young, posing for the photo after the interview│Photo by AVING News

50604.x: Toonsquare (CEO Lee Ho-young) participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tue) to 12th (Fri) local time, introducing ‘Tooning Studio’ featuring generative AI technology at the Eureka Park booth.

Toonsquare operates the web browser-based Software as a Service (SaaS) AI artificial intelligence webtoon creation platform called ‘Tooning’ service. Tooning incorporates Toonsquare’s core AI technology optimized for digital creation, including Tooning Editor, Tooning Magic AI (Beta), and Tooning World (Beta) services (as of July 2023).

Tooning Editor is an AI-based content creation service that allows users to create various forms of digital content easily and quickly based on their writing or stories. Additionally, Tooning Magic AI is a high-quality image creation service that allows anyone to generate high-resolution images by clicking on or directly entering prompts needed for image creation within the service.

Tooning World is a platform where users can experience original webtoon content from Tooning and various webtoons and share and post their own created webtoons. In Tooning World, AI is used to develop Webtoons (for all generations) and Toptoons (for adults), offering Webtoons created with AI and Webtoons by professional artists and allowing readers to share their works.

By integrating Toonsquare’s natural language processing AI technology (NLP: Natural Language Processing), which includes ‘emotion analysis’ and ‘morpheme analysis,’ with image-generating AI models such as Stable Diffusion and ChatGPT, Toonsquare explains that it can reduce working hours in the digital content production process and enhance the completeness of digital content. Furthermore, Tooning is creating a low-cost, high-quality webtoon production environment by applying Toonsquare’s Webtoon auto-generation AI technology to the existing webtoon production process.

50604.cap: Toonsquare booth at CES 2024 Eureka Park │Photo by AVING News

50604.x: In the future, Toonsquare plans to release the web browser-based ‘Tooning Magic AI’ (SaaS) beta globally, not only in Korea but also centered around the United States.

Regarding this, Lee Ho-young, CEO of Toonsquare, who met with Aving News at CES 2024, said, “Visitors to our booth are already familiar with and have experience using generative AI, making the meetings at the exhibition meaningful. Many visitors asked specific questions based on their experience with various generative AIs.” He also expressed hope to meet companies with expertise in collaboration or research through this exhibition and ongoing research projects with an AI company in Canada that learns emotions.

He added, “This participation goes beyond a simple exhibition; it has become a space for exchanging generative AI technology. Through networking among leaders, experts, and practitioners in the generative AI field, Toonsquare had in-depth discussions on the rapidly evolving AI ecosystem. Such exchanges will play an important role not only in the technological development of Toonsquare but also in promoting innovation throughout the AI industry.” He further emphasized that direct feedback from users received during this exhibition would be a valuable asset in advancing AI technology and products.

Regarding plans, CEO Lee mentioned, “Especially at CES, there was strong interest from investors, leading to more secondary meetings upon returning to Korea. This is evidence that Toonsquare’s growth potential has been recognized internationally, and we can now anticipate expectations for future development.” He concluded that all these experiences catalyze solidifying Toonsquare’s capabilities in ‘generative AI technology,’ ‘hustle and passion as a startup,’ and beyond, fostering ‘ambitious dreams.’ Based on this foundation, Toonsquare will continue to pursue innovation and explore the path of new possibilities.

50606.cap: Camelotech booth at CES 2024 │Photo by AVING News

50606.x: Camelotech (CEO Jung Won-chul) participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tue) to 12th (Fri, local time), and unveiled a specialized herbal medicine production automation system for traditional Korean medicine clinics and hospitals.

Since its establishment in 2020, Camelotech has been devoted to innovating the manufacturing, compounding, and prescribing methods of traditional herbal medicines in traditional Korean medicine. Camelotech’s HAP system automates virtually every step of the herbal medicine production process, from preparation and manufacturing to packaging and cleaning, with just one click, according to the company. Additionally, this system allows users to check the remaining herbal medicines in real-time and place orders online.

In traditional Korean medicine, treatment and prescription occur within hospitals, involving the compounding and manufacturing of herbal medications on-site. The HAP system aims to automate and streamline these manual processes, ultimately reducing the workload of traditional Korean medicine clinics.

In particular, existing herbal medicine manufacturing equipment is known to have a minimum boiling time of 200 minutes. After transferring to packaging equipment, it is cleansed to prepare herbal medicines for the next patient. In contrast, the HAP system can produce up to 40 sheets (2 boxes) in under 5 minutes, and its internal facilities can be automatically cleaned and sterilized, according to the explanation.

A Camelotech representative met at CES 2024 and said, “Our company aims to expand beyond traditional herbal medicine manufacturing into the market for creating customized medicines. We especially aim to enable personalized prescriptions for healthy functional foods that can be consumed,” and added, “Through this exhibition, we hope to gain insights into how to localize and approach the U.S. market actively.”

50606.cap: Camelotech booth at CES 2024 │Photo by AVING News

50606.x: He continued, “The company’s vision is to expand globally, starting from Japan beyond the Korean market. Following CES, we plan to actively enhance the recognition of our solutions in the U.S. market,” explained the background of their participation in the exhibition.

50607.cap: RUAHLAB received the CES 2024 Innovation Award with the wearable respiratory measurement and analysis system ‘RUAH.’ │ Photo by AVING News

50607.x: RUAHLAB (CEO Lee Tae-yang) participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tue) to 12th (Fri, local time).

RUAHLAB is a technology startup with a core value of promoting human health through research and development related to respiration. In line with this philosophy, the company is researching the RUAH system, which allows individuals to monitor their breathing easily through an app at home. RUAHLAB provides lifestyle health management devices and app services related to breathing, sleep, exercise, and mental health. The company is collaborating with outstanding professors from Hanyang University’s College of Engineering and College of Medicine, conducting R&D and verifying the functionality of RUAH products.

RUAH is a wearable respiratory measurement and analysis system targeting the global sleep apnea diagnosis market. By acquiring and analyzing respiratory-related indicators during sleep, the solution can actively manage abnormal respiration, such as sleep apnea and snoring, that impairs sleep quality. As a result, it has secured clear differentiation from other healthcare solutions. According to the company’s explanation, it simultaneously allows the management of daily health indicators such as sleep, exercise, and mental health.

The RUAH solution, consisting of a dedicated wearable device and app, maximizes the reliability and utility of the data obtained through an AI (artificial intelligence) sleep analysis algorithm. This simple configuration is considered a significant advantage, resolving issues such as the one-time nature and low convenience of the standard sleep apnea test, known as polysomnography.

A representative of RUAHLAB said, “The RUAHLAB team has improved the technological capabilities and accuracy of ‘RUAH’ through various prototype versions. In this process, we also increased our expertise in respiration and sleep by consulting experts and professors from the College of Medicine and Engineering. Efforts were made to solve problems arising from numerous variables. Through these efforts, we also developed an AI sleep analysis algorithm.” He added, “We requested an evaluation from a national certification agency for RUAH and obtained achievements in the minimum flow rate measurement and respiratory rate accuracy sections. In this way, RUAH takes a step closer to the goal of digitalized respiratory management for health management, receiving recognition for its innovation and technological capabilities by winning the CES 2024 Innovation Award.”

50607.cap: Lee Tae-yang, CEO of RUAHLAB, demonstrated the ‘RUAH’ solution in person. │ Photo by AVING News

We held meetings with various companies for business purposes, including those that can distribute our products, those with whom we can discuss investment, and those that can help us explore overseas markets. 50608.cap: Phantomics received the CES 2024 Innovation Award in the digital healthcare sector for its non-invasive myocardial disease diagnostic solution ‘Myomics.’ │Photo by AVING News

50608.x: Biotech startup Phantomics participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tue) to 12th (Fri, local time), to showcase its medical AI solution ‘Myomics.’

Phantomics possesses image biomarker technology that provides rapid and accurate diagnostic results through medical images such as MRI or CT. Based on this technology, the company introduced the myocardial disease diagnostic solution ‘Myomics.’ Phantomics continues its research and development to expand the scope of non-invasive diagnostic solutions for rapid and accurate diagnoses in cardiovascular, liver, and muscle wasting diseases.

Biopsy tests of myocardial tissues by inserting a catheter into the heart were essential for accurately diagnosing and monitoring many heart diseases. The company explains the Myomics-virtual biopsy as a safe, fast, and accurate non-invasive AI diagnostic solution replacing invasive myocardial tissue tests.

Non-invasive diagnostics, such as Phantomics’ Myomics, diagnose without creating holes or incisions in the body. Representative non-invasive diagnostic technologies include X-rays, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and computed tomography (CT). While non-invasive diagnostics are less painful and more comfortable than invasive methods that require creating wounds in the body, they are known to have lower accuracy. However, recent technological advancements have improved the range and accuracy of non-invasive diagnostics. Phantomics released Myomics in early 2022, using cardiac MRI to extract dozens of image biomarkers non-invasively. This allows for the safe and accurate diagnosis of myocardial diseases such as heart failure, myocarditis, and amyloidosis.

Regarding this solution, a Phantomics representative stated, “We have developed the optimal model using the best artificial intelligence algorithms, and we have optimized it based on local data to enhance diagnostic accuracy. We have also implemented a sophisticated algorithm that allows continuous updates for all publicly available clinical evidence up to the present.”

50608.cap: Reporter Jay Kennedy Marcus is interviewing at the Phantomics booth. │Photo by AVING News

50608.x: Recognizing such technological capabilities, Phantomics received the Innovation Award in the digital healthcare sector at CES 2024.

In addition, Myomics was praised for its optimized explanation function for doctors, nurses, patients, and caregivers and its workflow that approaches the presentation of essential evidence, available in all systems such as hospital information systems, web, and mobile.

The representative stated, “Currently, Myomics is used in major hospitals in Korea, Japan, China, Taiwan, and Singapore. We have obtained approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. We have also completed sales contracts with medical device distributors in Southeast Asia and South America and are in the process of obtaining local medical device approvals.” He added, “We participated in CES to introduce our differentiated products to medical companies in North America and Europe. By revolutionizing MRI interpretation, we aim to provide rapid and accurate information to doctors, contributing to human health.”

50609.cap: At CES 2024, mpWAV received CES Innovation Awards in the ‘Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps’ and ‘Digital Health’ categories for its hearing assistance application ‘ClearSense Audio.’ | Photo by AVING News

50609.x: mpWAV, led by CEO Park Hyeong-min, showcased its hearing assistance application, ‘ClearSense Audio,’ at CES 2024, held in Las Vegas from January 9 to 12. With this application, the company received the CES 2024 Innovation Awards Honoree in the ‘Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps’ and ‘Digital Health’ categories.

mpWAV actively introduced its award-winning hearing assistance application, ‘ClearSense Audio.’ ClearSense Audio goes beyond simply replacing the basic hearing aid function to alleviate hearing loss issues in older people. It helps everyone, including those without hearing impairment, hear desired sounds clearly in noisy environments.

mpWAV, founded to productize core technologies for advanced voice enhancement and voice recognition, boasts a rich research experience in the field. Professor Park Hyeong-min and his research team from Sogang University successfully developed essential technologies for voice enhancement and recognition applicable in real-world complex noise environments. The technologies include multi-channel acoustic echo cancellation, beamforming, signal separation, and robust speech recognition. The company offers comprehensive solutions encompassing hardware and software for various voice interface applications, ranging from innovative hearing aids to smart homes, smart cars, electronics, robots, kiosks, and voice chatting in diverse meeting systems.

A mpWAV representative stated, “Many challenges arise for the middle-aged and elderly due to hearing loss and various surrounding noises, hindering effective communication with others. We noticed that a significant portion of this demographic, not necessarily suffering from severe hearing loss, faces discomfort. Moreover, even those who need hearing aids are reluctant due to the exposure of wearing them, excessive auditory stimulation from sound amplification, and high costs.”

To address these issues, mpWAV developed its technology, allowing users to use their smartphones and earphones to selectively remove distortion-free noise in noisy acoustic environments, enabling them to hear desired sounds anytime. This approach not only resolves fundamental issues with hearing aids but also presents an affordable app format, allowing the general public to access hearing assistance when needed easily.
In this way, mpWAV has succeeded at CES 2024 by receiving innovation awards in two categories, recognizing its contribution to improving users’ quality of life and realizing social value.

Additionally, discussions are underway for collaborations with partners requiring hardware and software technology related to voice interfaces, aiming to introduce various application products.”

Furthermore, they added, “During this exhibition period, we observed significant interest from U.S. and European companies in our technology. Meaningful discussions were also held with venture-accelerating companies located in Silicon Valley.”

50610.cap: The M.E.N.D. BioSimulator showcased the ‘CARDIOS’ solution for automatic cardiovascular disease risk prediction at CES 2024. | Photo by AVING News

50610.x: The M.E.N.D. BioSimulator, led by CEO Lee Jun-sang, participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas from January 9th to 12th.

The M.E.N.D. BioSimulator provides an automatic cardiovascular disease risk prediction solution using precision 3D vascular models and artificial intelligence-based algorithms. The company’s flagship software, CARDIOS (Coronary Artery Risk Diagnostics Integrating On-site Software), automatically acquires a 3D cardiovascular model from patients’ X-ray and CT images. It performs high-dimensional operations to identify the major lesions in the cardiovascular system within minutes.

According to officials, this solution enables non-invasive, AI-based, and accurate data-driven cardiovascular diagnostic factor predictions throughout the entire process from pre-diagnosis to treatment. Skipping the probing process required for patient visits and tests for cardiovascular diagnostic factor measurements can lead to significant cost savings in the treatment process.

CARDIOS automates the entire process required for cardiovascular diagnosis, allowing immediate use in medical settings without the assistance of external experts. Moreover, by utilizing vascular shape data, blood flow data, and patient physiological data directly from the medical field, the system prevents the leakage of medical clinical data to external sources.

An official from The M.E.N.D. BioSimulator stated, “This solution enhances the possibility of early diagnosis through the utilization of health checkups and can also be used for procedure prognosis monitoring. It has achieved 98% accuracy compared to conventional testing methods and can produce diagnostic results within 5 minutes.”

50610.x: The M.E.N.D. BioSimulator introduced a range of AI-based medical software and physiological monitoring systems at CES 2024, including MIASfacial (Facial Asymmetry Quantification and Filler Procedure Monitoring System), N-UDS (Non-invasive Urodynamic Test System), Blood Glucose Monitoring System (System predicting and monitoring blood glucose levels using real-time biosignal data measured through wearable devices), and CBCT Denoising sCT System (CBCT Image Noise Reduction System). Through these innovations, the company aims to secure independent influence in the global medical device market.

The official further emphasized, “While focusing on securing certification and inspection institution infrastructure using our software and devices domestically, our goal is to enhance momentum for market expansion and global business development in the future. They continued, “During the exhibition period, we introduce the company through consultations with various companies from different countries. Additionally, we anticipate creating valuable opportunities by meeting with participating startup companies.

We plan to achieve over KRW 30 billion in sales by 2027, securing a main business. Starting with inspection institutions, between 2024 and 2027, we intend to expand our revenue model through annual subscriptions, indefinite licenses, and additional CT services, intensifying our focus on the health checkup market following the aging trend.”

The company is developing medical devices for managing symptoms of the autonomic nervous system and a wellness platform in the form of consumer electronics. NeuroTX’s technology is focused on customizing functionality to stimulate the release of specific neurotransmitters and activate the anti-inflammatory pathway according to each patient’s needs. SleepAid-P enables users to effortlessly utilize periodic sleep management functions based on the collected data. The device uses this data to deliver personalized stimuli to the user’s autonomic nervous system. This not only promotes safe and effective sleep but also enhances the overall quality of sleep. Additionally, the wearable patch design minimizes discomfort during use.

50613.cap: Park Chan-sik, CEO of ConTILab, posing at his company booth at CES 2024 in Las Vegas from January 9 to 12. | Photo by AVING News

50613.x: ConTILab, led by CEO Park Chan-sik, participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas from January 9 to 12.

Established as an experimental company from the Construction Technology Innovation Lab at Chung-Ang University in 2022, ConTILab has been developing the industrial site safety accident prevention solution ‘iSafe’ platform to achieve ‘zero workplace accidents.’ The core of their technology is an artificial intelligence (AI) model that automatically identifies and assesses visible risk factors in industrial sites.

Their construction site risk detection solution, known as ‘iSafe-Guard,’ stands out with its specialized functionality in detecting potential risks that may occur during specific tasks, unlike conventional intelligent CCTV. Based on user requirements, the AI detector embedded in this solution can operate on various systems, such as cloud, server, edge, and mobile. It can also be linked to multiple video acquisition devices, including fixed and mobile CCTV, robots, and drones. Furthermore, beyond simple risk detection and notification methods, it offers information on safety levels for each task, showcasing excellent versatility as an industrial safety solution.

Additionally, iSafe-Meta creates a metaverse environment using 3D-Mesh generated from actual footage and images captured on-site. This provides a space for industry experts and workers to share insights.

User-generated content is rewarded with blockchain-based Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) to encourage the influx of many users. The solution also enables communication independent of nationality using ChatGPT and automatic translation features.

Through the iSafe solution, ConTILab successfully applied it to large-scale research projects of government agencies, seven construction projects, and two private construction projects last year, completing demonstrations in safety planning, education, and monitoring. Starting this year, ConTILab is in discussions with local departments to introduce iSafe to mandatory CCTV application sites in regional governments in South Korea, and they are planning to expand into overseas markets, starting with Southeast Asian countries such as Vietnam and Indonesia.

To become a global leader in the construction safety field and a ‘First Mover’ in safety management across all industries, ConTILab attended CES 2024. They conducted multiple meetings with domestic and international companies and institutions that showed significant interest in their solution for maintaining safety in various industrial sites.

ConTILab emphasized, “We were able to meet with domestic and international companies and institutions that showed great interest in our solution, which can maintain safety in various industrial sites,” and explained, “Our technology, utilizing over 120 self-developed AI algorithms to recognize objects and achieve automatic reading, seems to meet their needs.”

They added, “Investment institutions in the United States and Korea also visited ConTILab’s booth, expressing their intention to invest. As a result, we expect to accelerate the company’s growth even after the exhibition.”

50615.cap: On the 9th (local time), at the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, ‘CES 2024,’ held in Las Vegas, USA, CEO So Yeon Kim of PCL (pictured center) posing with representatives from her company. | Photo - AVING News

50615.x: PCL Co., Ltd. (CEO So Yeon Kim) participated in the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from the 9th (Tuesday) to the 12th (Friday, local time).

PCL, which went public on the KOSDAQ in 2017, is a company developing in vitro diagnostic solutions. Through CEO So Yeon Kim’s nationally designated research laboratory project (supported by the Ministry of Science and Technology), the company has secured 3D immobilization technology for compounds and proteins. PCL presents new indicators for multiple immune diagnostics through the so-called ‘SG CapTM’ core technology.

In particular, PCL garnered attention by being the first in the world to launch a multi-immune diagnostic product for high-risk viruses. The company has also demonstrated advanced technological capabilities with the ‘HiSU’ system, a high-speed automated testing device, and an on-site diagnostic compact equipment named ‘PCLOKII.’

Furthermore, during the COVID-19 pandemic, PCL developed a self-diagnosis kit for diagnosing COVID-19 using saliva. The company achieved significant results by exporting these kits to 50 countries worldwide. Additionally, PCL has expanded its business into the AI-based medical electronics field, leading in the future of digital healthcare. The company has collaborated with Gangnam Severance Hospital and NHN Cloud to pioneer AI-based medical electronics, further broadening its business scope.

In addition, PCL has received recognition for its technological capabilities through various certifications and designations, including being designated as a Seoul-type specialized small and medium-sized enterprise, an innovative medical device company selected by the Ministry of Health and Welfare, a designated innovative prototype by the Public Procurement Service, and a family-friendly company certified for possessing national core technologies by the Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy.

At CES 2024, PCL showcased its flagship product, the ‘Smart Healthcare Platform.’ This platform aims to go beyond traditional hospital settings by providing more accurate test results. The company anticipated that the Smart Healthcare Platform would lead medical diagnostic innovation by addressing issues arising from medical care delays during emergency conditions, such as cerebrovascular diseases.

Particularly, this platform boasts exceptional user-friendliness as a compact medical device usable at home. The product’s strengths include an AI-driven analysis process that enables early risk detection, timely diagnosis, and treatment.

50615.cap: A glimpse of PCL’s disease diagnostic solution product line exhibited at the world’s largest consumer electronics and IT exhibition, ‘CES 2024,’ held in Las Vegas on the 9th (local time) | Photo - AVING News

50615.x: The collaboration with NHN Cloud and Gangnam Severance Hospital will aim to contribute to comprehensive data management and prevention of five major environmentally related diseases (Green Healthcare Cloud Platform). In addition, prediction and management services for chronic cardiovascular diseases can provide accurate risk assessments without the need for traditional testing systems, utilizing IVD devices and machine learning.

So Yeon Kim, the CEO of PCL, stated, “There is a growing demand worldwide for digital healthcare platforms that enable effective diagnosis and prediction of various diseases at home.” She further mentioned, “Our products will significantly impact countries where the universality of medical services is relatively low, as they offer more in-depth and advanced diagnostic solutions. Indeed, during this CES event, we received considerable interest from potential customers in regions such as Africa and Central Asia.”

CEO Kim said, “Although domestic laws currently restrict it, we anticipate that soon, there will be a time when diagnostic medical devices can be bought and sold like household appliances.” She added, “In line with this, we are investing our capabilities in developing more convenient and innovative products. It’s also gratifying to have the opportunity, here at CES, to meet with technology companies that can collaborate on product expansion and discuss future trends in the medical device market.”

50616.cap: PIA Space’s Booth at CES 2024 │Photo - AVING News

50616.x: PIA Space Inc. participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time).

Established in 2021, PIA Space is an AI technology-based company currently developing and commercializing a solution that utilizes multi-modal artificial intelligence (AI) to detect specific situations in CCTV. Particularly, the company is commercializing the MACS (Multi-modal AI for CCTV Situation detection) technology, which can detect complex conditions that conventional intelligent CCTV systems may not properly identify. PIA Space is conducting Proof of Concept (PoC) for various potential clients in Korea and Singapore.

Participating in CES 2024, PIA Space showcased its main product, the CCTV Real-time Video Automatic Monitoring Solution (MACS). MACS is a real-time video automatic monitoring solution applicable to security CCTV, CCTV safety monitoring, and CCTV security solutions. It automatically detects complex situations, securing the golden time to reduce critical damage by triggering alarms and subsequent actions. Notably, this solution can detect difficult-to-analyze violent or criminal cases and recognize risks such as falls from various heights by contextualizing hazardous situations.

PIA Space is conducting pilot projects with domestic institutions, including the Gwangjin-gu and Songpa-gu Office, to test its AI-based CCTV solution, MACS. On the international front, PIA Space is engaged in Proof of Concept (PoC) projects with KABAM Robotics, supplying security robots at Singapore Changi Airport and Semb Corporation, a plant operator on Jurong Island. Plans include expanding paid services within the CCTV control rooms of various district offices in Korea and supplying automated surveillance solutions to Singapore Changi Airport, large hotels, and more. PIA Space aims to achieve approximately $12 million in revenue by 2025, targeting markets including North America.

PIA Space stated, "At this exhibition, many government officials and corporate security personnel from North America, South America, and Turkey visited our booth. Visitors were in a situation where they did not know how to utilize their existing CCTV systems effectively. However, they responded positively, expressing that our product could enhance the utility of their CCTV systems," adding, "We want to create user cases that verify whether we can accurately align our technology with the needs of potential clients and implement the desired services for them."

50617.x: Creo Korea Co., Ltd. (CEO Hyun Woo Choi) participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time).

Creo Korea is a comprehensive food tech solution company that operates in various aspects of the food industry, including food smart factories, robot-based kitchen automation, and data-driven order processing. With core competencies in hardware and software development and implementation, the company develops its solutions and operates actual stores applying them, accumulating expertise in the food tech industry.

At CES 2024, Creo Korea introduced the smart automatic cooking robot 'Eight Kitchen' and the smart kitchen control solution 'ETAA.' Eight Kitchen and ETAA are robot-based kitchen automation solutions that replicate chef recipes. According to the company, from order processing to cooking, these solutions automate the operational processes of commercial kitchens, ensuring optimal efficiency, consistent taste, and hygiene with minimal staffing.

'Eight Kitchen' features a patented 'contactless electromagnetic dual induction heating system' and a 'special coating automatic rotating wok,' allowing it to recreate chef recipes. The most notable feature of Eight Kitchen is its complete automation of the entire cooking process, including recipe selection, cooking initiation with simple button controls, temperature control, rotation, timing, food plating, and cleaning. ETAA, designed to work seamlessly with Eight Kitchen, can be easily applied to any commercial kitchen.

Furthermore, these two solutions underwent operational verification for over a year at two directly managed Creo Korea stores in Seoul. During this validation period, the practicality and efficiency, including cost savings in labor and enhanced convenience for kitchen staff, have been directly confirmed.

50618.x: Monit Corp (CEO and Co-Founder Tony Park) participated in CES 2024, which took place from January 9th (Tuesday) to January 12th (Friday) in Las Vegas, USA.

Monit started as a research project at Samsung C-Lab in 2016. After successfully validating its business model, it became an independent corporation through a spin-off with support from Samsung Venture Investment in April 2017. Founded by four engineers with a background from Samsung Electronics, the company oversees all development internally. Monit is known for its distinctive technological prowess, particularly in diaper detection systems that combine advanced detection algorithms based on IoT communication.

In this manner, Monit has successfully developed its proprietary diaper status monitoring system called ‘MECS (Monit Elderly Care System).’ Through this system, the company aims to address common issues such as urinary tract infections and pressure sores that often occur in elderly patients requiring care. Additionally, it anticipates improving the efficiency of diaper-related tasks for caregivers.

MECS monitors the diaper status in real-time and notifies when a change is needed. The primary goal is to minimize the risk of infections that can occur when diapers remain unchanged while also allowing for the management of diaper usage and bedding. The upcoming version of MECS for care facilities manages multiple patients simultaneously in settings such as hospitals and nursing homes. With the capability to monitor the diaper status of various patients concurrently, it enhances caregiver quality and reduces the complexity of management. Optimizing the ability to manage multiple patients simultaneously improves operational efficiency, and the system can meet the facility’s specific requirements.

In addition, Monit introduced an AI chatbot service for parenting beginners at the exhibition. This chatbot app provides trustworthy advice and information related to parenting in a question-and-answer format, offering refined data verified by experts to address queries about parenting promptly.

It is meaningful that many Japanese investment firms and companies visited our booth at CES 2024,” adding, “We also had meetings with representatives from the American Association of Retired Persons (AARP). 50619.cap: Romansive’s 'COZA SLEEP' beverage at CES 2024. │ Photo - AVING News.

50619.x: The company Romansive (CEO Soo Hyun Lee) participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time) and introduced a sleep beverage.

Sleep tech company Romansive, which develops sleep beverages, collaborates with a research team from Seoul National University to create products based on scientific research and innovative approaches. According to officials, this collaboration represents Romansive's commitment to providing new solutions for individuals seeking better health and well-being by improving sleep quality.

'COZA SLEEP,' unveiled at this exhibition, is a sleep beverage promoting effective sleep using natural ingredients without melatonin. Instead of melatonin, this beverage supports the body in naturally producing melatonin by including L-tryptophan, vitamin B6, and vitamin B12. COZA SLEEP, in particular, incorporates fermentation and post-biotic technology, featuring a patented fermented jujube seed extract developed through collaborative research with Seoul National University as a key ingredient. Additionally, the product includes sleep-promoting components such as jujube seeds, hops, theanine, and tryptophan.

COZA SLEEP has completed registration as a dietary supplement with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and is also available on Amazon. The product holds certifications such as FSSC22000, ISO 14001, ISO 22000, and HACCP, emphasizing its commitment to meeting high standards in terms of quality and safety.

According to Romansive, "We are focused on continuous innovation and market expansion in the sleep industry. Our products target B2C, aiming to provide customers with direct experiences and enhance brand awareness. Participating in the exhibition allowed us to seize the opportunity for IR presentations at CES, where we achieved significant outcomes such as attracting investors and engaging in consultations at our booth. Building on this, we plan to actively promote our products in the wellness-conscious and high-purchasing-power markets of the United States and Japan, expanding our distribution network. Through these efforts, we aim to provide more opportunities for Romansive's products to reach a broader audience."
