50620.cap: VANAM’s booth at CES 2024. | Photo - AVING News

50620.x: VANAM (CEO Soo Deok Han) participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time).

Established in early 2022, VANAM, an early-stage startup, uses its proprietary thin film growth technology to develop next-generation semiconductor thin film materials and components. This technology forms from an exclusive process that precisely controls the thin film's thickness, composition, and other characteristics, creating high-quality, highly uniform thin films. VANAM's technological prowess received appreciation for its significant potential. It ensures the quality of thin films and opens up endless possibilities for using materials and devices previously inaccessible to traditional manufacturing technologies and methods. In line with this, VANAM is constructing a micro foundry in downtown Seoul, focusing on deposition processes and expanding its manufacturing capabilities.

At this year's CES, VANAM showcased energy-sensitive semiconductor thin film materials and components essential for applications such as fire detectors and protective circuits. The company actively promoted these products to global electronics companies, particularly battery and IoT device manufacturers. By emphasizing safety, a common trend in both the international industry and consumer technology sectors, VANAM aims to seek sales opportunities in the global market.

In response, VANAM pointed to the commercialization of its first project, the energy-sensitive semiconductor thin film 'VM1.' High-quality semiconductor thin films produced through environmentally friendly vacuum deposition produce VM1. It is the first in energy-sensitive semiconductors to adopt a thin film form.

According to the company, VM1 can react very sensitively to heat and electrical energy due to its form, significantly enhancing the detection performance of safety systems. It is a key component that could replace bulkier semiconductor components like thermistors and varistors commonly used before.

50620.cap: VANAM representatives, including CEO Soo Deok Han (pictured right), posed with their products. │ Photo - AVING News

50620.x: A VANAM representative stated, "As safety-related trends strengthen in industries and consumer technology worldwide, our product, which boasts specialized responsiveness, can be an attractive alternative." The representative expressed the company's goal of commercializing materials made thinner through environmentally friendly processes that have yet to appear in the market. They emphasized their commitment to collaborating and exchanging ideas with participating companies offering diverse services to explore potential applications and continue ongoing research and development.

In addition to VM1, they are simultaneously conducting promotional activities for the ongoing construction of their micro foundry project. The representative mentioned, "Having secured specialized thin film manufacturing capabilities that meet various industry requirements, we are positively evaluating the potential for attracting customers." They added, "Especially considering the market demand for responsive semiconductors, we expect to achieve export results of over one million dollars in 2024."

50621.x: EmotionWave, represented by CEO Soonchul Jang, participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time).

Since its establishment in 2013, Emotionwave, an AI-based metaverse specialist, has created a new culture under the ‘Convergence of Art and Technology’ slogan, aiming to make creative activities accessible to everyone. The company possesses various metaverse-related technologies, including AI music technology, media live streaming technology, music performance robotics technology, virtual human creation technology, virtual performance production technology, blockchain, and NFT technology. Emotionwave leverages these technologies to develop metaverse platforms and offers diverse services, including content creation.

Emotionwave offers a range of services, including the AIoT music platform ‘RIMA,’ the media live streaming platform ‘VISCOOP,’ the digital human blockchain agency platform ‘AIMPLE,’ the metaverse-based AI music education platform ‘MEW,’ and the metaverse music platform ‘MUTA.’ In addition, the company provides services such as web/app service planning and development, as well as software development for music and performances.

During this exhibition, Emotionwave actively introduced the upgraded version of AIMPLE 1.0, called AIMPLE 2.0, which first debuted at CES 2022. Additionally, they showcased the new stage cloud service set to launch in June.

AIMPLE utilizes generative AI technology to enable anyone to engage in activities as a virtual human. It provides entertainment services that support the creation of digital humans with desired appearances, AI albums based on generated digital human IPs, video content creation, and online and offline activities. Through the AIMPLE Studio, a web3 virtual broadcasting program, users can engage in activities as virtual models, influencers, YouTubers, musicians, and more. The platform also supports revenue generation by allowing the issuance and trading of NFTs for created AI albums and video content on its self-developed NFT marketplace.

In addition, StageCloud offers an opportunity to experience the freedom of various musical creations. Users can access all necessary instruments and tools in their studios and engage in community activities with other users across different genres such as hip-hop, ballad, orchestra, and more. The AI prompt interface technology, allowing the realization of any musical idea, garnered particular attention for its ability to create music collaboratively with creators worldwide.

StageCloud provides a core experience and interface for K-POP auditions in the metaverse environment, allowing users to experience auditions in virtual spaces similar to real-life scenarios. The platform emphasizes offering a setting in the metaverse where users can participate in the entire process, from music creation to the challenge of becoming a musician. It aims to connect K-POP musicians and aspiring artists, fostering mentor-mentee relationships and presenting a new business strategy for artists to grow and debut. Additionally, customers can directly participate in the growth and success of artists through a DAO-based voting system, providing a chance for collaborative development.

In addition, StageCloud offers a digital twin program that integrates with various existing offline auditions and K-POP festivals. Emotionwave, in collaboration with its ‘AImple’ digital human studio, plans to support virtual YouTuber auditions concurrently.

Emotionwave stated, “Our AImple digital human solution has already signed MOUs with overseas companies such as Cakap, an online education company in Indonesia, and Soon Entertainment, a global TikTok MCN company. We provide metaverse content based on digital humans and digital human IPs.” They further mentioned, “At this CES, meetings with many game-related companies were held regarding our new solution applying LLM to digital humans, presenting valuable business opportunities in the global market.”

50622.x: PeoplesHealth Co., Ltd. (CEO Eunsun Kim) participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time).

PeoplesHealth is a company that aims to provide innovative healthcare services to patients who might otherwise be unable to receive treatment due to language and location constraints. The company operates ‘ToggleDoc,’ which supports medical institutions in attracting more patients from overseas, and ‘K-Doc,’ which connects international patients who wish to receive treatment in Korea with Korean hospitals. The goal is to assist more people in accessing the necessary medical care.
At this CES, PeoplesHealth introduced the web application ‘ToggleDoc,’ which effectively manages customers and patients worldwide.

ToggleDoc, providing an intuitive and user-friendly environment, allows for effective management of customers and contracts. This platform enables businesses to streamline their processes and quickly access essential information. Additionally, ToggleDoc automates repetitive and time-consuming tasks, maximizing the efficiency of business processes and reducing workload.

ToggleDoc, with its features like easy communication with customers, workflow optimization, and cost reduction, effectively supports globally distributed patient management, according to the company’s explanation. 50625.x: XAIMED Co., Ltd. (CEO Sang Min Park) participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time).

XAIMED is a leading company in AI medical devices that connect daily life, healthcare, AI, and people. XAIMED's "eXplainable AI (XAI)" technology addresses the black box issue of medical AI while providing customized solutions based on medical images, time-series biological data, and structured data.

XAIMED expanded its AI product range from AI for eye diseases and arterial sclerosis to urology, laparoscopy, endoscopy, and more. The company strives to connect AI and humans by providing eXplainable AI (XAI) solutions. These solutions aim to offer clearer evidence, allowing both doctors and patients to trust artificial intelligence in various medical fields.

At this year's CES, XAIMED unveiled the 'XAI Bio-Integrated Sensor Intelligent Solution,' which allows individuals to check and manage their health status in everyday life. This solution integrates fragmented body measurement devices such as electrocardiographs, thermometers, body composition analyzers, blood pressure monitors, and corneal saturation monitors. XAIMED has developed and incorporated a miniaturized module for skin fluorescence advanced glycation end products (AGE) sensor, a core technology for non-invasive measurement for diabetes prevention, management, and monitoring.

Thus, the XAI Bio-Integrated Sensor Intelligent Solution can simultaneously measure vital signs such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, skin temperature, body composition, and skin fluorescence advanced glycation end products (AGE) with just one test. XAIMED emphasized that they have enhanced the testing performance by applying their self-developed AI module and firmware to the product, allowing it to collect multiple biosignals simultaneously with low power consumption.

50627.cap: Mayor of Seoul Se-hoon Oh visited the VEStellaLab booth at CES and commemorated the visit with a photo. │Photo provided by VEStellaLab

50627.x: VEStellaLab participated in CES 2024, held from January 9th (Tue) to 12th (Fri) in Las Vegas, USA, and introduced their 'ZeroCruising' solution, which delivers infrastructure-collected information to autonomous vehicles to achieve autonomous valet parking as well as their last-mile parking navigation service 'Watchmile.'

The Mayor of Seoul, Se-hoon Oh, visited the VEStellaLab booth at CES, showing interest in the autonomous parking solution, ZeroCruising, and also discussed the expansion of Watchmile to public parking lots throughout Seoul. Mayor Oh shared a successful case of solving complex parking issues by introducing the solution at the Seoul Cheonho Station public parking lot.

Watchmile and ZeroCruising utilize VEStellaLab's non-GPS indoor positioning technology and real-time static and dynamic information analysis within parking lots through video AI technology. The infrastructure installed in parking lots, such as CCTV, collects information, which is standardized and optimized before being transmitted to service users and autonomous vehicles. Since it maximizes the use of existing infrastructure, it does not require expensive sensors like lidar or special devices for users. Ordinary drivers can use Watchmile with just a smartphone, while autonomous vehicles need only a terminal for communication to utilize ZeroCruising.

Watchmile provides route guidance to empty parking spaces based on the location of vacant parking spaces identified by video analysis AI and the user's position determined through indoor positioning. Like conventional navigation systems, it guides regular drivers to the nearest empty parking space, allowing them to reduce the time and cost associated with parking significantly. With Watchmile remembering the parking location, the entire process from entry to exit becomes more convenient. The system is active at various landmarks and large residential complexes, including Cheonho Station, Seoul Station, Incheon Airport, KINTEX, and more. Following the meeting with Mayor Se-hoon Oh, the company plans to expand its services further.

ZeroCruising transforms autonomous driving in indoor parking lots, such as underground garages or parking towers, where general road rules are not applicable and GPS positioning is challenging. Autonomous vehicles with ZeroCruising can safely perform last-mile autonomous driving indoors by receiving indoor positioning information and static/dynamic data through V2I (Vehicle-to-Infrastructure) communication. This process eliminates the need to roam in search of parking spaces. It also enhances the capability to avoid blind spots that are difficult to address with only onboard sensors, thereby improving overall safety.

A representative stated, "Following the success of our services in the domestic market, we are now actively expanding into the global market, particularly in the Middle East and Southeast Asia, where demand for smart city and smart parking solutions is rapidly increasing. As a leader in smart parking solutions, we aim to provide tailored solutions that address local challenges and lead the global smart parking market."

51213.cap: On August 27th (Tuesday), Palsoo Jang, CEO of PALSOO, pitched at the Global Media Meetup Season 2 at the MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, organized by AVING News with the American tech media Ubergizmo. | Photo by AVING News

51213.x: From August 27th (Tuesday) to 28th (Wednesday), PALSOO (CEO Palsoo Jang) participated in the 'Global Media Meetup' Season 2 event at the MIK Basecamp in Seocho District, Seoul, targeting Korean startups. This event, co-organized by AVING News and the American tech media Ubergizmo, focused on introducing Korean startups' products and technologies to the global market. It targets to expand business opportunities by preemptively reporting through global media about startups applying for the CES 2025 Innovation Award and participating in CES.

Since 2022, PALSOO has been developing a portable plasma sterilization sprayer, completing over two years of R&D. The company is preparing for its first product launch in December. The patented plasma sterilization sprayer, described as the world's first technology to generate and immediately spray sterilizing water using only water and air, has received certification for killing over 99.5% of airborne viruses among more than three international standards (KOLAS certification, KTL (Korea Industrial Technology Test Institute): SPS-KOUVA AS 01-1889 Air Sterilizer, KRIBS (Microbiome Center): Analytical Method (ASTM E2315-16)).

From the plasma sterilization sprayer’s development stage, PALSOO has conducted online and offline consultations with various countries. As a result, in 2023, PALSOO signed an MOU and Letter of Intent to Purchase with HOME N STYLE TEXTILES CEO Balaji Rajagopal of India. Furthermore, consultations at CES 2023 led to the sharing of an export database with companies such as MedScenker Inc. of the USA, RAAS PAL Co., Ltd of Thailand, and TechBlick of Germany. In 2024, prototype supplies are planned through consultations with ESPADA MEDICAL of Turkey and Hijaz Medical Supplies Trading LLC of the UAE.
PALSOO plans to showcase the plasma sterilization sprayer at CES 2025 in Las Vegas early next year and is also challenging for an innovation award.

51213.cap: From left to right: ECORO backpack-type sprayer, FRIRUS portable sprayer | Provided by PALSOO

51213.x: The portable plasma sterilization sprayer, measuring 485x180x250mm and weighing 3.5kg, is a compact product suitable for all ages, designed with an ergonomic grip at the handle.

The pesticide-free backpack-type sprayer is designed with a 15-degree angle for user comfort, reducing fatigue during prolonged use. The sprayer stick (1m) is made of ultra-lightweight stainless steel, and the backpack's design shifts the center of gravity upwards to minimize fatigue. It can spray continuously for over 60 minutes with a battery charging system and be fully charged (60 minutes) using solar power.

Additionally, when plasma-activated water is aerosolized into droplets, it can remain suspended for an extended period, effectively reducing odors and sterilizing viruses in the air. The system converts water and air into sterilizing water without chemical agents, significantly reducing costs.

This patented plasma sterilization sprayer generates oxygen-based active species such as OH-, O3, and H2O2 and nitrogen-based active species such as NO2-, NO3-, and ONOOH through atmospheric pressure corona discharge. These active species react with water to create plasma-activated water, which possesses strong antimicrobial properties and can disinfect substances. The nitrogen in the water also acts as an eco-friendly liquid fertilizer.

51213.cap: Palsoo Jang, CEO, pitching at the Global Media Meetup Season 2. | Photo by AVING News

51213.x: The use of eco-friendly materials is also notable. The material of the plasma sprayer is eco-friendly, and the sprayer body, packaging box, portable bag, and catalog are made from biodegradable materials.

CEO Palsoo Jang stated, "The emergence of COVID-19 variants continues to pose a constant threat, while traditional disinfection systems rely on chemical agents, leading to high production and distribution costs. Additionally, these chemicals can be harmful to human health due to inhalation toxicity and residual toxicity. Our plasma sterilization sprayer combines plasma-activated water with a special spray nozzle, using only water and air to enable immediate sterilization and disinfection."

He added, "Our plasma-activated water has been certified to reduce airborne viruses by 99.5% and airborne bacteria by 99.2%. It has also been proven to kill over 95% of E. coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, and Streptococcus pyogenes within 40 seconds after application. Our certified technology effectively responds to the emergence of coronavirus variants."

This environmentally friendly technology also introduces a new paradigm in organic farming. Applying plasma-activated water to crops promotes healthy roots, stems, and leaves growth by 30-50% or more. Moreover, CEO Jang emphasized that PALSOO's technology effectively protects workers from residual, inhalation, and contact toxicity caused by chemical use in traditional agriculture. Additionally, using various chemical agents leads to soil acidification and water pollution, but the portable plasma sterilization sprayer avoids these concerns.

51213.cap: Palsoo Jang, CEO of PALSOO, Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo, and Lee Seong-Tae, Vice President of PALSOO, posing for a commemorative photo after the Global Media Meetup Season 2. | Photo by AVING News

51213.x: CEO Palsoo Jang explained, "Recent climate changes have led to more frequent natural disasters such as droughts and floods. Especially in underdeveloped countries, poor sanitary conditions expose them to the spread of waterborne diseases like malaria, cholera, and typhoid. Our product meets the hygiene needs of the most vulnerable populations in children, the elderly, and developing countries with innovative cost savings."

He continued, "The FRIRUS_24 brand holds a patent for instantly generating and spraying sterilizing water using only water and air. This technology utilizes infinite natural public resources to sterilize and disinfect, presenting an innovative approach to sustainable ecosystem conservation."

At the 'Global Media Meetup' Season 2 event with Ubergizmo held on August 27th, pitching based on these details was followed by a Q&A session. In response to a question about the definition of plasma, PALSOO explained, "Plasma is defined as an ionized state of gas. Just as ice (solid) melts into water (liquid) when heated, and water turns into steam (gas) when heated further, plasma is a state where gas atoms receive sufficient electrical energy to change into electrons, ions, and excited radicals."

They stated that lifespan “ varies depending on the temperature and type of plasma. If in a gaseous state, the lifespan is longer but shortens when converted to activated water. It lengthens at lower temperatures and shortens at higher temperatures. Typically, plasma-activated water has a lifespan of about 15 minutes at 25 degrees Celsius, which is sufficient to kill bacteria and is better as it disappears quickly, posing no harm to humans. While plasma and plasma-activated water were discovered long ago, plasma-activated aerosol is new. The lifespan of plasma is very short and difficult to store, but our technology immediately activates the plasma aerosol, making it more effective than other products."

51213.cap: Hubert Nguyen, Co-founder and CTO of Ubergizmo | Photo by AVING News

51213.x: They also noted that any water could be used as long as it does not clog the nozzle, but cleaner water, like tap water, is preferable. In response to a question about usability, they mentioned, "It can also be used in the medical industry, and some hospitals have sought it as a disinfectant. Additionally, if drones are used, they can be utilized in rural areas. The oxygen type kills bacteria, and the nitrogen type acts as a fertilizer, promoting plant growth while killing viruses and bacteria, but it also promotes seed germination."

Finally, PALSOO shared their goal of contributing to society. They stated, "For example, in underdeveloped countries, when floods occur and waterborne diseases break out without medical facilities, our product can be sterilized using only water and air, preventing waterborne diseases. An earthquake that causes buildings to collapse can also be used as a social public good. Secondly, it can contribute to carbon-neutral policies and carbon reduction for global warming. The main body of our machine is biodegradable, and the packaging box also utilizes recycled paper. In this way, we are striving to achieve RE100."

Meanwhile, Ubergizmo, founded in 2005, operates the Silicon Valley Post and posts in six languages, targeting 200 countries worldwide. Focusing on electronics and tech, it covers major international exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Hubert Nguyen, CTO and co-founder of Ubergizmo, attended the event. Hubert Nguyen has worked as a programming engineer at NVIDIA, managed developer education programs, and has been a 3D graphics programmer. He also attends CES annually to cover products and technologies from companies worldwide.

51215.cap: Chongkul Yi, CEO of Spaid, pitching at the ‘Global Media Meetup’ with GEEKSPIN on July 25th at MIK Basecamp │ Photo by AVING News

51215.x: Spaid (CEO Chongkul Yi) participated in the ‘Global Media Meetup’ for Korean startups held from July 24th to 26th at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul.

The ‘Global Media Meetup’ event, co-hosted by global media AVING News and American tech media GEEKSPIN, focuses on introducing Korean startups’ products and technologies to the worldwide market. The event aims to expand business opportunities through proactive media coverage of CES 2025 Innovation Award applications and startups participating in CES.

Founded in December 2023, Spaid aims to maximize the possibilities for customers to intuitively experience and directly utilize various insights by connecting all location-based data in the world with real physical and digital environments.

Founded by a CEO from Samsung and Gary Technology and a CTO with 30 years in IT development, Spaid seeks to enhance the utilization of information in all industries that produce, collect, and apply geospatial information based on location. Integrating data from various fields based on location derives new information and provides services that allow businesses to make synergetic final decisions based on regional data analysis.

Spaid’s data transformation and integration engine, CYLO, standardizes and programs data regardless of its format, source, or size and provides information in the form desired by customers. Its solution, ADEK, visualizes 3D spatial information implemented based on GIS data, providing a highly immersive visual experience. It is one of the ‘GeoAI’ solutions that support business feasibility studies and optimal decision-making based on insights derived through spatial information integration.

Spaid’s GeoAI solution monitors location-based information to detect anomalies and predict responses. The 3D maps created based on GIS data allow for checking basic details such as land, buildings, facilities, population, and traffic by region, enabling analysis based on specific regional conditions.

Based on this technology, Spaid intends to offer integrated management services for smart cities and factories using digital twins, real estate location environmental value analysis, building energy control, financial investment and risk management, and telecommunications network resource management.

The company has established a database and server system specialized for real-time monitoring of GIS-related data. It has the advantage of establishing an AI-based automated analysis process by refining, integrating, and extracting data necessary for specific fields.
At the ‘Global Media Meetup’ event with GEEKSPIN on July 25th, a Q&A session based on this content followed the pitching.

51215.cap: ADEK smart city application example │ Image by Spaid

51215.x: Initially, regarding whether Spaid’s technology applies only to satellite photos, the company stated, “It can be applied to all images, but the results vary depending on the image detail. Satellite photos are blurry, so drone photos are recommended if more delicate results are needed. The technology can be applied to various fields, such as defense systems, agricultural management, weather forecasting, disaster control, and monitoring. Although our technology started with satellite photos, as our understanding of technology has improved, we have realized that basic technologies such as scripting or machine learning can be applied in various environments.”

51223.cap: Jin Ouk Kim, CEO of DEOGAM, pitching at the ‘Global Media Meetup’ held at MIK Base Camp on July 26th │ Photo by AVING News

51223.x: DEOGAM (CEO Jin Ouk Kim) participated in the ‘Global Media Meetup,’ held from July 24 to 26 at MIK Base Camp in Seoul. The event was co-hosted by AVING News and U.S. tech media Geekspin and focused on introducing innovative technologies from Korean startups to the global market. It aimed to provide early reports on CES 2025 Innovation Award applications and increase business opportunities through global media exposure.

Founded in 2022, DEOGAM specializes in energy efficiency solutions for electric vehicles (EVs), contributing to their sustainable production and consumption. DEOGAM’s core technology recycles energy lost from harmonics generated during vehicle operation, converting it into usable EV power.

Electric vehicles’ power for motor rotation and driving comes from the battery, which stores direct current (DC) and converts it to alternating current (AC) through an inverter. During this conversion, energy loss generates heat and harmonics. As EV performance and output increase, power efficiency decreases due to this energy loss.

51223.cap: Jin Ouk Kim, CEO of DEOGAM, pitching at the ‘Global Media Meetup’ | Photo by AVING News

51223.x: DEOGAM developed an Electric Recycling System using a Toroid energy core to address this issue, which induces electromagnetism and converts harmonic energy back into electric power. The recovered energy, with its high electromotive force, can be stably converted and transmitted within a Buck & Boost converter, even with significant fluctuations in input voltage.

In DEOGAM’s internal tests, the system demonstrated significant results. It recovered 18% of the energy lost due to harmonics during driving, increasing the EV range by up to 10%. For electric taxis, this could save approximately KRW 700,000 (USD 500) in annual maintenance costs.

This innovative technology earned DEOGAM a spot in the TIPS program for developing an energy efficiency system utilizing electromagnetic waves from EVs. The company is conducting related projects and plans to apply its technology to commercial EVs in Korea this year. The field test results will be presented at CES 2025 in Las Vegas.

51223.cap: Overview of DEOGAM’s Electric Recycling System │ Image provided by DEOGAM

51223.x: Looking to 2025, DEOGAM has signed an MOU with Kakao Mobility to supply its technology to electric taxis. The company aims to expand its success in the Korean market, entering mobility markets in Germany, Norway, and major U.S. cities to promote eco-friendly mobility on a global scale.

During the media meetup, CEO Kim remarked, “Considering the global industry’s need to achieve carbon neutrality, our technology will continue to demonstrate increasing value.” He explained, “If DEOGAM’s system were installed in 14 million electric vehicles worldwide, and each vehicle drove just 30 km, the system would recover over 3 million megawatts of energy. This is equivalent to the daily output of 10 nuclear power plants or the environmental benefit of planting 12 million trees.”

DEOGAM plans to install its Electric Recycling System in 500 electric taxis in Jeju starting in April 2025. By partnering with Kakao Mobility’s nationwide network, the company intends to strengthen its presence in the commercial vehicle market and explore opportunities in the private EV market.

Kim further emphasized, “Our goal is to make DEOGAM’s Electric Recycling System a ‘must-have’ for electric vehicles worldwide. We plan to market the system’s near-zero carbon emissions during energy production, particularly appealing to the environmentally conscious European market.”

DEOGAM also aims to lead a global movement for EVs that maximize the balance between power and performance. Unlike regenerative braking systems that recover energy through braking, DEOGAM’s system increases energy recovery while the accelerator is engaged.

51223.cap: Jin Ouk Kim, CEO of DEOGAM (far left), and Helena Stone, Geekspin Editor-in-Chief (far right), during a Q&A session at the ‘Global Media Meetup’ │ Photo by AVING News

51223.x: The system also tracks real-time power usage from the battery and motor and recovered energy from the system. DEOGAM plans to collect this data to create a database that offers insights into EV users’ driving habits to maximize energy recovery.

Kim added, “Starting with electric taxis in 2025, we aim to expand our supply to electric buses by 2030. We will continue collecting and refining data from public transportation to foster an eco-friendly mobility culture. We aim to introduce groundbreaking technology and become a company that normalizes renewable energy use.”

After learning about DEOGAM’s long-term vision and values, Helena Stone, Geekspin Editor-in-Chief, remarked, “The idea of recovering and utilizing lost electricity has been around for a long time. However, the bold move to introduce this to EVs highlights DEOGAM’s uniqueness.” She added, “The message they convey through technology is expected to impact EV users’ lives worldwide significantly. I wish DEOGAM a successful journey in revolutionizing how we approach EV energy efficiency.”

51224.cap: Giuk Lee, CEO of HUROTICS, pitching at the ‘Global Media Meetup’ held at MIK Base Camp on July 26th │ Photo by AVING News

51224.x: HUROTICS (CEO Giuk Lee), a spin-off from the Assistive & Rehabilitation Robotics Lab at Chung-Ang University, participated in the ‘Global Media Meetup’ from July 24 to 26 at MIK Base Camp in Seoul. The event, co-hosted by AVING News and U.S. tech media Geekspin, focuses on introducing Korean startups’ products and technologies to the global market. The event aims to increase business opportunities for CES 2025 participants through global media exposure.

Founded in 2022, HUROTICS specializes in wearable robotic suits for various applications, including rehabilitation, assistance, and sports. Its exosuit technology overcomes the limitations of traditional robotic exoskeletons, which tend to be bulky, uncomfortable, and expensive. HUROTICS offers lightweight, customizable exosuits tailored to individual users’ needs, providing solutions across medical, assistive, and athletic fields.

HUROTICS gained international attention at CES 2024, where its soft robotic suit, H-Flex, won the Innovation Award in the Robotics category. The overwhelming response from North American attendees highlighted the company’s potential in that market. In April, HUROTICS exported its first model, the passive H-Band for muscle recovery and joint motion rehabilitation, to the University of Illinois Chicago (UIC) and Northwestern University. This demonstrated the product’s innovation and performance, leading to further partnerships with other institutions.

In Korea, HUROTICS has won the K-R&D Award for two consecutive years (2023-2024), obtained several intellectual property rights, and secured Seed funding and GMP certification for Class 1 medical devices. Recently, the company attracted KRW 3.5 billion (USD 2.5 million) in pre-Series A investment from venture capital firms such as AJU IB Investment and Wonik Investment Partners.

At CES 2025, HUROTICS plans to introduce its wearable exosuit solutions as a response to global aging issues. The company’s H-Medi and H-Flex products will offer users the flexibility to assist with mobility in various environments, whether for rehabilitation or daily activities.

During the Global Media Meetup, HUROTICS’ CEO Giuk Lee spoke about his academic background from Seoul National University and Harvard and how it contributed to founding the company with CTO Seungtae Yang, a Ph.D. expert in wearable robotics. Lee emphasized their expertise in biomimetic robotics and how HUROTICS’ technology mimics tendon structures to provide personalized assistance, ensuring users experience minimal discomfort or side effects.

The company has developed five types of wearable robotic technologies. Still, it focuses on two key global release models: the H-Medi rehabilitation robot and the H-Flex everyday mobility assist robot. The company places great importance on collaborating with rehabilitation therapists and medical professionals, who provide direct feedback after testing the technology.

CEO Lee stated, “Rehabilitation professionals have given feedback like, ‘Robots are still too heavy and expensive,’ and ‘Even new exoskeletons feel bulky and are not practical for patients.’ We took this feedback to heart and created H-Medi to weigh only 15 kg, with the H-Flex modules weighing just 0.6 kg each.”

51224.cap: Giuk Lee, CEO of HUROTICS, pitching at the ‘Global Media Meetup’ │ Photo by AVING News

51224.x: HUROTICS is testing its technologies at several medical institutions in Korea. For example, in tests conducted with sarcopenia patients at Chung-Ang University Hospital, H-Medi significantly increased exercise duration and improved walking posture. The company also plans to apply the technology to early-stage Parkinson’s disease patients. While the product is ready, HUROTICS is working toward obtaining GMP and medical certifications by May 2024 before launching full sales.

The H-Flex model is also being developed to work seamlessly with everyday activities, providing custom support for specific body parts like arms or legs. HUROTICS is working to obtain medical certification for H-Flex and plans to release it alongside a companion app in mid-2025, allowing for flexible and personalized adjustments.

The Q&A session with Geekspin raised the question of who would benefit most from HUROTICS’ technology. CEO Lee responded, “Patients with weak hamstrings or muscle loss, such as those with sarcopenia, can benefit from partial support, while patients with more severe conditions, like Parkinson’s, may require full-body support. We are creating a user manual to ensure doctors and therapists can teach proper usage. Full clinical trials will begin in 2025, and we expect positive outcomes for patients with mobility challenges, including those recovering from strokes.”

HUROTICS is also making strides in the sports technology sector. In its research article on Science Robotics, the company’s H-Fit sports training robot improved wearers’ athletic performance. For example, users could reduce their 200-meter sprint time by 3 seconds and increase their golf swing distance by 7%. The suit also helps improve posture for running and other sports.

At CES 2025, HUROTICS plans to showcase both the H-Medi and H-Fit models, with H-Fit specifically targeting elite athletes. The company has already received interest from an Italian national track coach, who contacted HUROTICS after struggling to improve athlete performance. HUROTICS also demonstrated its technology at CES 2024 and conducted tests with Japan’s NHK to evaluate the potential performance gains.

CEO Lee concluded, “Following the commercialization of personalized wearable robots, we plan to enter the digital healthcare and sports technology sectors. Our long-term goal is to expand into these growing fields and continue innovating in wearable robotics.”

51226.x: Aram Huvis (CEO Dongsoon Park) participated in the ‘Global Media Meetup’ Season 2 event, which targeted Korean startups and took place from August 27 (Tuesday) to 28 (Wednesday) at the MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul.

Aram Huvis, a company that has been manufacturing and distributing skin and scalp diagnostic devices for 22 years, collaborates with major cosmetic brands such as LVMH, L’Oréal, Guerlain, Estée Lauder, P&G, Aveda, Beiersdorf, and L’Occitane, maintaining long-term partnerships.

In CES 2023, Aram Huvis was recognized for its product innovation by receiving an Innovation Award for its AISG (AI Scalp Diagnosis Device). This device provides an accurate diagnosis report by learning from over 100,000 pieces of biometric data collected by the company. It offers approximately 3 million personalized “recipes” for custom shampoos and serums. AISG is registered with the Korean Intellectual Property Office as a “Big Data-Based AI Scalp Diagnosis and Analysis System.”

Based on this innovative technology, the company plans to expand its business into ‘Ellapiel (Customized Scalp Cosmetics)’ by transmitting consultation data to a smart factory for immediate manufacturing after diagnosis. Additionally, they have developed the portable ECW-CUBE, a small diagnostic device using AISG technology, and hold 42 domestic and international patents based on this technology.

51226.cap: Sanghyun Park, Vice President of Aram Huvis, answering questions during the ‘Global Media Meetup’ with Ubergizmo | Photo by AVING News

51226.x: Aram Huvis exports its skin and scalp diagnostic devices to over 70 countries, with 80% of its sales coming from overseas. Domestically, it collaborates with brands such as LG Household & Health Care and Juno Hair. The company has seen great success in global diagnostic device markets, including countries like Spain, Poland, Italy, France, the U.S., Canada, UAE, China, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, India, South Africa, and Turkey. Furthermore, through long-term partnerships with over 100 global brands, including the Top 10 brands, Aram Huvis has solidified its position in the market.

Aram Huvis was also recognized as a “Global Small Giant” by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups and listed as a “World-Class Product” by the Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy and the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA).

At CES 2025, Aram Huvis plans to unveil the ‘ECW CUBE’ and ‘Ellapiel Tailor.’ The ECW CUBE is a portable AI-based scalp care device that uses patented AI scalp grading technology (AISG) to analyze seven scalp conditions and categorize them into ten types. Equipped with a 1/4-inch color CMOS sensor with 2 million pixels at 60x magnification, it provides high-resolution images for precise diagnosis, according to the company. The device is Wi-Fi enabled and features automatic LED control, allowing for detailed scalp analysis anytime, anywhere, without specialized equipment or knowledge.

51226.cap: ECW CUBE (Lilai View)│Image provided by Aram Huvis
Ellapiel Tailor │Image provided by Aram Huvis

51226.x: Additionally, Aram Huvis developed the ‘Ellapiel Tailor,’ which allows consumers to manufacture customized skin care and scalp care products at home, tailored to their skin and scalp characteristics through precise AI diagnostics. The company confirmed receiving regulatory exceptions for customized cosmetics from the Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy. Furthermore, Aram Huvis published the study “Artificial intelligence-based prescription of customized scalp cosmetics improved the scalp condition: efficacy results from 100 participants,” which was selected and featured in the UK’s ‘Journal of Dermatological Treatment.’

The ‘Ellapiel Tailor’ provides a personalized formula based on AI diagnosis of an individual’s skin and scalp conditions. It includes a high-speed homogenizer (12,000 rpm) and precise temperature control up to 100°C, ensuring stable emulsification for various products. Pre-measured ingredient packs simplify production, allowing fresh small batches (50–200g) to be created within 10 minutes. The components are easy to clean, and the device features automatic shut-off and safety locks, emphasizing user safety.

Aram Huvis plans to launch the ‘ECW CUBE’ and ‘Ellapiel Tailor’ domestically, with CES 2025 marking the start of its expansion into the U.S. market. Following CES, the company aims to launch and sell its new products globally through its distribution networks and partners in Spain, Italy, Poland, Germany, France, the U.S., Canada, China, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia.

Additionally, after CES, Aram Huvis will participate in the influential global beauty exhibition Cosmoprof Bologna, Italy (to be held in March 2025), where it will meet with its European distributors. The company plans to attend up to 10 exhibitions annually, expanding sales to over 100 countries and increasing the number of new distributors by more than five each year.

51226.cap: Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo │Photo by AVING News

51226.x: At the Global Media Meetup, Aram Huvis’ pitch was followed by a Q&A session with Ubergizmo. Ubergizmo’s CTO, Hubert Nguyen, raised questions regarding the quality of the images, asking about the camera used and how it compares to a smartphone camera. Sanghyun Park, Vice President of Aram Huvis, explained, “We use a high-magnification microscope, not a camera. Issues related to the scalp require detailed images between the hair strands to analyze symptoms and colors. The lighting is also crucial—it must not be too bright, just the right amount.”

He further explained, “The Ellapiel Tailor is like a personalized cosmetic manufacturing machine, similar in size to a home coffee machine. You insert one of the three pouches, select the settings, and display the temperature and mixing speed, making it easy to use. These characteristics ensure that our products are fresh and must be used promptly. Even if unopened, the shelf life is about one year, but once opened, it is best to use the product within six months. Since users make the products themselves and they are reusable, there’s no need for excess packaging or plastic. Plus, the machine has a built-in cleaning function, making it easy to maintain.”

Vice President Park noted that regarding FDA requirements for exports, “The pouches will be registered with the FDA and CPAP, and we are already progressing through the KFDA in Korea, awaiting government approval. Once these procedures are complete, we will sequentially seek approval from other countries. Developing and launching such products as a small business is difficult, but we have invested heavily in R&D and achieved satisfying results. This year and next January will be crucial business milestones for our company.”

He concluded, “Aram Huvis aims to continue growing, to make the world more beautiful and beneficial through innovative ideas. We provide personalized care products and services without harmful preservatives based on accurate skin and scalp diagnoses using our accumulated data and AI technology.”

SHECO specializes in water treatment solutions using aquatic robots, addressing pollutants such as oil spills in marine and aquatic environments. By integrating technologies like robotics, AI, drones, and system integration (SI), SHECO transforms water resource pollution management—traditionally handled by large equipment, ships, or manual labor—into a process accessible to non-experts for monitoring, response, and prediction.

SHECO emphasizes that its solutions allow marine-based facilities, previously dependent on public institutions due to labor, costs, and technology challenges, to manage water quality independently. Guided by the slogan “Going Green with Robotics,” SHECO aims to automate water quality management across marine and aquatic industries for present and future generations.

The impeller and filters, developed in-house, are designed to recover effectively and separate liquid and particulate pollutants, such as oil, ship paint debris, algae, and cargo dust. A key feature is its user-friendly operation, requiring only 30 minutes of training for a non-expert operator. The device can process up to 30,000 liters per hour and operates within a 1-kilometer radius via remote control.

A company representative explained, “Industries such as thermal power plants, shipyards, reservoirs, rivers, ports, and water treatment plants face diverse pollutants, each requiring unique processes, equipment, and personnel. Ark-M, in contrast, serves as a beacon for unified water quality management. Its economic viability, accessibility, safety, versatility, and convenience support effective, independent water management across various sites.”

The representative added, “Ark-M addresses workforce shortages and industrial safety issues in developed countries while tackling water management challenges stemming from limited equipment, technology, and capital in developing nations. Beyond environmental benefits, Ark-M also enhances economic, food, and safety security, contributing to human security. By removing pollutants effectively, it supports aquatic ecosystems and stabilizes fisheries. In one case, SHECO resolved algae issues in a drought-affected reservoir within three days, supplying 200,000 tons of agricultural water to 1,320,000 square meters of farmland. SHECO’s solutions solve pollution problems and ensure worker safety by preventing exposure to toxic substances during cleanup operations.”

SHECO aims to leverage its participation in CES 2025 to connect with government entities, corporations, and potential co-developers in water resource management, accelerating the localization and advancement of its technology.

51692.cap: AnyAble’s 3DPE printer. | Photo provided by AnyAble

51692.x: AnyAble, Ltd. (CEO Choi Dong Cheul) announced its participation in CES 2025, to be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will present its cutting-edge 3D Printed Electronics (3DPE) printer and its research and development roadmap at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Established in September 2023 as a research-focused company, AnyAble was born from the technology transfer and equity investment by the Korea Electrotechnology Research Institute (KERI). Since then, the company has concentrated on advancing its 3DPE and biosensor technologies capabilities, aiming to become a global leader.

AnyAble plans to showcase its 3DPE printer internationally at CES 2025. The printer, which utilizes a conductive ink dispensing method, supports high-precision 3D printing at 100µm resolutions, making it versatile for applications across multiple industries.

By the end of this year, AnyAble aims to develop a 50µm-class 3DPE printer, which it plans to market to domestic and international professionals. To enhance its offerings, the company is also investing in developing bio-MEMS sensor chips using Solution Immersed Silicon (SIS), a semiconductor-based technology.

These Bio-MEMS sensor chips are designed to grant higher resolutions (100–50µm) to AnyAble's 3DPE printers, enabling the creation of complex 3D structures beyond traditional PCBs. The chips will also support diverse experimental conditions, ensuring flexibility and user convenience.
Additionally, AnyAble is expanding its product lineup to include industrial-grade and nanometer-scale 3DPE printers, further solidifying its leadership in the global 3DPE market.

An AnyAble representative explained, “With the demand for 3DPE technologies rising in advanced industries like semiconductors, there’s a lack of established brands or manufacturers leading this sector, apart from a few niche startups. CES 2025 provides us a strategic opportunity to showcase our technological capabilities, gather feedback from diverse international customers, and expand our market presence.”

The representative added, “While targeting the highly receptive North American and European markets, we plan to initially penetrate Southeast Asia, where market entry barriers are relatively lower. By supplying research-oriented products in this region, we aim to accelerate the commercialization process and eventually deliver high-quality solutions to global markets.”

51693.x: IOPS Co., Ltd. (CEO Kim Youngwook) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will present its satellite operations expertise, including the innovative IOPS SPACE platform, at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Founded in 2015, IOPS specializes in AI-driven end-to-end services, satellite ground station operations, development and services, satellite assembly and integration testing (AIT), and ground system integration. The company’s expertise has earned it many clients in South Korea, including prestigious institutions like the Korea Aerospace Research Institute and the Korea Institute of Ocean Science and Technology.

IOPS offers optimized solutions across the entire satellite operational lifecycle, from early deployment to stable operation. With over a decade of experience operating satellites for various organizations, IOPS is a leader in ground station construction, pre-launch electrical and electronics testing, and comprehensive AIT services.

At CES 2025, IOPS will unveil its IOPS SPACE platform, drastically reducing the cost, manpower, and physical space required for satellite ground station operations. The platform enables satellite control in web and mobile environments, emphasizing flexibility and user convenience.

The fully in-house developed platform supports cost-efficient satellite management. Its integrated AI capabilities diagnose potential satellite anomalies early, minimizing the risk of malfunctions throughout a satellite’s mission lifecycle. By addressing these issues before they occur, IOPS SPACE helps prevent the creation of space debris, which poses significant challenges for satellite operations.

An IOPS representative highlighted the company’s extensive history: “Before our formal establishment in 2015, IOPS had already accumulated years of expertise as the exclusive operator of South Korea’s national space program since 2006. The representative added, “Our comprehensive support for every stage of space missions, from launch to final orbit, holds immense value in today’s expanding private space industry. 51699.x: Sierra BASE (CEO Kim Songhyun) announced its participation in CES 2025 at the K-Startup Pavilion from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas.

The company specializes in developing autonomous drones and robots that offer 3D modeling and fully automated inspection services for infrastructure and facilities. Its proprietary technologies have been employed in over 50 structures, including 45 bridges, coal storage facilities, power plants, ports, tunnels, and steep slope cuts.

Sierra BASE is also exploring international markets, particularly Japan and the UAE. In October, the company partnered with Japanese ICT firm AQUBER to establish its presence in Japan, with notable outcomes anticipated in 2025. Following its third-place finish at the GITEX AI Challenge, the UAE market has shown keen interest, with multiple partnership requests from local companies.

At CES 2025, Sierra BASE will showcase its SIRIUS solution, an intelligent 3D autonomous robotic system. SIRIUS features multi-sensor fusion SLAM technology, utilizing rotating LiDAR for stable operations in both indoor and outdoor environments. Its precise imaging capabilities enable the detection of cracks smaller than 0.1mm, and its AI engine, trained on over 100,000 damage data points, ensures comprehensive inspection capabilities. The solution also integrates autonomous drone and robot control, AI damage detection and analysis, and web-based centralized management.

The company aims to expand into the Japanese and U.S. markets. A Sierra BASE representative commented, “Japan's focus on safety due to frequent earthquakes aligns well with our technology. We seek potential customers, partners, and investors to solidify our presence. Similarly, we hope to gain recognition in the U.S. for our capabilities, from 3D mapping to autonomous operations and safety diagnostics."

The representative added, "Exporting SIRIUS to certain countries requires navigating certification systems, which can take time. Sierra BASE plans to accelerate its global expansion, starting with Japan and the Middle East and then the U.S. “Our participation in GITEX revealed significant potential in the Middle Eastern market, and we are currently engaging with companies interested in local collaborations. Founded in November 2024, EVERPONIC specializes in modular container plant factories that integrate ICT technology and automated systems. CEO Soo Keun Kim, an economics graduate from the University of Minnesota, established the company to address challenges in crop production in extreme climates, such as deserts.

EVERPONIC’s smart farm technology enables year-round cultivation of diverse crops regardless of climate, location, or time. Designed for extreme environments, the system optimizes water usage while minimizing its ecological footprint. Central to this solution is a vertical tower structure that maximizes cultivation space and employs a recirculating water system to reduce consumption.

The system also creates an independent environment, insulated from external factors, and features an automated control system for precise environmental management. LED grow lights within the container ensure uniform light distribution, facilitating the easy production of fresh and healthy produce.

EVERPONIC's system is noted for its flexibility and scalability, allowing users to adjust cultivation capacity based on their needs. Vertical hydroponic facilities boost productivity while efficiently using water and resources, making them an environmentally friendly solution.

An EVERPONIC representative highlighted the smart farm’s ICT integration, which allows users to remotely control all internal systems via a proprietary mobile control system. The system monitors real-time environmental and nutrient solution data, enhancing operational convenience. "It’s a user-centric technology designed for accessibility, enabling anyone to operate the system effortlessly," the representative explained.

EVERPONIC’s automated technology and vertical hydroponic system ensure high yields with minimal labor. The system also delivers consistent, high-quality harvests and enables consumers to access fresh produce year-round at reasonable prices through planned cultivation. This approach promotes sustainable agricultural ecosystems, addresses climate crises, global warming, and aging rural populations, and sets a new paradigm for agri-tech.

EVERPONIC’s vertical hydroponic systems are setting new standards for sustainable farming. They offer solutions that benefit growers and consumers while contributing to global ecological and agricultural advancements.

51703.x: Orange Biomed Co., Ltd. (co-CEOs Unghyeon Ko and Yeaseul Park) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will occur from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. At the K-Startup Pavilion, it will showcase its portable HbA1c monitor, the "OBM rapid A1c. "

The OBM rapid A1c is a groundbreaking device designed to simplify diabetes management by enabling accurate and convenient hemoglobin A1c testing at home. Hemoglobin A1c, a critical indicator of blood glucose control for diabetes patients, offers a stable measure less affected by testing time or short-term fluctuations, unlike traditional glucose tests. Elevated glycated hemoglobin levels increase blood viscosity, damage blood vessels and tissues, and contribute to diabetes complications.

Developed to make diabetes and its complications more manageable, the OBM rapid A1c leverages microfluidic technology to measure glycated hemoglobin—making it the world's first device. The device's ability to deliver reliable and precise measurements using only a small blood sample underscores its innovation and potential to revolutionize home diabetes care.

Yeaseul Park, Co-CEO of Orange Biomed, stated, "Introducing OBM rapid A1c at CES 2025, the world's largest consumer electronics show, is a significant milestone. By empowering individuals in areas with limited access to hospitals to manage diabetes complications using cutting-edge medical technology, we aim to contribute to greater healthcare equity."

51732.x: Alwaygen (CEO Minsub Chung) will showcase its groundbreaking molecular diagnostics platform at CES 2025 in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10 as part of the K-Startup Pavilion.

The company aims to revolutionize molecular diagnostics by addressing accessibility challenges with its innovative EZprep PCR platform. Unlike traditional methods that rely on complex pre-processing equipment, EZprep utilizes patented lipid-based chemical purification to directly isolate nucleic acids (DNA/RNA) for PCR testing, eliminating the need for bulky and expensive instruments.

CEO Minsub Chung, a chemical engineering professor at Hongik University, developed the technology in response to the limitations of existing diagnostic tools exposed during the COVID-19 pandemic. While PCR is celebrated for its accuracy, its dependence on costly equipment and specialized personnel limits its use in smaller healthcare settings, veterinary clinics, and agricultural sites.

Alwaygen’s technology simplifies pre-processing, enabling high-performance molecular diagnostics even in environments with limited resources. The EZprep platform is designed as a versatile PCR solution that can handle multiple diagnostic applications by swapping out cartridge-based reagents, allowing seamless transitions between tests for various diseases. Currently, the platform targets applications like pet dermatological conditions, avian influenza, and foot-and-mouth disease, with plans to expand into human diagnostics for respiratory illnesses, sexually transmitted infections, and cancer-related viruses.

51732.cap: EZprep PCR Device | Photo provided by Alwaygen

This innovation reduces diagnostic complexity, making molecular testing accessible in remote areas such as farms, border checkpoints, and small medical facilities. The platform’s modular cartridge system further enhances usability and cost-efficiency, allowing users to switch between tests without investing in new devices. Its compact and cost-effective design positions EZprep as a game-changer for institutions with budget constraints or low testing volumes.

Alwaygen’s software complements the hardware by offering intuitive real-time monitoring of amplification curves and results, even for non-specialists. Plans include cloud integration for remote collaboration in epidemic monitoring and R&D applications, broadening the platform’s utility.

51740.x: LORDSYSTEM (CEO Yangho Jang) will participate in CES 2025, held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, USA, as part of the ‘K-Startup Pavilion.’

LORDSYSTEM offers a passport DID (Decentralized Identifier) authentication solution that enables real-time verification of passport authenticity via mobile devices. The solution compares information on the user’s passport with data stored in its electronic chip and cross-verifies the user’s facial recognition information to generate a secure QR code containing user details. Encrypting personal data with blockchain technology ensures robust security, preventing data leaks and fraudulent use during authentication.

Building on its passport DID platform, LORDSYSTEM operates TripPASS, a mobile platform that allows foreign tourists to access transportation and financial services seamlessly, equivalent to domestic users. The platform also issues prepaid cards and supports services like mobile tax refunds, duty-free identity verification, and casino entry authentication for foreigners, with plans to expand its applications further.

At CES 2025, LORDSYSTEM will introduce its non-face-to-face authentication platform, LORDPASS. This platform separates TripPASS's eKYC (electronic Know Your Customer) functions to create a scalable system. LORDPASS leverages blockchain technology to verify user data in real time, serving as a gateway for membership registration, payments, and broader foreign market expansion.

LORDSYSTEM has been actively building partnerships, including with Japan’s DNP (Dai Nippon Printing Co., Ltd), and is a founding member of the Asia-Pacific Digital Identity Consortium (APDI). APDI aims to standardize and enhance interoperability for digital identity solutions across the Asia-Pacific region, with plans for a mobile authentication proof-of-concept (POC) by late 2025.

The company expressed its ambition to identify global partners at CES 2025 to expand passport application further DID authentication and eKYC solutions, emphasizing its commitment to innovation and cross-border digital identity initiatives.

51743.x: PIASPACE (CEO Yu Heonsu) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10, as part of the K-Startup Pavilion.

PIASPACE is an AI company that specializes in solutions that analyze and interpret complex situations in real time using CCTV footage. It leverages multi-modal AI technology based on the Vision-Language Model (VLM).

The company’s flagship solution, MACS (Multi-modal AI for CCTV Solution), goes beyond simple monitoring by recognizing and categorizing conditions that align with pre-set user prompts, offering advanced situational responsiveness.

Established in 2021, PIASPACE has rapidly grown by distinguishing itself with next-generation AI technology. Unlike traditional object detection-based CCTV systems, MACS delivers real-time analysis and understanding of complex scenarios, according to the company, setting a new standard in video analysis.

PIASPACE has successfully executed high-level proof-of-concept projects across various sectors in South Korea. These include detecting fires, collapses, violence, and disasters at control centers of major districts in Seoul, identifying anomalies in highway tunnels, monitoring incidents in large e-commerce logistics centers, and ensuring intrusion-free, large-scale port security against smuggling or unauthorized entry.
Building on its domestic achievements, PIASPACE is expanding into Southeast Asian markets, including Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia, establishing its presence on the global stage.

PIASPACE was selected as a finalist for the Infocomm Media Development Authority’s (IMDA) RTPD (Risk/Threat Prediction and Detection) program in Singapore. The company is also collaborating with Sembcorp Cogen, a national energy corporation, on a PoC project to enhance plant safety management systems, integrating patrol robots and worker safety analysis technologies.

In Thailand, PIASPACE is in exclusive supply negotiations with major hotel chains as part of a smart city project and is working with the state-owned oil company PTT to commercialize safety management solutions. In Indonesia, the company is pursuing opportunities tied to defense ministry projects, continuing its momentum in global market expansion.

At CES 2025, PIASPACE will unveil MACS, a solution that simultaneously uses multimodal AI to analyze video and text data. By assessing the similarity between visual and textual modalities, MACS utilizes linguistic intelligence alongside visual AI to analyze complex situations and contexts previously beyond the scope of conventional visual AI. This allows for precise, real-time detection of anomalies and predefined scenarios.

According to the company, MACS’ core technology enables accurate detection through CCTV, preventing emergencies and mitigating secondary damage. The solution can be integrated into existing CCTV systems by adding an AI server (SaaS or On-Premise), transforming them into next-generation multimodal AI-powered systems.

MACS integrates retrieval models for video and text with object detection algorithms. The solution further analyzes behaviors and situations by cropping detected objects (e.g., people, vehicles) and feeding them into a second input stream.

"Most currently commercialized intelligent CCTVs rely on single-modality AI models that detect specific objects or basic movements but fail to understand complex situations or anomalies. MACS addresses these limitations," a PIASPACE representative explained.

The company also shared its plans to expand from Southeast Asia into North America and Europe, targeting $12 million in global sales by 2027. "PIASPACE aims to promote its technology on global stages like CES 2025 while accelerating market expansion through diverse PoC projects and commercialization efforts," the representative added.

51760.cap: | DEOGAM's electric recycling system module | Photo by DEOGAM

51760.x: DEOGAM INC. (CEO Kim Jinouk) announced its participation in CES 2025 in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10. The company, founded in 2022, aims to promote the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and contribute to the growth of sustainable mobility. DEOGAM focuses on reclaiming energy lost to harmonics generated in EV power systems and recycling it for vehicle power usage.

Electric vehicles rely on secondary batteries to power their motors. The energy stored in these batteries is converted from DC (direct current) to AC (alternating current) through an inverter, generating heat and harmonics. These harmonics lead to energy loss, which increases with higher power input and vehicle performance.

To address this, DEOGAM developed an "electric recycle" system that uses a toroid-shaped energy core to capture harmonics and convert them into usable electrical energy. The company plans to showcase this system and its demonstration results at CES 2025 to accelerate its global market entry.

DEOGAM's recycling system generates high electromotive force, allowing stable energy conversion even with significant input voltage fluctuations within a Buck & Boost converter. Internal tests indicate the system can reclaim 18% of energy lost to harmonics, increasing EV driving range by up to 10%.

51760.cap: | DEOGAM's electric recycling system and internal design | Photo by DEOGAM

51760.x: Selected for TIPS’ project on “Energy efficiency systems utilizing electromagnetic waves generated during EV operation,” DEOGAM has been developing this technology since September 2023. In 2024, the company conducted field tests on domestic commercial EVs, measuring the increase in driving range achieved with its technology.

DEOGAM partnered with Kakao Mobility through an MOU to target the domestic electric taxi market in 2025. This collaboration aims to establish successful use cases in South Korea and pave the way for market entry into Germany, Norway, and key U.S. cities.

Kim Jinouk, CEO of DEOGAM, stated, “If our electric recycling system were applied to 14 million EVs worldwide, each driving 30 kilometers, the reclaimed energy would total approximately 3 million megawatts (MW). This efficiency underscores the system’s growing importance in achieving global carbon neutrality.”

Kim added, “With this technology, DEOGAM aims to make the electric recycle system an essential component for every EV worldwide. Since the system’s carbon emissions during energy production are nearly zero, we plan to focus on markets in Western Europe, which are leading the charge in carbon neutrality.”

51779.x: AEOL KOREA, led by CEO Jeong Whan Kim, announced its participation in CES 2025, which will occur in Las Vegas from January 7th to 10th (local time) under the 'K-Startup Pavilion.'

Founded in 2018 at Korea University's Campus Town, AEOL KOREA focuses on developing technologies for a sustainable future. Initially, the company aimed to improve energy efficiency and dehumidification in buildings. By leveraging waste heat recovery and dehumidification technologies, it set out to reduce energy consumption within buildings. According to the company, these innovations are critical in lowering energy use while enhancing indoor air quality and energy efficiency.

AEOL KOREA has expanded its research to carbon capture, gas separation, and energy storage by utilizing the potential of Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs), a porous material. MOFs are known for their advanced microstructure and excellent adsorption capabilities, making them suitable for addressing various environmental challenges.

The company successfully produced MOFs at a large scale for the first time in Korea and has made significant strides in commercializing them. AEOL KOREA's technologies have yielded carbon capture and gas separation results, offering sustainable energy solutions. By utilizing the porous structure of MOFs, the company effectively captures greenhouse gases and separates harmful gases, contributing to carbon neutrality efforts.

AEOL KOREA is also conducting research to commercialize antimicrobial and antiviral technologies. Although these efforts are still in their early stages, MOFs’ ability to absorb or block bacteria and viruses holds promise for innovations in healthcare and hygiene.

The company emphasized that its innovative technologies align with global trends such as carbon neutrality and ESG (environmental, social, and governance) goals. AEOL KOREA's MOF technology can be applied across various industries, including greenhouse gas reduction, energy efficiency, moisture adsorption, and gas separation. The company collaborates with global firms pursuing carbon neutrality and has established partnerships in North America and New Zealand.

AEOL KOREA received an Innovation Award at CES 2024 and the Grand Innovation Award at FIX 2024, earning global recognition for its technological achievements. These awards mark a significant milestone in the company’s journey as a leader in developing innovative carbon-neutral technologies.

AEOL KOREA collaborates with major domestic appliance companies to explore MOF applications through R&D contracts and research partnerships. The company is conducting studies on improving building energy efficiency, enhancing indoor comfort, and integrating MOFs into home appliance drying solutions.

AEOL KOREA also supplies MOF technology to various industries. Collaborating with oral care specialist Re:Brush, sleep care brand Re:Sleep, and women's hygiene product company Aroundbody, the company delivers MOFs for antimicrobial, dehumidification, and deodorization purposes.

At CES 2025, AEOL KOREA will unveil its next-generation CO₂ capture technology, the CarbonSorV Wheel, developed to achieve sustainable carbon neutrality. The CarbonSorV Wheel captures atmospheric carbon dioxide with greater efficiency and environmental friendliness than existing technologies, helping address climate change issues.

The core of this product is MOF technology. MOFs, composed of metal ions and organic materials, feature a porous structure capable of selectively adsorbing and separating carbon dioxide. The MOF technology applied to the CarbonSorV Wheel extends beyond carbon capture, offering potential in energy storage, moisture adsorption, gas separation, and biomedical fields.

The CarbonSorV Wheel employs a rotary design for continuous CO₂ adsorption and desorption, minimizing energy consumption while maintaining high capture efficiency. The company highlights its low-energy adsorption-desorption process, which significantly reduces the energy required for carbon capture and eases economic burdens.

The CarbonSorV Wheel also separates carbon dioxide from mixed gases 80 times more efficiently than previous methods. An AEOL KOREA representative stated, "Our proprietary MOF mass production technology ensures stable quality and cost efficiency. We minimize environmental pollution by using water as a solvent in eco-friendly manufacturing. The CarbonSorV Wheel is more than just a solution for climate change. It is a powerful tool for building a sustainable future."

The representative added, "AEOL KOREA aims to become a global leader in driving innovation for a sustainable future with a clear vision and plan. Our MOF-based innovations hold significant potential to achieve carbon neutrality and address environmental challenges. Through CES 2025, we plan to showcase our technology and vision on the global stage."

In the short term, AEOL KOREA is accelerating technology development and commercialization by strengthening collaborations with global corporations, international universities, and government research institutions. The company supplies MOF materials on a laboratory scale to establish trust in early markets while expanding its influence across industries through engineering services and licensing agreements. It is also researching resource recycling by extracting MOF raw materials from waste plastics and metal sludge, enhancing MOF’s affordability while promoting sustainable resource circulation.

In the midterm, AEOL KOREA plans to establish a large-scale MOF production system to expand its global supply chain. The company aims to meet market demands by developing various application products, such as carbon capture devices, air purifiers, and energy storage solutions. To secure stable market shares and expand its global network, it seeks to provide localized solutions in key overseas markets, including the United States and China.
In the long term, AEOL KOREA envisions entering the carbon credit trading business to drive tangible change in addressing climate change.

The company stated, "Our technology provides practical solutions to various environmental issues, including greenhouse gas reduction, energy efficiency, and resource recycling. These efforts will solidify AEOL’s position as a partner for businesses and governments seeking to solve global environmental challenges."

51780.x: Seoreu (CEO Yeoun Joo Lee) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7th (Tuesday) to January 10th (Friday). The company will showcase its AI-powered capsule endoscopy video analysis system, CAPTOS, at the "K-Startup Pavilion."

Seoreu has been dedicated to developing proprietary AI technologies that aim to revolutionize the treatment and management of gastrointestinal diseases. The company aims to provide reliable data for diagnostics, prognosis management, and regular health checkups, enabling individuals to easily access high-quality medical services.

Previously, Seoreu gained industry recognition with its capsule endoscopy reading assistance program, which addressed a critical demand in medical practices. The company has since expanded its portfolio to cover a broader range of gastrointestinal technologies and products. It has also secured large-scale projects for building medical datasets, focusing on acquiring medical imaging essential for AI development while addressing the high costs of large-scale data processing.

At CES 2025, Seoreu will introduce its CAPTOS system. This system analyzes capsule endoscopy videos using AI to identify and accurately analyze various small bowel lesions. It employs quantitative analysis to distinguish disease severity, facilitating prompt and precise diagnoses. This technology is particularly effective for the early diagnosis and treatment planning of pediatric Crohn's disease (CD).

The CAPTOS system’s AI algorithm features three main capabilities: identifying the small intestine by accurately distinguishing the position of the stomach, small intestine, and large intestine; detecting and distinguishing four key types of lesions essential for disease diagnosis; and determining the visible range within the small intestine. These algorithms also summarize critical lesions and generate automated reports, including accuracy assessments.

This functionality significantly reduces the time medical professionals spend reviewing and analyzing data. It eliminates concerns about diagnostic errors caused by human mistakes, offering patients highly reliable results. CAPTOS has demonstrated diagnostic accuracy of up to 95% compared to experienced medical professionals.

A Seoreu representative stated, “CAPTOS AI supports the assessment of lesion severity through quantitative analysis. It is optimized not only for pediatric CD but also for adult CD diagnostics. The algorithm, trained and refined using intestinal image data from over 500 pediatric CD patients, achieves exceptional accuracy. It is also compatible with various hardware systems, allowing comparison of results from different capsule endoscopy devices.”

The representative continued, “By revolutionizing the diagnostic and treatment processes for Crohn's disease, CAPTOS AI has immense utility beyond Korea, particularly in countries that share modernized dietary habits and meat-centric diets. At CES 2025, we aim to establish a foothold in markets such as Central Asia, including Kazakhstan, where Crohn’s disease cases are rapidly increasing, as well as in the U.S. and Europe.”
