51782.x: Morphing I Inc.(CEO Kim Ki Young) announced that it will participate in CES 2025, held from January 7th (Tuesday) to January 10th (Friday) in Las Vegas, USA, under the "K-Startup Pavilion."

Since its establishment in 2021, Morphing I has accumulated IT and software development expertise. Using advanced AI technology and robotics solutions, the company has revolutionized safety inspection processes for water and drainage pipes, focusing on preventing water resource loss and safety incidents.

In line with this vision, Morphing I developed Morphing-BOT, a robot designed to inspect the interiors of enclosed pipelines, such as water pipes, and detect abnormal signals. Morphing I will showcase this product at CES 2025 to showcase its technology and products to the global market.

Morphing-BOT uses AI algorithms developed in-house to analyze data in real-time and predict the condition of pipelines. The model can foresee leaks, damage, and contamination, enabling faster and more accurate diagnoses than traditional inspection methods. It also allows for 24-hour continuous monitoring, which is a significant advantage.

Additionally, Morphing-BOT integrates multimodal solutions to collect and analyze diverse data, including images, sounds, and vibrations, to evaluate pipeline conditions comprehensively. This capability enables it to diagnose structural abnormalities and their causes more accurately than traditional video-based inspection systems.

Morphing-BOT also supports a digital twin feature visualizing real-time data through 3D mapping. This feature lets users intuitively identify problem areas and integrate them with customers' BIM systems, improving operational and maintenance efficiency.

Moreover, Morphing-BOT enhances inspection quality through self-learning while eliminating human error, ensuring reliable inspections and evaluations. Its modular system adapts to various pipeline types, and its compliance with international standards allows it to inspect pipelines worldwide, including water and oil pipelines.

A Morphing I representative stated, “By showcasing our latest technologies, including Morphing-BOT, on the global stage at CES, we aim to emphasize Morphing I's competitiveness in pipeline inspection and management. The representative added, “We hope to enhance our understanding of target countries and regional environments while strengthening localization strategies. This event allows us to analyze market trends, observe competitors’ products and technologies, and respond effectively to market changes.”

Leveraging its domestic references, KNR is preparing to enter the U.S. market and was selected to participate in CES 2025 as part of its global strategy. Acknowledged for its next-generation nuclear technologies, KNR was named to the Ultra-Gap Startup 1000+ program and received the Minister of Trade, Industry, and Energy Award on the 14th Nuclear Safety and Promotion Day, solidifying its technical innovation and capabilities.

51815.x: Airthings, a leading global technology company headquartered in Oslo, Norway, has launched Corentium Home 2, its latest innovation in radon detection. Announced at CES 2025 in Las Vegas, the Corentium Home 2 builds on the success of its predecessor and features enhanced technology to provide more accurate and actionable insights for homeowners. The device is designed to meet the growing demand for smarter indoor air quality monitoring.

Airthings specializes in award-winning radon detectors and indoor air quality monitors for homes, workplaces, and schools. With over one million devices sold globally, the company has received accolades like the TIME Best Inventions Award and the CES Innovation Award Honor. Airthings is committed to empowering people to improve their air quality and health through innovative, user-friendly solutions.

Radon, an invisible and odorless gas, is the second leading cause of lung cancer in the United States, claiming over 21,000 lives annually. Despite increasing awareness, surveys indicate that 75% of Americans have never tested their homes for radon.
“You can’t see or smell radon. Everyone should test their home to know if radon threatens you or your family. We believe that radon detection can save lives,” said Emma Tryti, CEO of Airthings.

The Corentium Home 2 utilizes redesigned sensor technology developed by Airthings engineers to deliver even more reliable data. The device connects to the Airthings app, which offers users real-time radon level updates and additional insights, such as neighborhood comparisons and personalized advice on mitigating risks.

As global awareness of indoor air quality grows, Airthings continues to lead with innovation. Over 500,000 homeowners worldwide have purchased the original Corentium Home, receiving high praise for its reliability and ease of use.
“With new studies around radon and growing competition, Corentium Home 2 exemplifies our commitment to innovation and maintaining our global market leadership,” added Tryti.

Airthings plans to make Corentium Home 2 available by Q2 2025. Additional radon insights and app features will roll out throughout the year. These updates aim to help people better understand and mitigate their indoor air quality risks at home, school, and work.

51816.cap: | EcoFlow showcased OASIS energy management solution at CES 2025 | Photo by EcoFlow.

51816.x: EcoFlow, a leader in portable power and eco-friendly energy solutions, unveiled its groundbreaking AI-powered energy management system, EcoFlow OASIS, at CES 2025 in Las Vegas. Designed to enhance home energy storage, prepare for weather-related power outages, and reduce electricity costs, OASIS marks a new era of smart energy solutions for homeowners.

Since its founding in 2017, EcoFlow has empowered over 4.5 million users in 140 markets worldwide. It is committed to being the "FIRST" in power solutions: Flexible, Innovative, Reliable, Simple, and Thorough.

EcoFlow OASIS leverages artificial intelligence and real-time data, such as past energy consumption, local electricity rates, solar energy generation, and weather patterns, to provide personalized recommendations. With the ability to automate energy-saving actions, OASIS ensures batteries are charged before severe weather and optimizes energy usage to reduce costs. The built-in smart assistant responds to natural language queries, offering actionable insights like maximizing solar energy use or shifting energy-intensive tasks to cost-efficient periods. “As the first in the portable power industry to launch a user-focused mobile app, EcoFlow now leads again by integrating AI into a comprehensive energy management system,” said Peter Linghu, EcoFlow's Director of Product Strategy and Development.

51816.cap: | EcoFlow showcased OASIS energy management solution at CES 2025 | Photo by EcoFlow.

51816.x: EcoFlow OASIS integrates seamlessly with EcoFlow products like DELTA 3 Plus and RIVER 3 Plus, offering features such as Storm Warning Alerts and Time-of-Use Mode. Its full capabilities are realized in EcoFlow's Whole-Home Power Backup Solutions, including DELTA Pro Ultra with Smart Home Panel 2 in North America and PowerOcean grid-tied energy systems in Europe. EcoFlow also plans to launch OCEAN Pro, a grid-tied solar battery solution, in the U.S. later this year, fully leveraging OASIS’s advanced AI functionalities. Additionally, OASIS supports third-party devices compatible with Shelly and Matter, providing a unified overview of energy sources, consumption insights, and management controls—an industry-first innovation. Linghu emphasized, “With increasingly capable systems, EcoFlow OASIS simplifies home energy management, maximizing the value of every energy investment.”

51817.cap: | BionicM unveils the award-winning Bio Leg® at CES 2025 | Photo by BionicM.

51817.x: BionicM (CEO: Sunny Xiaojun Sun, Ph.D) has announced the launch of its U.S. subsidiary, BionicM USA, in the Virginia area near Washington, D.C. The establishment of this office underscores the company’s dedication to delivering advanced powered prosthetics to the world’s largest prosthetics market. This strategic move is complemented by unveiling its flagship product, the Bio Leg®, at CES 2025, where it earned the prestigious Best of Innovation award.

The Bio Leg®, a powered microprocessor knee, represents a leap forward in prosthetic technology. By replacing lost muscle strength with advanced robotics, the device reduces physical strain and enables natural, intuitive movement, empowering users to lead active lifestyles. Following its successful FDA Class II registration in July 2023 and insurance coverage approval in May 2024, the Bio Leg® entered the U.S. market in the summer of 2024, surpassing revenue expectations.

The new U.S. headquarters will act as an operational hub, streamlining inventory and delivery processes, expediting sales, and providing comprehensive after-sales support to prosthetic practitioners and patients. This expansion aligns with BionicM's vision to address the increasing demand for powered prosthetic solutions in the U.S. market, which offers significant growth potential. The launch follows notable achievements, including delivering the first Bio Leg® units to U.S. customers and completing a $3 million fundraising round in September 2024.

At CES 2025, BionicM showcased the Bio Leg® at the J-Startup/JAPAN Pavilion in Eureka Park (Booth No. 61000 & 61001, Tech West, Venetian Expo, Level 1, Hall G). This event allows attendees to experience the transformative potential of the Bio Leg® and connect with industry leaders.

The Bio Leg® has undergone extensive trials involving over 300 participants, with users praising its seamless integration, safety, and life-changing capabilities. This advanced device reflects BionicM’s mission to "Power Mobility for All" by improving the quality of life for individuals with lower-limb amputations through innovative robotics technology.

Founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the University of Tokyo, BionicM draws on the pioneering research of its CEO, Sunny Xiaojun Sun, under the mentorship of Professor Inaba. With support from JST's START program, the company has emerged as a leader in powered prosthetic technology, leveraging humanoid robotics to develop solutions that empower users worldwide.
Through its U.S. expansion and the continued success of Bio Leg®, BionicM reaffirms its commitment to advancing mobility and transforming lives.

51819.cap: | Evenflo's SensorySoothe™ offers customizable lights and sounds for stress-free travel with infants | Photo by Evenflo.

51819.x: At CES 2025, Evenflo introduced SensorySoothe™, a groundbreaking innovation designed to soothe crying babies and reduce parental stress during travel. Unveiled at CES 2025 in Las Vegas, this first-of-its-kind technology integrates app-connected lights. It sounds directly into the handles of Evenflo’s newest premium car seats and travel systems, setting a new standard in the industry.

SensorySoothe allows parents to create a calming environment tailored to their child’s needs. Accessible via the Evenflo app, voice commands with Siri or Google, or on-unit buttons, this advanced system provides customizable light and sound combinations that leverage research on infant sensory preferences. SensorySoothe delivers a personalized experience to enhance infant comfort and parental peace of mind, from calming white noise and lullabies to dynamic light effects synchronized with sound.

“Any parent has been there—stuck in a car or public place with a crying baby, feeling helpless. SensorySoothe aims to alleviate stress in those moments,” said Sharon Ruggieri, Senior Director of Product Management at Evenflo. “It’s all about making parents’ lives easier and creating a calming environment wherever you go, tailored to your family’s needs.”

Beyond convenience, SensorySoothe enhances safety by integrating soothing features directly into the car seat, eliminating the need for aftermarket attachments that could become hazardous in the event of a crash. Sarah Haverstick, Senior Manager of Safety Advocacy & Consumer Care at Evenflo, emphasized, “With built-in lights and sounds, parents no longer need to rely on add-ons, ensuring babies are entertained and safe during travel.”

51819.cap: | Evenflo's SensorySoothe™ offers customizable lights and sounds for stress-free travel with infants | Photo by Evenflo.

51819.x: SensorySoothe will debut in two new premium products: the Shyft™ Intuiti™+ Travel System and the Revolve180™ LiteMax™ NXT. Both are designed to accommodate preemies and infants from 3 to 30 pounds and feature sustainable Green & Gentle™ Fabric made from recycled plastic bottles, free of added chemicals. The Revolve180 LiteMax NXT includes a gentle amber nightlight for nighttime travel and provides over 15 hours of battery life with four AA batteries, making it ideal for extended trips.

Available in six modern colors, these products will begin shipping in mid-February 2025 through online retailers such as Babylist, Amazon, Target, and Walmart. With SensorySoothe, Evenflo reaffirms its commitment to continuous innovation, making travel safer, more convenient, and less stressful for families.

51820.cap: | WYBOT S3 revolutionizes pool care with autonomous 3D mapping and self-emptying capabilities | Photo by WYBOT.

51820.x: WYBOT, a global leader in innovative pool maintenance solutions, has introduced the WYBOT S3 Pool Cleaning Robot at CES 2025 in Las Vegas. This groundbreaking device redefines pool care with advanced autonomous features, including 3D mapping, self-emptying, automatic solar charging, and real-time underwater control. Designed to deliver hands-free maintenance for up to a month, the WYBOT S3 sets a new standard in convenience and sustainability.

“The WYBOT S3 Pool Cleaning Robot is the ultimate testament to WYBOT’s commitment to innovation and pool owner convenience,” said José Vallés, Vice President and General Manager of Americas at WYBOT. “With the integration of cutting-edge robotic technologies, the WYBOT S3 represents the pinnacle of innovation in the industry, offering pool owners a smarter, more efficient, and environmentally friendly way to maintain their pools.”

The WYBOT S3 introduces features that transform pool cleaning from a chore into an effortless experience. Using advanced 3D mapping technology, the robot creates a precise underwater map to plan the most efficient cleaning routes, ensuring full coverage, even in irregularly shaped pools. Its Smart Debris Management system includes the world’s first self-emptying feature for a robotic pool cleaner. Debris collected in the robot’s onboard bin is transferred to an above-ground base station, enabling up to eight cleaning cycles or 30 days of operation without user intervention.

51820.cap: | WYBOT S3 revolutionizes pool care with autonomous 3D mapping and self-emptying capabilities | Photo by WYBOT.

51820.x: Equipped with dual charging capabilities, the robot leverages solar-assisted charging for reduced energy consumption. Under optimal sunlight, the solar panel provides 1.5 hours of runtime after a single day of charging. Traditional DC charging ensures consistent performance in all weather conditions. The WYBOT S3 also features vision-aided debris detection, allowing it to prioritize heavily soiled areas, and real-time monitoring via Wi-Fi and sonar, enabling users to adjust settings and track progress through a mobile app.

The robot’s innovative technology ensures a sparkling, clean pool with minimal effort. Available for pre-order starting in Q2 2025, the WYBOT S3 Pool Cleaning Robot is priced at $2,999, with exclusive launch incentives for early adopters.

With its cutting-edge features and commitment to innovation, WYBOT continues to set benchmarks in robotic pool cleaning. It has earned accolades such as the 2025 CES Best of Innovation Award and the 2024 French, New York, and Paris Design Awards.

51821.cap: The Hurotics booth at CES 2025 in Las Vegas, USA | Photo by AVING News

51821.x: Hurotics (CEO Giuk Lee), a medical, wellness, and sports wearable robot suit specialist, captured global visitors' attention at CES 2025 with its innovative technology.

At this exhibition, Hurotics showcased the sports wearable robot "H-Fit" and the "H-Medi" rehabilitation device," demonstrating how personalized robotic technology has become integrated into daily life.

The most popular program at the Hurotics booth was the H-Fit experience event. H-Fit is a sports wearable robot designed to maximize athletes' performance. Visitors could test it in a sprint challenge against a Korean national track and field athlete.

The event, held from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m., offered an exciting challenge. Participants who beat the athlete's record received a $3,000 prize. Visitors who participated remarked, "It was not just a simple technology demonstration but a new experience combining sports and technology."

The H-Medi experience event took place from 2 to 5 p.m. H-Medi, a double winner of the CES Innovation Award, is a wearable robot that introduces a new paradigm in rehabilitation through AI-based personalized gait support technology and a cable-driven system.

Visitors personally wore the robot, experiencing its natural movements and comfortable fit. Many expressed surprise, saying, "I didn't expect rehabilitation therapy to become so simple and accessible daily." H-Medi received high praise for its ability to adjust flexibly to various patient physiques and symptoms and its lightweight design that allows use without environmental or location constraints.

51821.cap: The H-Fit experience event featured a sports wearable robot designed to maximize athletes' performance. | Photo by AVING News

51821.x: Through special experience events at CES 2025, Hurotics emphasized the innovation and practicality of its technology. The booth in Hall D of the Venetian Expo in Las Vegas continuously attracted visitors from the opening day.

A representative from Hurotics stated, "H-Fit and H-Medi are products that will redefine the future of sports performance and rehabilitation therapy. We are pleased to show visitors through these experience events how robotic technology has come so close to individuals' lives."

At CES 2025, Hurotics demonstrated that wearable robot technology can practically change individuals' lives in sports and medical fields, going beyond mere technological demonstrations. The innovative products and experience programs impressed visitors with the realization that robotic technology is no longer a distant future concept. One attendee commented, "It's amazing that robotic technology in sports and rehabilitation feels so realistic. H-Fit and H-Medi are not just devices but companions that enhance the quality of life."

As a leading company in the wearable robot field, Hurotics plans to further solidify its position in the global market through its participation in CES 2025. Through ongoing innovation, the company aims to develop practical, user-friendly robots that anyone can use.

51822.cap: AFS CEO Taehee Kim (left) poses with the precision hair loss diagnostic device 'AFS 3D' | Photo by AVING News

51822.x: AFS (Advanced Future Systems), led by CEO Taehee Kim, is an innovative startup reshaping the global hair loss treatment market. On January 7 (local time), it participated in CES 2025 in Las Vegas, USA.

AFS unveiled its groundbreaking hair loss diagnostic device, AFS 3D, which combines AI and 3D technology to surpass the limitations of traditional diagnostic tools. Attendees of CES 2025 had the opportunity to experience the future of hair loss diagnosis firsthand through live demonstrations of the device.

The AFS 3D employs AI-based analysis and 360-degree rotational imaging technology to precisely diagnose hair follicles and scalp conditions. Its user-friendly features, such as automatic focus adjustment and one-click capture, ensure ease of operation, while advanced lighting control maintains consistent imaging conditions. The integrated AI program (AFSS) evaluates hair thickness, density, and distribution with unparalleled precision, offering comprehensive analysis.

“Our device is more than just a diagnostic tool; it’s a platform for building trust between medical professionals and patients, enabling visual tracking of hair loss treatment progress,” said CEO Taehee Kim, emphasizing the product’s differentiation and global competitiveness.

51822.cap: AI-powered hair loss diagnostic device 'AFS 3D' | Photo by AVING News

51822.x: Winning the CES Innovation Award served as a testament to the technological sophistication and market potential of the AFS 3D. AFS is now leveraging this accolade to accelerate its expansion into global markets.

The device has already achieved initial sales success in Hong Kong and China. At CES 2025, it garnered significant attention from healthcare professionals and consumers worldwide. International buyers and medical experts praised its precise diagnostics and ease of use, highlighting its potential as a game-changer in hair loss treatment.

CEO Taehee Kim’s unique insight into the device’s development stemmed from observing the precision of cone-beam CT scanners used in dentistry. “I realized the need for a systematic and precise device for diagnosing hair loss, which led to the creation of AFS 3D,” Kim explained.

Designed to help patients intuitively understand their hair loss condition, the device helps build trust between doctors and patients and facilitates systematic management of treatment plans. Kim stressed, “Accurate diagnosis is the foundation of effective treatment,” underscoring the value of the AFS 3D.

51822.cap: AFS booth at CES 2025 in Las Vegas | Photo by AVING News

51822.x: Beyond developing medical devices, AFS aims to advance the globalization of K-Medical. “AFS 3D is a prime example of K-Medical’s competitiveness,” Kim noted, expressing the company’s commitment to maintaining its technological edge in the global healthcare market.

51823.x: Otiton Medical, led by CEO Kim Jaeyoung, drew global attention at CES 2025 in Las Vegas with its innovative smart thermometer and telemedicine platform, “Dr. In Home.”

The award-winning Dr. In Home integrates temperature measurement with telemedicine capabilities, offering a groundbreaking solution to improve healthcare accessibility. This device measures body temperature and captures high-definition images of the ears, nose, and throat, transmitting the data to a mobile app for real-time remote consultations with physicians.
Equipped with a high-resolution camera, Dr. In Home allows parents to monitor their child’s health and easily diagnose conditions such as otitis media, sinusitis, and tonsillitis from home.

51823.cap: The Dr. In Home smart thermometer enables body temperature measurement and imaging of the ears, nose, and throat. | Photo by AVING News

51823.x: The platform facilitates instant telemedicine consultations through its seamless connection to healthcare professionals. CEO Kim Jaeyoung explained, “Dr. In Home was developed to help families maintain their health in environments with limited medical access.” He cited his experiences in Vietnam during the COVID-19 pandemic as the inspiration behind the product’s development.

Otiton Medical’s participation in CES 2025 and its recognition as an Innovation Award Honoree reaffirm its technological capabilities and market potential. The company has previously garnered attention at international exhibitions in Japan, the U.S., and Silicon Valley, further solidifying its global presence. It was also selected for Japan’s startup program, accelerating its international expansion.

Kim expressed confidence in the product’s future: “Winning the CES Innovation Award and participating in the exhibition validate our technology and market differentiation. This milestone will help us grow into a global brand.”

Looking ahead, Otiton Medical is expanding its offerings to include pet health management solutions. The upcoming “Dr. Pet Care,” set for release next year, will help diagnose ear conditions in dogs and cats at home.

The company’s vision extends beyond a simple thermometer to providing professional diagnostic capabilities and secure telemedicine connections from the comfort of home. Kim emphasized, “Dr. In Home is designed to help parents confidently care for their children and aims to usher in a new paradigm for telemedicine.”

51824.x: ECOPEACE Co., Ltd. (CEO In Won Chae) made waves at CES 2025 in Las Vegas, showcasing its groundbreaking ‘Healing Boat’—a solution that combines water recreation with algae removal for sustainable water management. The Healing Boat, winner of the CES 2025 Innovation Award in the Smart Cities category, highlights the potential of eco-friendly technologies in addressing environmental challenges.

ECOPEACE has earned recognition for its AI-powered autonomous technology and solar energy modules, which underpin its eco-friendly water purification robots. The Healing Boat actively removes algae while generating its energy via solar power, offering a sustainable approach to water resource management. This technology has already been validated through partnerships with public corporations and local governments in South Korea, including deliveries of the ECO-BOT and ECO-STATION products.

The Healing Boat goes beyond environmental technology by incorporating entertainment features. Passengers aboard the autonomous boat can enjoy 3D digital video content, offering a unique experience of underwater ecosystems. This water recreation and resource conservation combination earned the Healing Boat its prestigious CES Innovation Award.

51824.cap: ECOPEACE’s ECO-BOT, a water purification robot, on display at CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

The company is already in talks for Healing Boat sales in Vietnam and is conducting a proof-of-concept project for a customized water purification robot in Singapore.

In addition to the Healing Boat, ECOPEACE is expanding its product lineup to include oil removal robots, recreational boats, and bubble removal solutions. The company is setting a new sustainable robotics and mobility standard by leveraging autonomous technology and renewable energy.

ECOPEACE CEO In Won Chae stated, “CES 2025 is the perfect platform to showcase our vision to a global audience. We aim to create new business opportunities by collaborating with water resource management agencies and corporations worldwide. 51826.cap: DEOGAM CEO Jinouk Kim (center) poses at the company booth during CES 2025 in Las Vegas. | Photo by AVING News

51826.x: DEOGAM INC (CEO Jinouk Kim) gained attention at CES 2025 in Las Vegas with its innovative electric vehicle energy recycling system, “EnerShift.” The company aims to revolutionize the electric vehicle (EV) industry by addressing energy efficiency challenges and has set its sights on expanding to global markets.
Founded in 2022, DEOGAM focuses on resolving energy inefficiencies in EVs by reclaiming harmonic distortion and energy losses from drivetrain systems and converting them into reusable power.

The Toroid energy core is at the heart of DEOGAM’s technology, which converts harmonic distortion into electric energy. This breakthrough reduces energy loss by up to 18% and extends vehicle driving range by up to 10%, a feature that has garnered interest from both domestic and international EV markets.

51826.cap: (Left) Demonstration of technology converting harmonic distortion into electric energy. (Right) Fully integrated product for EVs. | Photo by AVING News

51826.x: During CES 2025, DEOGAM showcased the internal design and performance of its electric recycling system, supported by empirical data to highlight its reliability. The system incorporates a Buck & Boost converter to ensure stable energy delivery despite input voltage fluctuations, enhancing efficiency and sustainability in EV applications.
DEOGAM plans to use the exhibition as a launchpad for expansion into key European markets, including Germany, Norway, and major U.S. cities.

The company’s innovative approach has already led to a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Kakao Mobility, facilitating its entry into the electric taxi market. In 2024, DEOGAM successfully demonstrated its system's driving range benefits during field tests on commercial EVs in Korea.

“Applying DEOGAM’s electric recycling system to the 14 million EVs worldwide could recover approximately 3 million megawatts (MW) of electricity daily,” CEO Jinouk Kim said. “This technology will play a crucial role in achieving carbon neutrality.”
Kim also emphasized, “Our electric recycling system, which approaches zero carbon emissions, will become an essential feature of EVs worldwide, starting with Western Europe.”

51827.cap: CIT CEO Seung Jeong (left) and team presenting their transparent display product at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

51827.x: Advanced materials startup CIT(CEO Seung Jeong) gained attention at CES 2025 in Las Vegas, which runs until January 10. CIT’s groundbreaking transparent antenna, Dolphin, an Honoree of the CES 2025 Innovation Awards in the Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility category, drew significant interest from global industry leaders, as did its transparent display technology.

The transparent antenna ‘Dolphin,’ unveiled for the first time at CES 2025, supports six frequency bands from the L-band to the K-band, with coverage extending up to 20GHz. Designed for autonomous vehicles, Dolphin facilitates vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication, aligning with the demands of the software-defined vehicle (SDV) era by delivering high-speed data transmission.

Dolphin’s ultra-thin copper circuit, less than 10 nanometers thick, achieves 90% transparency while being 1,000 times thinner than conventional antennas. This remarkable combination of aesthetics and performance captivated CES attendees. Furthermore, Dolphin employs an eco-friendly manufacturing process utilizing recycled wires, reducing its carbon footprint to 1/1000th of traditional products.

An automotive executive who visited the CIT booth remarked, “Dolphin’s technology dramatically increases design flexibility in autonomous vehicle development and promises to elevate communication performance to new heights.”

51827.cap: CIT’s ‘Dolphin’ transparent antenna supports up to 20GHz across six frequency bands. The product won the CES 2025 Innovation Award. | Photo by AVING News

51827.x: CIT also showcased its transparent display technology, leveraging ultra-thin copper circuits to deliver near-invisible transparency. This innovation attracted interest from professionals in commercial facilities and public transportation.
One exhibition planner stated, “Transparent displays offer a groundbreaking solution to seamlessly blend content with the environment, making them highly versatile for various applications.”

CIT’s booth became a hub for representatives from global automakers, smart building developers, and public transport operators eager to experience the Dolphin antenna and transparent displays firsthand. According to CIT, the strong reception reflects the market’s appreciation for their innovative, sustainable solutions.
CIT CEO Seung Jeong commented, “Dolphin is just the beginning. With technologies like transparent and stretchable displays, CIT aims to be at the forefront of global innovation.”

51827.cap: Prototypes featuring CIT’s ultra-thin copper circuit technology on display at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

51827.x: Founded in 2023, CIT has achieved remarkable milestones within two years, including winning the CES Innovation Award, the FLY ASIA 2024 Advanced Manufacturing Award, and a gold medal at the Seoul International Invention Fair.

Focusing on transparent antennas and display technology, CIT is accelerating commercialization through partnerships with global companies and establishing itself as a leader in next-generation communication and electronic substrate materials.

CIT’s technologies showcased at CES 2025 demonstrate applications across automotive and smart urban infrastructure industries, revealing new possibilities for futuristic communication and electronic material technologies.

51828.cap: SOLVIT System's booth at CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

51828.x: SOLVIT System (CEO Yeong-Goo Kim) is making waves at CES 2025 with its award-winning intelligent search and rescue system, SOLVIT-iSAR. Recognized with a CES 2025 Innovation Award in the Smart City category, this groundbreaking solution addresses the challenges of locating individuals in communication dead zones, attracting global buyers and visitors alike.

SOLVIT-iSAR combines radio wave analysis with intelligent reasoning to detect missing persons in areas without conventional communication signals. By reducing search zones by up to 1/25 and automating manual data analysis processes that typically take over three hours to just 10 minutes, the technology offers a transformative approach to securing the golden hour in rescue operations.

The system uses communication records and time-diffusion models to predict precise search locations, leveraging radio data to reflect the movement patterns of those in distress. This approach significantly enhances accuracy, paving the way for efficient rescue missions in rural, mountainous, and low-signal environments and mobile device battery depletion cases.

51828.cap: Live demonstration of the SOLVIT-iSAR system in action | Photo by AVING News

51828.x: The CES booth provided live demonstrations of SOLVIT-iSAR’s capabilities, showcasing how the system identifies a person’s last known signal and pinpoints their location even in signal-dead zones. The compelling demos resonated strongly with global buyers, with one stating, “SOLVIT System’s technology offers a realistic and innovative solution to a critical problem. If adopted globally, this could save countless lives.”

Additionally, SOLVIT System showcased how the technology adapts to specific scenarios, including weak signal areas in rural regions, mountain rescue operations, and emergency response in remote environments. This versatility has sparked interest from emergency response organizations in the U.S., Europe, South America, and Africa.

51828.cap: SOLVIT System booth at CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

51828.x: SOLVIT-iSAR's innovation was further validated by its CES Innovation Award in the Smart City category. CEO Yeong-Goo Kim remarked, “We are honored to have our solution recognized globally for addressing rescue blind spots in communication dead zones. This exhibition marks a significant step in showcasing our technology and fostering collaborations with global institutions to advance regulatory and technological support.”

Kim expressed gratitude to local fire and police departments for their support during the system’s development and the Korea Communications Agency (KCA) for providing access to radio resource information. “We look forward to meeting more partners at CES and setting new standards in the global rescue market,” he added.

51829.cap: Spaid CEO Chongkul Yi (far right) poses with his team at the Spaid booth at CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

51829.x: Spaid (CEO Chongkul Yi) captured global attention at CES 2025 in Las Vegas. The company unveiled its award-winning image-based 3D geospatial metaverse solution, AI2RE (AI to Reality Engine), alongside its upcoming OpenAI-powered geospatial information platform, setting a new benchmark in geospatial AI innovation.

Spaid's AI2RE leverages a proprietary AI engine to extract 2D vector data from aerial imagery and transform it into 3D models of terrains, buildings, roads, and more. This solution addresses data loss and compatibility issues in traditional 3D cadastral map production, automating over 80% of the process and enabling swift, lossless data output. With applications spanning digital twin operations for smart cities, defense simulations, and real estate value analysis, AI2RE has become an essential tool for governments and corporations. Visitors to CES experienced a one-click demo showcasing object detection, 2D line extraction, and 3D model generation, which garnered enthusiastic responses.

51829.cap: AI2RE Geospatial AI Solution │Provided by Spaid

51829.x: Spaid also debuted its OpenAI-based geospatial information platform at the exhibition. This platform uses OpenAI agents to recommend customized geospatial data cards, which users can drag and drop to visualize and analyze on a 3D map viewer. By eliminating the need for complex software or tools, this intuitive solution significantly simplifies the use of geospatial data. At the CES booth, attendees explored a demo featuring 3D-visualized geospatial data cards from San Francisco, showcasing Spaid’s technological prowess.

Spaid has already demonstrated the efficiency of AI2RE in the European Union’s data management and utilization strategy project, reducing the time needed for cadastral map production from six months to just five days. The company is also in discussions for collaborations in South America and Africa, rapidly expanding its influence in the global market.

CEO Chongkul Yi expressed pride in Spaid’s innovation being recognized through the CES Innovation Award, stating, “This exhibition is an opportunity to showcase the excellence of our geospatial AI and metaverse solutions and accelerate our entry into global markets.”

51829.cap: Spaid CEO Chongkul Yi consulting with visitors | Photo by AVING News

51829.x: Spaid connects physical and digital environments through data, driving innovation across smart cities, defense, finance, and telecommunications industries. With its CES 2025 presence, the company is setting a groundbreaking new standard for digital twins and geospatial AI.

51830.cap: WiseJet CEO Chul Soon Park (center) poses with staff at the company’s exclusive CES 2025 booth. | Photo by AVING News

51830.x: WiseJet Co., Ltd. (CEO Chul Soon Park) captured the spotlight at CES 2025 from January 7–10 in Las Vegas. With a bold vision of replacing all electronic cables with wireless technology, the company unveiled its groundbreaking innovations at a dedicated booth in the Las Vegas Convention Center’s South Hall 3.

WiseJet’s centerpiece innovation, the Wireless CMOS Solution, is based on 60GHz high-speed wireless communication technology, pushing the boundaries of ultra-fast, high-definition data transmission. The XR-JET chip leads the showcase, capable of transmitting 8K/60Hz ultra-high-definition video over a 10-meter range with latency below 1 millisecond. Supporting data speeds of 10Gbps per lane, the chip has the potential to replace traditional cables in ultra-slim TVs, AR/VR, robotics, and medical devices.

CEO Chul Soon Park emphasized the company’s ambition: "We aim to remove all cables from electronic devices.” He highlighted WiseJet’s capabilities: "Our technology surpasses existing wireless standards like Wi-Fi, minimizing data loss and latency through uncompressed transmission.”

WiseJet’s booth has been a hub of activity, drawing visitors eager to witness its 8K/60Hz video transmission demos and proximity-based wireless data and power transfer solutions. The company’s beamforming technology, which enables data to bypass obstacles seamlessly, has particularly wowed audiences, demonstrating how it eliminates the need for HDMI and USB connectors in ultra-slim TVs.

51830.cap: A variety of chips showcased at WiseJet’s CES 2025 booth | Photo by AVING News

51830.x: In addition to long-range wireless solutions, WiseJet introduced its short-distance connectors, capable of working from 1mm to several centimeters. These connectors support various applications, from displays and VR/AR devices to camera inspection equipment, offering the industry a full-package wireless solution.

The company’s high-speed, high-definition data transfer solutions are poised to play a pivotal role in sectors like robotics, autonomous vehicles, medical devices, and digital signage. “WiseJet technology is perfectly aligned to meet the demands of the rapidly growing high-speed wireless communication market,” said Park.

Currently, WiseJet is collaborating with domestic and international clients on proof-of-concept (PoC) projects, solidifying its technological credentials. At CES 2025, visitors will experience firsthand how the company is reshaping the future of electronics with its cable-free innovations.
The industry eagerly anticipates WiseJet’s solutions' transformative impact, and CES 2025 will serve as a launchpad for its vision of a cable-free world.

51832.cap: Stella Lee, International Sales Team Staff at Aram Huvis, holding AI-ScalpGrader | Photo by AVING News

51832.x: CES 2025, the world’s largest tech exhibition, concluded successfully, drawing global attention to innovative technologies from companies worldwide. Among the participants, Korea’s Pangyo Techno Valley once again made a notable mark on the worldwide stage. Startups based in Pangyo showcased cutting-edge advancements in AI, smart healthcare, and eco-friendly technologies, captivating visitors and investors.

Leveraging the unique strengths of the Pangyo region, where the government and private sectors collaborate to foster an innovation ecosystem, the achievements displayed at CES 2025 highlight the Region’s growing status as a global innovation hub.

Aram Huvis (CEO Park Dongsoon) is a leader in K-beauty and K-healthcare innovation, using AI-based scalp diagnostic systems and personalized cosmetic manufacturing technologies to impact the global market significantly.

The company’s flagship product, AI-ScalpGrader, employs high-resolution cameras and AI algorithms to conduct detailed scalp analyses. This system examines six scalp areas, identifying micro-flaking, excess sebum, dandruff, and redness. Results are provided within 10 to 40 seconds, allowing customers to view real-time scalp conditions on display and receive recommendations for customized cosmetics tailored to their specific needs.

Aram Huvis excels at creating personalized cosmetics that reflect individual skin and scalp characteristics. To overcome the limitations of mass-produced products, the company offers data-driven, customized solutions that significantly improve customer satisfaction and scalp health. In 2021, Aram Huvis secured a Korean patent (10-2271558) for its big data-powered AI scalp diagnostic and product recommendation system.

In collaboration with Bundang Seoul National University Hospital, Aram Huvis conducted clinical trials to validate the efficacy of its customized scalp care products. Among 100 participants, 93% reported improved scalp conditions, with average scores increasing by more than 50% within four weeks. These results have established the company as a trailblazer in the global K-beauty market.

Founded in 2002, Aram Huvis has pioneered the skin, hair, and scalp diagnostic industry for over 23 years. In 2023, the company’s AISG (AI Scalp Grader) won an innovation award at CES, affirming the groundbreaking nature of its AI-driven scalp diagnostic technology. Building on this success, Aram Huvis introduced the ECE CUBE, a portable B2C diagnostic device, and the Elapiel Tailor, a home-use machine capable of manufacturing personalized cosmetics.

51832.cap: Aram Huvis booth at CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

51832.x: Aram Huvis exports diagnostic devices to over 70 countries, with approximately 80% of its revenue generated internationally. It collaborates with renowned global brands such as Estée Lauder, L'Oréal, Aveda, Guerlain, L'Occitane, and Caudalie. Over the past two decades, the company has collected and analyzed over 100,000 scalp data points to accurately diagnose conditions using AI and provide customized shampoos and serums to customers worldwide. Aram Huvis strives to enhance beauty and well-being globally by moving beyond diagnostics to deliver tailored solutions.

With its AI and big data integration, Aram Huvis sets new standards for personalized scalp care and cosmetic manufacturing. Through continuous technological development and an expanding global network, the company is solidifying its position as a leader in K-beauty and K-healthcare.

Pangyo Techno Valley is a global integrated R&D hub focused on IT, BT, CT, and NT, integrating Research (R), People (P), Information (I), and Trade (T). As Gyeonggi-do’s representative innovation cluster, Pangyo Techno Valley was established to secure national new growth drivers such as technological innovation, human resource development, job creation, and enhancing international business competitiveness. As of 2023, 1,666 companies employ 78,751 people, and it has positioned itself as the most innovative hub in South Korea, with sales amounting to 167.7 trillion KRW (125.5 billion USD).

Furthermore, the Techno Valley Innovation Division of the Gyeonggi-do Business & Science Accelerator (GBSA) holds monthly events such as the Pangyo Evening Meet-Up, Pan-Pan Day, and the Pangyo Startup Investment Exchange “In-Best Pangyo” to maximize the value of Pangyo Techno Valley. They also support the Pangyo Overseas Promotion Program, which publicizes information about Pangyo’s companies, products, and services to domestic and foreign investors and the media, thereby facilitating foreign investment.

51833.x: MTSCompany Co., Ltd. (CEO Heewon Chung) participated in CES Unveiled, a pre-CES 2025 event held on January 5th (local time) in the United States. This expertise has allowed the company to expand its influence in the domestic business messaging industry while exploring applications of its technology in new fields.

The platform analyzes cells and tissue captured in pathology images with AI technology, identifying biomarkers for cancer diagnosis. AI-ALPA predicts lymph node metastasis and genetic test results by integrating pathology image data with clinical information, offering unique diagnostic capabilities.
AI-ALPA automates complex pathology processes while delivering over 90% accuracy, enabling precise and timely diagnoses and supporting efficient treatment planning.

51833.cap: Jangwon Seo, team lead at MTSCompany, introduces AI-ALPA at CES 2025 Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

51836.cap: Apollon showcased the ultra-compact, non-invasive continuous glucose monitor "MOGLU" at CES 2025 Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

51836.x: Apollon (CEO Hong Aram) participated in CES 2025 Unveiled, a global media event held on January 5th (local time) before the official opening of CES 2025.

Apollon develops needle-free continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) and holds proprietary technology for ultra-compact devices that use Raman spectroscopy signals to detect glucose in the body. Since its establishment in 2021, Apollon has filed and registered over 30 patents related to this field in South Korea and the United States.

Apollon has earned recognition for its technological innovation, winning awards such as the Minister of SMEs and Startups Award, TIPS Program Selection, LG Open Innovation Grand Prize, and the CES Innovation Award. In 2023, the company established a U.S. subsidiary in Cambridge, Massachusetts, to solidify its plans to enter the U.S. market, representing the largest CGM sector globally.

Apollon unveiled its noninvasive and ultracompact CGM, MOGLU, at CES 2025 Unveiled. This next-generation CGM combines advanced engineering with user-centric design. It eliminates the need for needles and sensor replacements and offers exceptional efficiency compared to traditional glucose monitors.

MOGLU employs Raman spectroscopy to focus on specific glucose signals, bypassing the conventional full-spectrum analysis approach. This eliminates the need for gratings, drastically reducing the device's size and enhancing user convenience.

The device also uses narrow-band filters placed in front of high-sensitivity photodiodes to transmit specific Raman signals selectively. This optimization of the optical path improves the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and maximizes energy efficiency.

51836.cap: | Overseas media representatives visiting Apollon's booth at CES 2025 Unveiled. | Photo by Aving News

51836.x: Unlike spectrometers using CMOS sensors, MOGLU employs multiple photodiodes to reduce dark noise at room temperature significantly. It eliminates unnecessary wavelengths and captures only desired signals for superior SNR performance.

In addition, MOGLU uses an 830nm laser to measure glucose levels in the body directly, meeting FDA standards. This approach demonstrates superior accuracy and safety compared to indirect measurement methods. The device causes no skin irritation, is smaller than a smartwatch, and features a form factor similar to existing CGMs, allowing users to transition seamlessly.

An Apollon representative highlighted, "MOGLU is designed to be worn on the wrist, arm, or other body parts, offering high usability. It does not require sensor replacements, significantly reducing waste and maintenance inconveniences. Moreover, its low power consumption ensures stable daily performance and real-time data is transmitted to a mobile app, enabling effective glucose management without disrupting daily life."

The representative added, "Apollon plans to expand beyond the domestic market into the U.S. with innovative products like MOGLU. To this end, we will actively engage with domestic and international investors during CES. We are thrilled to have received significant attention from global media at the event, especially as a CES Innovation Award winner in digital health alongside leading brands like Abbott and Dexcom."

51844.cap: Sunghun Yu, CEO of Deep-fusion AI, presented the company's 4D imaging radar solution to AVING News reporter Alex Sigrist at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

51844.x: Deep-fusion AI Inc., led by CEO Sunghun Yu, participated in CES 2025, held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, under the Incheon IFEZ Pavilion. The company aims to revolutionize autonomous driving by offering cost-effective 4D imaging radar solutions as alternatives to expensive LiDAR systems. It has developed applications such as 360-degree deep learning and HD maps, integrating them into proprietary controllers offered as complete solutions. The innovative approach to 4D imaging radar deep learning has been demonstrated on vehicles from multiple global automakers.

At CES 2025, Deep-fusion AI showcased its flagship 360-degree deep learning for 4D imaging radar. Unlike optical sensors like cameras or LiDAR, radar-based sensors lack standardized datasets for deep learning. To address this, the company created pre-training models by simulating 4D imaging radar in virtual environments tailored to various manufacturers’ specifications. This approach allows radar manufacturers to meet performance benchmarks and enables automakers to adopt tailored solutions for specific vehicle models upon product release.

The innovative platform developed by Deep-fusion AI enables automakers to select 4D imaging radar solutions based on mounting location, cost, and intended use. A representative from the company highlighted the company’s goal of fostering collaborative projects with radar and automotive manufacturers. The company showcased real-time robot deep-learning recognition and spatial mapping using 4D imaging radar. The demonstration emphasized its potential as a cost-effective alternative to LiDAR solutions.

Deep-fusion AI plans to launch a series of advanced solutions in 2025. These include a 4D imaging radar controller equipped with recognition functions for vehicle autonomous driving and auto valet parking, a radar controller with recognition capabilities for autonomous maritime navigation and docking systems, and a comprehensive sensor module combining multiple 4D imaging radars and cameras for autonomous navigation.

Deep-fusion AI’s participation in CES 2025 highlights its commitment to driving autonomous and robotics innovation. The company aims to expand its influence by delivering high-performance solutions tailored to global market demands.

With its slogan, “Going Green with Robotics,” the company is committed to delivering innovative technologies that ensure a cleaner environment for present and future generations.

At CES 2025, Sheco introduced its flagship product, the "Sheco Ark-M." With a collection capacity of 30,000 liters per hour and a remote control range of up to 1 km, the Sheco Ark-M stands out for its efficiency and user-friendly design.

DEEP IN SIGHT Presents Next-Generation Mobility Solution ‘Camosys’ at CES 2025
DEEP IN SIGHT Co., Ltd. (CEO Eunsong Lucas Oh) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10, to showcase its in-cabin monitoring system, ‘Camosys.’

Founded in June 2020, DEEP IN SIGHT specializes in AI-driven 3D camera solutions, combining advanced sensing technology with AI. The company’s offerings cater to key industries of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, including mobility, proptech, medical devices, smart construction, and smart logistics. Its flagship solutions include the in-cabin monitoring system ‘Camosys’ and the portable 3D spatial scanner ‘DIMENVUE Pro.’

It efficiently generates the high-density point cloud data (PCD) required for 3D modeling, reducing time and costs in architecture, civil engineering, and construction projects. Experts enthusiastically responded to the scanner.

51860.cap: ILias AI’s Digital Sniffer Dog was showcased at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

51860.x: ILias AI Co., Ltd. (CEO Ko Bumsuk) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the Incheon IFEZ Pavilion. Since its founding in 2022, it has aimed to commercialize olfactory-based products and service platforms across various industries.

At CES 2025, ILias AI introduced its flagship product, the Digital Sniffer Dog, designed for use in airports and seaports. This innovative scanner captures and analyzes odors from passengers and luggage to detect illegal drugs. Using a multi-channel sensor array and AI-driven scent intelligence, the device mimics human olfactory receptors to identify specific airborne odors.

The embedded AI system leverages pre-trained drug scent data for accurate and reliable detections. Unlike traditional visual, chemical, or physical drug detection methods, the Digital Sniffer Dog digitizes odors and processes multidimensional data for precision. This reduces the discomfort associated with physical inspections, provides rapid screenings, and enables the detection of new and evolving drug types through continuous deep-learning updates.

51860.cap: ILias AI’s Director Mark Junggook Seo (left) explaining the Digital Sniffer Dog to AVING News reporter Alex Sigrist at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

ILias AI emphasized, “Our Digital Sniffer Dog revolutionizes traditional drug detection methods, offering exceptional value in large-scale security environments like airports and seaports. The AI-driven olfactory technology ensures fast and accurate detection, enhancing operational efficiency and security reliability.”

The company further explained its strategic goals: “Participating in CES 2025 allows us to demonstrate our advanced technology globally, particularly as we aim to establish a U.S. branch by mid-2025. 51861.cap: UNIUNI’s SAVVY Accessible Restroom display at CES 2025. The solution earned the company the CES 2025 Smart City Innovation Award. | Photo by AVING News

51861.x: UNIUNI Corp. (CEO Sooyeon Han) participated in CES 2025, held from January 7 to 10 (local time) in Las Vegas, as part of the Incheon IFEZ Pavilion. The company focuses on integrating safety and privacy into human-centric technology solutions to create inclusive and empowering spaces for all.

The company’s name, UNIUNI, reflects its mission of fostering a shared, inclusive environment. UNIUNI combines advanced technology and a human-centered approach to use non-identifiable data, enabling individuals, particularly those with disabilities, to maintain dignity, improve safety, and enhance independence. Their solutions also optimize facility management through real-time analytics, transforming public and private spaces into trusted environments.

At CES 2025, UNIUNI introduced the SAVVY Accessible Restroom, a deep-learning solution designed to ensure the safety and privacy of restroom users with disabilities. The system detects abnormal movements, such as falls, dizziness, or unusual posture changes, and promptly notifies caregivers or facility managers via phone, alerts, or automated alarm systems.

A standout feature of the system is its use of non-identifiable depth data, focusing on movement rather than personal details to preserve privacy. Operating continuously, the system employs advanced deep-learning algorithms to monitor behavioral patterns and respond in real time, ensuring quick intervention during emergencies.

The SAVVY Accessible Restroom’s design aligns with UNIUNI’s vision of providing safe, private, accessible public restrooms. Using non-identifiable Time-of-Flight (ToF) data, the engineering team created a product that detects irregular movements within restrooms without compromising users’ dignity. The solution addresses the need for real-time monitoring and support, particularly for individuals with physical disabilities.

51861.cap: UNIUNI's representative discusses the SAVVY Accessible Restroom with AVING News reporter Alex Sigrist. | Photo by AVING News

51861.x: UNIUNI reported that rigorous testing has resulted in the solution achieving outstanding performance metrics, including 97.2% precision, 98.84% recall, and a 98.01% F1 score. Designed with scalability in mind, the SAVVY Accessible Restroom aims to enhance safety and accessibility in public restrooms globally. It embodies UNIUNI’s commitment to improving the lives of individuals with disabilities by anticipating their needs, fostering independence, and ensuring privacy and safety across public spaces.

Recognized for its innovative approach, UNIUNI received the CES 2025 Smart City Innovation Award. The company attributed this achievement to its team’s dedication and partners’ support. UNIUNI emphasized its vision of building a future that advances smart city technologies and inclusively addresses the needs of socially and physically disadvantaged individuals.

CEO Sooyeon Han stated, “Our goal at UNIUNI is to use technology to provide safety and convenience in all spaces. We aim to establish ourselves as a global leader in technological solutions for vulnerable populations.”

LITBIG Showcases Future Mobility with QuadEYE, Drawing Attention with 3D Surround Recording Technology

LITBIG Inc. (CEO Peter Lee) showcased its advanced driver-assistance system (ADAS) product QuadEYE at CES 2025, innovatively combining safety and entertainment for drivers and passengers. The system integrates three key technologies: Surround View Monitor (SVM), 3D Recorder (Drive Video Recording System), and Moving Object Detection (MOD), making it the world's first to offer full 3D recording functionality. This lets users capture accident scenes or scenic drives in real-time 3D and replay them from any angle, ensuring safety and enhancing enjoyment.

LITBIG is a leader in embedded system development that combines AI and camera vision technology. The company offers solutions such as 3D SVM, DVR, Driver Monitoring System (DMS), MOD, and smart in-vehicle infotainment (IVI) systems. These advanced technologies aim to enhance safety and convenience, embodying a vision for the future of mobility.

A LITBIG representative emphasized, “QuadEYE is more than just a technology—it is a comprehensive solution offering both safety and enjoyment to drivers. By implementing next-generation mobility, we aim to create safer and more convenient driving environments for users worldwide.”

QuadEYE uses four cameras mounted on the vehicle’s front, rear, and sides to provide a 360-degree 3D surround view. This intuitive system enhances driver awareness, particularly during parking or navigating tight spaces, significantly boosting safety.

Its motion object detection (MOD) function alerts drivers with visual red boxes and audible warnings when nearby objects or pedestrians are detected. Using AI-based image recognition, the system distinguishes between people, vehicles, and other objects, offering unparalleled precision compared to traditional sensors.

QuadEYE’s 3D recording functionality addresses the limitations of traditional dashcams, which only record front and rear views. By capturing 360-degree footage in real-time, the system offers a comprehensive view of the vehicle's surroundings, ensuring critical details are recorded during an incident.

Designed for seamless integration, QuadEYE can be easily installed into existing vehicle systems. Its hardware, including cameras and control boxes, is available for aftermarket and dealer installation. The plug-and-play design enhances installation convenience and fosters collaboration with retailers, distributors, and automakers.

At CES 2025, LITBIG forged partnerships across the mobility industry, aiming to expand into global markets. CEO Peter Lee highlighted the technology’s utility, particularly in regions with high freight traffic like North America. He noted, “QuadEYE addresses the challenge of limited situational awareness for drivers. Using CES 2025 as a launchpad, we aim to set a new standard for mobility safety globally and continue driving innovation.”

Pangyo Techno Valley is a global integrated R&D hub focused on IT, BT, CT, and NT, integrating Research (R), People (P), Information (I), and Trade (T). As Gyeonggi-do’s representative innovation cluster, Pangyo Techno Valley was established to secure national new growth drivers such as technological innovation, human resource development, job creation, and enhancing international business competitiveness. As of 2023, 1,666 companies employ 78,751 people, and it has positioned itself as the most innovative hub in South Korea, with sales amounting to 167.7 trillion KRW (125.5 billion USD).

Furthermore, the Techno Valley Innovation Division of the Gyeonggi-do Business & Science Accelerator (GBSA) holds monthly events such as the Pangyo Evening Meet-Up, Pan-Pan Day, and the Pangyo Startup Investment Exchange “In-Best Pangyo” to maximize the value of Pangyo Techno Valley. They also support the Pangyo Overseas Promotion Program, which publicizes information about Pangyo’s companies, products, and services to domestic and foreign investors and the media, thereby facilitating foreign investment.

Practical assistance, such as booth rentals, translation services, and logistics, was also offered to enhance their presence.
SungHo ATEC Showcases AI-Based EVE System for Full Automation in Agriculture

SungHo ATEC Agricultural Corporation, led by CEO Park Sung Ho, is at the forefront of smart farming and AgTech, incorporating AI into agricultural processes. Based in the Gimje Smart Farm Innovation Valley, the company grows strawberries, melons, and tomatoes while continuously collecting real-world data to advance its technologies. SungHo ATEC has also successfully implemented vertical farming modules to mass-produce lion's mane mushrooms and cultivate leafy greens indoors. These practical experiences and data serve as a foundation for advancing agricultural technologies.

The company’s flagship product, the EVE System, automates agricultural management. The system uses advanced sensors and cameras to analyze crop growth in real time and features modular designs tailored to diverse customer needs. With a single charge, the EVE System can operate for over five hours and harvest up to 180kg of fully ripe tomatoes per hour, demonstrating exceptional efficiency.

The EVE System employs phenomics analysis to detect interactions between crop genetics and environmental factors, enabling real-time data analysis to inform operational decisions. It identifies growth inhibitors such as pests, runners, and side shoots while determining optimal harvest timing with precision. Additionally, the system integrates with environmental control systems and weather data to automate nutrient supply and farm management processes. All data is stored on a cloud server, accessible through a farm note format, allowing users to manage farms efficiently from anywhere.

What sets the EVE System apart is its AI-driven decision-making capabilities. The system acquires detailed growth information by mapping labeled data with depth values and automatically manages pest control and harvest timing. This ensures optimal growing conditions, supports the production of high-quality crops, and significantly improves automation, efficiency, and productivity.

SungHo ATEC focuses on providing solutions to farmers to enhance productivity and reduce operational costs. The company also offers automated harvesting robots to distributors, enabling them to optimize efficiency and scalability. Government agencies managing high-value crops are another key focus, with the company proposing precision agriculture solutions to support their initiatives.

Climate change and geopolitical factors drive food security concerns, and global demand for agricultural automation technologies is rising. SungHo ATEC plans to enter overseas markets, targeting countries with large farming areas. The company aims to establish partnerships and secure buyers through advanced growth analysis, environmental control, and robotics technologies.

In November 2024, SungHo ATEC demonstrated its technological prowess at the Agricultural Machinery Expo in Daegu. The event attracted significant interest from high-ranking officials, including South Korea’s Deputy Prime Minister and several government ministers. Following the expo, the EVE Clever was displayed at the National Agricultural Museum, marking the first time an agricultural robot was showcased in a South Korean museum.
By integrating AI with agriculture, SungHo ATEC is setting new benchmarks for automation and solidifying its position as a globally recognized leader in AgTech.

The company recently received a 300-million-won seed investment through the Korea Technology Finance Corporation, highlighting its potential.

The award-winning product Self-Insight Therapy (SITh) offers psychological counseling services using XR (Extended Reality), AI (Artificial Intelligence), and VH (Virtual Humans). This cutting-edge solution immerses users in realistic environments where their behaviors and emotions are tracked, providing a unique method for psychological diagnosis and therapy.

These programs aim to enhance character education for elementary and middle school students while helping local youth counseling centers assess and foster positive future thinking among adolescents.

51867.cap: MOVIC Lab's machine failure prediction solution 'WatchBAT,' showcased at CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

51867.x: MOVIC Lab Inc. (CEO Lee Wonkeun) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

MOVIC Lab specializes in smart factory solutions based on AI technology. Its flagship service is an AI-based facility fault detection solution that excels in time-series data analysis for various industrial signals, including current, voltage, vibration, temperature, and humidity, combined with high-performance deep learning algorithms.

The company emphasized the importance of early fault detection in manufacturing, stating, "Manufacturing relies heavily on equipment, and failures lead to significant economic losses. Detecting early signs of failure and performing predictive maintenance before breakdowns occur is crucial. However, conventional methods have limitations." MOVIC Lab aims to overcome these limitations by leveraging ultrasonic and AI technologies to improve manufacturing environments and set a new standard for facility management.

The 'WatchBAT' solution, presented at CES 2025, predicts machine failures using ultrasonic data and AI. Ultrasonic data refers to sounds emitted by machines in the ultrasonic frequency range (above 20 kHz), which humans cannot hear. These signals occur before visible signs like vibration, heat, or noise, enabling the detection of subtle changes in manufacturing equipment.

The company explained that ultrasonic sensors are non-contact, making them more versatile than traditional contact sensors. They also quantify equipment conditions, allowing easy and intuitive assessment on-site.

51867.cap: Alex Sigrist, AVING News reporter, interviews Lee Wonkeun, CEO of MOVIC Lab | Photo by AVING News

51867.x: Regarding their participation in CES, a MOVIC Lab representative said, "In Korea, MOVIC Lab is the only company utilizing ultrasonic and AI technology to predict equipment failures, and we've confirmed strong interest from major clients. This being our first CES, we aim to showcase our products (WatchBAT and WatchBAT KIT) and technological expertise in the U.S., a leader in advanced technology, while gauging market responses. Conducting market research for U.S. entry was another reason for our participation. In October, we secured a U.S. patent and plan to identify collaborators and partners to prepare for entry into the U.S. market."

MOVIC Lab targets manufacturers and equipment makers in high-tech industries such as semiconductors, secondary batteries, and displays. Its focus includes local U.S. companies and Korean corporations operating in the U.S. During CES, the company demonstrated its ultrasonic diagnostic solution, explaining the principles of ultrasonic generation and showcasing the differences between audible and ultrasonic sounds.

The representative added, "We are finalizing PoC verification with major Korean companies on mass production lines, and visible revenue is expected next year. We are expanding the range of verified equipment, including pumps, blades, motors, bearings, and actuators. Based on proven domestic references, we plan to collaborate with local companies to enter overseas markets. The U.S., with its well-established cloud infrastructure, is a key market for us. After verifying our solutions on key equipment in the U.S., we aim to offer them as cloud-based SaaS. Additionally, we are working on simplifying our solution to operate via connected ultrasonic sensors on tablets."

Ultrasonic technology extends beyond manufacturing equipment to electrical fault detection and fire prevention applications. Recognizing its vast potential, MOVIC Lab plans to enhance its technology further and expand into safety and fire detection markets.

51868.cap: The SpeedFloor booth at CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

51868.x: SpeedFloor Co., Ltd. (CEO Hyunjin Hong, Austin Hong) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

SpeedFloor, which provides fully automated logistics solutions, introduced its automated loading and unloading system. This system is designed to enhance operational efficiency at logistics sites while reducing the physical burden on workers. The company emphasized that its efforts extend beyond device development and supply, aiming to achieve full automation by integrating with automated logistics centers.

The automated system has garnered demand from government entities such as Korea's Ministry of National Defense and Incheon Metropolitan City and private companies like Kurly. A SpeedFloor representative stated, "Our solution has been validated to reduce labor loads for logistics workers, ranging from soldiers to delivery drivers. Transport companies have also reported increased profits due to shortened turnaround times. Based on this data, we are planning to expand internationally."

Participating in CES 2025, SpeedFloor sought to identify the specific needs of global businesses and government agencies in preparation for its overseas expansion. The company also aimed to build partnerships and explore new business opportunities through networking with venture capitalists, logistics companies, and tech firms.

The automated loading and unloading system showcased at CES 2025 allows users to move cargo forward and backward inside a truck's cargo space without physically entering it. This is achieved using a conveyor belt-like device operated via simple button controls. The system, which combines chain and belt structures, is supported by 17 patent applications. The integrated chain-belt conveyor and moving partition plate enable seamless transportation of irregularly shaped cargo, including bulk goods, without malfunctions.

51868.cap: SpeedFloor introduces its solution to Alex Sigrist, AVING News reporter | Photo by AVING News

51868.x: This innovative technology has already led to significant achievements, including an initial purchase of one unit by Korea's Ministry of National Defense and an additional 18 units. The representative explained, "Loading and unloading heavy military supplies traditionally requires many personnel, and the risk of injury is high. The Ministry adopted our product to offset reduced manpower and alleviate the workload of soldiers." Furthermore, 17 units have been deployed in Incheon Metropolitan City's logistics digitization project.

SpeedFloor expressed its ambition to realize fully automated logistics. In logistics centers, cargo typically moves through three stages: unloading from large transport vehicles, sorting, and reloading onto smaller delivery vehicles. Currently, all these stages require human intervention. The company emphasized that integrating its solution into warehouses would minimize labor requirements, saving time and costs.

A representative stated, "When large transport vehicles arrive at logistics centers, cargo can be unloaded automatically, sorted using our ongoing research into an automated sorting system, and reloaded onto delivery vehicles without manual intervention. This process will enable fully automated logistics centers. Furthermore, we plan to expand automation by integrating autonomous driving technologies." They concluded, "As logistics demand continues to grow, SpeedFloor's solution is positioned to respond efficiently."

51870.cap: Gbrain's booth at CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

51870.x: Gbrain (Co-CEOs Sunggu Yang and Byoung Kim) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

As a pioneering company in the Korean neurotechnology market, Gbrain leads advancements in brain-computer interface (BCI) medical solutions. It is the first in Korea to commercialize invasive electrodes and holds unparalleled expertise in designing and manufacturing flexible, noninvasive thin-film electrodes for high-resolution brainwave acquisition. According to company representatives, these electrodes are designed to attach to the brain cortex, minimizing tissue damage and adapting seamlessly to the brain's curvature. They enable stable and efficient acquisition of high-quality brainwave data.

Gbrain’s innovative technologies are opening new possibilities in neuroscience and medicine, garnering attention in global markets. Notably, Gbrain’s excellence was recognized as an Honoree in the Digital Health category of the highly competitive CES Innovation Awards.

At CES 2025, Gbrain introduced Phin Stim, a cortical monitoring and stimulation implant system that provides a groundbreaking treatment option for patients with intractable brain diseases, such as Parkinson's and epilepsy. This solution offers an alternative to traditional drug therapies or surgical treatments.

51870.cap: Alex Sigrist, AVING News reporter, interviews Sunggu Yang, Co-CEO of Gbrain | Photo by AVING News

51870.x: A Gbrain representative explained, "Current treatments for intractable brain diseases typically involve deeply invasive electrode therapies or cortical monitoring/stimulation techniques that require a seven-day hospital stay with direct connection of brain electrodes to computers via wires, significantly limiting mobility. Gbrain’s Phin Stim overcomes these challenges by minimizing brain tissue invasion and employing wireless communication technology, making it the first domestic attempt to commercialize this innovative approach."

The representative further noted, "Led by Sunggu Yang, a professor of Nano-Bioengineering at Incheon University, and Byoung Kim, a former executive at Celltrion, Gbrain’s board includes electronics, neuro-engineering, and materials science experts. Together, they are advancing interdisciplinary and integrative BCI technology solutions."

Gbrain also shared its plans. In the short term, the company aims to solidify its position as Korea’s first to develop minimally invasive electrode solutions for treating intractable brain diseases. In the medium and long term, it plans to integrate IoT and AI technologies to enable brainwave-based control and communication with surrounding objects, pushing the boundaries of BCI technology.

51871.cap: IDCITI's booth at CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

51871.x: IDCITI Co., Ltd. (CEO Jihoon Ryoo) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

IDCITI is a pioneer in providing precise indoor positioning solutions. Its innovative uGPS (underground GPS) technology is designed to address the challenges of GPS signal blackouts in shadowed areas.

A company representative explained, "Indoor positioning information is crucial in various scenarios, including traffic information systems, large facility operations, and emergencies. However, GPS signals are unavailable in underground or indoor environments. GPS, a proprietary technology of IDCITI, is significantly more robust than traditional GPS repeaters and delivers uninterrupted signals in real-time, even to fast-moving vehicles and indoor or underground locations."
The uGPS system is tailored to the needs of diverse industries and offers a fundamental solution to indoor positioning challenges.

At CES 2025, IDCITI highlighted the unique advantages of its technology, capturing the attention of global visitors. The company emphasized the versatility and scalability of its satellite software system. Users can employ the solution with existing GPS receivers without requiring additional hardware or software installations. The system is suitable for worldwide applications and is built on global standard GNSS technology.

51871.cap: uGPS system diagram | Image by IDCITI

51871.x: The uGPS system also supports vehicles traveling at high speeds (up to 100 km/h), ensuring seamless GNSS signals between indoor and outdoor environments. It offers superior price competitiveness at just one-tenth the cost of overseas products. Additionally, it requires no preprocessing, is operational immediately after installation, and features low maintenance costs, enhancing user convenience.

IDCITI has already demonstrated its expertise in the "Technology Development and Verification Study to Resolve Satellite Positioning Blackouts on Highways" in 2023. The company installed its uGPS system in sections of the Seoul Ring Expressway, including the 1.8 km and 1.2 km segments of the Suri-Suam Tunnel (Ilsan-bound).

IDCITI's achievements include resolving satellite signal limitations in the uphill section of Namsan Tunnel 1, providing GPS services in the underground parking lot of Incheon Startup Park, and reducing bus arrival time errors at the Jamsil Bus Transfer Center from 600 seconds to just 14 seconds.
