51874.cap: AHN Materials' portable liquid hydrogen storage container on display at CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

51874.x: AHN Materials Inc. (CEO Ahn Hoseon) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

Founded in 2020, AHN Materials has been developing solutions to enhance the energy efficiency of eco-friendly mobility. The company was the first to introduce a triple-structure gaseous hydrogen storage cartridge, offering miniaturized, advanced solutions tailored to customer needs.
At CES 2025, AHN Materials showcased a portable liquid hydrogen storage container featuring a patented quadruple insulation structure and liquid nitrogen as a cooling medium.

Traditional liquid hydrogen storage tanks are typically large, suitable for use in plants or trailers, and require additional cooling systems, which limit portability and mobility. AHN Materials has overcome these limitations with its innovative technology, enabling compact and stable liquid hydrogen storage without additional cooling devices.

This technology utilizes liquid nitrogen as both a coolant and sacrificial layer. By leveraging the latent heat of vaporization from evaporating liquid nitrogen, the system minimizes heat transfer and achieves a daily nitrogen boil-off rate of just 8%.

51874.cap: Alex Sigrist, AVING News reporter, interviewing AHN Materials representatives | Photo by AVING News

51874.x: The storage container combines two double-vacuum chambers with dual coolant layers. Its design allows the chambers to be connected and secured via an upper cover, significantly improving the convenience of charging liquid nitrogen and liquid hydrogen.

With these technological advancements, the 5-liter model can store 354 grams of hydrogen, more than double that of similarly sized Type 4 gaseous hydrogen containers. Furthermore, it operates at a low pressure of 3 bar, offering enhanced safety during storage and transportation.

An AHN Materials representative stated, "Our innovative quadruple insulation technology enables the miniaturization of liquid hydrogen storage containers, expanding the usability of hydrogen energy and accelerating the development of next-generation energy sources. We gather feedback from potential global customers through CES to develop tailored solutions that meet their needs."

The representative added, "We aim to demonstrate the market potential of our technology to domestic and international investors, attract new investments, and identify strategic partners to collaborate with on our vision. Expanding our network on the global stage and exploring opportunities for international market entry will position us as a leading company in the hydrogen economy."

51875.x: AstroX Co., Ltd. (CEO Jeon Boohwan) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

AstroX specializes in developing high-capacity, long-range drones and personal air vehicles (PAVs), positioning itself as a leader in high-performance unmanned and manned aircraft technology. The company boasts engineering and manufacturing capabilities, collaborating with global partners to optimize components such as battery packs and control systems for producing fully integrated aircraft.

AstroX also leverages expertise in CFRP (carbon fiber-reinforced polymer) and aerospace composites, enabling rapid response from development to production. The company aims to commercialize safe and affordable air mobility solutions by applying aerospace certifications to its technologies, supporting reliable operations for all drone service providers.

AstroX’s core technologies include airframe design and structural analysis for optimized safety and performance. Its proprietary vacuum thermal molding and manufacturing techniques for aerospace CFRP composites enhance material lightweight and fuel efficiency. The company also offers advanced power management systems (BMS) for drones, ensuring stable power supply to propulsion systems and custom ground control systems (GCS) for user-specific operation needs.

51875.cap: Scale Model of AX-P80D | Photo by AstroX

51875.x: At CES 2025, AstroX showcased a scaled model of its high-capacity, long-range air vehicle and screened flight demonstration videos at its booth to highlight its technical capabilities.

The 'AX-P80D,' introduced at CES, features a BLDC motor electric propulsion system with an operational range of 10 km, a flight altitude of 150 meters, and a maximum takeoff weight of 200 kg. With a payload capacity exceeding 50 kg and a flight time of over 30 minutes, it is designed for diverse applications, including firefighting and logistics.

Key features include heat and body temperature management, video transmission capabilities, and specialized lifting mechanisms, such as a drone-specific vertical lift system based on existing ATV winches. The drone also supports modular attachments for firefighting, including a quick-release mechanism for fire suppression modules and a rapid-drop liquid dispersion system ('Bambi Bucket').

AstroX has also developed an amphibious PAV with domestic technology that can operate on land and water. This PAV is suitable for tourism, leisure, and sports, offering an expanded range of applications.

South Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, and Transport has certified the PAV for ultralight aircraft safety. It has been successfully tested in real environments, including the Han River, Gyeongin Ara Waterway, and Songdo.

51875.cap: AstroX demonstrates firefighting capabilities during ship fire scenarios | Photo by AstroX

51875.x: AstroX’s self-developed 100 kg payload PAV platform supports various models, including 30 kg and 50 kg payload options, addressing various market demands. With a 30-minute flight time and a 10 km delivery range, these solutions are optimized for island and port logistics.

AstroX’s firefighting drones are particularly notable for their amphibious capabilities. Equipped with a 60 kg fire suppression module, they excel in land and maritime fire suppression, including onboard ship fires. The company’s firefighting solutions have demonstrated outstanding performance and practicality in these challenging scenarios.

51876.x: 10km.ai (CEO Elton Kim) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time).

Specializing in AI-powered corporate video production platforms, 10km.ai automates the entire video production process, from creation to editing and distribution, while reflecting a company's brand identity. The company is the first in the generative AI field to be selected for Deep Tech TIPS (Tech Incubator Program for Startups).

The company's flagship solution, '10kM,' is a mobile app that transforms text-based documents into professional-grade videos within one minute. This solution automates document analysis, reference video identification, and template generation, reducing pre-production time from one day to just one minute. Its CSS animation-based HTML content also allows real-time editing of all video elements. Hybrid rendering technology between client and server enhances the efficiency of high-quality video production.
Protected by four registered patents and eight pending applications, 10kM makes professional video creation accessible to all.

At CES 2025, 10km.ai showcased its cutting-edge technology and earned an Innovation Award in the 'Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps' category. The company highlighted its patented document-to-video auto-generation system and AI-powered editing platform for the award. Key innovations include the Gen&Edit model, which integrates foundational models, and the Plug&Show engine, which leverages edge computing to reduce video production time from 72 hours to just 5 minutes.

The solution has been validated through partnerships with over 15 companies, including Samsung Life, KT, and CJ-ENM. Notable achievements include producing 20-language safety education videos for Samsung Heavy Industries and visualizing sales condition sheets for KT.

At CES 2025, 10km.ai also introduced ‘GemGem,’ a solution that generates real-time videos from text, handwritten notes, and uploaded images. The booth attracted numerous global corporate representatives who experienced the technology firsthand. This exposure led to technical validation, investment proposals, and new opportunities.

A 10km.ai representative stated, "We aim to use CES as a launchpad for accelerating global market entry. We will focus on expanding into key markets such as the United States, Japan, and China to set a new global AI video market standard.”

51879.x: CES 2025, the world’s largest IT and tech exhibition, concluded on January 10 (local time) in Las Vegas, USA. The event featured the largest-ever "Seoul Pavilion," which drew significant attention from global visitors.

This year's Seoul Pavilion, spanning 1,040 square meters, was set up at Eureka Park, CES’s startup exhibition zone. The pavilion showcased Seoul’s startup ecosystem and began with an opening ceremony on January 7 at 10 a.m. and continued for four days.

The pavilion was a collaborative effort among three Seoul districts (Gangnam, Gwanak, and Geumcheon), five startup support organizations (Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Tourism Organization, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul AI Hub, and Campus Town Growth Center), and eight major Seoul-based universities (Konkuk University, Kyung Hee University, Kookmin University, Sogang University, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Yonsei University, Chung-Ang University, and Seoul National University).

At the opening ceremony, representatives from 16 participating organizations and 104 companies, along with 103 supporters, declared their vision for "Team Seoul" and announced their ambitions to take on the global tech stage.

Under the slogan “Team Seoul, ON BOARD to Dive in!” Representatives from 16 organizations took the stage for a "boarding ceremony," and student supporters in the audience used “Green Aurora” glow sticks to mark the start of the Seoul Pavilion.

Representing one of Seoul’s major universities, Sogang University participated in the Seoul Pavilion with ten companies, including faculty-led startups recruited through the Industry-Academia Cooperation Foundation.

This marked the university’s third appearance at CES. Since establishing its Industry-Academia Cooperation Foundation in 2004, Sogang University has been actively supporting R&D-focused activities and fostering startups. Initially managing an external research fund of 10 billion KRW, the foundation has grown to handle over 60 billion KRW, bolstered by numerous large-scale research projects.

The foundation has also been advancing by actively establishing joint ventures with its tech holding company. This has allowed it to consolidate and expand the university’s infrastructure, creating a leading industry-academia collaboration model.

Sogang University’s foundation has been building a business-friendly industry-academia collaboration system, completing joint commercialization platforms, specializing in human resources, and nurturing seed-stage businesses in emerging industries. Using its CES 2025 participation as a springboard, it aims to accelerate the global expansion of promising startups and promote "K-technology" worldwide.

During CES 2025, Sogang University attracted multinational visitors and showcased its roadmap for corporate-driven economic growth in Seoul. AVING News interviewed Kwanwoo Shin to learn more about the university’s plans.

These 30 students actively introduced local businesses to visitors and facilitated smooth communication between corporate representatives, global media, potential customers, and partners.

51880.x: The Ministry of SMEs and Startups (MSS), led by Minister Youngju Oh, operated the "K-Startup Pavilion" at CES 2025, which took place in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10. The pavilion supported 127 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in creating global market opportunities.

The K-Startup Pavilion, located at Eureka Park, CES’s startup exhibition zone, was created in collaboration with 30 startup-supporting organizations, including public institutions, local governments, universities, and major corporations. It showcased 127 startups, a significant increase from the 91 startups and 26 institutions last year.

The pavilion’s scale and the qualitative growth of its participating companies resulted in 12 Innovation Awards at CES 2025. AI solution provider NationA achieved double honors in the Metaverse category for the second consecutive year, contributing significantly to the pavilion’s 13 awards.

Sierra BASE, GhostPass, and Suprema AI were recognized with Best of Innovation Awards for their groundbreaking technologies in smart cities, fintech, and embedded technology, respectively. These achievements drew significant attention from global industry players, academics, and media even before the event began.

MSS's impact on Korea’s startup ecosystem extended beyond the K-Startup Pavilion. Among the 458 Innovation Awards announced by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), 208 were awarded to 151 Korean companies, the highest number for any participating country. Of these, 127 were SMEs, with 86.6% receiving support through MSS initiatives such as R&D projects and venture capital investments.

KISED, established in 2009 as the nation’s only dedicated startup support agency, played a pivotal role in these accomplishments. Since 2020, KISED has facilitated the participation of 420 Korean startups at global exhibitions, helping them establish a presence in international markets and contribute to the worldwide startup ecosystem.

In 2022, KISED underwent a significant reorganization, establishing the Startup Korea Initiative to focus on globalizing Korea’s startup ecosystem. Debuting at CES 2025, the initiative actively supported the pavilion’s operations, collected feedback, and provided real-time solutions to participants. AVING News interviewed Changhyoung Lee, the initiative’s inaugural head, to discuss the journey of preparing the K-Startup Pavilion and plans for the future.

51880.cap: Changhyoung Lee, Head of the Startup Korea Initiative at KISED, is interviewed by AVING News at CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 (Tuesday) to 10 (Friday). | Photo by AVING News

51880.x: Q. AVING News: CES 2025 marked the largest K-Startup Pavilion ever. What are your thoughts on its success, and how would you summarize the atmosphere at this year’s event?

A. Changhyoung Lee: Managing the pavilion, from planning to on-site operations, has been an intense but rewarding experience. The energetic atmosphere at Eureka Park has been invigorating and helped offset the exhaustion.

As the gathering point for global startups, Eureka Park feels more dynamic than other CES venues, such as the Las Vegas Convention Center (LVCC). I believe the K-Startup Pavilion significantly contributed to this energy.

The pavilion featured 127 startups, making it a standout presence. Approximately 1,300 startups participated in Eureka Park, with 650 from Korea, so our pavilion’s scale and impact were unparalleled. This achievement was possible thanks to the collaboration of over 30 public and private organizations. Overcoming challenges such as obtaining CTA approvals and preparing participants was no small feat, but our problem-solving approach proved effective. I’m proud of our efforts and deeply grateful to all the organizations and companies involved.
Q. AVING News: KISED is a leading institution driving innovation in Korea’s startup ecosystem. How does it plan to navigate the challenges posed by the current global economic downturn?

A. Changhyoung Lee: The government recently introduced the "Startup Korea" comprehensive strategy, focusing on supporting outbound ventures. This approach emphasizes helping startups refine their products and technologies to meet the demands of specific markets.

KISED acts as a coordinator, connecting companies with potential partners in target countries, simplifying local validation processes, and facilitating collaborations. The government views globalization as a key strategy for overcoming economic challenges, making 2025 the inaugural year of K-Startup’s "Global Voyage." Our startups, equipped with advanced technologies and strong potential, are ready to spread their wings on the global stage.
KISED will adopt a proactive and efficient approach to support these initiatives. Starting with CES 2025, we aim to lay a solid foundation for broader global success.

51880.cap: Changhyoung Lee, Head of the Startup Korea Initiative at KISED, is interviewed by AVING News at CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 (Tuesday) to 10 (Friday). | Photo by AVING News

51880.x: Q. AVING News: The K-Startup Pavilion attracted significant attention. Could you highlight any standout companies?
A. Changhyoung Lee: The pavilion’s appeal lies in its scale and the exceptional quality of its participants. Many companies won Innovation Awards, showcasing their global competitiveness.

Sierra BASE, which received a Best of Innovation Award for its automated infrastructure inspection solution, exemplifies the synergy between KISED’s support and the company’s innovative capabilities. This recognition elevated the pavilion’s profile among global attendees.

Another notable participant is Greeneta, which developed the Keeep platform for creating high-quality 3D content. By drastically simplifying object creation and reducing data size while maintaining visual quality, Greeneta secured an MOU with NVIDIA.

Three companies won Best of Innovation Awards, and nine received Innovation Awards, achieving 13 honors. These accomplishments were made possible by leveraging insights and experiences accumulated over the years, creating a robust foundation for future pavilions.

A. Changhyoung Lee: While data collection and evaluation are ongoing, the immediate results—such as contracts, MOUs, and investment deals—have been remarkable. We’ll continue supporting participating startups to ensure their CES experience translates into tangible value.

Upon returning to Korea, KISED will use its extensive expertise to solidify the outcomes of CES 2025. We also plan to share insights gained at CES through various programs and networking opportunities, inspiring other companies and institutions to pursue global expansion.
Our ultimate goal is to foster a virtuous cycle of input and output growth, elevating the K-Startup Pavilion’s standards and increasing the likelihood of participants achieving their objectives.

51890.x: Korean company WiseJet (CEO Chul Soon Park) is making waves at CES 2025 with its ambitious vision of eliminating cables from all electronic devices and robots. By presenting its advanced wireless data and power transmission technology, WiseJet set new standards for innovation in the robotics industry.
"WiseJet Technology Becomes an Essential Solution for Global Robotics Companies"

CES 2025, held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10, highlighted various robotics innovations, including combat, industrial, and household robots. WiseJet gained significant attention by showcasing its wireless solutions for robotic joints, drawing keen interest from leading global robotics firms.

WiseJet’s booth attracted over 110 companies, with approximately 50 major robotics, automotive, and consumer electronics companies initiating follow-up meetings. A company representative stated, "The high interest in WiseJet’s technology at CES has opened doors for global collaborations."

51890.cap: Various WiseJet chip-based modules featured wireless data and power transmission technology. | Photo by AVING News

51890.x: "Wireless Data and Power Transmission: A Revolutionary Proposal for Robot Design"

WiseJet introduced a chip module capable of wirelessly transmitting data and power simultaneously, which is crucial for robotic joints. The system can transfer power wirelessly over distances of 1-10mm, eliminating the wear and speed limitations of traditional mechanical power supply methods. This breakthrough enables 360-degree rotation and unrestricted movement for robotic components.

Unlike traditional data-only transmission solutions, WiseJet’s technology integrates power transmission, providing enhanced flexibility and durability, fundamentally reshaping robot design and operation.
"WiseJet’s Bold Vision for a Cable-Free Future Gains Attention"
At CES 2025, WiseJet’s chip module-based wireless data and power supply method received high praise for simplifying complex cable designs while ensuring efficient power delivery.

Global robotics companies see WiseJet’s technology as a crucial component for robotic joint design, offering enhanced reliability and design flexibility. CEO Chul Soon Park stated, "CES has confirmed that our technology can play a vital role in the global robotics industry. We also anticipate expansion opportunities in autonomous vehicles, medical devices, and other industries."

51890.cap: WiseJet demonstrated its wireless power transmission technology using a chip-based modular monitor (left), repeatedly attaching and detaching it to showcase real-time operation. | Photo by AVING News

51890.x: Additionally, WiseJet unveiled its ‘Wireless CMOS Solution,’ utilizing 60GHz high-speed wireless communication technology to pioneer new horizons in ultra-high-speed, high-definition data transmission. Notably, its ‘XR-JET’ chip, capable of transmitting 8K/60Hz ultra-high-definition video over 10 meters with latency under 1 ms, garnered attention from the global TV and consumer electronics industry.

51912.cap: Official Poster of 2025 SXSW Film & TV Festival | Image by SXSW

51912.x: South by Southwest (SXSW) Conference and Festivals has revealed the lineup for its 32nd edition of the SXSW Film & TV Festival, which will occur from March 7 to 14, 2025. This year’s festival will open with the highly anticipated Apple TV+ series The Studio, created by Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg, who also serve as executive producers. The series stars Rogen as Matt Remick, a newly appointed studio head who navigates the turbulent world of Hollywood filmmaking.

The 2025 SXSW Film & TV Festival will showcase 96 feature films, including 82 world premieres. Highlights include Holland by Mimi Cave, Ash by Flying Lotus, Death of a Unicorn by Alex Scharfman, The Accountant 2 starring Ben Affleck, The Astronaut by Jess Varley, Drop by Christopher Landon, and The Makings of Curtis Mayfield directed by H.E.R. The festival will also feature 57 short films, 18 music videos, and an extensive lineup of episodic programming, including 16 TV projects with five world premiere series.

Claudette Godfrey, VP of Film & TV at SXSW, emphasized the festival’s commitment to bold storytelling: “The same undeniable creative electricity in The Studio runs through our 2025 program. This year’s lineup celebrates fearless storytellers who push boundaries and spark conversations in unexpected ways.”

The festival features a Headliner, Narrative Feature Competition, Documentary Feature Competition, Narrative Spotlight, midnighters, Global, 24 Beats Per Second, and Special Events. The TV program includes the Independent TV Pilot Competition, TV Spotlight, and TV Premiere sections. The XR Experience Program will highlight groundbreaking work in immersive storytelling, with 31 projects featured.

The Headliner section will showcase high-profile premieres, including The Accountant 2, Ash, Death of a Unicorn, Drop, and Holland. Meanwhile, the Narrative and Documentary Feature competitions will spotlight emerging voices and powerful storytelling.

51912.cap: A Still Image from Fly To You, Directed by Youngyun Song and Sngmoo Lee | Image Credit: Youngsam Jung

51912.x: The XR Experience Program will present 31 projects, including 15 in the XR Experience Competition and 16 in the XR Experience Spotlight. Immersive projects such as the 1906 Atlanta Race Massacre and The Secret Life of Monsters—The Gateway Experience will redefine storytelling through interactive and virtual reality elements. Among projects featured in this category, Fly to You, directed by Youngyun Song and Sngmoo Lee of Korea National University of Arts, will have a North American Premiere. The only work from South Korea to be part of the competing lineup of 2025 SXSW, Fly To You presents the tragic story of 85-year-old Kang Songjeol, who struggles with her childhood memory of abrupt separation from her cousin during the Korean War.

51912.cap: Youngyun Song (left) and Sngmoo Lee (right) | Image Credit: Youngyun Song and Kyunghee Kim

SXSW remains an Academy Award-qualifying festival, with its Best Animated, Best Narrative, and Best Documentary Short Film winners eligible for Oscar nominations.

In 1987, SXSW became a premier global platform for creative professionals in film, television, music, tech, and culture. 51923.cap: Rendering of the Healing Boat in operation. | Image provided by ECOPEACE

51923.x: ECOPEACE specializes in manufacturing AI water purification robots. These robots autonomously navigate contaminated areas in freshwater facilities such as reservoirs, lakes, dams, and water supply sources, performing real-time water quality analysis and continuous filtration. The company supplies its AI water purification robots to public enterprises and local governments while seeking overseas expansion. ECOPEACE is also diversifying its product applications, including foam removal robots, oil-cleaning robots, and leisure boats, targeting domestic and international markets.

At CES 2025, ECOPEACE plans to showcase its flagship product, the Healing Boat. This autonomous vessel removes excessive algae that can cause mass fish and animal deaths, human diseases, and fatalities. Equipped with self-driving technology, it navigates various water bodies while providing leisure and relaxation experiences on the water.

The Healing Boat integrates 3D digital video content, allowing users to explore underwater ecosystems, engage in water leisure activities, and contribute to water conservation simply by boarding with family and friends. ECOPEACE emphasized that the Healing Boat is an advanced robot designed to revolutionize water pollution management and water-based leisure activities.

51999.cap: Mediaiplus Presentation at CES 2025 Pangyo Lunch Talk | Image by AVING News

51999.x: Mediaiplus participated in the CES 2025 Pangyo Lunch Talk on February 20 at the Gyeonggi Startup Campus in Pangyo Techno Valley. This event showcased the innovative technologies of Pangyo-based companies attending CES 2025, facilitated discussion of industry trends, and expanded global business opportunities.

At this event, Mediaiplus shared insights on its first participation in CES 2025, detailing its success strategies and key trends in the digital health sector. Chaneung Park, Mediaiplus's Business Development Manager, presented the company’s participation strategies, achievements, and major insights from the exhibition.

Founded in 2019 by CEO Jihee Jung, Mediaiplus was established to resolve bottlenecks in clinical trials that she encountered while working with global pharmaceutical companies Roche and Bayer. The company provides two core solutions, MediC and FiCRO, to enhance clinical trial efficiency.

MediC is an integrated platform that consolidates crucial clinical trial design information. It has the most extensive clinical trial database globally, surpassing even U.S. government-operated sites. MediC offers clinical trial reports, research papers, and patent guidelines.

‘FiCRO’ addresses challenges in selecting suitable contract research organizations (CROs) for clinical trials. It utilizes a database of over 29,500 CROs worldwide to analyze clinical trial RFPs (Request for Proposals) and match them with the most appropriate institutions.

51999.cap: Chaneung Park, Business Development Manager at Mediaiplus | Image by AVING News

During CES, Mediaiplus systematically documented daily meeting results and promptly followed up on potential business leads. The company also engaged in technical discussions with developers to stay ahead of industry trends. Park highlighted that “80% of exhibition success is determined in the preparation stage,” underscoring the importance of structured pre-event planning.

Building on its CES experience, Mediaiplus plans to continue deal-closing efforts and strengthen inbound sales capabilities. In March, the company will apply insights gained at CES 2025 to maximize its success at upcoming global exhibitions, including MWC and BIO USA.

52026.cap: Flow chart of SOLVIT-iSAR | Image by SOLVIT System

52026.x: SOLVIT System (CEO Yeong-Goo Kim) will unveil its cutting-edge intelligent search and rescue system, SOLVIT-iSAR, at MWC 2025 in Barcelona from March 3 to 6. Designed to save lives in communication blind spots, this CES 2025 Innovation Award-winning solution integrates radio wave analysis and intelligent prediction technology to reduce search areas by up to 1/25, significantly improving rescue efficiency in disaster-stricken regions.

Current technologies fail to track individuals in areas without mobile signals, leaving emergency response teams struggling to locate missing persons. SOLVIT-iSAR (Intelligent Search and Rescue) leverages advanced signal analysis and AI-driven predictive modeling to identify probable last-known locations, effectively closing the gaps in emergency search operations.

At MWC 2025, SOLVIT System will demonstrate how its groundbreaking system can be deployed in challenging environments—such as rural areas with weak signals, mountainous regions with poor reception, and cases involving lost persons or drained mobile batteries—where conventional emergency location services (E911) fail to operate.

52026.cap: SOLVIT-iSAR on display at MWC 2025 | Photo by AVING News

52026.x: The company has developed proprietary technologies to enhance search efficiency, including LPS - Last Position of Signal - Analysis for radio signal-based location estimation, temporal communication access record analysis, radio shadow area subtraction, and movement-based spread analysis.

SOLVIT System aims to introduce its solution to global emergency response agencies, including fire departments and law enforcement in large territories with vast communication blind spots. The company is also seeking channel partners to expand its market presence worldwide.

Furthermore, telecom operators facing limitations in E911 services can integrate SOLVIT-iSAR into their ESG initiatives or differentiate themselves from competitors by offering an exclusive life-saving service.

The U.S. Civil Air Patrol (CAP) employs radio forensic analysis for aircraft-related search and rescue operations. However, SOLVIT-iSAR surpasses existing technologies by offering fully automated, AI-driven search and rescue intelligence, setting a new global benchmark.

SOLVIT System has been actively collaborating with national emergency agencies in South Korea. In 2019, the Korean Alpine Rescue Association and Jeonbuk Fire Service introduced radio line-of-sight analysis for mountain rescue operations. In 2020, the Korea Communications Agency commissioned the company to study radio data utilization for search and rescue efforts. By 2024, SOLVIT-iSAR was officially deployed by the Gyeonggi Northern Fire & Disaster Department, receiving high satisfaction ratings and proving its effectiveness in real-world operations.

For SOLVIT-iSAR to fully maximize its potential, emergency response agencies need real-time access to detailed base station connection records from telecom providers. However, current policies limit access to only the last connected base station's address, making precise predictive analysis and search prioritization difficult.

52026.cap: CEO Yeong-Goo Kim, at CES2025 Review Conference at MIK Base Camp last January | Photo by AVING News

52026.x: CEO Yeong-Goo Kim emphasized, “Anyone, anywhere—our families, our people, or anyone in the world—can find themselves in a life-threatening situation where E911 is unavailable. We hope our CES 2025 award-winning SOLVIT-iSAR will gain global recognition as a breakthrough solution to save lives in blind spots.
We also urge policymakers to establish clear regulations regarding personal location data for emergency services, ensuring that life-saving technologies like ours can be fully utilized.
We thank local fire departments, the Gyeongnam Police Agency, and the Korea Communications Agency (KCA) for their support in verifying our system.”

Additionally, SOLVIT System has recently completed the development of the ‘BRIDGE’ Intelligent Radio Relay Drone System, which will be commercialized later this year. Designed to work with SOLVIT-iSAR, this drone-based search solution can locate missing persons with 95% accuracy—200 times faster than human search teams.

Founded in 2007, SOLVIT System has established itself as a leading expert in military communications modeling & simulation (M&S) and radio wave analysis. Expanding into embedded systems and edge AI platforms, the company was recognized as a Top 100 Defense Innovation Company in AI by South Korea’s Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) in December 2022.

52109.cap: GEOGRID’s smart water purification system ‘BLOS’ on display | Photo by AVING News

52109.x: South Korean startup GEOGRID, a partner of the Ministry of Environment and K-water, showcased its smart water purification system ‘BLOS (Building Oasis)’ for the first time at CES 2025, held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10 (local time).

Located in Eureka Park, the startup exhibition section of CES, GEOGRID’s booth attracted significant attention throughout the event. The Small Business Administration (SBA) recognized BLOS’ innovative water quality management solution as a prime example of ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) management, impressing visitors and representatives from global corporations.

BLOS is a system that cleans and maintains the interior of water pipes using ionization and artificial intelligence (AI) technology without replacing existing pipelines. This technology removes impurities from water and enables real-time AI-based water quality monitoring and predictive analysis to detect issues in advance.

Its eco-friendly ion sterilization method eliminates chemicals, reduces reliance on plastic bottled water and conventional water purifiers, and reduces carbon emissions. This dual benefit of environmental protection and economic efficiency has made BLOS an attractive business solution. A European hotel chain executive who visited the booth remarked, “BLOS perfectly aligns with our ESG goals.”

GEOGRID CEO Kihyun Kim stated, “BLOS is not just about providing clean water; it is a sustainable technology that considers both the environment and people. We are delighted to introduce BLOS’s value to global partners at CES 2025.”

Co-founder James Jeong highlighted, “In the U.S., managing old building pipelines is a significant challenge. Conventional solutions often rely on chemicals like PFAS or only provide temporary prevention. However, alternative technologies are needed with stricter environmental regulations and growing health concerns.” He added, “BLOS integrates permanent ionization technology with AI to maintain clean pipelines without relying on PFAS, offering an eco-friendly solution that sets a new standard in the water quality management industry.”

52109.cap: GEOGRID’s booth at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

52109.x: Overseas Business Manager Sangmi Oh commented, “BLOS is being recognized as an alternative technology that surpasses the limitations of existing water purification systems while meeting environmental regulations and carbon reduction demands. At CES, we engaged in business meetings with key facility operators from hotels, hospitals, and schools, actively discussing initial export opportunities and receiving positive feedback on potential partnerships.”

Through CES 2025, GEOGRID demonstrated BLOS’s excellence on the global stage and introduced a new paradigm in water quality management. It merged environmental, technological, and economic innovations to reshape the global water purification market.

Recently, GEOGRID was selected for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups’ TIPS R&D program, further validating its technological capabilities and growth potential. With this support, the company is accelerating research and development of the BLOS system and expanding into global markets.

CEO Kihyun Kim stated, “Being selected for the TIPS R&D program is a significant milestone proving BLOS’s technological excellence and global competitiveness. We leverage this opportunity to expand our business into the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, establishing ourselves as a global leader in ESG-driven innovation.”

52472.cap: HADA CEO Jongwoo Ha pitches during the Global Media Meet-Up with Ubergizmo held at MIK BaseCamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul on Tuesday, July 1 | Photo by AVING News

52472.x: HADA Co., Ltd. (CEO Jongwoo Ha) participated in the Global Media Meet-Up held on July 1 in collaboration with U.S. tech media outlet Ubergizmo, targeting Korean startups and companies.

Co-hosted by global media outlets AVING News and Ubergizmo, the Global Media Meet-Up aims to introduce domestic technologies and products to the worldwide market. It also serves to promote CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and startup exhibitors to international media outlets and business partners in a preemptive manner.

HADA, founded in 2012 with the development of a garlic planter, has grown into a specialized agricultural machinery company by mechanizing the entire process of field crop farming. The company has expanded beyond equipment supply to offer comprehensive farming solutions, now leading the advanced agricultural machinery market by integrating smart control systems and agrarian robotics based on autonomous driving technology. With in-house development and production capabilities in both hardware and software, HADA has been delivering practical, field-oriented products and is accelerating global market entry through collaborations with renowned research institutions.

With strong capabilities in developing machinery for all stages of field crop farming and agricultural robotics, HADA has introduced AI and digital transformation (DX) into its operations. It has developed and commercialized unmanned agricultural transport robots, greenhouse sprayers, and orchard sprayers in Korea and is preparing for rapid overseas expansion.

In 2024, HADA launched its flagship product, the unmanned orchard spraying robot ‘Purida P1’, and was recognized by international research institutions as the only Korean company to commercialize such a robot, further validating its technological excellence.

52472.cap: Jongwoo Ha, CEO of HADA, delivers a pitch during the Global Media Meet-Up with Ubergizmo held at MIK BaseCamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul on Tuesday, July 1 | Photo by AVING News

52472.x: The greenhouse spraying robot and follower transport robot developed through smart farming R&D are now entering commercialization. Since 2025, they have been supplied to actual farms through the government’s New Technology Distribution Project, marking a successful application of R&D to real-world use.

HADA also revealed that it was selected for Korea’s national testbed project, which will enable large-scale testing of its unmanned orchard spraying robots starting in the second half of 2025. This initiative is expected to strengthen the robot’s market competitiveness further.

HADA signed an MOU with French agri-tech firm MYDITEK, establishing a foothold in the European market and forming a strategic partnership to expand globally. It has also partnered with Japanese nozzle manufacturer Arimitsu to improve key component technology and product quality through international cooperation.

Based on these domestic and international achievements, HADA is striving to become a leading K-AgriTech company in the global market, enhancing its competitiveness through proven technology and strong partnerships.

The company is preparing to launch its next-generation unmanned orchard spraying robot, ‘Purida P2’, in the first half of next year and aims to submit it for the CES 2026 Innovation Award. ‘Purida P2’ is fully autonomous, designed to address chronic issues in agriculture, including labor shortages, pesticide exposure, and environmental pollution.

The robot utilizes an AI-based terrain learning algorithm that integrates GPS, LiDAR, and vision sensor data in real-time, enabling it to navigate complex orchard layouts in 3D, avoid obstacles, and return automatically to its starting point after completing its task.

52472.cap: AI-powered unmanned orchard spraying robot ‘Purida P2’ | Image provided by HADA

52472.x: Purida P2 features a high-precision electrostatic nozzle system that attaches pesticide particles evenly to the underside of leaves, reducing pesticide use by 30–40%. A multi-blade system enables individual control of spray strength and direction, making it suitable for various crops, including apples, pears, and grapes. Domestic patents and multiple design rights protect the spray module.

The robot is 100% electrically powered, features a lightweight body that is 49.5% lighter than previous models, and utilizes a high-capacity lithium-ion battery that supports over 5 hours of operation—more than six times longer than drones—making it ideal for large-scale farms. Users can control the robot and manage task data via a cloud-based remote management platform, improving both productivity and sustainability.

In terms of design, Purida P2 embodies a “functional minimalism” philosophy, featuring a sleek, practical form that is well-suited for agricultural use. Its low center of gravity ensures stability on uneven terrain, while its modular structure allows for compatibility with other devices.

The aerodynamic housing, which integrates the electrostatic nozzle and multi-blower, enhances spray efficiency. Sensors are precisely positioned for optimal performance while being protected from external impacts.
The robot’s UX/UI has also been enhanced, featuring an intuitive 7-inch touchscreen and a smartphone-compatible remote control app that enables users to monitor and manage operations easily.

By integrating cutting-edge technologies, Purida P2 contributes to solving major global challenges. In terms of food security, it reduces crop loss from pests and ensures stable food production. It supports health security by eliminating pesticide exposure and reducing the burden of heavy labor for farmers.

The robot also contributes to environmental security by reducing pesticide use and carbon emissions, and to economic and community security by lowering labor and pesticide costs, increasing farm income, and promoting rural sustainability.

52472.cap: AI-powered unmanned orchard spraying robot ‘Purida P2’ in action | Image provided by HADA

52472.x: At the meet-up, HADA revealed that it is targeting key markets including North America (centered on the U.S.), the EU (focused on France and Germany), and Asia (including Japan). To facilitate this, the company plans to participate in international trade shows, such as CES, to connect with local testing partners and buyers. It is also working to obtain CE and FCC certifications to meet international technical standards and establish a bridgehead for overseas expansion.

As a certified research-based company, HADA also shared its long-term roadmap for transforming the future of agriculture. Under the leadership of CEO Jongwoo Ha, the company aims to build a sustainable agricultural ecosystem by advancing robot technology and expanding into eco-friendly agrarian platforms.

HADA plans to systematically expand its product portfolio to achieve full automation of farm operations. In addition to refining greenhouse and orchard spraying robots, it intends to develop high-versatility sprayers for rice paddies and open fields. The company is also preparing to enter the core agricultural machinery market with future developments in tractors.

Furthermore, HADA is conducting ongoing R&D for fruit thinning and harvesting robots, one of the ultimate goals of agricultural automation. This complex field, requiring image recognition and robotic arm grippers, is expected to take 3–5 years of additional research to achieve complete harvesting automation.

52472.cap: HADA CEO Jongwoo Ha (left) and Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen hold a Q&A session during the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK BaseCamp on July 1 | Photo by AVING News

52472.x: HADA emphasized that “safety” is the most important value in all its robot and machine development. The company plans to continue investing in safety technologies to prevent harm in unmanned environments.

Finally, CEO Jongwoo Ha shared his long-term vision for the company and its products. “We expect agricultural robot sales to reach break-even in about five years and become a major growth engine for the company. This will allow us to recruit more talent and expand our R&D centers and manufacturing facilities,” he said.

“The ultimate goal of HADA is not just to sell robots, but to help farmers cultivate with greater happiness. By reducing physical labor through technology, we aim to enable farmers to work with pride in a healthier environment. Based on this philosophy, our long-term vision is to become a globally recognized agricultural robotics company within the next 10 to 20 years.”

It focuses on electronics and tech coverage, regularly reporting from major global exhibitions, including CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo co-founder and CTO Hubert Nguyen, who previously worked as a programmer at NVIDIA and in 3D graphics, attended the event and has covered CES for years.

52473.x: BLACKYAK I&C Co., Ltd. (CEO TAE HYO KIM) participated in the Global Media Online Meet-Up held on July 2 in collaboration with U.S. tech media outlet Ubergizmo, targeting Korean companies and startups.

The Global Media Meet-Up, co-hosted by AVING News and Ubergizmo, aims to introduce Korean products and technologies to the global market. It also aims to promote CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and exhibitors to international media ahead of the event, creating more business opportunities.

BLACKYAK I&C is a company that leads innovation in the safety sector, leveraging BLACKYAK’s technology and expertise in functional outdoor gear since 1973. Its main products include safety shoes, industrial safety equipment, and protective clothing. Recently, it has focused on developing smart PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) and systems for recycling waste from safety shoes, industrial safety gear, and clothing.

It is expanding its product line centered on the premium workwear brand ‘BLACKYAK WORKWEAR’ and the casual workwear brand ‘WORXONE’, enhancing its B2B and B2C distribution strategies. The company aims to lead the industrial safety workwear market within five years by investing in continuous technology development and product innovation with a focus on tech-driven safety gear.

BLACKYAK I&C strengthened its global brand presence by participating in the A+A Trade Fair for Occupational Safety and Health held in Düsseldorf, Germany, in 2023. The company achieved sales of 37.7 billion KRW last year, recording a 27% CAGR over the past four years, outpacing industry peers. In January 2025, it became the first company in Korea’s industrial safety market to be listed on KOSDAQ, proving its market value and credibility.

Now, it is aiming for a CES 2026 Innovation Award with ‘Sky Shield’, scheduled for release in the first half of 2026. High-altitude worksites often feature severe noise, dust, and expansive work areas, making it challenging to detect and respond quickly to fall accidents. Sky Shield is a smart wearable safety product designed to help managers detect such accidents within the critical time frame, thereby preventing secondary accidents.

52473.cap: The smart wearable safety product ‘Sky Shield’ in action | Provided by BLACKYAK I&C

52473.x: Sky Shield attaches to the shock absorber of the safety belt worn by high-altitude workers. When a fall occurs, the absorber tears, distributing the user’s weight, causing the attached red safety pin to disconnect. The device then automatically transmits GPS location data via Google Maps to emergency contacts through smartphone linkage. It also emits an ultrasonic signal from the device itself, allowing rescuers to cross-check the worker’s location for quicker rescue and prevention of secondary accidents.

The device features precision location transmission using audio and communication technologies. It sends exact coordinates to emergency contacts based on GPS data. It also boasts military-grade ruggedness (MIL-STD-810), maintaining consistent performance in extreme environments from -20°C to 60°C. With an ultra-low power architecture and energy-saving algorithm, it reduces maintenance costs and improves operational efficiency.

The product’s intuitive and stable modular design also stands out. Its simple carabiner-compatible interface allows anyone to use it easily, and its black-red color scheme enhances visual recognition as a safety device.

Made of durable aluminum, it withstands external forces in rough work environments and supports repeated use without malfunction. Its universal design allows compatibility with most harnesses supporting loads of 60-120kg, using a lower carabiner attachment method.

From an innovation standpoint, it shifts the paradigm from passive to active safety. Rather than merely preventing falls, it proactively reduces preventable damage, introducing a new active safety paradigm that does not leave accidents unattended.

It also incorporates cross-verification technology that combines GPS-based location transmission with 100dB ultrasonic beacon signals, enhancing location accuracy in environments such as tunnels, underground sites, and densely populated urban construction areas with weak GPS signals.

52473.cap: The smart wearable safety product ‘Sky Shield’ | Provided by BLACKYAK I&C

52473.x: BLACKYAK I&C emphasized Sky Shield’s ability to address global problems. Accidents in the workplace result in significant financial losses for companies and nations, including insurance payouts, treatment costs, human losses, project delays, and shutdowns. By preventing serious accidents, the product can help mitigate these losses.

It also offers a low-cost smart safety solution accessible to developing countries and SMEs that struggle to afford high-end safety systems, helping reduce blind spots and promoting industrial safety equality.
Sky Shield can also address the shortage of safety personnel. A single safety manager can monitor multiple high-altitude workers in real-time, helping maintain safety even at understaffed worksites.

The potential to build an IoT platform based on wearable devices will accelerate the digital transformation of industrial safety, laying the foundation for future integration with smart cities and smart factories.

BLACKYAK I&C plans to participate in CES for the first time in 2026. If it wins the Innovation Award, it expects to position itself as a smart and eco-friendly safety solution provider in the global industrial safety market.

Breaking from the traditional perception of industrial safety products as manufacturing-based, BLACKYAK I&C is pursuing a transition to a PPP (Personal Protective Platform). Winning at CES would be a catalyst for realizing this vision. As international regulations on industrial safety tighten, building trust as a global tech company would help diversify business opportunities, such as attracting VC investment, public R&D projects, and global B2B procurement deals.

52473.cap: BLACKYAK I&C responds to media questions at the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Wednesday, July 2 | Photo by AVING News

52473.x: Looking ahead to CES 2027, BLACKYAK I&C plans to conduct direct sales activities targeting global buyers and partners, further executing its international expansion strategy.

It plans to focus first on countries with industrial safety markets structured similarly to Korea. Japan, with active tech exchanges with Korea and similar standards and regulations, has a low entry barrier. As construction workers age, physical accidents increase, and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, and Transport (MLIT) is promoting safety data systems as part of its construction DX policy. This is expanding the demand for smart safety devices like Sky Shield.

In Vietnam, where many Korean manufacturers, such as Samsung and LG, operate, trust in Korean products is high. Partnering with local safety distributors will facilitate the expansion of the B2B supply. Although PPE requirements are still in the early stages, demand for smart equipment is growing. BLACKYAK I&C views Vietnam as an environment where Sky Shield’s intuitive usability and reliability can spread quickly.

In the Middle East, where plant-based construction is prevalent and high-altitude work is common, demand for smart safety devices to prevent serious accidents is increasing. These markets actively import foreign technology and equipment, with foreign workers comprising a significant portion of the labor force. BLACKYAK I&C plans to highlight Sky Shield’s intuitive use and durability in this region.

52473.cap: BLACKYAK I&C presents its pitch during the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Wednesday, July 2 | Photo by AVING News

52473.x: Ultimately, BLACKYAK I&C aims to demonstrate the effectiveness of its technology in the highly regulated industrial safety markets of the U.S. and Europe. In the U.S., demand for smart safety solutions that comply with strict OSHA standards is high due to the presence of high-altitude work in construction, utilities, communications, and industrial plants. In Europe, industries such as wind power, logistics, and facility maintenance are showing growing interest in AI-based fall detection and wearable PPE. CE certification enables wide distribution across the continent.

A BLACKYAK I&C official stated, “Sky Shield, set to launch in the first half of 2026, marks the beginning of BLACKYAK I&C’s smart industrial safety platform initiative. Starting with this product, we aim to build a Personal Protective Platform (PPP) that connects future smart wearable devices through an IoT system, evolving into an integrated platform capable of real-time risk detection, location tracking, and safety management based on user data.”

They added, “Our challenge for the CES 2026 Innovation Award is just the beginning. We plan to continue promoting our product and technology globally by participating in Japan’s Industrial Safety and Health Exhibition and Germany’s A+A Trade Fair for Occupational Safety and Health. Our goal is to simultaneously establish global leadership and market share in the smart safety device field.”

52480.cap: Joy Kibbeum Na, CEO of Futureduck, delivers a pitch during the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Thursday, July 3 | Photo by AVING News

52480.x: Futureduck Inc. (CEO Joy Kibbeum Na) announced its participation in the Global Media Online Meet-Up held on July 3 in partnership with U.S. tech media Ubergizmo, targeting Korean startups and businesses.

This Global Media Meet-Up, co-hosted by AVING News and Ubergizmo, aims to introduce Korean startups and their products and technologies to the global market. Founded in February 2024 by IT and education experts, Futureduck is an edtech startup whose mission is “to cultivate independent thinkers.” In October 2023, it launched its writing education platform ‘Quewrite’, which supports students’ critical thinking and literacy development.

Quewrite is a platform that helps students complete the entire writing process independently through an AI tutor that asks guiding questions. It supports students who struggle with writing by helping them organize and articulate their thoughts, and also assists teachers in addressing practical challenges in writing instruction at schools and academies.

Futureduck is currently developing ‘Que:read’, a literacy education platform that expands the philosophy and technology of Quewrite into the domain of reading. Que:read is set for release in February 2026 and will form the foundation of a next-generation integrated literacy education platform alongside Quewrite.

52480.cap: Promotional banner for Futureduck’s AI-based reading support platform ‘Que:read’ | Image provided by Futureduck

52480.x: The beta version of Quewrite is currently being tested for educational effectiveness at 32 schools across Korea, involving 1,056 teachers and students. These trials are helping verify the platform’s practicality and efficacy in real classroom settings. Futureduck is incorporating positive feedback to enhance the platform further.

With a major update planned for late 2025, the company will officially launch commercial operations and expand its presence in both public and private education markets. With the growing demand for literacy instruction, Quewrite is quickly gaining traction as a practical teaching tool.

Based on its domestic user references, Futureduck is also preparing to enter overseas markets, focusing on Southeast Asia and North America. The company emphasizes that Quewrite’s multilingual adaptability and pedagogical design offer a competitive edge in global education markets. Futureduck aims to become a key partner in closing global literacy gaps.

Currently under development, Que:read is an AI-powered conversational reading support platform. It provides customized, dialogue-based questions before, during, and after reading to help users understand texts and deepen their thinking. Going beyond simple comprehension tools, Que:read diagnoses and improves users’ literacy as an intelligent reading companion.

Technologically, Que:read stands out with its conversational diagnostic capabilities, which allow it to identify weak literacy areas through natural dialogue. Leveraging advanced NLP and speech recognition, the platform offers real-time personalized learning guidance.

52480.cap: Joy Kibbeum Na, CEO of Futureduck, and Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo, pose for a commemorative photo during the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Thursday, July 3 | Photo by AVING News

Que:read’s most innovative feature is its AI philosophy: unlike traditional AI that limits thinking, it supports deeper, more critical, and creative thought.

Its design promotes cognitive growth through questions that foster critical and interpretive thinking. Globally, Que:read aims to tackle widespread literacy deficiencies. Its voice interface and personalized diagnostics will allow early learners and those in underserved regions to access high-quality reading education, contributing to educational equity.

Futureduck is entering the CES Innovation Awards for the first time, officially unveiling its flagship AI-based literacy platform, Quewrite, to the global market. TAILOR uses an LLM-based emotion recognition model to detect subtle emotional changes and delivers appropriate motivational, encouraging, and supportive messages. The result is a highly accurate, medically informed AI healthcare service.

CIT’s core technology, Atomic Sputter Epitaxy (ASE), enables uniform deposition of copper atoms without adhesive, arranging a trillion atoms per cubic centimeter. Its high heat and oxidation resistance also help lower energy use for data center cooling, which typically consumes 40% of a center’s power. 52664.cap: Promotional image of MUA | Image by NP

52664.x: MUA aims to create new opportunities in the wellness industry. It designs visual elements inspired by nature—such as clouds, lakes, and caves—and combines them with hyper-realistic 3D backgrounds to create immersive virtual environments. This helps users achieve deeper meditative states more quickly.

Beyond multisensory meditation content, MUA applies algorithms that maximize meditation experiences by analyzing biosignals. In collaboration with KAIST’s Department of Brain & Cognitive Sciences and the Meditation Science Institute, NP developed emotion inference algorithms based on biosignals, currently undergoing validation.

Biosignals are collected through MUA’s dedicated app installed on HMDs, smartphones, and wearables. Indicators such as age, gender, heart rate, heart rate variability, oxygen saturation, and sleep quality are analyzed to determine psychological and emotional conditions. Based on this, MUA delivers meditation content tailored to the user’s real-time needs, a key differentiator.

Collected biosignal data is analyzed using James Russell’s two-dimensional emotion model, which quantifies valence, arousal, and stress on scales of 1 to 10. These are then mapped onto 16 emotion states. During the first five sessions, user feedback fine-tunes discrepancies between subjective perception and algorithmic inference.

Most importantly, by delivering meditation content optimized to personal psychological and physiological conditions, MUA dramatically shortens the long learning curve of traditional meditation.

For example, traditional MBSR (Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction) meditation requires daily practice of at least 10 minutes for eight weeks to reach deep immersion. MUA, however, enables users to get focused states within just 3–5 minutes through audiovisual guidance and interactive elements.

MUA’s UX·UI prioritizes emotional stability with principles of balance, minimalism, psychological accessibility, and emotional-sensory touch. Polyphenol Factory is a beauty-tech startup founded in 2023 under the leadership of KAIST Professor Haeshin Lee, bringing together the expertise of promising Korean scientists and researchers. Under the slogan “Reinvent everyday life with science,” the company has introduced haircare solutions with scientific evidence.

The company designs its haircare lineup with polyphenols derived from nature. Polyphenols are potent antioxidants that plants produce to protect themselves, and they protect cells from reactive oxygen species by nature. When formulated into products like shampoo, they help prevent hair and scalp damage caused by external factors and improve the strength of hair that has thinned and breaks easily.

Polyphenol Factory releases these functional products under the brand ‘grab!ty,’ which launched in April 2024. The grab!ty shampoo has reached cumulative sales of 1.4 million bottles and generated about KRW 23.5 billion in revenue, becoming a mega-hit for the company.

After repeated appearances at CES and other trade shows in Korea and abroad, Polyphenol Factory secured sales channels in the United States, Japan, and Taiwan, and plans to enter Germany and Indonesia in the second half of this year.

As the name suggests, StraightMAX smooths curly hair and makes it similar to straight hair. Unlike conventional perm solutions used for the same effect, it completely excludes toxic chemicals such as formaldehyde, thioglycolic acid, and sodium hydroxide. This differentiates it as the industry’s first technology to remove these substances from the formula.

Instead, high-molecular polyphenols derived from natural sources apply precise molecular forces without breaking hair’s disulfide bonds (-S-S-) to produce a straightening effect. When applied to everyday haircare formats like shampoo and cream, users can enjoy straightening without scalp irritation, hair damage, or harmful gas concerns.

StraightMAX proposes a way to straighten curly hair without chemical damage or unpleasant odors, and it can also apply the same principle in reverse to add soft curls to straight hair. The platform supports multiple hairstyles on a single technology base. The company emphasized that StraightMAX surpasses the limitations of existing haircare technologies and products, resonating with users worldwide.

Its vision centers on simplifying complex medical procedures and enabling the same level of precision surgery in regions with limited healthcare access.
