Clinical trials involving more than 500 cases have demonstrated its stable performance with no errors. A cloud-based remote support function enables collaboration among medical staff worldwide. The company states that this standard-setting solution is accessible even to small hospitals and developing regions.

The device adopts a compact, modular design for maximum space efficiency in small operating rooms. Dental supports provide ergonomic comfort for patients, while simple skin markers do not hinder surgical access. Its interface offers color-coded 3D visualization, allowing surgeons to identify anatomical structures intuitively.

The external design features smooth curves and neutral tones to minimize visual impact, while premium medical-grade materials enable sterilization and repeated use. This balances aesthetics with practicality.

XAVE AIR presents an alternative to conventional, costly, and invasive navigation systems, achieving sub-millimeter precision without bone fixation. Cloud connectivity allows real-time surgical support from remote experts, overcoming geographic barriers. In education, it can serve as a simulation tool for students and residents to train in navigation safely. Its low-cost, high-efficiency structure highlights its innovation in expanding access to advanced medical technology.

This global problem-solving capacity is particularly significant. Precision surgical navigation has been limited so far to large hospitals due to high equipment costs and a shortage of specialists. XAVE AIR’s lightweight, affordable, non-invasive design bridges this gap, enabling precision surgeries even in small hospitals and developing regions. The remote support function enables regions with limited medical resources to receive real-time guidance from world-class experts. Educational use also boosts the capabilities of future surgeons, contributing to the advancement of global medical standards.

Building on this technology, A4LAB plans a stepwise global market strategy. Domestically, it will continue joint research with hospitals to gather more clinical data and strengthen the commercialization foundation.

Internationally, the company is prioritizing FDA approval for U.S. market entry, while expanding collaborative research and education programs with Indonesian institutions to strengthen its position in Southeast Asia. Mid- to long-term plans include strategic hubs in Cairo (Egypt) and Dubai (UAE) to expand into Africa and the Middle East.

To enhance global promotion and partnerships, A4LAB will continue to join major international exhibitions. Starting with CES 2026 in Las Vegas, the company also plans to participate in Arab Health 2026 (Dubai), MEDICA 2026 (Germany), and Hospital Expo Jakarta 2026 (Indonesia), where it will present XAVE AIR to medical experts and buyers worldwide.

A4LAB has also applied for the CES 2026 Innovation Award. The company stated, “This challenge represents an important opportunity for us to gain global recognition for our unique technology and competitiveness. CES can serve as a bridgehead for entering the global medical device market, and winning the Innovation Award would demonstrate our credibility and technical strength to international buyers, investors, and medical experts. It would also increase brand awareness and expand international partnerships, potentially leading to export contracts and collaborative research. Through this challenge, we aim to achieve tangible results and expand our global network.”
Alongside global network expansion, A4LAB also expressed its ambition to enhance technology reliability and achieve real export contracts.

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo runs Silicon Valley Post and publishes in six languages across 200 countries, focusing on electronics and technology. It covers major exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen, a former NVIDIA programming engineer and 3D graphics developer, attended the event and has reported annually from CES on global companies’ products and technologies.

52686.x: JENLiFE (CEO Jinwoo Oh) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, to be held in Las Vegas from January 6 to 9, and will also compete for the CES Innovation Awards.

Held annually in January, CES is one of the world’s three largest IT exhibitions, drawing global attention as a mega-event that showcases the latest products, technologies, and trends from companies of all sizes. The Consumer Technology Association (CTA), organizer of CES, reviews global submissions for the CES Innovation Awards ahead of the event. Only about 10 percent of applicants are typically selected, and less than 1 percent go on to win the Best Innovation Award, making it one of the most competitive recognitions in the industry. Winning companies gain immediate international attention and access to a wide range of business opportunities.

Against this backdrop, JENLiFE, a functional biomaterials startup specializing in electronic noses, aims to showcase its M13 bacteriophage–based technology at CES 2026. Unlike conventional gas sensor combinations with limited detection, JENLiFE’s approach uses phage display technology to create peptide receptors on M13 bacteriophages, mimicking human olfactory receptors. This enables the electronic nose to bind to and identify odor molecules with high precision and selectivity.

By arranging multiple bacteriophages on sensors, JENLiFE builds a bio-receptor library capable of detecting more than 800 odor molecules. The company emphasizes that this method ensures both high sensitivity and reproducibility, as identical bacteriophages can be replicated with consistent performance. Beyond detection, JENLiFE plans to present its vision of “olfactory intelligence” at CES 2026, where odor data can be analyzed and predicted for diverse applications.

The healthcare sector is expected to benefit significantly. Breath and body odor analysis could enable non-invasive early detection of diseases such as lung cancer, diabetes, and oral disorders. This aligns with global trends in preventive and patient-friendly healthcare. JENLiFE also sees opportunities in air purification systems that automatically adapt to air quality, food safety monitoring that detects spoilage levels, disaster response robots that identify survivors or chemical leaks, and metaverse environments that replicate scent for heightened realism. The company is already collaborating with businesses in consumer electronics, food, and automotive industries to translate the potential of its electronic nose platform into practical solutions.

At CES 2026, JENLiFE plans to demonstrate the technology live, showcasing its real-world performance to industry experts, buyers, investors, and media. JENLiFE sees this as a springboard into the U.S. and global markets, with particular focus on healthcare, food safety, environmental monitoring, and robotics.

A company spokesperson said, “We will showcase how our M13 bacteriophage-based electronic nose platform works in practice. Through this, we aim to directly convey its strengths and applications to experts and potential partners, and actively seek collaborations and investment opportunities.” The spokesperson added, “By leveraging market insights and networks gained on-site, we intend to establish a foothold for entry into the U.S. and other global markets. We will move quickly to form partnerships with local bio, electronics, and robotics companies and institutions, while continuing networking and pilot projects beyond CES.”

At CES 2025 earlier this year, Korean startups made a strong showing, winning seven of the 19 Best Innovation Awards and securing nearly half of all Innovation Award selections. JENLiFE aims to follow in these footsteps at CES 2026 with its groundbreaking “smelling electronic nose” technology.

52694.x: South Korean digital olfactory solutions company Deepscent Inc. announced that its flagship Deepscent AI platform has been submitted to the CES 2026 Innovation Awards in four categories: Home Appliances, Smart Home, Smart Communities, and Content & Entertainment. The platform leverages multimodal AI to autonomously generate custom scent blends by interpreting images, music, moods, and contextual inputs—without requiring user expertise.

Deepscent AI’s multimodal algorithm can analyze environmental and emotional cues in just three seconds to deliver optimal fragrance profiles. The system is trained on more than 100,000 fragrance metadata points, covering accords, notes, and reviews, enabling precise and context-aware blending. Its dynamic system uses 20 biodegradable capsules with three intensity levels, producing up to 392,445 unique scent combinations. The capsules automatically calibrate based on temperature, humidity, and airflow, while the diffuser covers up to 50m² with ultra-quiet performance under 30dB.

Designed with sustainability in mind, Deepscent AI is built with recyclable ABS-aluminum composites and 100% biodegradable capsules. It also supports MQTT and RESTful APIs for seamless IoT integration, making it suitable for both personal and shared environments.

To date, the company has secured six granted patents and 21 pending applications across hardware, algorithms, and system integration—fortifying its intellectual property in the field of AI-powered olfactory computing.

The platform’s potential impact spans multiple sectors. In Home Appliances, it enhances living spaces with adaptive scent personalization. For Smart Homes, it creates mood-driven atmospheres that respond to user context. Within Smart Communities, it can scale to public spaces, enhancing collective well-being and identity. In Content & Entertainment, it synchronizes with digital media to enable multisensory storytelling.
“By embedding scent into spatial computing, Deepscent AI establishes a new benchmark for immersive, emotion-driven innovation,” said Marco Kwon(권일봉), CEO of Deepscent.
CES 2026 will take place in Las Vegas from January 6 to 9, where Innovation Award winners will be officially announced.

52721.cap: Autonomous patroling robot by SK Shieldus exhibited at CES 2024 | Photo by AVING News

52721.x: As CES 2026 approaches, the focus once again shifts to robotics—a field that is rapidly transforming how people live, work, and interact. This year’s event promises an impressive lineup of innovations illustrating how robots are becoming deeply integrated into modern life, from smart homes and healthcare to hospitality, retail, and logistics.

No longer limited to industrial assembly lines, robots are now entering homes as practical helpers and even companions. One highlight from CES 2025 is Tombot’s Jennie, a robotic dog designed to provide emotional support to individuals with dementia and cognitive conditions. Meanwhile, Segway’s Navimow and Daedong’s multifunctional agricultural robot are revolutionizing outdoor maintenance and precision farming through autonomous operation and smart navigation.

Household robotics continues to advance with designs that combine utility and intelligence. Roborock’s Saros Z70, a vacuum cleaner equipped with a mechanical arm capable of moving small objects, demonstrates how automation extends beyond cleaning. Similarly, Samsung’s Ballie, a mobile home assistant, helps manage daily tasks while providing real-time updates such as weather and calendar alerts—marking a new era of personalized robotic companionship.

In the service and retail sectors, robots are transforming customer experiences. Richtech Robotics’ Adam, a robotic bartender and barista, is redefining hospitality service with style and efficiency. In retail settings, Kroger’s aisle-scanning robots streamline inventory management, while HERE Technologies advances autonomous navigation systems that enable precise indoor and outdoor mobility.

Driven by advancements in AI, machine learning, and automation, the global robotics industry continues to grow at an unprecedented rate. The U.S. home robotics market value has now reached approximately $1.1 billion, with the worldwide market projected to reach $178.63 billion by 2030. The rise of Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) models further accelerates adoption by lowering costs and offering scalable automation solutions for small and medium-sized businesses.

As robots assume increasingly sophisticated roles—enhancing agricultural productivity, improving factory safety, and bringing empathy into human-machine interactions—CES 2026 will serve as a key showcase of how robotics is evolving from a tool of efficiency into an intelligent and caring partner.

From smart factories to emotional AI-driven companions, the world’s largest tech event will provide a glimpse into a near future where robots are not just machines but meaningful participants in our everyday lives. Visitors to CES 2026 in Las Vegas (January 6–9) will be among the first to see these breakthroughs firsthand, witnessing the next major leap in the human-robot relationship.

52795.cap: Strutt Founder and CEO Tony Hong | Photo provided by Strutt

52795.x: Strutt, a new mobility technology startup, has given media and key industry partners an exclusive preview of its flagship product, the STRUTT ev¹, a smart personal vehicle that integrates advanced automotive sensing and robotics to redefine personal mobility. The private event, dubbed “Strutt Day,” served as a significant pre-launch milestone ahead of the ev¹’s official world premiere at CES 2026 in Las Vegas.

The ev¹ has already generated significant industry buzz, having earned the prestigious Red Dot: Luminary 2025—the highest design concept distinction globally—and the CES 2026 Best of Innovation award in the Vehicle Technology & Advanced Mobility category.

At Strutt Day, attendees were introduced to the company's vision by Founder and CEO Tony Hong, who explained that the mission is to bridge the gap between cutting-edge technology and the real, everyday challenges faced by mobility users.

“We started Strutt because we saw a gap between incredible technology and the real problems people face every day,” Hong said. “Strutt Day isn’t just about our product; it’s about showing the world how thoughtful design and intelligent technologies can transform lives.”

Barney Mason, Head of Design, articulated the design philosophy of “Quiet Empowerment,” aiming to create technology that subtly blends into daily life while boosting user confidence and independence. The development process involved extensive user research, guiding every detail from the chassis to the joystick placement, to ensure the design supports dignity and natural movement.
The STRUTT ev¹ is built around two core, proprietary innovations that bring self-driving car technology into personal mobility:

The first innovation is the evSense System, a 360-degree sensing and decision-making system. This system uses a combination of sensors, including LiDAR, cameras, ultrasonic, and Time-of-Flight (ToF). This advanced setup allows for safe, real-world navigation and automatic obstacle avoidance, significantly reducing the need for constant hyper-vigilance.

The second core innovation is the Quad-Drive System, a four-wheel active drive architecture with powerful quad motors. This system ensures smooth, controlled movement across diverse environments, from indoor spaces and carpets to challenging outdoor terrains and inclines, enhancing both safety and performance.

Attendees at the showcase experienced the vehicle’s capabilities firsthand, confirming its goal of addressing the current challenges of complexity, outdated technology, and the social stigma often associated with mobility devices.

The company, incorporated in Singapore and backed by investors including Matter Venture Partners and Vertex Ventures, combines world-leading expertise in advanced sensing and autonomous robotics with a people-centered research approach. The highly anticipated global launch at CES 2026 will unveil final details, including pricing and availability, setting the stage for Strutt to become a major player in the evolving smart mobility sector.

52806.cap: Bob Sternfels, Global Managing Partner at McKinsey & Company | Photo by CTA

52806.x: The Consumer Technology Association (CTA) has scheduled a major thought leadership event for CES 2026: a live, unscripted taping of the influential “All-In” podcast that will dissect the ongoing Artificial Intelligence (AI) revolution. The keynote will feature podcast co-host Jason Calacanis in conversation with two of the world’s most prominent business minds, Bob Sternfels, Global Managing Partner at McKinsey & Company, and Hemant Taneja, CEO of General Catalyst.

The event, set for 2 PM PST on Tuesday, January 6, in the Palazzo Ballroom at the Venetian, promises to explore how AI is fundamentally redefining global corporate strategy, investment priorities, and the future of innovation.

Kinsey Fabrizio, President of CTA, described the significance of the convergence of these voices: “This is CES at its best — a convergence of ideas, influence, and innovation. AI isn’t just reshaping industries, it’s rewriting the rules of leadership, strategy, and opportunity. CES is where innovators show up and lead the AI revolution.”

52806.cap: Hemant Taneja, CEO of General Catalyst | Photo by CTA

52806.x: The discussion will bring together different perspectives on where the smart money is moving within the AI sector, analyzing which technologies are currently overvalued and which are poised for explosive growth. Sternfels, whose firm McKinsey & Company has integrated its own generative AI platform, Lilli, into its operations, noted that the conversation will explore the technology’s potential to transform enterprises and guide leaders on building AI-driven value.

Taneja, who leads General Catalyst, a venture and transformation company with over $40 billion under management, views tech not just as a disruptive force, but as a “catalyst for complete industry transformation.” He suggested the keynote will unite strategic vision and investment power to help groundbreaking ideas mature into lasting enterprises. Calacanis, a well-known early-stage investor with a track record of spotting companies like Uber and Robinhood, is excited to bring the podcast’s signature “no-BS, full-contact” debate style to the CES keynote stage.

52806.cap: Jason Calcanis, Entrepreneur, Angel Investor, and Co-Host of the All-In podcast | Photo by CTA

52806.x: Further underscoring the shift from purely digital to physical applications of AI, CES 2026 will host the session “Transforming Industries with Physical AI,” presented by McKinsey. This specialized conference session will explore the real-world adoption of Physical AI, which refers to AI that enables machines to perceive, understand, and interact directly with the physical world using sensors and actuators—effectively serving as the “brain” for autonomous vehicles, robots, and innovative industrial systems.

This session will investigate how these advancements are reshaping industries, work, and the future of automation, moving beyond virtual capabilities to tangible physical impact. Speakers for this deep dive include Alex Panas, Senior Partner and Global Leader of Industry Sectors at McKinsey, and Ani Kelkar, a Consultant with the firm.

The All-In interview is part of a high-profile series of keynotes at CES 2026, which also features leaders such as Dr. Lisa Su of AMD, Joe Creed of Caterpillar, Yannick Bolloré of Havas and Vivendi, and Yuanqing Yang of Lenovo.

52814.cap: AI-powered mobility aid Free Wings developed by FAKE EYES | Photo by Next Generation Convergence Contents Industry Association (NCIA)

52814.x: FAKE EYES (CEO Mason Kim) announced that it has developed a mobility aid and walking navigation platform for the visually impaired, Free Wings. The product utilizes core technology from an ultra-lightweight Foundation AI model that integrates Semantic Segmentation (classifying objects pixel-by-pixel within an image) and Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) (deriving 3D information of the surroundings using only one camera). The company plans to enter the global market starting in the first quarter of 2026.

Developed in a consortium with SimSimi Inc. and DIVEXR Co., Ltd., Free Wings, designed to support independent mobility for the visually impaired, features vision intelligence AI technology, and is expected to bring revolutionary changes to their daily lives. Following the prototype release last year, the system was significantly refined and, after various user tests, has finally achieved commercialization success. FAKE EYES plans to unveil the product for the first time at CES 2026 in Las Vegas, USA, next January.

A key feature of Free Wings is that the AI operates solely on the wearable device, without external communication, enabling real-time, safe navigation even in outdoor walking environments with communication blind spots. Furthermore, by linking the device with a smartphone and a proprietary walking navigation platform, it offers a total solution for visually impaired mobility, providing both safe walking services and voice guidance for the walking route to the destination.

Mason Kim, CEO of FAKE EYES, expressed his ambition, “We take great pride in pioneering new artificial intelligence technology and application fields through this mobility aid for the visually impaired. Free Wings integrates AI Agent technology, voice recognition technology for controlling walking functions, and the ability to recognize dangerous situations on the walking path, identify dangerous objects, and infer their direction and distance, all with a single camera module on a very low-power, battery-operated device. It will deliver a significant impact to the global visually impaired mobility solution market.”

FAKE EYES plans to offer a free walking navigation service to visually impaired users who agree to share their walking data with the company. Walking data collected worldwide will be used to develop Physical AI technologies, such as drones and humanoid robots, that FAKE EYES plans to grow in the future.

Meanwhile, FAKE EYES, an occupant of the KoVAC (Korea VR AR Complex) XR Business Growth Support Center—an enterprise growth support facility backed by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the National IT Industry Promotion Agency—is a promising first-generation XR company established in 2016 and holds core virtual reality technology. Last December, the company received the Minister’s Award from the Ministry of Science and ICT in recognition of its achievement in producing a Software Development Kit (SDK) for Metaverse ethics standards. Additionally, it was selected for the Metaverse Alliance Outstanding Project Group for its plan to develop an XR nursing practice Metaverse solution based on hand-tracking, demonstrating its leadership in virtual convergence technology and achieving significant milestones toward global expansion.

52821.cap: Scott Seongwook Lee, CEO of Geeks Loft | Photo by AVING News

52821.x: “Where Tomorrow Is Created Today.” Geeks Loft (CEO Scott Seongwook Lee) is a global hardware company that has designed new user experiences at the intersection of technology and imagination, reflecting the philosophy this phrase embodies.

Based in Seongnam, Gyeonggi-do, the company values translating complex technologies into forms that users can naturally accept. It has developed interactive devices guided by two principles: intuitive use without additional learning and practicality in everyday life.

Geeks Loft has focused on merging audio and visual technologies to break existing boundaries. By adding visual experiences to a market for wearables that traditionally centered on audio, the company aims to expand the role of headphones from a device for “listening” to one that also allows users to see, capture, and share — creating an entirely new category.

This vision becomes clearer through the company’s integrated development system, where hardware, software, and design operate as a single team. Starting from real use cases, each field is co-designed to refine the user experience by translating complex technical elements into simple, approachable interfaces.

52821.cap: Promotional image celebrating Perisphere’s CES 2026 Innovation Award | Image by Geeks Loft

52821.x: The product that best embodies this philosophy is the smart headphone “Perisphere.” Perisphere is the world’s first smart headphone equipped with visual functionality, enabling music playback, video watching, 3D video recording, and real-time sharing seamlessly in one device. It connects wirelessly to a smartphone to support a continuous flow of “listening-watching-recording-sharing.” The name combines “Peri” (surrounding) and “Sphere” (space/world), reflecting the goal of expanding the user’s experiential world.

The most notable feature of Perisphere is its display band, which drops down in front of the eyes only when needed. When the screen is not required, the band can be lifted to function like a regular headphone, reducing the burden of wearing it. It addresses the complexity and fatigue often associated with VR and AR devices, while offering an everyday interface suitable for public environments. Dual stereoscopic cameras and stereo microphones capture the user’s perspective in 3D with immersive sound, and touch controls and smartphone connectivity simplify content management and real-time sharing.

Over the past four years, Geeks Loft has enhanced wearing stability, weight balance, display visibility, and connection reliability through 10 rounds of design revisions, more than 30 patent applications, and feedback from over 1,000 users. This integrated design approach and emphasis on everyday usage scenarios led to global recognition. Perisphere won the Best of Innovation Award in the “Headphones & Personal Audio” category at CES 2026, affirming both its technological direction and design quality.

52821.cap: Structure of Perisphere | Image by Geeks Loft

52821.x: Geeks Loft views its participation in CES 2026 and its Innovation Award win as more than a technical showcase. The company sees CES as an opportunity to accelerate market validation and commercialization. At the world’s largest consumer electronics event, it plans to advance partnership, investment, certification, and mass-production discussions simultaneously, establishing a firm foundation for global expansion. Since CES’s Eureka Park has long served as a hub for early-stage innovators building international networks, Geeks Loft considers this stage the starting point for major business expansion.

The company’s market strategy centers on the United States. Geeks Loft is reviewing the establishment of a U.S. subsidiary or corporate transition to strengthen North American investment and partnerships, while also preparing local distribution channels and market testing. At the same time, it is pursuing major global certifications, including FCC and CE, while building a stable supply chain and phased mass-production plans.

Aiming to launch in the first half of 2026, the company plans to enter the market through global crowdfunding platforms such as Kickstarter and Indiegogo, and expand into healthcare and entertainment use cases. In particular, through collaboration with Brain Vector, an Australian AI-based mental health content company, Geeks Loft is jointly developing immersive content for athlete mental care and wellness, demonstrating Perisphere’s value not only in daily life but also in professional fields.

52821.cap: Perisphere has been introduced as a product that not only supports listening and viewing but also allows users to capture and share what they see. | Image by Geeks Loft

52821.x: Geeks Loft’s mid- to long-term vision goes beyond establishing a new category of smart headphones. The company aims to evolve Perisphere into an AI-based everyday interface and grow into a global platform company connecting hardware, software, and content in one ecosystem. By offering user experiences where audio and visual elements blend naturally, Geeks Loft plans to expand users’ sensory worlds and build a hardware platform that connects to industries such as content creation, entertainment, and wellness.

The company plans to meet with global partners and investors in person at CES 2026 to refine collaboration models further. Those interested in experiencing the new “audiovisual headphone” Perisphere and its possibilities can visit Geeks Loft at Booth 62817 in Eureka Park during CES 2026.

Pangyo Techno Valley is a global R&D hub that integrates Research (R), People (P), Information (I), and Trade (T) across the IT, BT, CT, NT, and mobility sectors. It is a leading innovation cluster in Gyeonggi-do, established to drive technological innovation, talent development, job creation, and international business competitiveness.

The Gyeonggido Business & Science Accelerator’s Techno Valley Innovation Group has continuously promoted Pangyo Techno Valley’s value by hosting events such as the Pangyo Evening Meet-Up, Pan-Pan Day, Joy of Work in Pangyo, and Pangyo Startup Investment Exchange - In-Best Pangyo. These initiatives have facilitated networking between Pangyo companies, domestic and international investors, and the media. Similar events are planned for this year to support the growth and global expansion of Pangyo startups through various assistance programs.

52823.cap: Siemens AG President and CEO Roland Busch | Photo and logo provided by Siemens

52823.x: Siemens AG President and CEO Roland Busch will deliver a keynote address at CES 2026, where he is expected to showcase the company’s full suite of industrial technologies developed to usher in an AI-ready era for manufacturing, infrastructure, and transportation. The presentation will emphasize how Siemens is merging the real and digital worlds using AI, digital twins, and automation to drive tangible, real-world impact.

The CTA confirmed the keynote, with CEO Gary Shapiro stating that Busch and Siemens are demonstrating how AI, when combined with domain know-how and data, can “reinvent entire industries” by streamlining design, planning, engineering, operations, and maintenance.

Roland Busch, who holds a doctorate in physics and has over 30 years at Siemens, drew a comparison between the current AI transition and the advent of electricity. “There was a world before AI, right now we are transitioning to a world that makes full use of it – including in factories, buildings, grids, and transportation,” Busch said.

He framed Siemens as the global leader in industrial AI—“AI for the real world”—by embedding intelligence into every machine, device, and piece of infrastructure. The company plans to show how it is leveraging its deep domain expertise and established customer trust to scale industrial AI from a “once-in-a-century opportunity into tangible benefits for industries and society.”

Under Busch’s leadership, Siemens was named to TIME’s 2025 World’s Best Companies list, a testament to its focus on industrial automation, future-proofed energy systems, and adaptive infrastructure designed to be more competitive, resilient, and sustainable.

At CES, Siemens plans to demonstrate its AI-powered technologies alongside its complementary ecosystem of partners and customers. The goal is to explain how its tech stack enables AI to scale reliably in industrial environments. This focus includes transforming manufacturing processes, making cities more livable through adaptive infrastructure, and enhancing the sustainability of transportation.

The keynote, which follows the CTA State of the Industry Address, is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. PST on Tuesday, January 6, 2026, in the Palazzo Ballroom at the Venetian. Busch will join a high-profile keynote lineup that includes leaders from AMD, Caterpillar, Havas, Lenovo, and Vivendi, as well as a live All-In interview with McKinsey and General Catalyst.

Visitors will also be able to experience the technology firsthand at the Las Vegas Convention Center North Hall (booth 8725), where Siemens will host its mobile experience center and livestream a series of interviews from a dedicated broadcast booth (booth 8011).

52848.cap: Jin-Sik Lee, CEO of Mobilio, poses for a commemorative photo with the quadruped robot ‘LITE 3’. | Photo by AVING News

52848.x: Mobilio, an AI robot platform company located in Pangyo Techno Valley and led by CEO Jin-Sik Lee, aims to create robots that work alongside humans in industrial settings. In an interview, CEO Lee emphasized Mobilio’s vision of Physical AI, stating, “We are a company that develops not just the body of a robot, but also its brain, enabling it to judge and act in the physical world autonomously.”

Founded in September 2020, Mobilio is a startup specializing in industrial Physical AI platforms that integrate artificial intelligence and robotics. The company has established a corporate entity in McLean, Virginia, to enter the North American market and operates a liaison office in Nagasaki, Japan, thereby expanding its global reach. As of October 2025, Mobilio employs 11 staff members and has proprietary core technologies for autonomous driving, including SLAM, autonomous navigation, and sensor fusion algorithms.

The company’s flagship product is the quadruped robot LITE 3. LITE 3, powered by high-output joint motors and sophisticated walking algorithms, boasts maneuverability that can ascend and descend stairs, traverse slopes, and even perform jumps and backflips.

Built on the same platform, various versions are available, including models for research and development, industrial applications, autonomous driving specialized with LiDAR sensors, and entertainment. APIs and SDKs are also provided for research and service development. Users can control LITE 3 via a dedicated app, joystick, or voice commands, and the robot learns to recognize its surroundings, enabling autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance while moving.

52848.cap: Mobilio’s quadruped robot LITE 3 | Image provided by Mobilio

52848.x: CEO Lee Jin-Sik describes LITE 3 as “a robot that has taken another step closer to being like a dog running around and a human understanding situations.” He explains that while previous robots were limited to performing pre-programmed actions triggered by human button presses, Physical AI enables robots to perceive their environment, learn from data, and modify their behavior based on that learning. “One might think of the movie Terminator,” Lee stated, “but our aim is not to replace humans, but rather to be a colleague working alongside them.”

This perspective underpins his view of robots in industrial safety. Industrial sites are becoming increasingly complex and dangerous, while the young labor force is dwindling. Humans, fatigued by long hours, are prone to mistakes, but robots can perform the same tasks repeatedly for 24 hours a day with just a battery recharge. CEO Lee noted, “By deploying robots like LITE 3 into hazardous areas instead of humans, the risk of accidents can be significantly reduced.”

Mobilio is developing various industrial solutions based on robot platforms like LITE 3. Key examples include 360 TWIN, which creates digital twins by capturing site footage with a 360-degree camera; Navigate X, which generates real-time maps by fusing LiDAR and camera data to help robots find their way; AI Inspector, which uses AI vision to detect cracks, damage, gas leaks, and worker safety status; and Logis X, which performs inspections and patrols in logistics warehouses by recognizing labels and barcodes. These solutions hold significant potential for application in demanding work environments across industries such as shipbuilding, construction, manufacturing, logistics and distribution, power plants, and steel production.

52848.cap: Diverse application examples of Mobilio’s LITE 3 | Image provided by Mobilio

52848.x: Furthermore, Mobilio collects real-time environmental data, including vibration, temperature, humidity, fine dust, and gas concentrations, from over 80 types of wireless IoT sensors. This data is analyzed in the integrated dashboard i-mobilio to detect early signs of equipment malfunctions. When necessary, robots like LITE 3 are deployed for detailed on-site inspections, thereby establishing a safety net connecting people, robots, and sensors. In some locations, specialized robot solutions are also being tested to assist with last-mile delivery and fire suppression.

This technological prowess has fostered both domestic and international partnerships. Mobilio conducts joint research with government-funded research institutes, universities, and domestic and international robot manufacturers, leveraging infrastructure in Seongnam and Incheon. The company is also building project references with companies across various industrial sectors, including shipbuilding, heavy industries, automotive, glass, and logistics. CEO Jin-Sik Lee explained, “Our goal is to combine the expertise of each industrial site with our Physical AI technology to create truly beneficial solutions.”

Mobilio is already connected to the global robotics ecosystem, exporting LITE 3 and its self-developed AI engine to overseas markets like Thailand and Mexico. CEO Lee stated, “While many countries around the world manufacture robot hardware, the ‘brain’ technology that enables robots to think and move autonomously still has limited suppliers. Mobilio aims to establish itself as a provider of precisely that ‘brain’.”

52848.cap: Mobilio presented a solution combining AI robots and digital twins. | Image provided by Mobilio

52848.x: Mobilio recently earned external recognition for its technological capabilities by winning a CES 2026 Innovation Award. The company plans to showcase an even more advanced LITE 3 and industrial safety solutions at CES 2026. CEO Lee predicted, “When computers first emerged, only a few experts used them, but now they are essential tools used by everyone in their daily lives. In the near future, an era will come where a robot naturally coexists in every home or workplace.”

He lauded Pangyo Techno Valley as “the Korean Silicon Valley,” noting that it is “the optimal environment for collaboration, networking, and preparing for global expansion due to its concentration of tech startups and talent.” He added, “Korea already possesses world-class manufacturing and ICT capabilities. Mobilio aspires to be the bridge connecting Physical AI robots within this ecosystem, contributing to making Korea a hub for robot AI.”

Mobilio’s Physical AI robots, centered around LITE 3, aim to replace dangerous tasks, enhance industrial safety, and, in the long term, become companions that assist human life and daily routines. The realization of Mobilio’s vision—where robots are partners working alongside humans, rather than replacements—remains a focal point.

The Renuva filters to be unveiled at CES 2026 consist of two types: the superhydrophilic Renuva-Water (RW) and the superoleophilic Renuva-Oil (RO). In addition, ECORENEW Inc. will introduce two purification systems designed for resource circulation: the RenewFlow-Water (RFW) for industrial water purification/treatment and the RenewFlow-Oil (RFO) for industrial oil regeneration.

Renuva-Water (RW) applies fine filtration based on a superhydrophilic nano-coated filter, enabling the selective permeation of water/oil by allowing only water to pass through while removing oil (in water) and other contaminants. Through this process, the purified industrial water achieves a total oil content ≤ 25 ppm.

Renuva-Oil (RO) utilizes a superoleophilic nano-coated filter to separate water (in oil) and fine particulate contaminants from lubricating oil, achieving a water content in regenerated oil ≤ 200 ppm. Both types of Renuva filters are designed to maintain coating stability and separation performance over extended operating periods, with simplified operation and maintenance enabled through cartridge replacement.

The RenewFlow system is a continuous oil-water separation system that integrates Renuva filters into an on-site continuous purification/treatment system (water) and an on-site regeneration system (oil). The RenewFlow-Water (RFW) unit performs real-time purification/treatment of cooling water and process wastewater, while the RenewFlow-Oil (RFO) unit continuously treats used lubricating oil on site, converting it into reusable, high-quality regenerated oil.

Both systems are equipped with an automated control system that enables unattended operation, and apply a low-temperature, low-pressure process to minimize energy consumption. Through waste recycling and reduced consumption of virgin oil, the systems maximize resource circulation efficiency and contribute to reducing indirect (Scope 3) emissions.

ECORENEW Inc.’s core technology converts industrial oil-in-water emulsions and water-in-oil emulsions, including emulsified oil droplets and emulsified water droplets, into high-purity reusable resources. By increasing resource circulation rates and reducing waste, the company’s solutions support corporate ESG management and contribute to achieving carbon neutrality.

The Global Media Meetup focused on introducing Korean companies’ and startups’ products and technologies to the global market. In particular, it aimed to proactively share information on CES 2026 Innovation Award winners and CES-participating startups through global media channels and expand business opportunities.

Uniqconn was founded in 2022 by experts from multiple fields to address bottlenecks that occur in cable- and connector-based high-speed data transmission amid rapidly increasing data transfer speeds, while also improving user convenience.

The company is a fabless firm that designs and develops a single-chip solution capable of wirelessly transmitting data at 6.25 Gbps in the unlicensed 60 GHz band, and it also has in-house capabilities to design mmWave antennas using proprietary technology. Based on this foundation, Uniqconn specializes in providing technologies that replace existing wired interfaces with short-range, high-speed wireless connections for consumer electronics and industrial applications.

Leveraging this technological strength, Uniqconn collaborated with Samsung Electronics to verify and develop wireless solutions for debugging connectors exposed on the exteriors of home appliances, such as refrigerators and washing machines. This demonstrated its capability to process data wirelessly without cables during appliance assembly lines and after-sales service operations. In addition, by verifying wireless Ethernet data communication together with Germany’s Rosenberger, Uniqconn showed that its wireless data transmission technology has gained recognition overseas as well.

Through these efforts, Uniqconn has actively conducted technology validation projects and promotional activities with major domestic and global corporations, thereby presenting a new communication paradigm.

Against this backdrop, ahead of the opening of CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition to be held in Las Vegas, the United States, in January 2026, Uniqconn achieved the milestone of winning an Innovation Award for its small wireless chip ‘UC60,’ which enables high-speed wireless data transmission.

UC60 integrates a transmitter and a receiver into a single chip, enabling full-duplex communication with simultaneous two-way data transmission. The company explained that a key technical challenge was preventing interference from the transmitted signal from affecting the receiver.

To address this, the chip incorporates a dedicated isolation circuit that maintains signal clarity even when transmission and reception operate simultaneously. In addition, Uniqconn’s proprietary antenna technology provides additional external isolation, ensuring stable performance in real-world usage environments. The chip uses ASK modulation for data encoding.

Operating at 60 GHz, UC60 maintains ultra-low latency and high-reliability signal quality even at gigabit-class transmission speeds, making it well-suited for real-time streaming and interactive applications. This RF-based approach eliminates issues such as connector wear, corrosion, and electromagnetic interference (EMI), positioning the solution as a replacement for conventional connectors in applications requiring high-reliability, high-speed wireless data transmission, including docking stations, wearables, and fully sealed electronic devices.

The ultra-compact 3.5×3.5mm form factor of UC60 also has the potential to bring fundamental changes to electronic product design philosophy. By using flip-chip BGA packaging, the chip delivers high performance while occupying minimal PCB space, enabling smaller, slimmer product designs. By removing physical connectors, UC60 allows for smooth, portless exteriors, offering particular advantages for products where clean design matters, such as wearables, waterproof electronics, and premium consumer devices.

Furthermore, the wireless-based architecture removes existing constraints such as impedance matching issues and EMI associated with metal connectors. As a result, designers gain unprecedented freedom in component placement and routing, while also resolving reliability issues caused by connector wear and exposure to external environments.

52972.cap: Uniqconn CEO Young Dong Kim presents at the Global Media Meetup held on Tuesday, December 9, at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul. | Photo by AVING News

The solution has also been recognized for its innovation as a wireless platform that supports high-speed wired protocols. A Uniqconn official said, “Existing wireless technologies such as Wi-Fi struggle to reliably handle high-speed wired protocols that require strict bit error rates and precise timing. Gigabit Ethernet, USB 3.0, and MIPI interfaces demand data integrity and reliability beyond what conventional wireless technologies can provide.” The official added, “UC60 is a wireless solution that can bridge this technical gap and meet the demanding performance standards required by high-speed wired protocols.”

The official continued, “UC60 has a unique capability to convert high-speed wired interfaces into wireless connections within conditions of one-to-one communication within two meters and power consumption below 1 watt. This technological innovation fundamentally resolves the trade-off that had been unavoidable between ‘wireless convenience’ and ‘high-performance data transmission.’”

In addition, UC60 features a ‘Tap-to-Connect’ approach, where a high-speed data link forms instantly when devices are brought close together. Because it does not require separate pairing or authentication procedures, it delivers an intuitive and immediate user experience that is difficult to achieve with conventional wireless technologies.

This technology enables a modular device ecosystem. For example, detachable smartphone cameras, stacked computing modules, and AR accessories can connect naturally through simple contact. Users can physically attach compatible components to expand device functionality and configure devices in the form they desire.

Uniqconn positions itself as a wireless communication technology company proposing a new communication paradigm and aims to spread its technology across global industrial markets. 52981.cap: NUCODE’s ultra-low-power IoT communication modules and development boards integrated with external devices and modules. The modular expansion architecture supports a wide range of IoT device development and testing environments. | Source – NUCODE

52981.x: As artificial intelligence (AI) technologies continue to advance, the Internet of Things (IoT) is once again gaining strategic importance. By enabling sensors and devices to exchange data through network connectivity, IoT has become a core technology across smart cities, healthcare, industrial safety, and security. However, the global IoT market remains heavily dependent on communication modules sourced from specific regions, raising persistent concerns around technical support limitations, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and supply chain risks. As a result, demand is growing for more stable, flexible, and accessible IoT development environments.

NUCODE (CEO Bruce Lee) was founded to address these challenges. Centered on its ultra-low-power IoT communication modules, branded as the “NU Module,” and its integrated development environment, “NU-Works,” the company offers a modular development platform designed to make IoT product and service development significantly more accessible. Leveraging this technology, NUCODE plans to showcase its solutions to the global market at CES 2026.

NUCODE develops and manufactures ultra-compact, ultra-low-power IoT communication modules based on Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and Wi-Fi. Operating in unlicensed frequency bands including 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz, the modules are optimized for battery-powered devices and environments with limited power availability. According to the company, the modules achieve superior power efficiency compared to competing products under similar conditions, making them well-suited for IoT devices that require long-term operation.

A key differentiator of NUCODE’s approach lies in the dual-purpose design of its modules. Unlike conventional IoT development processes—where development kits, prototype boards, and mass-production components are typically separate—NUCODE’s modules are designed to support hardware integration, wireless communication, testing, and mass production within a single form factor. This unified approach reduces both initial development costs and reliance on specialized equipment.

52981.cap: Prototype of NUCODE’s ultra-low-power IoT communication module. Featuring a compact BLE-based design, the module is suitable for both development and mass production. | Photo – AVING News

52981.x: In addition, NUCODE provides its proprietary development environment, NU-Works, which helps users understand hardware design flows and communication structures even without deep technical expertise. By combining hardware modules with an integrated development platform, NUCODE aims to significantly lower the entry barrier to hardware and IoT development.

This strategy was further validated during the “:BUILD Physical AI Vibe Coding Hackathon 2025 (1st Edition),” held in late September. The hackathon, themed “Bluetooth Remote Control Ideas through Vibe Coding,” was conducted in collaboration with global technology companies and organizations including Glimpse, AskItMore, Nordic Semiconductor, TE Connectivity, and Geekble.

During the event, each team was provided with two NU40 DK units (based on the nRF52840 development platform) and personal smartphones. Participants successfully implemented Bluetooth-based remote control applications within a single day. Notably, more than half of the participants were non-developers—such as students, designers, planners, and marketers—yet every team achieved full functionality, including LED control and mobile app integration.

Today, NUCODE’s technology is being applied across a wide range of use cases, including construction site safety SOS buttons, medical biometric monitoring devices, vehicle and maritime safety equipment, smart city sensors, and security CCTV pilot projects. Several customers using NUCODE modules have demonstrated their technological competitiveness through international exhibitions and public-sector deployments.

Security and supply chain resilience have also become key factors driving global interest in NUCODE. The global IoT market’s heavy reliance on cost-competitive modules from a limited number of regions has intensified concerns over geopolitical risks, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and potential supply disruptions. In sensitive sectors such as smart homes, industrial sensors, and security systems, module-level reliability and source code controllability are increasingly critical decision criteria.

Against this backdrop, NUCODE positions its internally designed and developed ultra-low-power IoT modules as a compelling alternative. The company emphasizes full source code control and the ability to tailor designs to meet region- and market-specific security requirements. This approach offers global enterprises and system integrators (SIs) a viable option to diversify supply chains while addressing both security and operational stability.

The device supports use not only in hospital environments such as operating rooms, recovery rooms, and intensive care units, but also in home settings. It features a non-invasive heat-flux measurement method.

Heat flux is a physical quantity that quantitatively expresses the flow of heat through a surface, i.e., the thermal energy transferred per unit area per unit time. Thermosafer XST600 measures this value at the skin and reflects metabolic heat generated within the body and heat exchange via blood flow to estimate core body temperature.

Unlike conventional thermometers that primarily reflect skin temperature, the device analyzes heat flow through the skin to derive values closer to core body temperature. For this reason, it has drawn attention as an alternative for continuous patient temperature tracking in medical settings, demonstrating particular value in environments that require precise temperature control, such as operating rooms, intensive care units, and recovery rooms.

Without professional editing expertise, users can create brand promotions, product introductions, greeting messages, and event videos, with fast production and low cost highlighted as key strengths.

At present, ‘GemGem Video’ is in the service validation and expansion stage, centered on the domestic market. In the future, 10kM.ai is considering expansion into the United States, Japan, and Southeast Asia. The company said, “Demand for mobile-based short-form content is growing rapidly in these regions, and we expect GemGem Video to be highly competitive.”

The company added, “Along with advancing the B2C service of ‘GemGem Video,’ we plan to expand a B2B SaaS version. Through industry-specific templates and global localization, we aim to strengthen our position as an AI video production platform.”

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. 52994.cap: CES 2026 INCHEON-IFEZ poster | Provided by Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority

52994.x: The Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority (Incheon Free Economic Zone, hereinafter IFEZ Authority) announced on the 18th that it will participate in CES, the world’s largest information technology exhibition, for the third consecutive year to present Incheon’s AI city vision on the global stage.

From January 6 to 9 next year, at CES 2026 in Las Vegas, the United States, the IFEZ Authority will operate the ‘Incheon City–IFEZ Pavilion’ under the theme “Destination Incheon—From Smart City to AI City: The Next Evolution of Urban Life.”

CES (Consumer Electronics Show) takes place every January in Las Vegas and serves as a global platform where the latest technology trends and business opportunities converge. The IFEZ Authority will set up the pavilion in the AI Zone of the North Hall at the Las Vegas Convention Center (LVCC).

The CES 2026 Incheon City–IFEZ Pavilion will consist of the AI Smart Living Zone, which enhances citizen services such as mobility, safety, energy, and health; the AI Innovation Hub Zone, which drives innovation across industrial sites including manufacturing, logistics, food, and pharmaceuticals; and the AI Creative City Zone, which creates content and experiences. Through these zones, the pavilion will showcase Incheon’s innovative technologies as the city evolves beyond a smart city into an AI city.

On the opening day, January 6, following the opening ceremony, the main stage inside the Incheon City–IFEZ Pavilion will host various programs, including a Global AI City Session. Global city and industry experts will gather to discuss practical collaboration strategies to support Incheon’s leap from a smart city to an AI city.

On the second day, the ‘CES 2026 INCHEON Night’ event will bring together participating Incheon companies and overseas firms for networking aimed at fostering practical cooperation. Investors, buyers, and global partners will join the exchange, with partnership discussions and demo showcases taking place throughout the event.

On January 8, the authority will operate an intensive business day for 15 visiting companies, supporting overseas expansion through one-on-one matching and on-site meetings with buyers, venture capital firms, and accelerators.

The IFEZ Authority will showcase technologies from 10 innovative companies within the zone and support the CES participation of 51 companies, including 10 in the Eureka Park Integrated Korea Pavilion, 6 in the Global Pavilion Korea Pavilion, 15 visiting companies, and 10 showcase companies. Beyond simple exhibition participation, the authority will strengthen support by linking investor and global partner meetings, demo showcases, and local networking to achieve tangible global expansion outcomes.

The IFEZ Authority has prepared startups to participate in CES through programs such as pre-arranged business matching, global media meetups, training for international exhibitions, and support for the CES Innovation Awards. In particular, 14 companies won 17 CES Innovation Awards, the highest total ever. This year, given the record number of Innovation Awards, the authority plans to provide additional support by operating a CES Innovation Award Showcase for award-winning companies, further enhancing global visibility and follow-up business opportunities.

Incheon Mayor Jeong-bok Yoo said, “CES 2026 is an important opportunity to elevate the global capabilities of Incheon and its companies to the next level.” He added, “Under the ‘Destination Incheon’ theme, we will share IFEZ’s AI city strategy with the world and do our utmost to position Incheon not as a city people simply pass through, but as a destination the world heads toward and a global innovation city in the AI era.”
Detailed information on participating companies and programs is available through the official CES 2026 INCHEON-IFEZ website.

52996.cap: Officials pose for a commemorative photo at the launch ceremony for the CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion. | Provided by Seoul Business Agency

52996.x: The Seoul Business Agency (SBA, President and CEO Hyunwoo Kim) held the “CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion Launch Ceremony” on the 1st. It reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring a successful participation at CES 2026.

CES (Consumer Electronics Show) is the world’s largest technology exhibition, held every early January in Las Vegas, the United States, where global corporations such as Google and Samsung, along with startups, present future technology visions and cutting-edge products and services.

CES 2026 will take place from January 6 to 9 next year. The Seoul Pavilion will be located in Eureka Park, the startup-focused exhibition zone, and will operate as a dedicated pavilion showcasing advanced startups based in Seoul.

The Seoul Metropolitan Government and the Seoul Business Agency plan to promote Seoul startups’ global innovation by leveraging the collective strength of Seoul’s startup ecosystem, and to support international expansion through programs such as business matching and a global startup IR pitching competition.

The CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion will host 70 startups, with participation from 19 Seoul-based startup support organizations, including the lead organization SBA, district governments, related institutions, and universities. In addition, 70 university student supporters will be selected and matched one-to-one with participating companies to provide on-site support.

The 19 participating organizations include four district offices—Gangnam-gu Office, Gwanak-gu Office, Guro-gu Office, and Geumcheon-gu Office—six Seoul Metropolitan Government–affiliated startup support institutions, including the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), Seoul Campus Town Enterprise Growth Center, Seoul Tourism Organization, Seoul Social Venture Hub, Seoul AI Hub, and Seoul Fintech Lab (Yeouido), as well as nine universities based in Seoul: Konkuk University, Kyung Hee University, Kwangwoon University, Sogang University, Seoul National University, Sungkyunkwan University, Yonsei University, Ewha Womans University, and Chung-Ang University.
The 70 companies exhibiting in the Seoul Pavilion consist of startups with advanced technology–based products and services in fields such as AI, mobility, and healthcare.

52996.cap: Overview of the CES 2025 Seoul Pavilion held earlier this year. | Photo by AVING News

52996.x: To enhance external recognition and global visibility of Seoul startups’ innovation, SBA provided support for Innovation Award applications, including advanced consulting, for approximately two months from July to August. As a result, a total of 17 companies, including one Best of Innovation award winner, were selected for the CES 2026 Innovation Awards. The CES Innovation Awards are presented annually by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), the exhibition organizer, to technologies and products recognized for technological excellence, design, and innovation.

The Best of Innovation award was won by Studio Lab Co., Ltd., a member of the SBA-operated Innovation Award community, which proudly stood alongside global conglomerates such as Samsung and Qualcomm. The achievement is especially meaningful, as the award is granted to only about 30 companies worldwide each year.
SBA operates a CES Innovation Award community for award-winning companies and plans to continue follow-up support programs, including inter-company collaboration.

In addition, SBA plans to offer a broader range of business programs for participating companies, including pre-event and on-site investment and buyer matching, cross-country IR pitching and networking, investor networking events, exhibition booths, and on-site IR pitching, and on-site support by university student supporters.

SBA will closely manage the process from online matching before the exhibition to successful on-site meetings with buyers expected to attend CES. Participating companies will also receive sales opportunities, including participation in IR pitching sessions on the Seoul Pavilion stage.

The “University Student Supporters” program, which matches outstanding students selected by partner universities with participating companies on a one-to-one basis, will also be operated. This year, 70 global talents fluent in both English and Korean will be deployed on site, selected from nine Seoul-based universities and graduates of universities in Las Vegas, the United States.

52996.cap: Visitors at the CES 2025 Seoul Pavilion held earlier this year. | Photo by AVING News

52996.x: Participating companies will also gain comprehensive promotional and investment opportunities through the Global Innovation Forum, a national pavilion networking program hosted by the SBA. One outstanding company will be selected to compete in the forum’s flagship session, the Global Startup IR Pitching Competition.

Support will also be provided for participation in a Korean entrepreneur conference held near the CES venue in San Francisco, as well as the 2026 UKF 82 Startup Summit scheduled for January 9 to 12. Participating companies will receive admission tickets, and one outstanding company will have the opportunity to participate in an on-site pitching session. UKF is a nonprofit organization that supports the growth and mutual support of Korean entrepreneurs and startup ecosystem members, co-chaired by Gihah Lee, CEO of unicorn startup Sazze Partners, and Seju Jung, CEO of Noom.

In addition, SBA will provide a range of pre-education programs to maximize CES participation outcomes, from basic CES orientation to sales know-how, reflecting business trends such as LinkedIn. Various promotional programs will also be operated for supported companies. Each year, SBA develops new programs to enhance promotional impact, and this year it will introduce the ‘Innovation Award Showcase’ and ‘Media Center’ within the Seoul Pavilion.

The newly introduced Seoul Pavilion Innovation Award Showcase will serve as a promotional space for Innovation Award–winning companies. It will be placed at the pavilion’s main entrance to capture visitors’ attention. The Media Center, a filming and interview space inside the pavilion, will function as a hub for producing new media content that highlights exhibiting companies.

Selected outstanding companies will also have the opportunity to participate in CES’s official media event, Unveiled, which is aimed at major global media outlets, to maximize media exposure. SBA will further enhance media visibility for exhibiting companies by distributing press releases through collaboration with CES’s official global media partners and specialized outlets.

52996.cap: SBA President and CEO Hyunwoo Kim delivers opening remarks at the CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion launch ceremony. | Provided by Seoul Business Agency

52996.x: Meanwhile, the CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion Launch Ceremony, held on December 1 at SBA Hall, served as a declaration of the launch of a “one team” comprising companies, institutions, and university student supporters, and announced the pavilion’s operational plan. During the ceremony, participants received detailed guidance on key support items, exhibition preparation, and upcoming schedules, as well as training sessions to share CES participation know-how and strengthen global business capabilities.

The ceremony was attended by key officials from the 19 partner organizations, including SBA President and CEO Hyunwoo Kim and Center Director Mija Oh of Konkuk University’s WE人 Education Center. University student supporters for the Seoul Pavilion also attended, familiarizing themselves with exhibition participation details alongside their matched companies and strengthening their shared commitment.

Hyunwoo Kim, President and CEO of the Seoul Business Agency, said, “CES is a stage where global big tech companies and the startup ecosystem converge, and it offers the optimal opportunity for Seoul startups to connect directly with global investors, partners, and media.” He added, “SBA will spare no effort to provide a platform that enables Seoul companies to leap into the global market, using the Seoul Pavilion as a stepping stone.”

52997.cap: Visitors at the Seoul Pavilion during CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

52997.x: The Seoul Business Agency (SBA, President and CEO Hyunwoo Kim) announced on the 29th that it produced 17 CES 2026 Innovation Award–winning companies, including one Best of Innovation winner.

The CES Innovation Awards are presented in conjunction with CES, the world’s largest technology exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA). The awards recognize the most outstanding products and services through a comprehensive evaluation of innovation, technological excellence, and market potential. Winning a CES Innovation Award is a key indicator of global competitiveness.

The Seoul Business Agency has worked with 18 startup support organizations representing Seoul’s startup ecosystem to establish and operate the CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion and to provide consulting support for CES Innovation Award applications. As a result, SBA produced 17 CES 2026 Innovation Award Honorees and one Best of Innovation winner, achieving a milestone that showcased Seoul startups’ technological strength and innovation on the global stage.

Among the 17 CES 2026 Innovation Award winners, STUDIO LAB received the CES Best of Innovation Award, which goes to only about 30 companies worldwide each year, including major conglomerates. This marks STUDIO LAB’s second Best of Innovation win following CES 2024. Meanwhile, Otiton Medical, which has participated in CES under the Seoul Pavilion in both 2025 and 2026, once again earned a CES Innovation Award, achieving back-to-back wins. These results underscore how the Seoul Pavilion support program drives the sustainable growth of participating companies.

Sunghoon Kang, CEO of STUDIO LAB and a two-time Best of Innovation winner, pointed to SBA’s Innovation Award consulting as a key factor behind the achievement. Kang said, “I sincerely thank SBA for its generous, long-term support, including CES Innovation Award consulting, which enabled STUDIO LAB to pursue distinctive AI and robotics R&D. We will continue to create results through ongoing collaboration.” He added, “As AI models and robotics technologies advance rapidly, STUDIO LAB continues research to apply these innovations meaningfully to everyday life. We are delighted that the global market has recognized our work, and receiving the Best of Innovation Award for two years is a great honor. We will keep listening closely to customers so that companies and brands worldwide can gain tangible benefits through our technology.”

Jayden Kim, CEO of Otiton Medical, said, “Winning the CES Innovation Award reflects the combination of Otiton Medical’s technology and systematic consulting.” He added, “Market analysis and product positioning by professional consultants helped us establish our identity, which I believe led to our consecutive wins,” emphasizing the effectiveness of the CES Innovation Award consulting.

52997.cap: Otiton Medical’s pet smart thermometer wins a CES 2026 Innovation Award in the Mobile & Apps category. | Provided by Seoul Business Agency

52997.x: SBA’s CES Innovation Award consulting program pairs startups one-on-one with experts, with dedicated consultants providing close support from application drafting through submission. The program offers professional editing and English proofreading of applications and submission materials. It helps companies prepare and refine promotional assets, such as English-language websites and product videos, to meet global evaluation standards. SBA provides multiple rounds of feedback and ongoing Q&A support through the deadline, and guides companies through every step of the application process so they can craft product strategies aligned with judging criteria and submit highly polished applications.

The consultants’ capabilities also stand out. Through a cross-check system that brings together investment-focused accelerators, technical reviewers, and native English editors, the program delivers intensive one-on-one consulting to maximize engineering, design, and innovation—the core evaluation criteria for the awards.

In addition, engineering PhDs from leading U.S. research institutes analyze each company’s R&D capabilities to identify competitive strengths. At the same time, experts with experience as venture CEOs and KOSDAQ listing committee members assess global business appeal. Native English-speaking engineers from top overseas universities and global startup founders further enhance the quantitative and qualitative quality of applications with storytelling expertise, forming the core strategy of the program.

Within the community, companies voluntarily engage in small-scale team-building activities, while the SBA supports the formation and operation of these groups and provides grants to encourage collaborative outcomes. SBA also operates online communication channels to collect feedback and share information about support programs, increasing accessibility for participating companies. At the same time, SBA strengthens practical collaboration and results by linking internal and external resources through customized growth support programs that back companies’ post-CES development.

Through these efforts, SBA goes beyond simple exhibition support and builds a sustained support system that strengthens companies’ overseas expansion capabilities even after CES. By expanding cooperation networks with universities, public institutions, and private companies across Seoul, SBA continues to lay a solid foundation for Seoul’s startup ecosystem that supports companies throughout their entire growth cycle.

Hyunwoo Kim, President and CEO of the Seoul Business Agency, said, “I am proud of the Seoul startups that achieve outstanding results at CES every year.” He added, “By producing numerous Innovation Award winners annually, Seoul continues to prove the innovation and potential of its startup ecosystem in the global market. SBA will keep leveraging diverse support programs and close collaboration across public and private networks in Seoul to build an advanced, Seoul-style startup ecosystem that drives stronger global expansion outcomes.”

53000.cap: An example of an AI tracking and beamforming-based wireless power transmission system delivering RF energy to multiple devices | Provided by Warp Solution

53000.x: Warp Solution Inc. (CEO Kyunghak Lee) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition, to be held in Las Vegas, the United States, from Tuesday, January 6 to Friday, January 9 (local time).

Warp Solution is a Korean fabless company that has commercialized long-range, multi-device simultaneous wireless power transmission (WTP) technology using radio-frequency (RF) technology. The company has developed core semiconductor products for 5G- and RF-based wireless charging technologies, including ultra-compact RF power amplifiers and high-frequency rectifier components. It has secured several domestic and international intellectual property rights.

Building on this foundation, Warp Solution is also developing a radio energy platform with strong scalability across advanced industries such as IoT, smart homes, industrial automation, and healthcare, as well as AI-powered power control solutions. Through these efforts, the company aims to universalize innovative wireless charging environments across industrial and smart device markets.

At CES 2026, Warp Solution will present its WTP system that combines AI tracking and beamforming technologies. The system uses vision AI camera algorithms to track the location of receivers in real time within the coverage area, optimizes the path and angle of long-range RF energy delivery through AI beamforming, and implements adaptive RF directivity tailored in real time to constantly changing charging locations and environments.

The RF energy transmitted over long distances is converted into usable charging power through dedicated receivers. Warp Solution integrates its core semiconductor technologies, including RF power amplifier devices and high-frequency rectifier components, to deliver more stable, advanced energy. In particular, the company’s proprietary RF-DC rectifier chip “WEP” series supports power conversion efficiency of up to 60 percent.

In addition, efficient power distribution and transmission algorithms enable simultaneous wireless charging of multiple devices, while support for a wide frequency range from 100 MHz to 6 GHz ensures broad charging compatibility. These technological strengths translate into significantly greater freedom and spatial flexibility compared to conventional wireless charging methods.

Warp Solution plans to introduce its differentiated wireless charging technology at CES 2026 and accelerate full-scale expansion into global industries. A company official said, “Our multi-device long-range wireless charging platform delivers high utility across fields such as IoT, smart homes, and smart factories,” adding, “For example, when applied to industrial IoT sensors or edge devices that operate in large spaces with frequent movement or where battery replacement is difficult, it can serve as core infrastructure that maximizes productivity and operational continuity.”

The official continued, “By enabling stable and efficient power transmission anytime and anywhere, we aim to attract partners and potential customers across a wide range of domestic and global industries, while promoting the spread and standardization of next-generation wireless charging platforms,” emphasizing that “this year’s CES will be a critical testing ground for determining the success of these goals.”
