53001.cap: Neurélux brain health lighting solution | Provided by Korea Lighting

53001.x: Korea Lighting Inc. (CEO Dongwoo Lee) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition, to be held in Las Vegas, the United States, from Tuesday, January 6 to Friday, January 9 (local time).

Korea Lighting is a company specializing in functional optical semiconductor platforms and solutions. The company has steadily introduced products to domestic and global markets that support beauty and health improvement while also delivering substantial aesthetic value as lighting fixtures.

In particular, Korea Lighting has earned recognition for its technological edge through its core proprietary technology, HS FRAME, which integrates LED chips, circuitry, and thermal management into a single platform. The company explained that this technology enables stable, efficient output at high-power wavelengths suitable for medical-grade applications, while also enhancing design completeness and flexibility in compact platform products.

At CES 2026, Korea Lighting will highlight its healthcare product Neurélux, which is based on the HS FRAME technology. The company describes Neurélux as an “Ambient Brain Healthcare” solution that enables brain health management within everyday living environments.

As a wellness product, Neurélux derives its functionality from two near-infrared wavelengths, 810 nm and 1,064 nm. The 810 nm wavelength promotes mitochondrial activation in brain cells and plays a key role in neuroprotection and regeneration. It is selectively absorbed by cytochrome c oxidase, increasing the production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), a high-energy compound that, in turn, supports the recovery of damaged neural tissue and reduces inflammation.

53001.cap: Neurélux used as a bedside lamp | Provided by Korea Lighting

53001.x: The 1,064 nm wavelength penetrates more deeply into brain tissue, generating subtle thermal stimulation that activates ion channels in cell membranes, increasing neuroplasticity and cerebral blood flow. This effect enhances the supply of oxygen and nutrients to brain cells and supports higher-order cognitive functions such as working memory and attention.

Neurélux also offers high usability in daily life through an adjustable stand joint that flexibly adapts to installation locations, along with a minimalist design. Users can also use it as a general household lighting fixture, similar to a conventional lamp, by operating it as a light source rather than an infrared emitter. Unlike wearable devices that require continuous physical contact for biometric monitoring, Neurélux adopts a non-invasive, non-contact approach, further improving accessibility.

A Korea Lighting official said, “Neurélux is a solution that helps manage age-related dementia, one of the major challenges of a super-aged society, as well as various sleep disorders, in everyday life and in a completely new way,” adding, “As the industry’s first non-contact brain healthcare solution, we expect it to reshape the related market and secure a clear technological advantage.”

The official continued, “Neurélux will be unveiled for the first time at CES 2026 ahead of its launch in March, and this exhibition will serve as a key stage for accelerating the globalization of Korea Lighting as a functional optical semiconductor platform company,” adding, “Through this event, we plan to pursue strategic partnerships with leading healthcare companies and buyers in North America and Europe, and work to establish our proprietary technology as a global standard.”
Special coverage team: Dongkwan Kim, Gyeongha Lee, Jaeman Lee, Joseph Choe, Kidai Kim, Min Choi, Minseok Cha, Myungjin Shin, Mokkyung Lee, Seung Hyun Nam, Wonjae Jung

53002.cap: The image above is not a movie poster about robots. M.AX stands for Manufacturing AX (Manufacturing AI Transformation), a policy term used within the next-generation industrial strategy framework promoted by Korea’s Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy. It is not a simple brand name, but a strategic concept and key policy term that represents a fundamental AI-driven transformation of the entire manufacturing industry and symbolizes Korea’s national industrial transition. | Photo – AVING News

53002.x: The word most frequently heard on the CES 2026 keynote stage was “AI,” but the real theme that cut through the exhibition floor was far clearer. AI is no longer an algorithm confined to a screen—it has become a moving entity. At the center of this shift were robots, particularly humanoid robots.

Global semiconductor and computing companies, including AMD, identified “Physical AI” as the next destination of AI computation, while global manufacturing giants such as Hyundai Motor Group and LG positioned robots not as future concepts, but as immediately deployable industrial forces. CES 2026 clearly demonstrated that the show has fully transitioned from an exhibition of TVs and home appliances into a venue where robots compete head-on.

53002.cap: The Humanoid M.AX Alliance joint pavilion at CES 2026, crowded with global robotics companies, buyers, and media, continuously drew visitors throughout the event. | Photo – AVING News
The upper body of a Neuromeka-based humanoid robot unveiled at CES 2026 highlights precision control and industrial applicability. | Photo – AVING News

53002.x: Amid these changes, one space stood out with particularly strong presence—the Humanoid M.AX Alliance joint pavilion at CES 2026. Rather than listing individual corporate technologies, the exhibition brought together the overall structure and strategy of Korea’s humanoid industry into a single space. On site, it was naturally described as “a must-see booth at CES 2026” and “one of the most threatening robot booths.”

The M.AX Alliance joint pavilion is not led by a single institution. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy sets the policy direction, while the Korea Evaluation Institute of Industrial Technology (KEIT) serves as the secretariat overseeing the overall M.AX Alliance structure. The humanoid division is practically operated through cooperation between the Korea Institute for Robot Industry Advancement and the Korea Association of Robot Industry. The structure itself—where policy, public institutions, and industry operate as one continuous flow—constitutes the pavilion’s core message.

53002.cap: Global engineers and domestic robotics company representatives participating in the M.AX Alliance examine humanoid robot hand technologies together. | Photo – AVING News
Global visitors at the Humanoid M.AX Alliance pavilion closely observe robot hand technologies, showing strong interest in Korea’s collective humanoid ecosystem strategy. | Photo – AVING News

53002.x: The exhibition concept was also clear. The M.AX Alliance pavilion chose field-based,proof-of-concept demonstrations over a simple technology display. Instead of placing a single robot on display, multiple types of robots performed demonstrations based on real manufacturing scenarios, intuitively showing “where and how these robots can be used.”

This design went beyond passive viewing, enabling demand companies, component suppliers, and visiting corporate delegations to immediately begin business discussions on site. The decision to locate the pavilion in the Enterprise AI Zone rather than Eureka Park was also a strategic choice, positioning humanoid robots not as startup experiments but as industrial solutions ready for immediate deployment.

The response on site was intense. Crowds gathered in front of the booth throughout the exhibition, and VIP inbound tour schedules were fully booked for two consecutive days. Delegations from the National Assembly, local governments, public institutions, as well as major corporations such as Doosan, Samsung SDS, LG, and KT visited the pavilion, with meetings focused on real collaboration opportunities rather than simple observation. “It’s rare to see this many people gathered around a hardware robotics booth,” was a common reaction. Industry observers even rated the M.AX Alliance pavilion as one of the Top 10 booths at CES 2026.

53002.cap: From left, Byungtak Jang, founding chair of the Humanoid M.AX Alliance and professor at Seoul National University; Jaekwon Han, CEO of AEIROBOT; and Jangbeom Park, CEO of KBS, tour the M.AX Alliance pavilion at CES 2026. | Photo – AVING News

53002.x: Professor Byungtak Jang of Seoul National University described the Humanoid M.AX Alliance as “a strategy collectively chosen by Korea to become a global leader in humanoid robotics, and a declaration of national robotics strategy.” Since its launch in April with around 40 companies and universities, the alliance has expanded within just a few months into a large-scale ecosystem of more than 250 partners, including AI firms, robot manufacturers, core component suppliers, universities, research institutes, and actual robot users. Professor Jang explained that the pace of this growth itself reflects both the sense of crisis and rising expectations surrounding the humanoid industry.

He defined humanoid robots as the core battlefield of the Physical AI era following generative AI, representing the final stage where AI becomes physically embodied in industrial settings. Given the explosive growth projected for the global humanoid market over the next decade, he noted that Korea would struggle to break the U.S.–China duopoly if it remained confined to competition at the level of individual firms.

“The biggest differentiator is that those who create the technology and those who actually use it are bound together in a single alliance,” Professor Jang emphasized. He added that the Humanoid M.AX Alliance is not merely a consultative body, but a platform in which the public and private sectors jointly design both the direction and speed of the humanoid industry, with the goal of securing leadership not only in technology, but also in global standards and ecosystems.

53002.cap: Ki-won Kang, President of the Korea Institute for Robot Industry Advancement, conducts an interview at CES 2026 in front of the Humanoid M.AX Alliance pavilion. | Photo – AVING News

53002.x: Regarding global competition, President Kang described the joint pavilion as “a rare moment when a national team was formed in the robotics sector.” While the United States advances through Big Tech–driven AI model competition and China grows its robotics industry through state-led scale and volume, Korea has chosen to consolidate its limited resources through an alliance-based approach. Sharing dispersed technologies and jointly developing necessary areas, he explained, represents Korea’s most realistic competitive strategy.

Kang particularly highlighted Korea’s data competitiveness. Massive process data accumulated in manufacturing sites, world-class ICT and communications infrastructure, and high-level surgical data from medical fields constitute key assets in the Physical AI era. “Korea already has doctors known as ‘master surgeons,’” he said, adding that the emergence of “robot master surgeons” would not be unrealistic once robots begin learning from their surgical data. What Korea’s humanoid industry must prove after CES 2026, he stressed, is not technology demonstrations, but the ability to operate reliably in real-world environments based on data.

53002.cap: Park Ji-won, Vice Chairman of Doosan Group (far left), visits the Humanoid M.AX Alliance pavilion at CES 2026, conducting a VIP tour while examining humanoid robot technologies. | Photo – AVING News

Overview of the Humanoid M.AX Alliance joint pavilion. From core robot drive components to precision reducers, sensors, robot hands, control technologies, and fully assembled humanoid robots, the entire value chain is presented within a single alliance framework. The exhibition allows visitors to directly observe how component suppliers, robot manufacturers, and AI technology companies are seamlessly connected. | Photo – AVING News

A fully assembled humanoid robot on display at the Humanoid M.AX Alliance joint pavilion. Built on core drive components and control technologies, the robot is presented through live operation demonstrations, symbolically showcasing Korea’s humanoid strategy realized through a unified alliance framework—from components to finished products. | Photo – AVING News

53002.x: “The era of ideas is over—this is now a war of collective strategies that actually move robots.”

Innovation is no longer a matter of ideas, but of collective execution. From the very first day of the exhibition, robots took center stage across keynote sessions and major conference programs without exception. A shift from generative AI to the era of Physical AI was formally declared, and major corporations from around the world rushed to unveil their respective robotics strategies and application scenarios. CES 2026 has become less a venue for previewing technology trends and more the opening ceremony of a full-scale robot war—one that tests who can deploy robots into real industrial battlefields first.

Amid this intense competitive landscape, the Humanoid M.AX Alliance joint pavilion drew not only neighboring countries’ robotics companies but also representatives from global brands, prompting repeated questions such as, “Why is Korea organized in this way?” and “How does this structure actually work?”

53002.cap: Overseas visitors gather in front of the M.AX Alliance booth, listening to explanations of humanoid technologies and recording videos in real time. | Photo – AVING News
Overseas visitors stand in front of the M.AX Alliance booth, listening to explanations of humanoid technologies and recording videos in real time. | Photo – AVING News

53002.x: This was not a demonstration of technology by a single company, but a rare example showing how an entire nation designs and executes its robotics industry. At the heart of the CES 2026 exhibition—transformed into a full-scale battleground for robots—the M.AX Alliance joint pavilion naturally emerged as a benchmark.

At a moment when major corporations from around the world are stepping onto the stage with robots at the forefront, Korea is responding through the M.AX Alliance not as “one company,” but as “one national team.” By integrating research and development, manufacturing and components, and real market demand into a single structure, the alliance represents not merely an exhibition strategy, but Korea’s chosen mode of survival and a declaration of challenge in the global robotics industry.

53003.x: Luchrome, a pioneering French startup specializing in next-generation connected electronics displays, announced that it will unveil its proprietary ultra-low-power display platform, Lusight, at CES 2026, held from January 6 to 9 in Las Vegas, United States.

Founded in 2023, Luchrome has focused on developing display technologies that dramatically reduce energy consumption and improve how humans and machines communicate. The company received strong validation from the global technology community after being selected as a winner of the prestigious CES Innovation Award in the Sustainability & Energy Transition category, a recognition reserved for only a small fraction of applicants.

The award-winning platform Lusight represents a major shift in electronic display philosophy. Unlike conventional displays that require constant high power and complex integration, Lusight was engineered as a modular system that can be easily embedded in any connected object. According to Luchrome, the platform consumes up to ten times less power than current displays, making it suitable for truly autonomous, battery-efficient, and sustainable devices.

After years of research and development, the Lusight platform is now entering its final qualification phase. Luchrome explained that the technology will be available for pre-order starting in 2026, following qualification, and that commercial availability will begin with industry-focused showcases scheduled from March 2026.

CEO Romain Futsch emphasized the broader vision behind the debut. “With Lusight, we are reinventing electronic displays to address the energy and technological challenges of tomorrow. IFA 2025 and CES 2026 are not just exhibition participations for us, but important stages where we demonstrate Made in France responsible innovation to global buyers, partners, and consumers,” he said.

At CES 2026, Luchrome will conduct live demonstrations at Booth 60412 in the French Pavilion at Eureka Park, Hall G, Venetian Expo Center, presenting interactive Lusight experiences and diverse real-world applications. The company aims to showcase how Lusight can be applied to healthcare, industrial automation, logistics equipment, and consumer electronics markets worldwide.

Luchrome stated that CES 2026 will serve as a strategic launchpad for international collaboration. Through engagement with global media journalists, investors, and advanced-industry buyers, the company plans to expand API integration partnerships and propose a new global standard for energy-efficient human-machine interfaces.

The company also expressed gratitude to its ecosystem supporters. Luchrome thanked TeamNAqui, the Nouvelle-Aquitaine Region, CCI International, La French Tech, Business France, and the broader French technology ecosystem for their continued sponsorship and technical support, which enabled the company’s presence on the CES stage.

53004.cap: BTRY’s thin-film design enables flexible applications in consumer electronics, IoT and MedTech. | Image provided by BTRY

53004.x: Swiss deep-tech startup BTRY AG announced that it will participate in CES 2026, to be held from January 6 to 9 in Las Vegas, United States, where the company will present its breakthrough ultra-thin all-solid-state lithium-ion battery platform at the SwissTech Pavilion, Eureka Park Booth #61220.

CES is recognized as one of the world’s most influential IT and consumer electronics exhibitions, bringing together innovative companies, investors, global corporations, and media to showcase the latest technologies shaping future industries. Within Eureka Park, the exhibition serves as an important platform for advanced deep-tech startups seeking international partnerships and commercialization opportunities. Through this participation, BTRY aims to demonstrate that next-generation electronics no longer need to be constrained by conventional battery size, charging behavior, or safety limitations.

Founded as a spin-off from Empa and ETH Zurich, BTRY AG focuses on developing solid-state lithium-ion batteries optimized for connected devices. Unlike large-format energy storage designed for electric vehicles or national power grids, the company targets high-value applications where miniaturization, reliability, and longevity matter most. The battery platform introduced at CES 2026 reflects years of research and development rooted in semiconductor-style thin-film production processes, translated into sustainable roll-to-roll battery manufacturing.

53004.cap: Comparison of conventional Li-ion and BTRY’s all-solid-state design: fewer layers, no liquid electrolyte, and an ultra-thin, safer architecture. | Image provided by BTRY.

53004.x: The core differentiator of BTRY’s technology is its ability to enable ultra-fast charging with an exceptionally small footprint. Starting at a thickness of just 0.1 mm, the batteries can reach full charge in approximately one minute while operating safely at temperatures up to 150 °C (300 °F), in environments where conventional lithium-ion cells typically fail, swell, or pose fire risks due to liquid electrolytes. By removing liquid electrolyte layers and simplifying internal structures, BTRY implements a safer architecture with fewer layers, enabling direct power delivery for wireless transmissions without additional capacitors.

CEO and Co-Founder Dr. Moritz Futscher emphasized the significance of the milestone. “Electronics keep getting smaller and smarter, but batteries have not kept up. At CES 2026, we are showing that energy storage no longer needs to dictate device design or user behavior,” he said. “We intend to prove firsthand that the projector-sized screen experience of everyday devices can be matched with equally advanced, hair-thin, intrinsically safe batteries made in Switzerland.”

Industry experts and investors have also recognized BTRY’s potential. Redstone VC, the conference co-organizer’s investment partner, Mohamed Foulser, noted that the company is a frontrunner among Europe’s next-generation battery companies. The founding team’s combination of deep scientific expertise and entrepreneurial grit has earned high praise from partners across the logistics, healthcare, and industrial automation sectors seeking truly energy-autonomous solutions.

53004.cap: The BTRY team is shaping the next generation of solid-state batteries — from Swiss research labs to global production. | Photo by BTRY

53004.x: BTRY AG recently achieved a significant business milestone. In late 2025, the company closed an oversubscribed seed funding round totaling USD 5.7 million, led by Redstone VC. The investment will be used to accelerate industrialization through BTRY’s proprietary roll-to-roll manufacturing platform, strengthen customer product integration projects, and expand its global market strategy. The company says it plans to use this funding to stimulate applications such as active logistics tags, connected labels, high-temperature industrial sensors, MedTech devices, wearables, and other light consumer electronics, where traditional batteries have limited innovation.

Through demonstrations at CES 2026, BTRY plans to present use cases that directly address global challenges, including aging societies, portable device reliability, high-temperature safety, and the growing demand for smaller, smarter electronics. The company intends to continue follow-up meetings after the exhibition with Proof-of-Concept support and pilot projects to establish its technology as a new global standard for high-performance connected-electronics batteries.

Founded in 2023, BTRY AG is a Swiss deep-tech spin-off from Empa and ETH Zurich, specializing in the development of ultra-thin solid-state lithium-ion batteries. The company develops modular batteries that combine one-minute charging, extreme temperature stability, and intrinsic safety, enabling next-generation connected devices and wireless sensors.

53005.x: CubicSpace Technologies, Inc. today announced the launch of CubicScreen, a new consumer product designed to unlock the full potential of spatial photos and videos captured on iPhone. Built around proprietary adaptive stereoscopic geometry and glasses-free 3D display technology, CubicScreen allows users to experience their own everyday moments with natural depth and presence, without requiring special eyewear or additional hardware.

CubicScreen transforms iPhone-captured spatial media into vivid personal 3D experiences by combining a thin 3D optical screen protector with an intuitive spatial media application. The company explained that this approach reduces longstanding barriers to 3D viewing and positions smartphones as the most accessible entry point to the expanding spatial media ecosystem. Product availability is planned for the second quarter, with commercial release targeted for Q2 2026, and showcase demonstrations at CES 2026, Eureka Park Booth #60840.

Since Apple introduced spatial photo and video capture capabilities in 2023, hundreds of millions of iPhone owners have gained the ability to record memories in 3D using a device they already carry every day. However, most of that content can still only be viewed in 2D on phones, limiting the emotional connection and immersive impact captured in the original moment. CubicScreen directly addresses this gap by enabling natural and comfortable 3D playback on the same device used for capture, allowing users to relive personal memories exactly as they were intended to be seen.

The CubicScreen app, powered by CubicSpace’s adaptive 3D model, dynamically adjusts 3D geometry in real time based on the content, the individual viewer, and surrounding viewing conditions. The company emphasized that this scientific breakthrough replaces the one-size-fits-all assumptions that traditional stereoscopic displays have relied on for decades. As a result, users receive a guaranteed comfortable and intuitive 3D experience that works consistently in everyday life, requiring no technical expertise or manual adjustments.

Nicholas Routhier, President and Co-Founder of CubicSpace Technologies, described the product as an important milestone for mainstream adoption of 3D. “For the first time in history, hundreds of millions of people can capture their own memories in 3D using a smartphone,” he said. “With CubicScreen, we are removing the friction that has always held 3D back. No glasses, no extra devices, and no expertise required. Our mission is to make 3D as natural and universal as smartphone photography.”

At CES 2026, attendees will be able to experience live demonstrations showing how CubicScreen enables instant 3D playback of personal spatial photos and videos captured on iPhone. Visitors will also discover how the platform fits into a broader ecosystem of glasses-free 3D and XR devices, highlighting opportunities for integration, partnerships, and future content experiences.

CubicSpace Technologies added that its core adaptive stereoscopic geometry technology is protected by a growing intellectual property portfolio that includes four patent families across multiple jurisdictions, with nine patents already granted and nine additional patents currently pending worldwide. The company views this portfolio as a foundation for long-term global expansion and standardization in consumer spatial media.

Founded in 2023, CubicSpace Technologies, Inc. is a deep-tech company specializing in advanced stereoscopic image processing technologies. The company develops adaptive 3D playback solutions designed to deliver natural, comfortable, and intuitive 3D experiences across a wide range of devices and use cases. CubicSpace is headquartered in Montreal, Canada, and is dedicated to making 3D mainstream as part of everyday digital life.

53006.cap: At the EcoRenew booth at CES 2026, CEO Duckhyun Choi (front row, right) and the research team introduce the RenewFlow-Oil system, which purifies waste lubricating oil directly on site. | Photo – AVING News

53006.x: [Las Vegas, USA = AVING News] At CES 2026 in Las Vegas, one technology stopped industry professionals in their tracks—one that began with a deceptively simple question:
“Is it possible to remove only the water mixed inside oil using a filter?”
EcoRenew (CEO Duckhyun Choi) presented a clear and confident answer: a superhydrophobic filter that blocks water while selectively allowing oil to pass through.

At CES 2026, EcoRenew unveiled its superhydrophobic nano-coated Renuva-Oil (RO) filter as the centerpiece of its exhibition. While conventional oil–water separation technologies focus on removing oil from water, the Renuva-Oil filter takes the opposite approach—removing microscopic, emulsified water from within oil itself. This was long considered virtually impossible within the industry.

53006.cap: The superhydrophobic Renuva-Oil filter unveiled by EcoRenew at CES 2026. It represents a world-first nano-coating concept that selectively passes oil while blocking water. | Photo – AVING News

53006.x: “Hydrophobic Alone Is Not Enough” — Engineering Selectivity into the Filter

CEO Duckhyun Choi explained on-site, “Most hydrophobic filters end up blocking both water and oil. What EcoRenew achieved was precise control over nano-coating selectivity, allowing oil to flow smoothly while preventing water from passing through.”

With this single filter, traditional waste oil purification processes—previously dependent on high temperature, high pressure, and massive energy input—can be transformed into a low-temperature, low-pressure filtration process. Purification is possible without heating beyond 60°C, significantly reducing both energy consumption and carbon emissions.
"Field-Proven Technology… First Commercial Delivery Completed in Late December"

EcoRenew’s confidence in its technology has already translated into tangible results. In late December 2025, the company delivered its first Renuva-Oil–based purification system to a domestic metal forging company, officially moving beyond proof-of-concept and into commercial deployment.

In metal processing operations, lubricating oil and coolant are used simultaneously, inevitably generating waste oil over time. Traditionally, this waste oil had to be shipped to external refiners or discarded after weeks-long processing. With EcoRenew’s system, companies can now perform continuous on-site purification within just 2–3 hours, enabling stable reuse of several tons of lubricating oil per month.

53006.cap: EcoRenew’s Renuva filter lineup. The upper cartridge is the superhydrophobic Renuva-Oil, while the lower is the superhydrophilic Renuva-Water. By simply replacing the filter, the same system can switch between oil and water purification. | Photo – AVING News

53006.x: "Modular Architecture: Scaling Capacity Up to 100×"

Renuva-Oil is integrated into EcoRenew’s continuous purification system, RenewFlow-Oil (RFO). Its most notable feature is a multi-housing modular design. By increasing filter length and quantity, processing capacity can be expanded by 10 times—or even up to 100 times.

When superhydrophilic filters are installed instead, the same housing transforms into RenewFlow-Water, an industrial water purification system. In other words, a simple filter swap determines whether the system purifies oil or water.
“Equal to or Better Than Virgin Oil” — Quality Validation Achieved

The quality of the regenerated oil was another critical benchmark. EcoRenew has secured evaluations confirming reusability through analysis frameworks aligned with the Korea Petroleum Quality & Distribution Authority, as well as independent professional testing institutions. Formal certification procedures are currently underway, with completion targeted for the first half of the year.

“Compared to using virgin oil, reusing purified oil can reduce carbon dioxide emissions by up to 80%,” said Choi. “This technology simultaneously addresses two challenges: resource circulation and carbon reduction.”

53006.cap: A display panel illustrating the structure and operating principle of RenewFlow-Oil (RFO). The superhydrophobic filter selectively allows oil to pass while separating water and solid contaminants. | Photo – AVING News

53006.x: "From POSCO to Chemicals — Demand Is Already Wide Open"

EcoRenew’s target market is clearly defined: any industrial site that uses lubricating oil, including metal processing, steelmaking, machinery, chemicals, and cosmetics manufacturing. Looking ahead, the company also envisions applications in Middle Eastern crude oil extraction, where water injection is used to lift oil—resulting in moisture-laden crude that requires downstream dehydration.
“As a starting point, this is just the beginning,” Choi remarked. “But a filter that blocks water and passes only oil is a technology that fundamentally reshapes industrial processes.”
With CES 2026 as its launchpad, EcoRenew is accelerating a paradigm shift in waste oil purification—from thermal processing to selective filtration.
The technology has already been proven on-site.
Now, only one question remains: Which company will be the first to adopt it at scale?

53007.cap: A view of the Marketon booth at the KOCCA Pavilion inside the CES 2026 exhibition hall, where AI-powered interactive hologram technology is being introduced amid ongoing on-site discussions with global visitors. | Photo – AVING News

53007.x: CES 2026 was an exhibition that spoke repeatedly about “AI,” but beneath the surface, another question was constantly being raised: What will be the new form factor that represents the AI era?

The mobile internet era was symbolized by the smartphone. Mobile devices led by Apple and Samsung changed the world through screens held in the palm of one’s hand. However, innovators encountered at CES 2026 spoke with one voice. In the AI era, the interface will no longer remain a “touch-based screen.”

Changjun Yang, CEO of immersive display specialist Marketon, whom we met at CES 2026, began from the same line of questioning. “As Sam Altman has said, the device that defined the mobile internet era and the dominant device of the AI era could be completely different,” Yang noted. “AI is not a technology you press with your hands, but one you speak to, see, and interact with in space.”

53007.cap: Marketon CEO Changjun Yang explains usage scenarios and the technical structure of the mobile hologram product to global buyers and visitors at CES 2026. | Photo – AVING News

53007.x: “The answer he focused on was a new input/output device and a new form factor—holograms.”

“Meta is pursuing AI interfaces through smart glasses, and many companies are exploring new compact devices,” Yang said. “I believe holograms can take up one axis of that competition.” His focus is not on holograms as mere visual effects, but as practical interfaces combined with AI.

The new product Marketon unveiled at CES 2026 is the result of that philosophy. Named “Mobile Hologram,” the device breaks away from the limitations of large-scale hologram displays by maximizing portability and on-site usability. It is designed to project 3D images in midair at a smart-device scale and to be controlled without physical touch.

Yang defined the product as a “hologram mobile device.” Unlike public holograms fixed to a specific location, this concept allows users to carry and move the device themselves. It can be used in living rooms and bedrooms, concert venues and event sites, and even while on the move.

53007.cap: A demonstration of Marketon’s AI-based interactive hologram at CES 2026, showing 3D content projected in midair and controlled directly through gestures. | Photo – AVING News

53007.x: In particular, the product was designed on the premise of integration with AI agents. Users can control hologram content via voice commands and gestures, moving beyond simple playback to interaction structures that respond to user context. This directly embodies Yang’s concept of an “input/output device for the AI era.”

Marketon’s technology has already been validated in the education and exhibition sectors. It has been installed and operated at the Seodaemun Museum of Natural History, elementary and secondary schools in Korea, financial institutions in Singapore, and major banks, proving its immersion and usability. Key strengths include midair imaging visible even in bright environments, a reflector-free structure, and superior hygiene and safety compared to VR devices.

At CES 2026, Marketon shifted its focus toward the global K-pop fandom market. “The fastest way to prove the practicality of holograms is to combine them with content people are passionate about,” Yang explained. “K-pop is the optimal market where technology and experience intersect.”

The mobile hologram is designed for immediate use at concert venues, fan signing events, pop-up stores, and merchandise shops. Yang described it as a “concert in your hand.” The goal is to allow fans to encounter artists in three dimensions anytime, anywhere.

53007.cap: At the Marketon booth in the CES 2026 KOCCA Pavilion, overseas visitors experience the AI-powered Interactive Hologram while listening to explanations of the technology. | Photo – AVING News

53007.x: “What we want to create is not a display, but an experience,” Yang said. “When AI and holograms are combined, the relationship between fans and artists themselves can change.” He added, “Mobile holograms will become an essential item that transforms performances and fan engagement at global tour sites.”

At CES 2026, Marketon plans to expand collaboration with global buyers, focusing on the “AI & Entertainment” sector. The company is also preparing to build an ecosystem encompassing content production and distribution through partnerships with K-pop agencies, global fan platforms, and merchandise distributors.

The dominant device of the AI era has yet to be determined. What became clear at CES 2026, however, is one thing: AI has entered a phase of competition over which form factor it will operate on. Marketon has presented holograms as one of those answers. “There is still a vacancy for the device of the AI era,” Yang concluded. “The battle has begun to see who will turn that vacancy into reality first.”

53008.cap: Trophies from CES Innovation Awards 2025 and 2026 are displayed side by side at NEWJAK’s booth. The company has been recognized for innovation across XR & Spatial Computing, Content & Entertainment, and Metaverse categories.| Photo – AVING News

53008.x: At CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and electronics exhibition, NEWJAK Co. Ltd. (CEO Haehyun Jung) made its strategic direction unmistakably clear. Long perceived as an entertainment technology company, NEWJAK officially declared its transition into an XR platform company, positioning XR as a core infrastructure connecting defense, education, and public sectors.

The official theme of CES 2026, “Innovators Show Up,” signals a shift in expectations. Innovators are no longer expected to hide behind technology, but to step forward and take responsibility for its direction and impact. CEO Jung emphasized that “innovation is not about technology itself, but about attitude,” referencing AMD CEO Lisa Su’s CES keynote statement that AMD would take responsibility for the pace of AI advancement. NEWJAK, he explained, stood at CES with the same mindset.

53008.cap: Visitors experience NEWJAK’s XR interactive sports content ‘SPORTRACK’ at the CES 2026 exhibition. The platform combines real-world movement with XR graphics, without requiring HMDs.| Photo – AVING News

53008.x: “Exhibition-Only XR Is Over”… From Military Training Centers to Public Sector Deployment

According to Jung, many still view NEWJAK through the lens of entertech, but that perception no longer reflects reality. “We are not just creating XR content,” he said. “We are building an XR platform capable of operating entire service structures across industries.”

A representative example is defense. NEWJAK recently deployed its XR system at the Nonsan Army Training Center’s Mental Strength Education Facility, introducing XR-based content not for shooting or tactical drills, but for psychological and values-based training. The project is regarded as one of the earliest cases where XR has been practically adopted within a public defense education environment. Jung noted, “Immersion and comprehension are critical in military education as well. XR can fundamentally change how training is delivered.”

Implementation has also begun in education. NEWJAK completed delivery of an AI-powered XR learning playground at an elementary school in Goyang, where students engage in content that integrates physical activity with learning. Discussions are also underway with the Hanam Public Health Center regarding XR applications in public services, signaling expansion beyond defense and education.

53008.cap: A visitor interacts with immersive visuals projected across the floor and walls inside NEWJAK’s six-sided XR space. The experience requires no wearable devices, relying solely on physical movement.| Photo – AVING News
Overseas visitors listen to explanations of NEWJAK’s XR platform and real-world use cases at the company’s booth within the Jeonnam Technopark joint pavilion at CES 2026.| Photo – AVING News

53008.x: “Drop a Pin on Google Maps, Done in 10 Minutes”… A Field-Ready XR Platform

The technological strength of NEWJAK’s XR platform lies in speed and immediacy. According to Jung, by simply selecting coordinates on Google Maps, real-world distances and environments can be converted into XR simulations in under 10 minutes. This eliminates the need for physical mockups or lengthy environment preparation, enabling instant indoor simulations.

Such capability proves critical in time-sensitive fields such as defense and disaster response. “When situations are urgent, traditional preparation-heavy methods fall short,” Jung said. “XR platforms can provide immediate alternatives.”

This platform-oriented approach aligns closely with NEWJAK’s recognition at the CES 2026 Innovation Awards. The company drew attention with SPORTRACK, an XR interactive sports platform that allows multiple participants to engage simultaneously without head-mounted displays. Designed as a board-game-style system incorporating 16 XR physical education maps aligned with Korea’s 2023 revised national curriculum, the platform enables full physical education classes to take place even in a standard 6m × 6m classroom.

Jung concluded, “We do not see XR as a single industry. Starting from entertainment, moving through defense, education, and public services, we envision XR becoming a core interface across industries.” As CES 2026 shifts the central question from “What can be built?” to “Who will take responsibility?”, NEWJAK is stepping forward with its XR platform as a direct answer.

53010.x: ORPHE Inc., a Japan-based startup specializing in gait analysis and smart footwear technology, is showcasing its ORPHE INSOLE at CES 2026, where the product has been named a Best of Innovation Award winner in the CES Innovation Awards 2026.

ORPHE INSOLE is designed to bring lab-grade biomechanical analysis into everyday footwear. The system integrates a six-axis inertial measurement unit (IMU) and six pressure sensors per foot, enabling continuous tracking of motion and pressure during daily activities. According to the company, the insole lasts more than 24 hours on a single charge, supports real-time Bluetooth data streaming, wireless and magnetic charging, and offers an open-source software development kit compatible with Python and JavaScript.

The company positions the product as a solution to long-standing limitations in gait analysis, which has traditionally relied on expensive force plates, laboratory environments, and expert interpretation. ORPHE aims to enable real-world data collection by allowing users to generate movement logs simply by wearing smart shoes, with data aggregated in the cloud and accessible to medical professionals via an API.

At the core of the technology is ORPHE’s dual-sensing approach, which fuses motion data from the IMU with plantar pressure data sampled at up to 200 Hz. The system also incorporates edge computing, allowing real-time gait analysis and machine-learning inference directly on the device without reliance on cloud processing. A proprietary algorithm based on Zero-Velocity Updates (ZUPTs) is used to reduce sensor drift and improve the accuracy of distance, posture, and gait calculations.

ORPHE’s technology is already being used in healthcare and research settings. The company reports that its ORPHE ANALYTICS MEDICAL platform is currently deployed in dozens of medical institutions across Japan for daily gait evaluations, including post-orthopedic surgery assessments. Ongoing research projects also include rehabilitation for Parkinson’s disease, using smart shoes to detect freezing of gait and deliver real-time auditory cues, as well as industrial safety applications developed in collaboration with Mitsubishi Materials to prevent workplace falls.

In addition to medical and research use cases, ORPHE has partnered with ASICS since 2019 to develop smart running and walking shoes. Previous collaborations include EVORIDE ORPHE and RUNWALK ORPHE, which integrate ORPHE’s motion sensors into commercial footwear.

Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Shibuya, Tokyo, ORPHE Inc. focuses on the research, development, and commercialization of DX and IoT-based gait analysis solutions for healthcare, sports, and industrial applications. The company holds multiple patents and has received several design and innovation awards in Japan. Its corporate mission is summarized as “Sensing Feet, Changing Everything.”

At CES 2026, ORPHE is exhibiting at the Venetian Campus, Venetian Expo, Level 2, Halls A–D, at booth number 54199, seeking research partners and global collaborators to expand its smart footwear platform into international markets.

53011.cap: Panel discussion underway at the Global Innovation Forum, with representatives from national startup support organizations participating. Strategies for global startup ecosystem collaboration were discussed. | Photo – AVING News

53011.x: Amid CES 2026, the world’s largest technology exhibition, the Global Innovation Forum (GIF 2026) was held in Las Vegas, drawing global attention as a rare platform where startup pitching and cross-national startup cooperation converged on a single stage.

Hosted by the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), the forum took place on January 7 (local time), the second day of CES 2026, at the Emperors Ballroom of Caesars Palace. GIF 2026 stood out as the only global startup pitching event during CES officially joined by multiple national startup support organizations, positioning itself at the very center of the exhibition’s global innovation ecosystem.

CES 2026 served as a high-density global arena where investors, innovative companies, and decision-makers gathered in unprecedented concentration. With approximately 53% of CES participants identified as executive-level decision-makers, startup pitching during this period functioned not as a separate IR event, but as the market itself—where audiences, media, and venture capital naturally intersected. Within this environment, GIF 2026 operated as a platform for the most realistic validation of startup value.

53011.cap: Kim Hyun-woo, President of the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), delivers the opening remarks at the Global Innovation Forum held during CES 2026, sharing the direction of cross-national startup ecosystem collaboration. | Photo – AVING News

Venture capitalists and global accelerator representatives from the United States, Korea, and Europe evaluate IR pitching sessions at the Global Innovation Forum, conducting practical, investment-oriented assessments on site. | Photo – AVING News
A French startup presents its technology and global market strategy on the IR pitching stage at the Global Innovation Forum. | Photo – AVING News

53011.x: “Innovators Show Up” Comes to Life at CES 2026

The forum aligned closely with CES 2026’s official theme, “Innovators Show Up.” Rather than focusing solely on technical explanations, the event highlighted a shift to a new era in which founders and leaders must step onto the stage themselves and demonstrate judgment, strategy, and conviction.

The GIF 2026 IR pitching stage featured eight startups representing seven countries—Korea, France, Japan, Taiwan, Israel, Canada, and Switzerland. Each startup was directly selected by its national startup support organization, forming a structure in which technology, business models, and global scalability were evaluated simultaneously under global standards.

Participating startups represented key CES 2026 technology trends, including AI and robotics, digital health, mobility, battery and energy, and spatial and photonics technologies. Their presentations emphasized global expansion strategies, business models, and investment readiness rather than technical demonstrations alone. In CES’s high-pressure decision-making environment, pitching immediately led to direct feedback and follow-up discussions, reinforcing its role as a live market engagement.

53011.cap: Following the IR pitching sessions, global media outlets including Forbes conduct on-site interviews with participating startups and stakeholders. Pitching outcomes translated simultaneously into investment consideration and global exposure. | Photo – AVING News

Evaluation score sheets used during the Global Innovation Forum (GIF 2026) IR pitching competition, featuring global assessment criteria such as technological innovation, market potential, storytelling, and social impact. | Photo – AVING News

53011.x: Judging was conducted by 25 venture capitalists and global accelerator representatives based in the United States, Korea, and Europe. Institutions such as Plug and Play Korea participated, applying a practical evaluation framework focused on market viability, team capability, and investment suitability. The structure was designed to facilitate post-pitch investment reviews and follow-up meetings rather than simple ranking.

This approach distinguished GIF 2026 from conventional pitching competitions. The evaluation process itself functioned as a first meeting between startups and investors, with immediate Q&A and discussions following each presentation. The emphasis was placed on long-term connectivity and expansion potential rather than short-term outcomes.

Global media presence further amplified the forum’s impact. More than 100 journalists and influencers from over 20 countries, including representatives from Forbes, Digitimes, and Innovation & Tech Today, attended the event. As a result, pitching outcomes translated simultaneously into investment consideration and global exposure. GIF 2026 was widely recognized as a practical global startup stage where evaluation, media coverage, and connection operated concurrently.

53011.cap: A representative from Plug and Play Korea explains the evaluation criteria and judging process for the Global Innovation Forum IR pitching competition. | Photo – AVING News

53011.x: "From Player to Architect: Korea’s Evolving Role"

Beyond individual startup outcomes, GIF 2026 also symbolized the evolution of Korea’s startup policy. Korea has long been recognized for its world-class startup support infrastructure. However, GIF 2026 demonstrated a shift beyond being a strong “supporting nation” toward becoming a designer of global startup ecosystems—connecting countries, structuring collaboration, and orchestrating shared platforms.

The IR pitching competition stood at the center of this transformation. Unlike closed IR rooms or limited investor-only presentations, CES itself functioned as a natural point of contact. Startups engaged immediately with global VCs, media, and industry stakeholders, extending discussions well beyond the stage.

Following the pitching sessions, panel discussions featuring national startup support organizations explored global startup trends and country-specific support strategies. These discussions served not only as knowledge-sharing sessions but also as checkpoints for cross-national policy collaboration. Subsequent networking sessions enabled startups, investors, media, and ecosystem operators to pursue tangible business opportunities.

53011.cap: Global investors and industry stakeholders applaud during an IR pitching presentation, reflecting CES’s uniquely high-density decision-making environment. | Photo – AVING News

Representatives of First Habit, winner of the Grand Award at the Global Innovation Forum (GIF 2026) IR Pitching Competition, pose for a commemorative photo holding the trophy and prize. | Photo – AVING News

53011.x: After the IR pitching sessions, panel discussions featuring representatives from participating countries followed. The sessions shared the latest trends in the global startup ecosystem and country-specific startup support strategies, serving as a platform to review cross-national policy alignment and collaboration models beyond the growth of individual companies. The networking sessions that followed allowed startups, venture capitalists (VCs), media, and startup support organizations to interact freely and explore tangible business opportunities.

At the event, startups that demonstrated innovation and global scalability through the IR pitching sessions were presented with the Grand Award, Scale-up Award, and Impact Award. 53014.x: [Las Vegas, USA = AVING News] SPAID drew strong attention from global public-sector and urban infrastructure stakeholders at CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition held in Las Vegas, as it unveiled its 3D GIS platform strategy integrating disaster response and geospatial intelligence for smart city safety infrastructure.

"Wildfire and Flood Response ‘Geo Safe MAP’… From Spread Prediction to Route Recommendations"

Using this analysis, the system predicts fire spread patterns and recommends optimal response routes, moving beyond traditional manual-based firefighting access paths to routes optimized for real-world conditions.

While conventional disaster response systems rely primarily on maps and numerical data, Geo Safe MAP is designed to enable decision-makers to understand disaster situations as spatial environments. Through 3D simulations that accurately reflect on-site terrain, the platform supports intuitive risk assessment and strategic response planning.

Flood and inundation response capabilities are implemented by linking water level gauges and sensor data to visualize the inflow and spread of water across affected areas over time. Beyond simply marking flooded zones, the system allows real-time monitoring of where water enters and how it propagates through urban and natural landscapes in a 3D space.

This approach supports proactive response measures, including early control and evacuation planning for flood-prone areas, supplementing existing systems that typically enable disaster recognition only two to three hours in advance. SPAID expects the technology to help overcome the limitations of post-incident-focused disaster management frameworks.
"Geospatial Intelligence ‘Geo Data MAP’… A Collaboration Model for Data Owners"

Beyond disaster response, SPAID also introduced its ‘Geo Data MAP’ platform, which focuses on geospatial data integration itself. Geo Data MAP is a 3D GIS platform that consolidates drone imagery, satellite data, and existing GIS datasets, providing a foundation for organizations that possess geospatial data but lack the infrastructure to operationalize it.

Against the backdrop of a growing consensus that traditional camera- and radar-based systems struggle to detect small drones and low-altitude aerial objects, LINSOL’s non-vision acoustic detection approach was increasingly recognized as a viable alternative.

53022.cap: A sample of GeoWind’s icosahedron vertical-axis wind power system showcased at the CES 2026 Unveiled in Las Vegas on January 4 (local time) | Photo by AVING News

53022.x: GeoWind (CEO Young June Jeon) participated in CES 2026 Unveiled, held on January 4 (local time) in Las Vegas, the United States.

GeoWind is a climate tech startup that develops small- to mid-scale vertical-axis wind power systems designed for installation and operation across a wide range of environments, including urban, industrial, and off-grid settings. To address the limitations of conventional large horizontal-axis wind turbines—such as installation constraints, noise, and maintenance burden—the company focuses on distributed wind technologies that enhance structural stability and environmental adaptability.

Beyond positioning wind turbines solely as energy-generation equipment, GeoWind also proposes a model that expands their role to distributed nodes capable of collecting climate and environmental data. According to the company, this approach not only broadens the functional scope of wind power systems but also enhances their aesthetic value, enabling applications in education, exhibitions, public spaces, and other diverse settings.

At CES 2026 Unveiled, GeoWind introduced a vertical-axis wind power system based on an icosahedron structure. This polyhedral geometry, composed of 20 triangular faces and 12 vertices, distributes external loads throughout the frame rather than concentrating stress at specific points. As a result, the system maintains structural stability even under irregular wind conditions, including gusts, rapidly changing wind directions, and urban turbulence.

The wind blades adopt a vertical-axis lift-based and hybrid lift-drag design, enabling initial rotation even in low wind-speed environments. Blade shapes and angles are optimized to secure torque at low cut-in wind speeds, while the system operates omnidirectionally across 360 degrees regardless of wind direction. This eliminates the need for a yaw system, simplifies mechanical components compared to horizontal-axis turbines, and significantly reduces maintenance requirements.

In addition, the system incorporates damping structures that minimize vibration transmission between the rotor, generator, and frame. By reducing vibration and structural fatigue at frame joints, bearing supports, and shaft connections, the design prevents long-term deformation during extended operation. This translates into low noise and vibration, which are particularly important in installation-constrained urban environments.

53022.cap: Young June Jeon, CEO of GeoWind (left), introduces the company’s technology and products to visitors at CES 2026 Unveiled | Photo by AVING News

53022.x: GeoWind’s wind power system also supports the integration of sensor modules for climate and environmental data collection. In addition to basic environmental metrics such as wind speed, wind direction, temperature, humidity, and pressure, the system can gather operational data including power generation output, rotational speed, and load status. Through this configuration, the company aims to propose diverse use cases spanning educational content development, public project monitoring, research, and experimental applications.

To this end, GeoWind continues domestic validation of structural stability, low-wind-speed performance, and installation and operational feasibility, while overseas, it advances pilot projects in cooperation with educational and public institutions in regions such as Southeast Asia, including Vietnam. The company plans to further refine models tailored to regional climate conditions and installation environments, while gradually expanding its business and partnerships into the North American market.

A GeoWind official said, “Unveiled, the official pre-event of CES, brings together global media and industry stakeholders seeking to grasp advanced technology trends across industries,” adding, “Through this event, GeoWind aimed to objectively introduce its technology and gather market feedback on its early-stage solutions.”

The official continued, “Based on the market response confirmed this time, we plan to adjust product configurations and demonstration strategies, and further specify technology application models customized to national and regional requirements.”

Meanwhile, GeoWind will also participate in the main CES 2026 exhibition, held from January 6 to 9, as part of the Seoul Pavilion located in Eureka Park, the startup-dedicated exhibition zone. The CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion, led by the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), brings together 19 startup support organizations in Seoul, including district offices, related institutions, and universities, to support 70 startups. The participating companies span advanced technology fields such as AI, mobility, and healthcare, and selected outstanding firms receive opportunities to participate in the official CES media event, Unveiled.

‘CES Unveiled’ is a key official event held ahead of the CES opening, bringing together innovation award winners and companies showcasing cutting-edge products. The event gathers global media, company executives, government officials, and major players from the technology industry in one place.

53023.cap: A demo model of the ‘Ascender’ showcased by Safeway at CES 2026 Unveiled, held in Las Vegas on January 4 (local time) | Photo by AVING News

53023.x: Safeway Inc. (CEO Dongho Kim) participated in CES 2026 Unveiled, held on January 4 (local time) in Las Vegas, the United States.

Safeway is a Korean company that has developed technologies to address long-standing limitations of commercialized robots and unmanned mobility systems, including obstacles, steps, and rough-terrain mobility. Through continuous development and accumulation of proprietary technologies, the company achieved tangible results by combining adaptive elastic wheel structures with AI-based control technologies.

Between 2024 and 2025, Safeway recorded cumulative domestic sales exceeding 1 billion won, laying the foundation for the commercialization of its technology. The company is currently conducting joint development and demand-linked R&D projects with the Korea Expressway Corporation on traffic signal robots, while also expanding its domestic and overseas business footprint through exports and technical cooperation with electric wheelchair manufacturers.
At CES Unveiled, Safeway introduced the modular mobility solution ‘Ascender,’ which integrates adaptive elastic wheels with AI-driven driving control technology.

The wheel structure of Ascender flexibly deforms in response to obstacles and steps encountered during driving, optimizing ground contact area and propulsion. This enables the platform to overcome heights of up to approximately 1.3 times the wheel radius without relying on complex joint structures or track mechanisms, while maintaining structural simplicity and energy efficiency.

The AI control technology applied to the platform analyzes wheel deformation patterns, ground contact conditions, and motor torque in real time to adjust driving modes accordingly. Through this approach, the company emphasized that Ascender maintains consistent performance on flat surfaces while delivering enhanced stability on irregular terrain, including stairs, curbs, and rough ground. The control system is also designed as a modular solution applicable to various robotic and mobility systems, offering strong scalability.

53023.cap: Safeway CEO Dongho Kim is interviewed by AVING News reporter Jay Kennedy Marcus | Photo by AVING News

53025.cap: Awesome Lab’s hot water and heating solution, ‘Thermoflux,’ is based on electrolysis ionization heat-generation technology. | Photo by AVING News

53025.x: Awesome Lab Co., Ltd. (CEO Martin Kim) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

Awesome Lab is a startup developing electric hot water and heating solutions based on electrolysis ionization heat-generation technology. Since developing the core technology in 2022, the company has secured domestic and international patents and certifications and increased brand recognition through its B2C-focused ‘WATERWARMER’ brand.

Building on WATERWARMER, Awesome Lab confirmed overseas demand by raising 5,100% of its funding target through a crowdfunding campaign in Japan. The company has also been steadily expanding its business scope and markets by supplying hybrid heating solutions to commercial and residential facilities, smart farms, smart cities, and manufacturing sites.

At CES 2026, Awesome Lab showcased its hot water and heating solution, ‘Thermoflux.’ Thermoflux operates by using ionization reactions that occur during the electrical activation of water, generating heat directly from the water itself without separate heaters or combustion.

Unlike the indirect heating structure of conventional electric boilers, this heat-generation method enables simultaneous heat production and fluid circulation, reducing heat loss while increasing heat transfer efficiency. According to the company, under the same hot water and heating output conditions, Thermoflux maintains 20–30% lower power consumption than conventional electric heating systems, while also offering fast heating response and stable, continuous operation.

In addition, Thermoflux delivers heating speeds up to twice as fast as typical electric boilers and achieves carbon emission reductions of approximately 25–80%. Awesome Lab also emphasized that the system reduces installation space by up to 30% and maximizes installation and maintenance efficiency through a modular design approach.

Thermoflux further operates based on proprietary electrode design and current-control technologies, enabling precise suppression of overheating and structurally reducing safety risks, such as fire hazards, often associated with high-temperature heaters or gas combustion equipment.

At CES 2026, Thermoflux was introduced as a heat-source technology applicable not only to domestic hot water and heating but also to a wide range of industrial environments that require continuous heat supply. As an electric system with no combustion process, it drew attention as an effective alternative to conventional hot water and heating systems amid tightening global regulations on gas boilers and decarbonization policies.

An Awesome Lab representative said, “We were pleased to confirm global market interest in our next-generation hot water and heating solution at CES,” adding, “We received positive feedback by presenting objective data on tangible benefits such as improved heating response and carbon reduction, and by clearly highlighting Thermoflux’s advantages through comparisons with existing boiler systems.”

The representative continued, “Through the networks gained at this exhibition, our goal is to solidify partnerships for overseas pilots and commercialization and to open sales channels in markets around the world,” adding, “Having already accumulated meaningful data and references through PoC projects in Japan, the United States, and Mongolia, we view the potential to attract new customers and partners very positively.”

53026.x: Warp Solution Inc. (CEO Kyunghak Lee) showcased its next-generation charging infrastructure technology at CES 2026, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

Warp Solution is a Korean company that has developed RF (radio frequency)-based long-range wireless power transfer (WTP) technology. Since its establishment in 2016, the company has continued to advance RF application technologies that enable multiple devices to operate without physical contact or precise alignment, with the goal of realizing next-generation power infrastructure that supplies electricity across entire spaces, the company said.

To this end, Warp Solution has independently designed and developed key semiconductor products, ranging from RF power amplification devices to high-efficiency RF-DC rectifier chips. The company explained that these technologies represent a rare case in Korea of advancing core long-range wireless charging technologies to the commercialization stage.

Warp Solution’s technology has drawn strong expectations for use in systems and infrastructure where wired power supply or frequent battery replacement poses challenges, including industrial IoT sensors, smart logistics, building automation, and healthcare equipment. Based on this technological foundation, Warp Solution introduced its next-generation WTP platform, ‘WARPS (Wireless Autonomous RF Power System),’ highlighting its technological competitiveness.

WARPS consists of an RF transmission unit that outputs power, a dedicated receiver that captures and rectifies the energy, and software algorithms that control power flow. Unlike conventional wireless chargers that require physical contact or precise alignment between the charger and device, WARPS is designed to simultaneously charge multiple devices located within a defined space without physical contact or alignment.

53026.cap: Semiconductor components applied to WARPS. | Photo by AVING News

53026.x: More specifically, RF energy transmitted from the RF module is converted into electrical power by the receiver, which then charges batteries or directly powers devices. At the same time, the system integrates AI-based tracking and beamforming control technologies through software, enabling real-time recognition of device locations and movement paths and dynamically adjusting the directionality and output of RF energy.

As a result, WARPS can provide stable power even to devices that move frequently or lack fixed installation points, while enabling simultaneous charging of multiple devices through efficient power distribution. Warp Solution emphasized that the use of its in-house semiconductor lineup further enhances both power delivery stability and conversion efficiency.

Warp Solution has secured broad applicability by positioning WARPS as a continuous power supply for smart logistics facilities, factory automation equipment, and healthcare devices that require frequent battery replacement or struggle to deploy wired power infrastructure. The company introduced WARPS as a next-generation power infrastructure that supplies energy on a space-by-space basis, drawing significant attention from on-site visitors.

A Warp Solution representative said, “Long-range wireless power transfer technology has now moved beyond the proof-of-concept stage and reached a level suitable for real industrial applications,” adding, “At CES, we emphasized that our technology meets the stability and continuity requirements of industrial environments and presented a new paradigm for wireless charging technology.”

The representative continued, “By demonstrating that WARPS can serve as a practical alternative for wireless, battery-free power environments across various industries, we received meaningful interest and inquiries from industry stakeholders,” adding, “We will do our utmost to turn the networks gained here into tangible results.”

53032.x: Choosing “Non-Contact”: A New Standard in Brain Healthcare, Targeting Dementia

Neurélux is a non-invasive, non-contact brain healthcare device that utilizes specific wavelengths of light to influence brain function without physical contact or mechanical stimulation. Designed in a form factor similar to a conventional lighting stand, the device allows users to experience light therapy naturally within everyday spaces—without the need for wearing, pressure, or physical attachment. This design makes it particularly suitable for elderly users and environments requiring long-term use.

Technologically, Neurélux is built on a dual near-infrared wavelength structure. The 810nm wavelength activates mitochondria within brain cells, promoting ATP (cellular energy) production and supporting neuroprotection and recovery—mechanisms that are drawing attention in neurodegenerative conditions such as dementia. The 1,064nm wavelength penetrates deeper brain tissue, improving cerebral blood flow and supporting neuroplasticity to help maintain cognitive function.

Korea Lighting defines this approach as “Ambient Brain Healthcare.” Rather than treating brain health as a clinical procedure confined to hospitals, it reframes care as an environmental element embedded in daily life. This concept extends beyond dementia prevention and cognitive care for older adults to include modern individuals experiencing sleep disturbances or cognitive fatigue. Neurélux proposes a new standard: creating an environment where brain health can be managed continuously and naturally as part of everyday living.

53035.cap: CIT’s CuFlat Package Core (CuFlat-PKGCore) on display at CES 2026. | Photo by AVING News

53035.x: Advanced materials and packaging technology startup CIT (CEO Seung Jeong) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, which opened on January 6 (local time) in Las Vegas, where it unveiled its CuFlat Package Core (CuFlat-PKGCore).

Last year, CIT exhibited its transparent antenna “Dolphin,” featuring ultra-thin copper circuitry deposited using its proprietary Atomic Sputtering Epitaxy (ASE) technology, and received a CES Innovation Award.

This year, the company once again won a CES Innovation Award by applying the ASE process to glass substrates for semiconductor packaging with CuFlat-PKGCore, marking two consecutive years of recognition. This achievement indicates that CIT has advanced beyond a materials technology startup to become a company specializing in AI semiconductor packaging technologies, and that its technology has been recognized as a consistent, scalable, and sustainable materials solution.

ASE, which underpins CIT’s consecutive awards, is a process that stacks copper atoms layer by layer on insulating surfaces, bonding the copper and the insulator into a single-crystal structure without adhesives. With the ability to precisely control thickness and surface roughness at the nanometer scale, ASE enables high-quality copper deposition on glass. In this area, conventional technologies have faced stability limitations.
ASE’s innovation has also been recognized in academia. Related research was published in Nature in May 2022 and later featured in Advanced Materials, a leading journal in materials science.

The CuFlat Package Core selected for the CES 2026 Innovation Award applies the ASE process to glass substrates used in semiconductor packaging. Achieving surface roughness below 3 nanometers offers a level of flatness more than 200 times smoother than HVLP4 copper foil, considered one of the flattest materials currently used for AI accelerator package substrates.

53035.cap: CIT’s booth at CES 2026. | Photo by AVING News

53035.x: Such an ultra-smooth surface significantly reduces signal scattering and loss during high-frequency transmission. This contributes to stable signal integrity and improved power efficiency in packaging environments for AI accelerators, high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and network chips that handle high-speed, high-frequency signals. According to CIT, the material also enables delicate patterning and high-density routing, allowing engineers greater design flexibility in semiconductor packages.

CuFlat-PKGCore also demonstrates advantages in thermal stability. While conventional copper materials tend to oxidize and degrade in performance at temperatures around 100°C, CuFlat-PKGCore maintains stability without oxidation or delamination even at 250°C. This makes it suitable for high-performance AI accelerator packages, where heat generation is significant and thermal stress can affect reliability.

The technology further differentiates itself in process efficiency and environmental impact. CIT uses 100% recycled copper scrap to produce CuFlat-PKGCore and employs a dry ASE deposition process that eliminates the need for seed layers and chemical mechanical polishing (CMP). As a result, carbon emissions are reduced by 95% compared with conventional processes, and chemical wastewater generation is minimized because electroplating is absent.

With its ultra-flat copper structure on glass substrates, CuFlat-PKGCore is expected to meet the demanding design and process requirements of the AI semiconductor industry, supporting the computational performance and memory bandwidth needed in next-generation devices. Given the versatility of glass substrates across cores, interposers, and other package structures, the technology may also emerge as a standard platform in advanced high-density packaging environments such as 2.5D and 3D packaging.

CIT is currently conducting proof-of-concept (PoC) projects with leading companies in the United States and Japan—including glass substrate and transparent antenna manufacturers and semiconductor equipment firms—to supply products leveraging CuFlat-PKGCore and ASE technology. The company is also pursuing joint development of AI accelerator substrates with major domestic corporations.

As CIT expands its global collaboration network across semiconductor hubs such as Korea, the United States, Japan, and Taiwan, it aims to actively promote its technology’s strengths and potential impact to overseas customers through continued participation in CES 2026.

Seung Jeong, CEO of CIT, said, “With two consecutive CES Innovation Awards, our ASE technology has been recognized globally for its technical maturity and potential value. We expect CES 2026 to open new opportunities for collaboration and market development. By delivering stability, energy efficiency, and environmental sustainability required in the AI semiconductor era, we aim to set a new standard in the global semiconductor packaging market.”

53036.x: OptAI Inc. (CEO Jaeho Lee) participated in CES 2026 Unveiled, held on January 4 (local time) in Las Vegas, the United States.

OptAI is a deep-tech startup that provides hardware-aware AI optimization technologies to industries where real-time processing, low power consumption, and data integrity are essential, including automotive, robotics, and mobile. By leveraging Korea’s competitiveness as a manufacturing powerhouse, the company aims to lead the global adoption of differentiated on-device AI technologies.

At CES Unveiled, the company actively promoted not only its core technologies but also the references it has accumulated in Korea to global media outlets.

OptHancer, the solution exhibited by OptAI, is an end-to-end on-device optimization platform designed to resolve performance bottlenecks that arise when running high-performance AI models on low-spec, low-power devices. Unlike general-purpose automated toolkits that treat hardware characteristics as a secondary consideration, OptHancer adopts a hardware-first strategy that begins with analysis of the target silicon.

At the core of the platform is OptAI’s “Surgical Model Re-Architecture.” This approach uses AI-agent-based hardware analysis to identify processor architectures and computational characteristics automatically, then reconstructs AI models in a hardware-friendly manner by combining techniques such as quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation.

According to the company, OptAI minimizes the accuracy loss that often occurs during optimization while ensuring consistent inference speed and stability on actual devices. In addition, the platform provides heterogeneous processor scheduling technologies and an equivalence verification system to guarantee performance reliability even after model lightweighting.
