53037.cap: At CES 2026, visitors speaking different languages are seen conversing naturally at the LEION booth while wearing the ‘LEION HEY2,’ watching real-time translated subtitles appear before their eyes. As spoken words are instantly converted into on-screen text, many attendees reacted with visible surprise and delight, smiling and laughing as they experienced seamless cross-language communication. | Photo – AVING News

53037.x: At the world’s largest IT and electronics exhibition, CES 2026, global AR communication technology company LEION (developed by LLVision) captured widespread attention with the unveiling of its next-generation AR smart glasses, ‘LEION HEY2.’ Long lines formed in front of the booth as visitors waited to try the device, while scenes of people speaking different languages and communicating smoothly were repeatedly witnessed across the exhibition floor. As translated subtitles appeared in real time before users’ eyes, many remarked that “AI has truly become part of human perception.”

LEION HEY2 positions itself as the world’s first “professional AR translation glasses.” While smartphone apps and conventional AR glasses have treated translation as an auxiliary feature, HEY2 was designed from the outset specifically for face-to-face multilingual communication. When a conversation partner speaks in a foreign language, the audio is converted into subtitles within an average of 0.5 seconds and displayed directly in the wearer’s field of view. Notably, the other party does not need to wear the glasses; they can follow the translated conversation in real time via a smartphone screen. This enables both sides to maintain eye contact and converse naturally without looking down at a phone or wearing earphones. At CES 2026, the device was widely described as “a product that redefines the direction of translation devices.”

53037.cap: The physical unit of the AR smart glasses ‘LEION HEY2’ on display at the LEION booth. Through the ‘Free Talk’ function, real-time translated conversations are possible even when only one person is wearing the glasses. The wearer reads subtitles through the glasses, while the conversation partner follows the translation on a smartphone display. | Photo – AVING News

The AR smart glasses ‘LEION HEY2’ on display at the LEION booth at CES 2026. With the ‘Free Talk’ feature, real-time translated conversations are possible even when the conversation partner is not wearing the glasses. | Photo – AVING News
Subtitles displayed in the wearer’s field of view during use of ‘LEION HEY2.’ Spoken Chinese is instantly translated into Korean text and projected in real time. | Photo – AVING News
A dedicated carrying case and product components for ‘LEION HEY2,’ designed for everyday portability and use as a global communication tool. | Photo – AVING News

53037.x: “Conversations Don’t Break” — The Advantage of Subtitle-Based Real-Time Translation

The most enthusiastically received feature at the show was the continuity of conversation. Unlike conventional translation devices that deliver translated content only after a speaker finishes talking, HEY2 continuously assembles and displays text in real time as speech progresses. Even before a sentence is completed, users can grasp the context, preventing interruptions in conversation. Many hands-on users commented that “being able to see the translation as it forms makes responses much faster.”

This capability is enabled by HEY2’s dual-eye optical display and head-up interaction structure. Subtitle size and position can be adjusted and remain consistently within the user’s field of view. Beyond general users, these characteristics also make the device valuable as a real-time captioning aid for people with hearing impairments or partial hearing loss.

53037.cap: The companion smartphone app for ‘LEION HEY2,’ which allows intuitive control of real-time translation, subtitle display, and teleprompter functions. | Photo – AVING News

At the LEION booth, demonstrations of the real-time translation function drew intense attention from global media outlets. As subtitles appeared instantly before users’ eyes without disrupting conversation flow, interviews with numerous international media organizations followed. | Photo – AVING News

A scene at the LEION booth at CES 2026 where the real-time translation function is being demonstrated. Translated content appears as subtitles directly in the user’s field of view, allowing conversations to continue without interruption. | Photo – AVING News

53037.x: "Over 100 Languages and Three-Way Translation — AI Proven in the Real World"

In terms of functionality, HEY2 ranks among the most advanced wearable translation devices currently available. It supports two-way translation across more than 100 languages and dialects, can recognize up to five languages simultaneously, and enables three-way multilingual conversations. Its ability to perform reliably even in noisy environments such as CES is attributed to four built-in microphones, 360-degree spatial audio recognition, and a forward-facing speaker focus algorithm covering approximately 60 degrees. These features suppress ambient noise and isolate the voice of the conversation partner, enhancing translation accuracy. Neural network-based noise reduction further ensures stable performance in exhibition halls, streets, and meeting rooms.

HEY2 goes beyond translation alone. With Free Talk mode, two-way communication is possible even when the conversation partner is not wearing the glasses. The user reads translated subtitles, while their own speech is output as translated audio through the smartphone app. In presentation or lecture settings, the teleprompter function displays scripts as subtitles, enabling smoother and more natural delivery.

The AI Q&A assistant, activated by touching the glasses’ temple, also attracted attention. It provides instant responses to simple questions, explanations of terms, and multilingual meeting summaries, complementing the translation experience. The company stated that while the initial model prioritizes stability, more advanced AI engines will be introduced gradually after CES.

53037.cap: An internal component display of ‘LEION HEY2.’ Core elements such as the camera-free AR display module, microphones, and battery are shown in a disassembled format, highlighting the physical AI architecture behind real-time translation while minimizing privacy concerns. | Photo – AVING News

A live multilingual interview conducted using ‘LEION HEY2’ at CES 2026. Questions and answers appeared instantly as subtitles, allowing uninterrupted communication between global media and buyers. | Photo – AVING News

53037.x: "Camera-Free AR Glasses — Trust Built Through Privacy-Centric Design"

Another defining feature of HEY2 is the absence of a camera. By deliberately excluding video capture and external speakers and focusing solely on voice-based translation, the device minimizes privacy concerns in business meetings, exhibitions, and public spaces. All data processing is conducted via Microsoft Azure-based cloud infrastructure in compliance with GDPR standards, and users retain control over managing and deleting translation records.

LEION previously launched HEY2 in South Korea as its first global market. As access to the U.S. market has become more challenging for Chinese technology companies, South Korea has emerged as a strategic testbed for global expansion. With high technology adoption rates and a strong base of early adopters, Korea was selected as the initial launch market. LEION currently operates a local office in Korea and has reportedly received over 200 units in pre-orders through partnerships with local distributors. Building on this track record, the company plans to accelerate expansion into North America, Europe, and the Middle East.

The impression left by LEION HEY2 at CES 2026 was unmistakable. AI is no longer confined to screens; it is evolving into physical intelligence that extends human perception. Scenes of people wearing smart glasses with real-time subtitles while conversing effortlessly across language barriers became one of the exhibition’s most symbolic moments. By demonstrating AI that truly works in real-world settings, LEION’s CES 2026 debut signaled the next stage of global communication.

53044.cap: Kizling exhibition booth at CES 2026 Unveiled. Kizling received an Innovation Award in the Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps category at this year’s CES. | Photo by AVING News

53044.x: Kizling Inc., an AI-based children’s digital short-form challenge platform (CEO Hyelim Lee), participated in CES 2026 Unveiled, held on January 4 (local time) in Las Vegas, the United States.

CES Unveiled is a preview event held ahead of the main exhibition, starting January 6, designed to introduce selected innovative companies and their products to leading global media outlets. As a showcase for curated innovators to receive early, concentrated media attention, the event provided Kizling with an opportunity to showcase the competitiveness of its children-only interactive content platform on the international stage.

Ahead of CES 2026, Kizling was selected as a recipient of the CES Innovation Awards. Organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), the CES Innovation Awards recognize products and services that demonstrate outstanding technology, design, and innovation before the exhibition opens.

53044.cap: Hyelim Lee, CEO of Kizling, gives an interview to AVING News reporter Jay Kennedy Markus. | Photo by AVING News

53044.x: Kizling explained that the award recognized the innovativeness of its participatory edtech platform, which enables children to create content and participate in global challenges in a safe digital environment.

Beyond the CES Innovation Award, Kizling has continued to demonstrate its potential in the global market. The company recently gained recognition through its selection to HolonIQ’s “East Asia EdTech 150” and its third-place finish in the Korean finals of the Global EdTech Startup Awards (GESA), further validating the maturity and completeness of its service. Building on these achievements, Kizling is accelerating efforts to establish partnerships for entry into the U.S. and other global markets.

Through its participation in CES 2026 Unveiled, Kizling actively explored collaboration opportunities with global educational institutions, edtech companies, and content partners, particularly in North America. At the same time, the company introduced a SaaS-based solution for running online challenges and competitions for schools and institutions, signaling plans to expand into B2B and B2G markets.

Technologically, Kizling combines AI-based recommendation algorithms with content-safety filtering to deliver content optimized for children’s ages and interests. Its AI-driven challenge environment supports children in growing from passive content consumers into active creators, and has drawn attention as a next-generation solution that integrates digital literacy education with safe social networking.

Hyelim Lee, CEO of Kizling, said, “It is an honor to receive an innovation award at CES 2026, the world’s largest technology stage, and to participate in the Unveiled event where global media are focused,” adding, “We joined this event to share Kizling’s unique and innovative experience that enables children around the world to freely pursue their dreams in digital spaces.”

Meanwhile, the company will also participate in the leading CES 2026 exhibition, held from January 6 to 9, as part of the Seoul Pavilion located in Eureka Park, the startup-dedicated exhibition zone. The CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion, led by the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), brings together 19 startup support organizations in Seoul, including district offices, related institutions, and universities, to support 70 startups. The participating companies span advanced technology fields such as AI, mobility, and healthcare, and selected outstanding firms receive opportunities to participate in the official CES media event, CES Unveiled.

53045.cap: The image above is not a robot movie poster. M.AX stands for Manufacturing AX, or Manufacturing AI Transformation, and is a policy term used within the next-generation industrial strategy framework promoted by Korea’s Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy. It is not a simple brand name, but a strategic concept that signifies a fundamental, AI-based transformation of the entire manufacturing industry and a key keyword symbolizing Korea’s national industrial transition. | Photo by AVING News

53045.x: The word most frequently mentioned on the CES 2026 keynote stage was “AI,” but the real theme running through the exhibition floor was far clearer. AI is no longer an algorithm confined to a screen. It has become something that moves. At the center of this shift stood robots, particularly humanoids.

Global semiconductor and computing companies, including AMD, pointed to “Physical AI” as the next destination of AI computation. In contrast, global manufacturing giants such as Hyundai Motor Group and LG positioned robots not as future concepts but as industrial assets ready for immediate deployment. CES 2026 clearly showed that the event has fully transformed from an exhibition of TVs and home appliances into a competitive arena for robots.

53045.cap: The Humanoid M.AX Alliance joint pavilion at CES 2026, drawing constant crowds of global robot companies, buyers, and media. | Photo by AVING News
Neuromeka’s humanoid robot was unveiled at CES 2026, emphasizing precision control and industrial applicability. | Photo by AVING News

53045.x: Amid these changes, one of the spaces that stood out most strongly was the Humanoid M.AX Alliance joint pavilion at CES 2026. Rather than listing individual company technologies, the Humanoid M.AX (Manufacturing AX) Alliance Pavilion presented the structure and strategy of Korea’s humanoid industry as a whole, condensed into a single space. On-site, remarks such as “a must-see pavilion at CES 2026” and “one of the most threatening robot booths” naturally circulated.

The M.AX Alliance Pavilion is not an exhibition led by a single organization. The Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy sets the policy direction, while the Korea Institute for Advancement of Technology acts as the overall secretariat overseeing the entire M.AX Alliance. The practical operation of the humanoid division is carried out through cooperation between the Korea Institute for Robot Industry Advancement and the Korea Association of Robot Industry. The structure itself, where policy, public institutions, and industry operate as a single flow rather than in separation, delivers the core message of this joint pavilion.

53045.cap: Global engineers and representatives of Korean robot companies participating in the M.AX Alliance examine humanoid robot hand technologies together. | Photo by AVING News
Global visitors at the Humanoid M.AX Alliance Pavilion closely examine robot hand technologies and show strong interest in Korea’s collective humanoid strategy. | Photo by AVING News

53045.x: The exhibition concept was also clear. The M.AX Alliance Pavilion chose a field-oriented demonstration over a simple technology display. Instead of placing a single robot on display, multiple types of robots were demonstrated in real manufacturing environments, intuitively showing where and how they are used.

This structure goes beyond passive viewing and allows demand companies, component suppliers, and large enterprise delegations to begin business discussions on the spot. The strategic decision to locate the pavilion in the Enterprise AI Zone rather than Eureka Park also signals an intention to position humanoids not as startup technologies, but as solutions ready for immediate industrial deployment.

The response on site was intense. Crowds filled the pavilion throughout the exhibition period, and VIP inbound tour schedules closed early for two consecutive days. Visitors included members of the National Assembly, local governments, public institutions, and representatives from major corporations such as Doosan, Samsung SDS, LG, and KT. Meetings focused not on simple observation but on exploring concrete collaboration opportunities. Comments like “this is the first time I’ve seen this many people gathered at a hardware robot booth” emerged on site. Within the industry, some even described the M.AX Alliance Pavilion as “worthy of a CES 2026 Top 10.”

53045.cap: From left, Byoung-Tak Zhang, professor at Seoul National University and inaugural chair of the Humanoid M.AX Alliance, Jae-kwon Han, CEO of AEIROBOT, and Jang-beom Park, president of KBS, tour the M.AX Alliance Pavilion at CES 2026. | Photo by AVING News

53045.x: Professor Byoung-Tak Zhang of Seoul National University defined the Humanoid M.AX Alliance as “a collective strategic choice made by Korea to leap toward becoming a global humanoid powerhouse, and a declaration of a national robotics strategy.” Since its launch in April last year with around 40 companies and universities, the alliance has expanded rapidly to include more than 250 partners, spanning AI companies, robot manufacturers, core component suppliers, universities, research institutes, and even demand-side companies that actually use robots. Professor Zhang explained that this pace of growth itself indicates both the sense of crisis and the rising expectations surrounding the humanoid industry.

He described humanoid robots as the core battleground of the Physical AI era that follows generative AI and as the final stage in which AI technology takes physical form in industrial settings. With explosive growth expected in the global humanoid market over the next decade, he noted that Korea would struggle to surpass the U.S.–China duopoly if it remained confined to competition among individual companies.

“The biggest differentiator is that those who create the technology and those who actually use it are bound together in a single alliance,” he said, emphasizing that a structure where research, development, demonstration, and demand remain connected defines the essence of Korea’s humanoid strategy. He added, “The Humanoid M.AX Alliance is not a simple consultative body, but a platform where the public and private sectors jointly design both the direction and the speed of the humanoid industry,” making clear the goal of securing leadership not only in technology competition but also in global standards and ecosystem competition.

53045.cap: Gi-won Kang, president of the Korea Institute of Robotics & Technology Convergence, gives an interview at CES 2026 with the Humanoid M.AX Alliance Pavilion in the background. | Photo by AVING News

53045.x: Clear perspectives also emerged regarding the global competitive landscape. Gi-won Kang, president of the Korea Institute of Robotics & Technology Convergence, described the joint pavilion as “a rare scene where a national team has formed in the robotics field.” While the United States drives its robot industry through Big Tech–centered AI model competition, China expands through state-led scale, and Korea chooses to bundle its limited resources through an alliance. He explained that sharing scattered technologies and jointly developing what is needed represents a realistic strategic bet for Korea’s humanoid industry.

President Kang especially highlighted Korea’s data competitiveness. Vast manufacturing process data accumulated on factory floors, world-class ICT and telecommunications infrastructure, and high-complexity surgical data gathered in medical settings stand as core assets in the Physical AI era.

53045.cap: Doosan Group Vice Chairman Geewon Park, far left, conducts a VIP tour at the Humanoid M.AX Alliance Pavilion at CES 2026 while examining humanoid robot technologies. | Photo by AVING News

An overall view of the Humanoid M.AX Alliance Pavilion, where the entire value chain, from core drive components and precision reducers to sensors, robot hands, control technologies, and complete humanoid robots, appears unified within a single alliance framework. | Photo by AVING News

Complete humanoid robots displayed at the Humanoid M.AX Alliance Pavilion, symbolically demonstrating Korea’s humanoid strategy implemented as a unified alliance from components to finished systems through live operation demonstrations. | Photo by AVING News

53045.x: “The age of ideas is over. Now it is a war of collective strategies that move robots.”

Innovation is no longer a matter of ideas, but of collective execution. From the exhibition's opening day, keynotes and primary conference stages consistently placed robots at the forefront. The transition from generative AI to the Physical AI era was announced, and corporations from each country presented their robot strategies and application scenarios in turn. CES 2026 no longer serves as a place to forecast technology trends, but resembles an opening ceremony for a full-scale robot war to determine who can first deploy robots into real industrial battlefields.

Within this fierce competitive landscape, the Humanoid M.AX Alliance Pavilion attracted robot companies and global brand representatives from neighboring countries, who repeatedly asked, “Why is Korea so tightly unified?” and “How does this structure actually work?”

53045.cap: Visitors listen to explanations of humanoid technologies and record videos in real time at the M.AX Alliance Pavilion. | Photo by AVING News
Visitors watch a live demonstration of AEIROBOT’s humanoid robot ALICE at the company’s booth within the M.AX Alliance Pavilion. | Photo by AVING News

53045.x: This was not a demonstration of a single company’s technology, but a rare case showing how an entire nation designs and executes its robot industry. In the middle of the CES 2026 exhibition hall, now transformed into a battlefield for robots, the M.AX Alliance Pavilion naturally became a reference point.

At a time when global corporations take the stage with robots, Korea responds not as a single company but as a national team through the M.AX Alliance. This alliance, which binds research, development, manufacturing, components, and real demand into a single structure, goes beyond an exhibition strategy and serves as both Korea’s chosen survival strategy in the global robot industry and a declaration of challenge.
If CES 2026 asked, “Who can build robots?” the answer offered by the M.AX Alliance is clear. “We are already moving together.”

53046.x: Bluerobin Inc. participated in the CES 2026 HUMANOID M.AX Alliance Pavilion, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), where it showcased its “remote-controlled multi-purpose humanoid platform.”

Bluerobin is a spin-off startup from the DYROS Laboratory at Seoul National University and operates two business divisions: remotely controlled humanoid robots that interact with humans, and care robots that support emergency response and rehabilitation medicine.

Building on extensive experience in mechanical design and software technologies for locomotion and precision control, Bluerobin develops high-performance humanoid platforms and aims to provide field-tailored solutions across shipbuilding, construction, healthcare, and logistics.

In this context, Bluerobin focuses on enhancing the technical maturity of humanoid robots and on verifying their applicability in real industrial environments. As a preliminary step toward commercialization, the company currently pursues validation in the medical field. It has established partnerships with major hospitals and medical institutions and is preparing proof-of-concept demonstrations of medical environment support robots. Through these efforts, Bluerobin plans to objectively verify system stability and effectiveness in real medical settings while securing operational data.

The humanoid robot introduced by Bluerobin at CES features a multi-purpose platform that combines sophisticated human interaction capabilities with the high-strength performance required in industrial settings. Designed on the technological foundation of Seoul National University’s DYROS Laboratory, the robot goes beyond simple mobility and is engineered to perform practical tasks even in complex, unstructured environments.

According to the company, Bluerobin’s products’ core strengths fall into three main areas. First, its advanced locomotion and precision control technologies enable stable walking on uneven terrain such as slopes and irregular surfaces, while also delivering flexible upper-body movements suitable for delicate tasks, including medical care and rehabilitation support.

53046.cap: To demonstrate the high-strength capabilities of its humanoid robot P-73, Bluerobin showed the robot lifting a 15-pound dumbbell with one hand while maintaining balance. | Photo by AVING News

Finally, the platform’s high payload capacity represents another major strength. This positions the robot as a practical solution for deployment in high-load industrial environments such as shipbuilding, construction, and logistics.

A Bluerobin representative said, “As a spin-off from Seoul National University’s DYROS Laboratory, we have secured technological reliability by advancing proof-of-concept demonstrations of medical environment support robots based on our accumulated precision control and mechanism design expertise. 53047.x: AIDIN ROBOTICS Inc. (CEOs Hyouk Ryeol Choi and Yoon Haeng Lee) participated on January 6 (local time) in the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance joint pavilion at CES 2026, a venue that offers a comprehensive view of “Korean-style humanoid” technologies.

AIDIN ROBOTICS is a startup founded in 2019 as a spin-off from Sungkyunkwan University’s Robotics Innovatory and is recognized for successfully localizing six-axis force and torque sensors for humanoid robots.

Building on this achievement, the company has expanded its portfolio of advanced sensors while broadening its business scope to include a range of robot modules and platforms. According to the company, all of these products are designed around AIDIN ROBOTICS’ proprietary force-sensing technology, delivering high reliability and stability.

At CES 2026, AIDIN ROBOTICS presented a comprehensive lineup of advanced force and torque sensors for humanoid robots. These sensors are designed to be mounted on humanoid robot hands, feet, and other joints to precisely detect force and torque, thereby maximizing the precision and delicacy of robotic motion.

The force-sensing technology that enables these capabilities combines multiple proprietary approaches, including detecting changes in electrode spacing and dielectric properties caused by pressure and deformation through capacitive measurement sensors, and intentionally controlling the spread of electric fields at electrode edges, known as the fringe effect, to enhance sensitivity.

53047.cap: AIDIN ROBOTICS’ force and torque sensor lineup for humanoid robot joints and applications. | Photo by AVING News

53047.x: In terms of sensitivity and stiffness, which are critical for robotic sensors, the company has achieved performance on par with or superior to traditional strain-gauge-based solutions, while also offering more competitive pricing than imported sensors.

Thanks to this balance of quality and cost competitiveness, AIDIN ROBOTICS’ sensors have reportedly received strong market responses. The wrist-mounted force and torque sensor AFT150 has been exported steadily to robotics companies and research institutions in 15 countries worldwide since its commercialization. In addition, the ankle-mounted three-axis force and torque sensor and the tactile sensor designed for integration into robot hands are scheduled for official launch in the first half of 2026, followed by domestic and overseas sales.

53048.x: Faraday Dynamics Inc. participated in the CES 2026 HUMANOID M.AX Alliance joint pavilion, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), showcasing high-torque-density drive technologies.
Faraday Dynamics develops next-generation servo motors and robot actuators to realize a future in which humans and robots can interact safely.

The company highlights core technologies that deliver torque performance improved by up to 217 percent over previous top-tier benchmarks, along with globally competitive torque density and continuous torque output. Through years of research and proprietary design and manufacturing capabilities, Faraday Dynamics achieves industrial value by simultaneously advancing miniaturization and weight reduction of robot actuators, lowering costs, and improving battery efficiency.

To date, Faraday Dynamics has accumulated tangible business results and technical validation references primarily in the domestic market by developing high-performance servo motors and actuators for next-generation robots. In particular, collaboration with major Korean robotics companies has led to verified applications of the FD-Series servo motors in humanoid, wearable, and collaborative robots. Based on these domestic references, the company has secured volume contracts approaching mass-production scale.

In overseas markets, Faraday Dynamics conducts technical meetings, prototype evaluations, and joint validation projects with robotics companies in the United States, Japan, and Europe. With some customers, it is carrying out phased verification procedures with export in mind. The company continues to expand global touchpoints through international exhibitions, including CES, to build a foundation for exports.

At this year’s CES, Faraday Dynamics introduced its high-torque-density drive technologies to the global market. The FD-Series servo motors serve as high-performance drive solutions for next-generation robots, including humanoid, collaborative, and wearable robots. With high torque density and superior stability in human–robot interaction, the series sets a new benchmark for robotic joint actuation.

53048.cap: FD-Series servo motors displayed by Faraday Dynamics. | Photo by AVING News

53048.x: The FD-Series QDD (Quasi-Direct Drive) servo motors achieve compact size and reduced weight through a structural design that maximizes internal space utilization and optimized housing. They incorporate Faraday Dynamics’ proprietary low-friction special-gear-tooth technology, minimizing mechanical losses. As a result, the motors deliver both smooth, natural motion and stable torque output required for robotic joints. Built on in-house production technologies, the motors support a wide range of diameters and gear ratios, enabling customized designs for applications ranging from small robots to large industrial robots.

The FD-Series DD (Direct Drive) servo motors feature a gearless, direct-coupled design that delivers outstanding torque performance and high backdrivability. The absence of gears reduces frictional losses and torque ripple, enabling smooth, compliant motion. Structural simplicity also enhances reliability and durability while making maintenance easier. Available in various combinations of outer diameter and height, the motors allow customers to select optimal specifications according to application size, weight, and performance requirements.

Notably, Faraday Dynamics supports rapid, custom motor production tailored to customer needs, leveraging facilities and technological capabilities that enable the company to perform more than 90 percent of the production process in-house.

A company representative said, “The FD-Series servo motors are next-generation drive solutions that simultaneously satisfy high torque, low friction, and high back-drivability. They can serve as a core actuator platform for the Physical AI era, in which robots interact safely with humans.”

Faraday Dynamics currently exports frameless motors to a humanoid robot platform company in the United States, where the products are applied as key components for robot joint actuation and are undergoing sample and performance verification. Through this process, the company validates product performance, reliability, and applicability.

53050.x: Robros (CEO Ryan Ro) participated on January 6 (local time) at the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance pavilion at CES 2026, a venue that brings together “Korean-style humanoid” technologies in a single space.

Robros is a Korean company that has built specialized expertise in humanoid robotics. It is developing robots equipped with precision control actuators, intuitive human–robot interaction (HRI) design, and proprietary algorithms that enable real-time motion prediction and situational adaptation.

The company has secured a full-cycle technology stack spanning mechanical design, system integration, assembly and production, control software, and AI. Based on this foundation, Robros currently offers solutions for research and exhibition purposes, while progressively advancing each technology component to realize platforms applicable to diverse industrial environments.

At CES 2026, Robros unveiled its flagship humanoid platform, IGRIS-C, representing the company’s core humanoid capabilities. The mid-size humanoid stands 154 cm tall and weighs 60 kg, and is designed with a total of 31 degrees of freedom (DoF) across the body, excluding the hands, to enable precise, expressive movement.

Each hand employs a tendon-driven structure in which actuators and joints are connected via wires, delivering 6 active DoF per hand. Including passive degrees of freedom, each hand reaches a total of 11 DoF. The lightweight robot hands, each weighing approximately 300 grams, can handle payloads of up to 3 kg per hand, providing sufficient performance for manipulating a wide range of everyday objects.

53050.cap: Robros booth at the CES 2026 HUMANOID M.AX Alliance pavilion. | Photo by AVING News

Notably, IGRIS-C won first place in the bipedal walking and static obstacle avoidance category at the 24th IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots held in late September.

At the same time, Neuromeka has expanded its joint projects with large enterprises as well as mid-sized and small manufacturers, based on a diverse lineup that includes collaborative robots, high-payload robots, and dual-arm robots. Through integrated automation capabilities, including robot controllers and software, the company has gained hands-on experience in real-world mass-production processes.

53052.x: AeiROBOT Co., Ltd. (CEO Sheal Eum) participated in the “HUMANOID M.AX Alliance” pavilion at CES 2026, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), where it showcased the “ALICE” series.

AeiROBOT is a startup that develops humanoid robots capable of replacing all types of labor that humans can perform, under the vision of “A Robot for All.” True to the meaning embedded in its name, the company aims to realize a humanoid platform that moves alongside people and creates practical value.

Founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the research team of Professor Jaekweon Han of the Department of Robotics Engineering at Hanyang University ERICA (HERoEHS), AeiROBOT began its path toward commercialization by leveraging robotic technologies developed in the laboratory. In its early stage, the company demonstrated its technical capabilities by participating in the development of the AI-based autonomous soccer humanoid robot “ALICE,” which achieved results in the RoboCup Humanoid League. It later introduced various robot platforms, including the welcome robot “Aimy” and the companion robot “Edie,” and it now accelerates its entry into the global market as its technology and growth potential gain recognition.

AeiROBOT emphasized that it now receives recognition as a specialized “physical AI” robot company capable of commercialization, beyond the level of simple research robots. The company’s core technologies are broadly into hardware and software.

On the hardware side, the company highlights its in-house-developed linear actuator technology, which serves as the muscles in robots. This actuator moves away from conventional rotation-motor and reducer-based systems, enabling more precise force-based control and a more natural physical interaction. The company explained that this technology serves as a key factor that simultaneously improves humanoid robot performance and reduces manufacturing costs.

On the software side, AeiROBOT internalizes AI-based autonomous system technologies, including the use of “Isaac GR00T,” a full-body control AI platform for humanoid robots. This technology integrates walking control, environmental perception, and autonomous decision-making, allowing robots to collaborate with humans and create value in real industrial sites and everyday spaces.

Furthermore, through collaborations with several major global tech companies, the company leaves open the possibility of joint research to embed large action models (LAMs) into robot hardware, preparing to leap beyond being a hardware manufacturer into a global AI platform company.

As external proof of its technological capabilities, AeiROBOT points to its consistent achievements in the RoboCup Humanoid League. Working with a research team led by CTO Jaekweon Han, the company achieved strong results on the global stage with the autonomous soccer humanoid robot “ALICE,” proving that its control technology, which enables robots to make decisions and walk autonomously in complex environments, has reached world-class levels. These technological assets now carry over into “ALICE 4,” the fourth-generation humanoid, which evolves into high-performance hardware that reduces noise while enabling precise force control.

Based on these achievements, AeiROBOT now concretizes proofs of concept with major domestic conglomerates and industrial sites. Focusing on industries facing severe labor shortages, such as manufacturing, logistics, and construction, the company aims to complete validation by 2028 and then deploy robots on real sites to generate tangible revenue, turning its commercialization roadmap into reality.

As a member of the “K-Humanoid Alliance,” AeiROBOT presented its booth in pavilion form at CES 2026. Through the “ALICE” series, the company demonstrated how robots can solve real challenges in industrial environments.

The company emphasized that the robot moves agilely even in narrow factory aisles, making it a practical solution optimized for logistics centers and manufacturing lines that require immediate deployment.

ALICE 4, which concentrates AeiROBOT’s technological capabilities, is a next-generation bipedal humanoid that mimics the human body structure. According to company representatives, by mounting in-house-developed linear actuators on all joints, the robot simultaneously achieves rough-terrain walking and precise force control, which conventional robots struggle to achieve. ALICE 4 moves freely in unstructured environments with stairs or obstacles and performs tasks using the same tools as humans. This means companies can deploy robots directly into existing industrial sites without modifying facility structures.
These two lineups share an AI platform based on Isaac GR00T and offer an optimal portfolio for users to select based on site difficulty and purpose.

At this exhibition, AeiROBOT demonstrated ALICE robots performing high-complexity tasks while safely collaborating with humans in complex, unstructured environments such as manufacturing, logistics, and construction, by combining linear-actuator-based precise force control with physical AI. Through this, the company conveyed that humanoids no longer represent future technology but rather tools that create immediate value in real-world settings.

53055.x: KEISER Inc. (CEO DuHeon Gyeon) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

KEISER operates a label and content platform that allows users to search for and recommend music using a Genre Component Combination (GCC) search engine, and to use, settle, and trade officially released music without concerns about copyright infringement.

Targeting a digital production environment where the boundary between creators and users has become increasingly blurred, KEISER has drawn attention by building a platform that integrates a copyright system with AI and blockchain technologies. As a result, since launching its service, the company has secured TIPS investment, obtained 11 certifications, including GS Grade 1 and Copyright Assurance, won 17 awards, including a CES Innovation Award and a ministerial commendation, and acquired a total of 12 patents, including three in the United States, thereby validating its technology and credibility.

At CES 2026, KEISER introduced its copyright-specialized content platform “JIGPU,” powered by the GCC engine, to global visitors. JIGPU optimizes transactions between content creators in video, games, metaverse, and broadcasting, and content suppliers such as composers and agencies. It moves beyond conventional genre- or mood-based search methods and allows users to find required content based on objective acoustic components of music.

These functions originate from the GCC engine, which forms the core of the platform. JIGPU’s search and recommendation system defines a wide range of musical characteristics by combining key elements such as tempo, density, and impact, enabling content creators to find music that more precisely matches their creative intent.

Furthermore, music discovered on JIGPU can be applied and used across various environments, including commercial use, without copyright concerns. For music producers, the platform supports a one-stop process covering release, settlement, and management, maximizing transaction efficiency for both sides.

In addition, KEISER implemented an integrated blockchain system on JIGPU that unifies the management, trading, and investment of music copyrights and ownership. Through its music release function, the platform completes the entire process from artist contracts to domestic and overseas distribution and settlement without intermediaries. KEISER also continues to expand its technological applications through partnerships with AI mental health solutions and app service companies.

KEISER has signed partnership agreements with more than 500 musicians and has released over 1,000 tracks since the platform’s launch. It is also expanding its affiliated artist network beyond Korea to the United States, Vietnam, and Japan. With its participation in CES 2026 as a turning point, the company aims to fully activate its overseas expansion strategy targeting the global content market.

A KEISER official said, “CES 2026 served as an important stage to confirm feedback from the global content market on JIGPU’s unique characteristics and technologies,” adding, “KEISER’s core goal is to technologically innovate the way music is used in creative environments that have long faced limitations due to copyright issues, and we are pleased to see positive responses to that value.”

The official continued, “Following our participation in CES this year, we plan to expand collaboration with local artists, agencies, and content production companies in the United States, the world’s largest content market, and further pursue the establishment of a local subsidiary and the advancement of our global app services,” adding, “Based on the networks and market feedback secured here, we aim to position JIGPU as a practical alternative platform within the global music content ecosystem.”

53056.cap: Gbrain’s fully implantable brain nerve electrical stimulation medical device, “Phin Stim.” | Photo by AVING News

53056.x: Gbrain (Co-CEOs Byoung Kim and Sunggu Yang) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

Gbrain has focused on treatment gaps and unmet medical needs that conventional deep-brain stimulation (DBS) cannot address, and has developed electrical stimulation therapy technology based on cortical electrodes. Founded in 2019 with the goal of commercializing medical devices that move beyond laboratory-level technology to actual patient treatment, the company has pursued full-scale business development.

Since its establishment, Gbrain has built the entire value chain of research and development, manufacturing, quality control, and clinical operations step by step, centered on fully implantable brain nerve stimulation technology. After completing an ISO Class 7 cleanroom-based manufacturing facility in 2022 to secure infrastructure for implantable medical device production, the company established a GMP-compliant production system in 2024 and obtained certification.

Furthermore, through national R&D projects, Gbrain advanced the development of fully implantable closed-loop brain nerve stimulation technology, verifying technological sophistication and clinical applicability, and it has attracted cumulative investment totaling approximately 8 billion won to date.

At CES 2026, Gbrain unveiled “Phin Stim,” a product that represents its accumulated R&D capabilities. Phin Stim is a fully implantable brain nerve stimulator that integrates ultra-thin, highly flexible cortical electrodes with circuitry. Using its proprietary electrode technology, the device closely adheres to the cortical surface to stably acquire high-resolution brain signals. The collected brain signals go beyond simple recording and are processed immediately within the device for therapeutic decision-making.

The circuitry of Phin Stim employs AI-based signal processing. This technology analyzes brain waves in real time to assess the patient’s current neural state and automatically adjusts stimulation intensity and patterns accordingly. Unlike conventional methods that repeat pre-set stimulation, Phin Stim implements a closed-loop, dynamically responsive stimulation that adapts to changes in brain state.

In addition, Phin Stim is designed to enable brain signal-based stimulation control and functional expansion through brain-computer interface (BCI) technology. This allows not only precise stimulation optimization according to patient condition but also future expansion into various neurological indications beyond Parkinson’s disease, including stroke rehabilitation and paralysis.

A Gbrain official said, “Phin Stim is a core product that embodies our technological differentiation and mid- to long-term growth strategy, and through it we sought to propose fully implantable brain nerve stimulation technology and a BCI-based approach to the global market.” The official added, “As we created meaningful opportunities by meeting various stakeholders, including global medical device companies, hospitals, and research institutions at CES, we plan to accelerate overseas partnerships and commercialization through continued technical and clinical discussions.”

The official continued, “Gbrain is currently establishing a systematic U.S. regulatory approval strategy with the goal of submitting to the FDA within this year, and we expect strong commercialization potential in North America, where demand for innovative medical devices is high and clinical infrastructure is well developed.” The official added, “While accumulating clinical evidence and responding to regulatory requirements in parallel, we will focus on securing global partnerships and pursuing phased business expansion.”

In particular, by embedding an AI engine that predicts accident risks and dangerous driving patterns, GLEC implemented a practical solution that goes beyond simple record-keeping to deliver tangible outcomes such as enhanced driver safety, reduced accident-related costs, insurance linkage, and extended vehicle lifespan. 53060.cap: UNIUNI’s non-vision spatial awareness AI solution “RestroomGuard Savvy.” | Photo by AVING News

53060.x: UNIUNI Corp. (CEO Sooyeon Han) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

UNIUNI is a deep-tech startup that has developed and commercialized “spatial safety AI” solutions that fundamentally eliminate concerns over privacy infringement. According to the company, it positions itself as a privacy-first AI company that simultaneously realizes technological innovation and personal data protection, guided by the philosophy of “safety that protects without seeing.”

In line with this value, UNIUNI successfully implemented non-vision AI technology that detects falls, abnormal behavior, and emergency situations in specific spaces without directly capturing video or images. This helps ensure user safety in locations where camera hardware use is restricted, such as public restrooms, hospitals, nursing facilities, and other multi-use spaces.

At CES 2026, UNIUNI showcased its flagship solution, “RestroomGuard Savvy.” Savvy is a non-vision spatial awareness AI solution that applies ToF (Time-of-Flight)–based 3D depth sensors and AI algorithms, delivering functionality that safeguards users in sanitary spaces within public restrooms and multi-use facilities.

The core hardware of Savvy, the ToF sensor, emits infrared light and measures the round-trip time of reflected signals, generating pixel-level distance (depth) maps from the data. Through this process, the system precisely captures changes in the shape of people or objects, movement trajectories, and dwell time.

In addition, low-resolution acoustic events such as screams, loud noises, and collision sounds, as well as abnormal air quality indicators such as smoke related to fire, serve as auxiliary signals. Using AI algorithms embedded in edge devices that analyze these inputs, the system comprehensively detects falls, assaults, illegal filming patterns, prolonged inactivity, vandalism, and signs of fire.

Furthermore, event data analyzed on the device is transmitted to control systems as anonymous metadata over encrypted channels, such as mTLS. This allows facility managers to receive immediate alerts through visual, audio, or vibration notifications and respond promptly to emergency or hazardous situations. Based on this technology that strengthens facility safety while strictly protecting user privacy, UNIUNI earned the honor of winning Innovation Awards in two categories.

53065.cap: Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK Co., Ltd., during a CES 2026 Innovation Company interview | Photo by AVING News

53065.x: NEWJAK Co., Ltd. (CEO Haehyun Jung) won a CES 2026 Innovation Award with its XR-based interactive sports content platform “SPORTRACK.”

NEWJAK has drawn global attention by presenting an education and sports convergence content strategy that combines immersive XR technology, allowing users to physically participate in real spaces without an HMD, with 16 physical education maps designed based on Korea’s 2023 revised national curriculum for elementary, middle, and high schools. In this context, Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News and also a judge for the CES 2024 and CES 2026 Innovation Awards, met with NEWJAK CEO Haehyun Jung to discuss the background of the Innovation Award win, technological differentiation, scalability, and global market strategy.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Please share your thoughts on winning the Innovation Award.

A. Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK: At first, I wondered, “Will this really work?” But once I tried it myself, I became confident that it could. The idea I pursued was in a field that did not yet exist in Korea, so many people told me, “Why don’t you make what consumers want?” Still, I pushed forward in the direction I believed in, and recent trends are proving that possibility. Receiving the Innovation Award in this context makes it even more meaningful.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Please introduce NEWJAK.
A. Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK: The company name “NEWJAK” combines the English word “New” with the Chinese character “作 (jak),” meaning “to create,” conveying the idea of “creating new media.”

It originally came from the name of a course I taught as a part-time lecturer at a university. At the time, I ran a convergence class in which students from the New Media Content Department and the Composition Department collaborated to create performances, and I combined the first letters of each department to form the names “New” and “Jak.” Since the company originated from that class, our early business model focused on performance and event production until before the COVID-19 pandemic.

53065.cap: Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News (left), and Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK (right), pose after the CES 2026 Innovation Company interview | Photo by AVING News

53065.x: Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: What technology earned you the Innovation Award at CES 2025?

A. Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK: In the early days of the startup, I set the Arte Museum as a role model and tried to create similar media exhibitions. However, as I continued, I realized it was difficult for a small company to replicate that scale. In that process, our own unique content naturally emerged.

I then started thinking about “content that gives people a reason to come back repeatedly,” and I found the answer in e-sports. Seeing my nephew receive prize money as a professional gamer made me realize the market potential, and I developed it into “interactive content that people physically participate in,” combined with immersive media spaces. This technology was recognized as a CES 2025 Innovation Award honoree.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Please introduce the technology that won the CES 2026 Innovation Award.

A. Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK: At CES 2025, we won an Innovation Award with XR content based on digital jump rope. After showcasing it, we received far more inquiries than expected from sports organizations, including the Korea Sports Promotion Foundation, which clearly confirmed that this technology could expand into education and sports.

As a result, at CES 2026, we positioned sports more explicitly. Based on the 2023 revised national curriculum for elementary, middle, and high schools, we developed 16 XR physical education maps in the form of a board game. We plan to complete all content this year and aim for actual school adoption next year.

Unlike most existing XR approaches that require wearing an HMD, our solution allows multiple people to participate together without equipment. The most prominent feature is that physical education classes can take place immediately in an empty classroom measuring 6 meters by 6 meters.

53065.cap: NEWJAK, winner of the Innovation Award in the XR & Spatial Computing category | Source: CES

53066.cap: Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System, during a CES 2026 Innovation Company interview | Photo by AVING News

53066.x: Solvit System (CEO Yeong-Goo Kim) won a CES 2026 Innovation Award with its “intelligent radio relay drone operation system,” which rapidly detects people in distress even in radio shadow zones.

Following last year’s Innovation Award for “iSAR,” an intelligent search support system that dramatically narrows search areas in radio shadow zones, Solvit System earned recognition for two consecutive years by unveiling “SOLVIT-BRIDGE,” a technology that uses radio waves to find actual missing persons faster and more reliably.

Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News and also a judge for the CES 2024 and CES 2026 Innovation Awards, met with Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System, to discuss the significance of the consecutive awards, core technologies, on-site responses, and global expansion strategies.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Please share your thoughts on winning the Innovation Award.

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: Last year, we received an Innovation Award for iSAR, our intelligent search support system, and this year, we are honored to win again with our intelligent radio relay drone operation system. We developed this technology through a public innovation R&D project by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, and we could complete it thanks to support from rescue organizations such as the Gyeongnam Provincial Police Agency and the Gangwon Fire Academy, as well as public data provided by the Korea Communications Agency. I sincerely thank everyone who collaborated with us.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Please introduce the technology that won the Innovation Award.

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: We won the Innovation Award in the Smart Communities category with SOLVIT-BRIDGE. As the name suggests, it means building a bridge of life for people stranded in radio shadow zones.

The iSAR system we won with last year narrowed the search area for missing persons by about 25 to 1. SOLVIT-BRIDGE takes the next step by conducting faster, more reliable searches within the narrowed area.

Currently, rescue sites use video drones, but limited visibility and obstacles such as vegetation or rocks make detection difficult. Radio relay drones transmit radio beams and check device responses, so they do not suffer from terrain limitations. As long as the device is not completely powered off, detection is possible even if the person cannot answer calls or has lost consciousness.

This approach allows searches about 200 times faster than human searches and 10 to 50 times faster than video drones, which is the greatest advantage because rescuers can locate people before their phone batteries run out.

53066.x: Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: How has the on-site response been?

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: iSAR already sees active use by the Gyeonggi Northern Fire Services, the Gangwon Fire Headquarters, and the Korea Mountain Rescue Association, and feedback from the field has been very positive.

We successfully completed demand-side field demonstrations for SOLVIT-BRIDGE at the end of last year, and we plan to supply it after registering it as an innovative product. Supply is expected via the Gyeongnam Provincial Police Agency as early as the end of this year, or at the latest by next spring.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Do you provide the entire drone-mounted service, or can other companies operate it by mounting only the required equipment?

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: We are not a drone manufacturer. The core of the radio relay drone lies in the search relay device and the software that intelligently operates the drone; Solvit System supplies both components. We design the system so that drones from any manufacturer can integrate with it and operate as third-party devices.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: I understand you also operate in the defense sector.

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: About 95 percent of our business comes from the defense sector. We applied radio analysis technologies used in defense to public life-saving applications. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News (left), and Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System (right), pose after the CES 2026 Innovation Company interview | Photo by AVING News
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: What core know-how made the Innovation Award possible?

The second is an intuitive application powered by adaptive stereoscopic geometry. Unlike traditional 3D, which uses “one-size-fits-all” settings, this AI-driven model dynamically adjusts 3D depth in real-time based on the specific content and the individual viewer’s conditions. This scientific breakthrough is backed by a robust intellectual property portfolio, including nine granted patents and nine others pending worldwide.

53117.cap: At CES 2026, Dr. Fei Wu, Founder of LLVision, demonstrates ‘LEION HEY2’ during an on-site interview. | Photo by AVING News

53117.x: At CES 2026, long lines formed in front of the LEION booth as visitors waited to experience the product. Scenes of attendees speaking different languages while wearing ‘LEION HEY2’ unfolded repeatedly. The moment subtitles appeared in front of their eyes, expressions shifted from surprise to genuine excitement. Language barriers seemed to dissolve in real time.

Dr. Fei Wu, Founder of LLVision, emphasized during the interview, “We did not create AR glasses with a translation feature added. From the beginning, we designed a professional AR translation device specifically for face-to-face multilingual communication.” It was not a matter of adding a function, but redefining the problem itself.

Traditional earbud-based translation devices and voice translation services deliver translated audio only after the speaker finishes. This inevitably creates a time gap. Waiting disrupts the flow of conversation. Dialogue becomes fragmented and mechanical.

HEY2 redefines real-time interpretation—not as something that is heard, but as something that operates directly within the user’s field of vision. Word-by-word subtitles appear as the speaker talks, forming progressively and completing as the sentence ends. Real-time interpretation, in LLVision’s view, should be presented to the eyes rather than the ears. This strategic belief forms the core philosophy behind HEY2.

53117.cap: AR Translation Glasses ‘LEION HEY2’ | Photo by AVING News
AR Translation Glasses ‘LEION HEY2’ Displayed at the LEION Booth at CES 2026 | Photo by AVING News

Real-time translation subtitles displayed within the user’s field of view while wearing ‘LEION HEY2.’ Chinese speech is instantly converted into Korean text and projected directly in front of the eyes. | Photo by AVING News

53117.x: “Engineering Uninterrupted Conversation”

The strongest reaction at CES was not about accuracy—it was about continuity. HEY2 does not wait until a sentence is fully completed to deliver translation. Subtitles generate in real time as speech unfolds, allowing users to grasp context before a sentence even finishes. Conversation does not stop.

This is enabled by a dual-eye optical display system and a head-up interaction structure. Subtitles remain within the user’s field of vision and can be adjusted in size and position. There is no need to look down at a smartphone or wait for audio translation through earbuds. Eye contact remains intact.

Another key differentiator is the “Free Talk” function. The other person does not need to wear the glasses. The wearer reads subtitles directly, while the conversation partner views translated content on a smartphone screen. Multilingual communication becomes possible with just one person wearing the device.

“Systems that require both people to wear equipment struggle to scale,” Dr. Wu noted. “The moment one person puts it on, they should be able to communicate with anyone. That’s what makes it a true communication tool.” HEY2 was not designed as a translation device—it was engineered as an environment where conversation never stops.

53117.cap: Dr. Fei Wu (吴飞), founder of LLVision and a first-generation developer of AR translation glasses, is being interviewed at the CES 2026 booth. | Photo by AVING News

53117.x: “A First-Generation Pioneer Opening the Era of AR Translation Glasses”

LLVision is a first-generation company that pioneered the AR subtitle glasses category. Dr. Wu commercialized real-time AR subtitle technology and introduced the first-generation product, ‘Leion Hey,’ establishing a new product category in the market.

Released in 2022, Leion Hey was recognized globally after winning the Global Innovation Top 10 Award at the UNESCO Netexplo Forum. The core philosophy was already present: placing AI within the user’s field of vision rather than confining it to a screen.

“We have been researching AR and real-time subtitle technology for over 10 years,” Dr. Wu explained. “HEY2 is not simply a new product. It is the result of accumulated first-generation experience, data, and user feedback.”
The “visual translation” strategy of HEY2 did not emerge overnight. It evolved from validated real-world use cases and practical refinements made through first-generation products.

53117.cap: Internal structure display of ‘LEION HEY2.’ Key components—including the camera-free AR display module, microphones, and battery—are showcased in a disassembled form, offering a clear view of the physical AI architecture that enables real-time translation. | Photo by AVING News

53117.x: "Focus on Trust: Removing the Camera, Concentrating on Translation"

AR glasses can include many features—cameras, spatial recognition, recording, media consumption, and more. HEY2 deliberately chose a different path. Its design began with one purpose: face-to-face multilingual communication.
HEY2 does not include a camera. External speakers are also excluded. The device focuses solely on voice-based real-time translation. This decision was made to minimize privacy concerns.

In environments such as trade shows or business meetings, camera-equipped glasses can cause discomfort. By removing the camera, HEY2 was designed to foster trust. All data processing operates on Microsoft Azure cloud infrastructure and complies with GDPR standards.
“We asked not what more we could add, but what we should remove to earn trust,” Dr. Wu said. “For AR glasses to enter everyday life, trust must come before technical specifications.”

53117.cap: At the LEION booth at CES 2026, visitors speaking different languages are engaging in conversation while wearing ‘LEION HEY2,’ viewing real-time translation subtitles as they talk. As speech is instantly displayed as text before their eyes, attendees react with visible surprise and delight, smiling and expressing amazement throughout the booth. | Photo by AVING News

53117.x: "AI That Becomes the Eyes, Ears, and Voice — Launching First in Korea"

HEY2 supports more than 100 languages and dialects and enables up to three-language simultaneous interpretation in multilingual environments. Four microphones, 360-degree spatial voice recognition, a 60-degree forward speaker-focus algorithm, and neural network-based noise reduction ensure stable performance even in noisy environments like CES.

By touching the temple of the glasses, users can activate an AI Q&A assistant. Beyond translation, the device supports information search and summarization, demonstrating its potential as an expandable AR information platform rather than merely a translation tool.

LLVision selected Korea as its first official launch market. With a high level of technology adoption and a strong early-adopter base, Korea serves as a strategic testbed before global expansion. The company has already established a local office, with more than 200 pre-orders secured.

Dr. Wu concluded the interview by stating, “What we want to create is not a grand vision of the future, but an environment where people speaking different languages can communicate naturally. We aim to remove the need to consciously think about interpretation or wait for translation. Technology should quietly support human conversation—not stand in front of it.”
At CES 2026, HEY2 demonstrated not just features, but direction. AI is no longer confined to monitors. It is moving directly into the human field of vision.
