53253.cap: CEO Seunghyuk Jang demonstrates the smart tumbler at the AllCOM booth during MWC 2026. | Photo by AVING News

53253.x: AllCOM (CEO Seunghyuk Jang) participates in ‘MWC (Mobile World Congress) 2026,’ held in Barcelona, Spain, from March 2 to 5 (local time), showcasing a smart tumbler capable of precise temperature control.

Founded in 2024, AllCOM derives its name from “All Comfort.” Headquartered in the Venture Business Incubation Center of Kumoh National Institute of Technology in Gumi, Gyeongbuk, the company was founded on the vision of ‘providing comfortable products to the market.’ Its very first item, this smart temperature-control tumbler, earned the CES 2026 Innovation Award 15 months after the company’s founding—even before its official launch—recognizing its technical prowess on the global stage. It is considered unusual for a nurtured company from the Gyeongbuk Gumi Gangso Special R&D Zone to sweep international innovation awards in such a short period.

The core of the smart tumbler unveiled at MWC 2026 is its ‘temperature modulation’ function. According to CEO Jang, existing tumblers and thermos products focus only on heating and maintaining temperature, with virtually no products allowing users to adjust the temperature precisely to their desired level. AllCOM’s product can adjust the temperature from 1°C to 85°C, and a sterilization effect can be expected at temperatures above 72°C.

The capacity is 20 ounces (591ml), approximately three times the 200ml capacity of existing overseas competitors. The water container part is detachable from the main body, making it dishwasher safe, and its battery-powered design allows for free outdoor use without a power source. It also features remote temperature setting via smartphone and tablet apps, with the final launch version planned to support home networking integration.

53253.cap: Three types of AllCOM brand smart tumblers are on display. | Photo by AVING News

53253.x: The design philosophy of this product is the ‘integration of fixed and portable use.’ In the existing childcare market, parents had to purchase a domestic formula warmer (fixed) and an outdoor thermos (portable) separately, with combined costs reaching 270,000 to 300,000 KRW. AllCOM’s smart tumbler covers all functions of a fixed warmer while remaining portable, replacing two products with one.

The estimated launch price is between 150,000 and 190,000 KRW, roughly half the cost of purchasing separate units. “Instead of buying two, our single product is sufficient. While typical warmers are difficult to dispose of after the childcare period, our product can continue to be used for exercise or outdoor activities,” Jang emphasized. He also noted that AllCOM is the only company in Korea that offers a service in which breast milk can be collected via a pump, stored in a tumbler at a controlled temperature, and carried around.

Jang also expressed confidence in scalability beyond the childcare market. “In midsummer, people often throw away water left in cars because it gets too hot, but with our product, you can drink it at the desired temperature immediately because it operates on a battery. In winter, you don’t need to melt frozen water; just set the heating temperature,” he said. He revealed a roadmap to expand temperature control technology from tumblers to various household goods, stating, “Our future goal is to become a global ‘Therm Solution’ company.”

AllCOM matched with buyers from the U.S., UK, and Japan through its participation in CES 2026 this January and is currently in detailed negotiations. Its participation in MWC 2026 is also a move to meet European buyers directly.

A startup in its 15th month is carrying the momentum of a CES Innovation Award to another global stage like MWC. Attention is now focused on whether this move will lead to a successful entry into the European market.

MWC (Mobile World Congress) 2026, hosted by the GSMA (Global System for Mobile Communications Association), is held at the Fira Gran Via exhibition center in Barcelona, Spain, under the theme ‘The IQ Era’. This year’s event is the largest ever, with approximately 2,900 companies from 205 countries and more than 100,000 visitors participating. Major exhibition fields encompass the entire ICT industry, including AI infrastructure, 5G Advanced, and 6G preliminary technology, mobility, and fintech. Additionally, more than 200 conference sessions involving global leaders run in parallel during the exhibition period.

53874.cap: WiseJet set up its first standalone booth at CES 2025 and has since exhibited for two consecutive years through 2026, with a CES 2027 booth also planned. Year after year, the company leaves its mark on the global stage, steadily building the presence of its 'Zero-Delay Wireless' technology. | Courtesy of WiseJet

53874.x: As the Physical AI era gathers pace, a new bottleneck has surfaced. For robots, autonomous vehicles and extended-reality (XR) devices to see, judge and move on their own, they must exchange vast amounts of video and data without interruption — and without delay. Yet cables run into the physical limits of rotation, detachment and space, while Wi-Fi is held back by compression and latency. The company driving into that gap with a 60GHz millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless chipset is WiseJet Inc. (CEO Chulsoon Park).

Founded in 2015 by Chulsoon Park, a former professor at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST), WiseJet is a fabless company developing chipsets that use the unlicensed 60GHz ultra-high-frequency band to replace conventional wired connectors and cables with wireless links. Its core message is simple: in an age when AI descends into the physical world, WiseJet realizes that connection "wirelessly."
"The technology risk has been removed" — Trust built on investment and exhibition momentum

WiseJet raised KRW 5 billion (approx. US$3.6 million) in a Pre-Series B round this June. Five investors took part, including ES Investor, Ecopro Partners, Muir Woods Ventures, NBH Capital and D&D. The round brings WiseJet's cumulative funding to KRW 14 billion (approx. US$10 million). Previously, in its March 2023 Series A, the company secured KRW 4.8 billion from L&S Venture Capital, Daedeok Venture Partners, Daesung Private Equity, Shinhan Capital and the Korea SMEs and Startups Agency.

The new capital serves as a "stepping stone" toward mass production: preparing the near-field wireless connector chip "WC6" for production, converting the video-transmission chip "WV6" to an application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC), and expanding the R&D team.

The company aims to ramp up full-scale production of both chips over the second half of this year and next, while mapping a roadmap toward a 2028 technology-based special listing in step with follow-on rounds.

Apart from fundraising, WiseJet has steadily accumulated exposure on the global stage. At CES 2025, its standalone booth at the Las Vegas Convention Center showcased a robot-joint wireless solution and 8K/60Hz wireless video transmission, drawing visits from more than 110 companies — of which some 50 global robotics and home-appliance firms moved on to follow-up discussions. At CES 2026, it demonstrated DisplayPort (DP) video transmitted wirelessly over 10 meters, and a CES 2027 booth is already secured in an LVCC hall, extending the run to three consecutive years. A Tokyo IT exhibition is also on the calendar for the second half of this year.

In short, WiseJet's current stage is not about proving whether the technology works, but about moving proven technology into the capital-intensive phase of mass production. The WV6 video chip has already completed development on an FPGA (field-programmable gate array) basis and awaits only ASIC conversion. The remaining question is execution and volume, not technical uncertainty.

53874.cap: WiseJet's near-field wireless connector chip "WC6," shown as an eDP-applied prototype (WC6-AiP-eDPv0.1). A wireless module takes the place of the connector slot where a cable once plugged in. | Courtesy of WiseJet

53874.x: "WC6 erases the 'connector,' WV6 erases the 'delay' — two pillars of a cable-free world"

WiseJet's core weapons in wireless transmission are two chips. One eliminates the physical "slot" where a cable used to plug in; the other eliminates latency, the chronic weakness of wireless. Their names are similar, but their roles are entirely different.

WC6 — the cable-free "wireless connector." WC6 (Wireless Connector) wirelessizes not the cable itself but the connector into which a cable plugs. Hold two devices within tens of millimeters of each other and data flows at 10Gbps. Where competing products top out at around 6Gbps, that is nearly double the speed — and, given that video transmission generally requires 8 to 10Gbps, it is the very threshold that decides whether a chip can be applied to video at all. On top of that comes a latency of 7 nanoseconds (ns); one nanosecond is one billionth of a second.

That is roughly the time light travels a little over 2 meters, so users cannot even sense whether the link is wireless or wired. With no physical contact point, there is no wear, no contact failure, no contamination. It turns domains that "only worked on contact" — robot joints spinning endlessly through 360 degrees, or display-inspection lines that press pogo pins onto each panel — into domains that "work without contact."

WV6 — the "wireless video" with neither stutter nor compression. WV6 (Wireless Video) is a video-streaming chip that sends 4K and 8K ultra-high-definition images over up to 10 meters with latency under 1ms. Its differentiator is "full, no-compression" transmission.

The reason mirroring a smartphone to a TV at home stutters and blurs is that Wi-Fi compresses the video before sending it. WV6 sends the image intact, without compression, so there is no quality loss; its beamforming steers around obstacles and blocks interference, so the picture holds steady even under heavy data load. Sending ultra-high-definition video wirelessly without any compression is a rare level of engineering worldwide, the company says. The 8K/60Hz and DisplayPort (DP) wireless transmissions shown at CES both belong to this line.

Why is this "zero latency" decisive? People notice on-screen lag once it exceeds 0.1 second. For a gamer it decides a win or loss; for an autonomous vehicle, the split second to read and react to traffic; in robotic surgery, exactly where the scalpel lands. In fields where a single beat of delay quickly becomes danger, wireless video transmission that reduces latency to virtually zero is not an option but a precondition.

53874.cap: Key specifications of WC6: 10Gbps throughput, sub-7ns zero latency, 0.01–30cm near-field operation, 150mW low power, 4.6×4.8mm compact size, and multi-lane operation free of RF interference. | Courtesy of WiseJet

53874.x: "Multi-lane and single-chip, at once" — WiseJet's claimed edge

The vision of wireless replacing cables is not new in itself. Standards such as WiGig and WirelessHD have existed for well over a decade but never cleared the wall of commercialization. WiseJet points to three areas where it says it differs from those earlier standards.

The first is zero-latency, fully uncompressed transmission. Where conventional wireless mirroring compresses data — inviting quality loss and stutter — WiseJet transmits video uncompressed and has all but eliminated delay. According to a comparison the company provided, WiGig-style video latency runs around 21ms, while WiseJet has cut it to near zero. The company cites same-band rivals Qualcomm and Peraso (in the 20ms range) and Sibeam (5ms), arguing that its video chip is ahead on the numbers.[^1]

The second is "multi-lane." Most competing products stay on a single channel (1×1) because of RF interference. WiseJet says its proprietary beamforming-based interference-blocking technology enables multi-lane configurations of 4, 8 and 16 lanes, securing an effective transmission speed of up to 180Gbps. "WiseJet is currently the only company to implement 10Gbps multi-lane and a single-chip solution at the same time," the company states. These comparative figures, however, rest on company-provided data; third-party verification against mass-production products is still under way.

The third is timing. Unlike the 2010s, when wireless video transmission was a "nice-to-have," today — when autonomous driving and humanoid robots must recognize and react to video in real time — ultra-low-latency, high-reliability wireless transmission has become a "must-have" piece of infrastructure.

53874.cap: CEO Chulsoon Park (second from right) explains WiseJet's wireless video transmission technology to a global buyer visiting the booth. | Courtesy of WiseJet

53874.x: "Not a choice but an inevitability"… CEO Chulsoon Park on what lies beyond mass production​​​​​​​
In person, CEO Chulsoon Park repeatedly stressed that WiseJet's technology is not a "nice-to-have" option.

"There are fields that simply have no choice but to go wireless. A prime example is large LED signage," Park said, adding that "replacing the cabling that ties countless panels together with wireless modules makes installation far freer — and, crucially, the cost is almost the same as existing cable." The moment the assumption that wireless is more expensive breaks down, he argues, adoption is only a matter of time.
"If the price is the same, there's no reason to cling to cable. LED is going this way, no question."

Asked about applications, he turned first to the medical field. "Robotic operating rooms are packed with cables. Going wireless cuts the wiring and lowers contamination risk. When a surgeon watches a screen while cutting, even a fraction of a second's lag can mean touching the wrong spot — our technology has almost no delay, so it reduces that risk."

He added that the company has also built wireless, portable versions of ENT endoscopes and dental 3D oral scanners. Display-panel inspection follows the same logic. "Right now you press pogo pins onto each panel to check the signal, and there are an enormous number of panels. If you can pick up the signal wirelessly as they pass by, you can drop it straight into high-volume inspection equipment."

Asked where the technology peaks, he pointed to "full no-compression." "Sending ultra-high-definition video wirelessly without compressing it is uncommon even globally. Compression introduces delay and quality loss — we solved both at once, combining no-compression with beamforming that also handles interference."

So when does mass production come? Park raised the term "single run." "A fabless company has no factory, so it entrusts chip fabrication to an outside foundry. The stage where only our volume is dedicated and fabricated is what we call a single run. Our roadmap targets reaching that single run this year."

Still, reaching mass production of the WV6 chip will take more capital — his candid assessment. "We have to actually mass-produce and show stability and performance directly; that's how you persuade the next customer and the next investor. That's why follow-on investment matters."

Indeed, earlier this year a global display company and an aerospace company took WiseJet's chips into proof-of-concept (PoC) evaluations. The names cannot yet be disclosed, but the weight of the parties running the tests speaks for itself. What remains is to carry that validation through to an actual design-win.

53874.cap: WiseJet executives and staff pose for a commemorative photo at the company's CES 2026 booth. CEO Chulsoon Park is at center. | Courtesy of WiseJet

53874.x: Throughout the interview, Park kept returning to one word: "connection." "Engineering research can't end at papers or patents. It has to become an actual product that delivers value to people." In an era when AI grows ever more tightly bound to reality, he said, "WiseJet will realize that connection in the form of 'wireless,'" adding a pledge to "tie people, devices and the world into one." WiseJet holds 36 patents, and 18 of its 21 employees are R&D staff, more than a third of them master's- and doctoral-degree holders from KAIST and other science-and-technology institutes, Seoul National University and Yonsei University.

Ultimately, where WiseJet now stands is not a stage of proving the technology's excellence, but of deciding when and where to apply it. The performance is already validated; the remaining variable is the timetable for mass production and adoption. The follow-on investment that will turn a dedicated production run — the single run — into reality is the next gate.

54130.cap: Hae-in Jung, Head of North America at Crosshub, delivers a presentation. | Photo by AVING News

54130.x: Crosshub, Inc. (CEO Jay Jaeseol Kim) participated on Tuesday, the 28th, in the ‘Global Media Meetup’ hosted for domestic companies and startups by AVING News’ ‘International Press Club (IPC)’ at the MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul.

Running for four days from July 27 to 30, this ‘Global Media Meetup’ focuses on introducing products and technologies of domestic companies and startups to the global market. In particular, it aims to report product and technology information of companies participating in global exhibitions, including CES 2027, through global media in advance and expand business opportunities. Hae-in Jung, Head of North America, and Eun Joo Lee, Head of Overseas Business, delivered the presentation for Crosshub on this day.

Headquartered in Yeouido, Seoul, Crosshub is a DeepTech innovator delivering identity verification, digital payment infrastructure, and AI security solutions across 20 countries. Founded as an AI and blockchain technology leader, the company bridges Web2 and Web3 ecosystems through full-stack authentication, biometric AI, and digital identity platforms. Crosshub expands its trust platform ecosystem globally through hubs in Silicon Valley in the US, Paris in France, Tokyo in Japan, and Hanoi in Vietnam. The company won the ‘Best of Innovation’ award in the FinTech category at CES 2026 with its Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI)-based identity authentication solution ‘IDBlock’ and payment API infrastructure ‘B-Pay’. At this meetup, it introduced its voice AI payment security technology ‘V·Pay’ and university digital credential ‘Smart ID’. Building on its global momentum, Crosshub is actively preparing to exhibit at CES 2027 in Las Vegas and submit its latest innovations for the CES 2027 Innovation Awards.

54130.cap: Voice payment authentication ‘V·Pay’ by Crosshub | Image provided by Crosshub

54130.x: V·Pay is a ‘triple voice authorization’ technology targeting screenless or AI agent-driven payment environments. When a high-risk transaction occurs—such as payments, high-value transfers, logins, or account recoveries—it simultaneously verifies registered devices, speaker voiceprints, and dynamic one-time authorization phrases within 1.2 seconds. Instead of simple voice-command recognition, V·Pay verifies one-time spoken phrases by analyzing both speech content (“what was approved”) and frequency, intonation, and pronunciation patterns (“who approved it”). Because the system generates a new phrase for every transaction, recording, replay attacks, or AI-generated voice cloning cannot pass verification. Designed to link with existing wallet and merchant apps via mobile SDKs and APIs without separate dedicated hardware, it features a risk-adaptive structure that requests additional step-up authentication only when detecting anomalies. Currently finishing MVP development, the company is preparing for commercialization through Proof of Concept (PoC) testing in financial and payment sectors.

Hae-in Jung, Head of North America at Crosshub, explained, “If voice assistants on mobile phones specialize in searches or device control, V·Pay serves as a payment-dedicated authentication layer that verifies not only ‘what was authorized’ but also ‘who authorized it at the exact moment the payment is processed.’” She added, “Starting as an additional authentication method for high-risk, high-value transactions, we will expand it into a core authorization tool for screenless payments and AI agent commerce, such as drive-thrus, in-vehicle payments, and smart glasses.” She also presented a concept connecting the moment a user reads brand names or campaign phrases aloud to a new spoken targeted advertising revenue model.

54130.cap: Digital student ID ‘Smart ID’ by Crosshub | Provided by Crosshub

54130.x: ‘Smart ID’, presented second, is an AI-based digital identity and credential platform that connects university campuses to smart cities. Engineered with a 3-layer security framework (Self-Sovereign Identity, Zero-Knowledge Proofs, and IDBLOCK), it converts university-approved academic statuses into ‘W3C Verifiable Credentials’. During enrollment, it unifies access, attendance, library usage, dormitory control, and academic administration onto a single mobile ID. Adopting a ‘Retrofit-First’ approach that links via APIs and SDKs without replacing existing university databases or readers, it realizes minimal data disclosure principles by reducing personal information exposure by up to 90 percent. Smart ID integrates seamlessly with local Vietnamese e-wallets (VNPay, MoMo, ZaloPay) and global payment networks for tuition, cafeteria, and off-campus partner purchases. Crosshub is targeting Vietnam as its first market, conducting PoC testing with three local universities in Da Nang, Ho Chi Minh City, and Hanoi, before expanding into smart city infrastructure, automated AIoT flip gates, and intelligent public buildings. Eun Joo Lee, Head of Overseas Business at Crosshub, said, “Our goal is to connect fragmented campus data into one, realizing ‘lifelong credentials’ that prove school resources and qualifications without repeated authentication even 10 or 20 years after graduation.” In addition, Crosshub expands its trust infrastructure through ‘Travel Pass’ (Travel-K smart wallet for visitors), ‘Smart RAG’ (an evidence-based AI engine for task automation), and ‘KPOP PRO’ (a global fandom platform).

In South Korea, Crosshub collaborates with major financial institutions including Woori Bank, IBK Industrial Bank of Korea, Shinhan Bank, and KakaoBank, executing support projects for the Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT), Ministry of SMEs and Startups (MSS), Seoul Metropolitan Government, KOTRA, Korea Tourism Organization, and Korea Credit Guarantee Fund. Recognized as a 2026 Next-Generation Unicorn by MSIT, it accumulated 2 million USD (3.05 billion KRW) in investments from 7 investors, including MYSC, Krypton, Y&Archer, Zetaplan, and ThinkZone. The company plans to seek collaboration opportunities with global fintech partners, payment gateways (PGs), tech companies, and educational institutions through its participation in CES 2027, while refining core engines such as voice AI and Smart RAG through Series A investment attraction.

AVING News has promoted South Korean companies worldwide through media partnerships with over 800 outlets across 54 countries over the past 22 years. Building upon its global media network, AVING News newly launched the ‘International Press Club (IPC)’ last August. Global US IT and tech media outlet Ubergizmo participated in this ‘Global Media Meetup’.

54183.cap: Flowchart showing the procedure of WARP Solution’s next-generation wireless energy architecture | Image provided by WARP Solution

54183.x: WARP Solution (CEO Kyunghak Lee) challenges the CES 2027 Innovation Awards with radio frequency (RF) energy technology that supplies energy to electronic devices via radio waves without constraints of power wires or batteries.

RF energy technology transmits energy in the form of radio waves from a transmitter, which a receiver then converts into power usable by electronic devices. Using this, WARP Solution provides a new power supply method for sensors, industrial equipment, and robots where power wiring is difficult, or batteries require repeated replacements. CEO Kyunghak Lee leads the company as an RF energy specialist who developed antennas and RF-DC rectifier circuits, establishing WARP Solution based on experiences accumulated in mobile communication antennas and high-frequency circuit sectors. To date, he filed 68 patent applications and registered 35 patents in related fields—such as RF energy receiver semiconductors, antennas, rectifier circuits, and power amplifiers—while securing US FCC Part 18 certification.

54183.cap: Illustration listing products where radio energy-based wireless charging can be applied. Rx chip | Image provided by WARP Solution

54183.x: Core technology is the GaN-based receiver semiconductor ‘WEP Series’, which converts energy transmitted via radio waves into direct current power. Designed by optimizing antennas and matching circuits for target products and operating frequencies, the WEP Series achieved an RF-DC conversion efficiency of over 60 percent under optimal conditions. In particular, WEP3 supports power conversion up to the 3W class based on a single IC, realizing high power with fewer components than conventional low-power receiver semiconductors. Through this, teams design smaller and simpler receiver modules, allowing broad applications ranging from small sensors and Internet of Things (IoT) devices to diverse industrial equipment.

WARP Solution develops not only receiver semiconductors but also power amplifiers (PA) that amplify and transmit RF energy, alongside ‘AI Tracking Beamforming’ technology that precisely steers radio beams based on AI. Combining transmitter and receiver antennas, rectifier circuits, and power management circuits with module design technologies, the company designs overall systems from RF energy transmission to reception and power conversion. Characteristically, moving beyond supplying semiconductors or general-purpose modules, the company analyzes client products’ power consumption, operating distance, installation space, mechanical structure, and surrounding environment to deliver optimized transmission and reception solutions tailored to target applications. Through this, the company aims to build RF energy infrastructure that supplies power across entire spaces beyond ‘device-unit charging’.

WARP Solution’s technology applies to fields where power wiring and battery maintenance prove challenging, such as smart factory sensors, electronic shelf labels (ESL), industrial IoT devices, logistics and security robots, semiconductor process sensors, and sensors embedded in architectural or civil structures. Business achievements continue as well. At CES 2026, WARP Solution signed multiple supply contracts domestically and internationally, strengthening sales performance. Domestically, the company conducts technology verification and empirical testing centered on smart factory sensors, electronic shelf labels, robots, semiconductor processes, and construction or infrastructure, supporting everything from prototype manufacturing to on-site verification. Overseas, the company reviews applicability and expands technology collaboration foundations centered on the US, Japan, and Canada, preparing the US and Japan in particular as priority entry markets. Currently, overseas operations progress through technology reviews, sample provisions, joint empirical testing, and local partner discovery rather than large-scale mass-production exports.

54183.cap: RF energy-based concrete-embedded sensor ‘Core:on’ | Photo provided by WARP Solution

54183.x: The product unveiled for CES 2027 is ‘Core:on’, an RF energy-based embedded sensor solution. Core:on is a sensor embedded inside concrete structures to measure condition information such as temperature, humidity, and vibration, operating by converting externally supplied RF energy into power. Usable for long periods even in environments where connecting power wires or replacing batteries after embedding proves difficult, it enables efficient inspection of internal conditions in buildings and civil infrastructure, improving the convenience of smart construction and infrastructure maintenance. Integrating an RF receiver, rectifier circuit, power management circuit, and composite sensors into a single package, the company verified sensor operation via RF energy reception and BLE-based data transmission capabilities even in constrained environments like internal cement.

Kyunghak Lee, CEO of WARP Solution, stated, “RF energy technology offers a new power supply method to devices where power wiring and battery replacement prove difficult.” He added, “By advancing charging into spatial infrastructure supplying power across entire spaces rather than device units, we will build a next-generation RF energy environment where electronic devices receive necessary energy free from wires and batteries, growing into a global RF energy solution enterprise.”

54184.cap: Dual-task cognitive rehabilitation training scene utilizing ‘EYAS Dual’ | Image provided by INTHETECH

54184.x: INTHETECH (CEO Seung-Ho Choun) challenges the CES 2027 Innovation Awards with its webcam-based dual-task cognitive rehabilitation platform ‘EYAS Dual’. The company is a digital healthcare specialist enterprise developing AI digital therapeutics (DTx) and cognitive rehabilitation solutions.

Focusing on its eye-tracking technology-based cognitive rehabilitation software series ‘EYAS’, INTHETECH earned recognition for its technological capability and clinical validity by winning a CES 2026 Innovation Award. Domestically, the company supplies and operates cognitive rehabilitation solutions across more than 300 medical, public health, and specialized institutions—including major university hospitals, public health centers, dementia care centers, and child development centers—while exporting products to 14 countries including India, Thailand, Malaysia, Australia, Russia, and Canada.

As approximately 55 million people worldwide have dementia and about 10 million new cases develop each year, demand for cognitive rehabilitation expands beyond hospitals into local communities and homes. However, conventional digital rehabilitation devices remain confined to seated ‘finger training’ on touch screens, lacking physical participation and real-life transfer. At the same time, costs and space burdens of specialized equipment, alongside mid-program dropouts, have been pointed out as limitations.

54184.cap: Cognitive rehabilitation training program screen of ‘EYAS Dual’ | Image provided by INTHETECH

54184.x: EYAS Dual directly targets this issue as a next-generation dual-task cognitive rehabilitation platform. Featuring a ‘dual-task’ structure performing physical exercise and cognitive training simultaneously, it recognizes multi-angle motions—including hand gestures, upper limb range of motion, full-body balance, facial expressions, and voice responses—training in a manner where tasks are “solved only through movement.” It applies to dementia prevention, stroke rehabilitation, and child attention enhancement, aiming for real-life transfer connecting to daily activities such as grocery shopping, waste sorting, and refrigerator organization.

Its most notable feature is that it incurs no additional hardware purchasing costs. Operating immediately with standard PCs, tablets, or smartphones equipped with cameras without expensive dedicated sensors, it supports major operating systems including Web, Android, Windows, and macOS, significantly reducing adoption burdens for institutions. Furthermore, after measuring initial cognitive and motor levels through 6 standardized screening tests, it automatically prescribes 43 customized training programs and issues automatic reports containing response times, movement trajectories, and left-right asymmetry after sessions, delivering one-stop services from testing to prescription, training, and reporting. Inclusive designs—such as hand tremor compensation, flexible evaluations without incorrect answers, large fonts, and voice guidance—alongside adaptive difficulty levels tailored to user conditions reduce usage burdens and mid-program dropouts for elderly users and patients.

Building on these achievements and technologies, INTHETECH accelerates global market expansion. In India, the company established a local joint venture (JV), signed a 3-year supply contract targeting 8 major cities, and conducts empirical collaboration with local universities and institutions. In the Middle East, attracting investment from Qatar Development Bank (QDB), the company plans to establish a Middle East entity in Qatar this August to expand business across the GCC region using it as a hub. In North America, pursuing US FDA approval procedures, the company targets medical institutions and rehabilitation markets led by EYAS Dual, which requires no hardware, while preparing entry into Northern Europe, including Finland. Participating in international exhibitions like MEDICA in Germany and WHX in Dubai alongside its CES 2026 Innovation Award win, the company aims to expand export destinations to over 20 countries.

An official from INTHETECH stated, “While conventional digital rehabilitation was limited to sitting down and touching screens, EYAS Dual stimulates the body and cognition simultaneously through a structure where tasks are solved only when moving the body.” The official added, “Because it can be used immediately with just a webcam, significantly lowering adoption barriers, we will present a new standard for cognitive rehabilitation in North American, European, and Middle Eastern markets using CES 2027 as a stepping stone.”
